Designed for continuous and ratio-scale variables with measurement noise, CR-FDH first identifies the upper-left non-dominated boundary cases using Free Disposal Hull (FDH) principles, and then fits a continuous, linear Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression line through the midpoints of the horizontal step segments of the CE-FDH envelope. Unlike CE-FDH (which permits zero sample inaccuracies and forms a rigid staircase), CR-FDH accommodates minor measurement error and produces a smooth linear ceiling line that yields intuitive bottleneck percentages.
terms.seminal_citation: Dul, J. (2016). Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA): Logic and methodology of 'necessary but not sufficient' causality. Organizational Research Methods, 19(1), 10-52. https://doi.org/10.1177/1094428115584005
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of CR-FDH Ceiling Line in NCA according to Dul (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The mathematical algorithm unfolds across four computational steps:
1. Boundary Identification: Identify the upper-left non-dominated coordinate points on the X-Y scatter plot satisfying the free disposal hull property.
2. Horizontal Segment Midpoint Fitting: Calculate the midpoint of each horizontal step segment formed by the orthogonal CE-FDH line.
3. OLS Linear Regression: Fit an OLS regression line Y_c = b₀ + b₁ X through these segment midpoints. If the slope is non-positive or violates monotonic theoretical necessity, mathematical constraints are imposed.
4. Inaccuracy and Effect Size Computation:
 - Inaccuracies: Observations that fall above the estimated ceiling line (Y_i > Y_c(X_i)) are counted as inaccuracies.
 - Accuracy: Accuracy = [(N - N_inaccuracies) / N] × 100%.
 - Effect Size (d): The area of the ceiling zone (C) above the line within the theoretical scope (S) divided by total scope area: d = C / S.
 - Permutation Significance: Calculating p-value via ≥ 10,000 permutations of X and Y.
terms.benchmarks:
Established NCA benchmarks (Dul, 2016, 2020):
- Accuracy Benchmark: CR-FDH accuracy should ideally be ≥ 95% (inaccuracies ≤ 5% of total sample size).
- Effect Size (d) Thresholds: 0 < d < 0.1 (Small), 0.1 ≤ d < 0.3 (Medium), 0.3 ≤ d < 0.5 (Large), d ≥ 0.5 (Very large).
- Data Suitability: Recommended when X and Y are continuous or interval variables with 10+ granular categories; discrete 5-point Likert data should use CE-FDH instead.
terms.pitfalls:
Common methodological traps in top-tier journal reviews:
1. Ignoring Low Accuracy: Reporting a high effect size d = 0.35 using CR-FDH while concealing that accuracy dropped to 85%; when > 10% of cases violate the ceiling, the linear necessity assumption is severely compromised.
2. Negative Slope Anomalies: Fitting unconstrained OLS on midpoints that yields a negative slope (b₁ < 0), violating the axiom that necessity requires higher X for higher Y.
3. Misinterpreting Bottleneck Tables: Treating bottleneck percentage requirements as sufficient triggers rather than minimal required baseline constraints.
terms.apa_reference: Dul, J. (2020). Conducting Necessary Condition Analysis for business and management students. SAGE Publications. https://doi.org/10.4135/9781529718423

terms.vietnamese: Thống kê Wald F của Cragg-Donald (Kiểm định công cụ yếu)
terms.core_definition: The Cragg-Donald Wald F-Statistic is a pivotal matrix-based diagnostic statistic in Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS) and Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) instrumental variables estimation, formulated by John G. Cragg and Stephen G. Donald (1993) and established as the gold-standard weak instrument test by James H. Stock and Motohiro Yogo (2005). Extending the simple Staiger-Stock rule-of-thumb (F > 10) to models with multiple endogenous regressors (K_e ≥ 1) and multiple excluded instruments (K_z ≥ K_e), the Cragg-Donald statistic evaluates the minimum eigenvalue of the canonical correlation matrix between endogenous regressors and instruments, testing the null hypothesis that instruments are weak under i.i.d. homoskedastic errors.
terms.seminal_citation: Cragg, J. G., & Donald, S. G. (1993). Testing identifiability and specification in instrumental variable models. Econometric Theory, 9(2), 222-240. https://doi.org/10.1017/S026646660000751X
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cragg-Donald Wald F-Statistic according to Stock & Yogo (2005).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The mathematical formulation and weak instrument testing protocol unfold as follows:
1. First-Stage Multivariate Regression: Regress the K_e endogenous variables Y₁ on excluded instruments Z and exogenous controls X₁.
2. Cragg-Donald Statistic Formulation:
g_min = λ_min ( Σ_Y₁ Y₁⁻¹/2 Y₁ᵀ P_Z̃ Y₁ Σ_Y₁ Y₁⁻¹/2 · (N - K_z - K_x)/(K_z)
where P_Z̃ is the projection matrix of the instruments orthogonalized with respect to controls, and λ_min is the minimum eigenvalue.
3. Comparison Against Stock-Yogo Critical Values: The calculated F-statistic is compared against Stock & Yogo's (2005) tabulated critical values for:
 - 2SLS Maximal Relative Bias: Thresholds for instrument strength such that 2SLS relative bias to OLS is bounded below 5%, 10%, 20%, or 30%.
 - 2SLS / LIML Maximal Size Distortion: Thresholds ensuring a 5% hypothesis test has true size no greater than 10%, 15%, 20%, or 25%.
4. Kleibergen-Paap rk Statistic Remedy: Under heteroskedastic, clustered, or autocorrelated errors, the classical Cragg-Donald statistic is biased upward; the Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F-statistic must be reported instead.
terms.benchmarks:
Econometric benchmarks (Stock & Yogo, 2005; Lee et al., 2022):
- Canonical Rule of Thumb: For a single endogenous regressor (K_e = 1), the Cragg-Donald F is identical to the first-stage regression F-statistic. The classic threshold is F > 10 for relative bias < 10%.
- Strict Stock-Yogo 10% Bias Cutoff: Typically requires F ≥ 16.38 for 3 instruments, and F ≥ 22.30 for 5 instruments.
- Contemporary Tighter Standard (Lee et al., 2022): Recent econometric literature demonstrates that to achieve standard 5% inference without size distortion, first-stage F should exceed 104.7.
terms.pitfalls:
Fatal econometric errors in empirical submissions:
1. Using Cragg-Donald with Clustered Standard Errors: Reporting the standard Cragg-Donald F on firm panel data with cluster-robust standard errors; Cragg-Donald strictly assumes homoskedastic i.i.d. errors and will severely overstate instrument strength. The Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F must be used.
2. Conflating Instrument Strength with Exogeneity: Assuming a massive Cragg-Donald F = 250 proves the instruments are valid; high F only proves first-stage relevance, saying absolutely zero about whether the exclusion restriction holds (Hansen J-test / Sargan test must be evaluated).
3. Proceeding with 2SLS Under Weak Instruments: When F < 10, continuing to interpret 2SLS coefficients; researchers must switch to weak-instrument-robust inference (Anderson-Rubin test or Limited Information Maximum Likelihood - LIML).
terms.apa_reference: Stock, J. H., & Yogo, M. (2005). Testing for weak instruments in linear IV regression. In D. W. K. Andrews & J. H. Stock (Eds.), Identification and inference for econometric models: Essays in honor of Thomas Rothenberg (pp. 80-108). Cambridge University Press.

terms.vietnamese: Giấy phép Creative Commons (CC-BY, CC-BY-NC)
vietnamese_variants: Giấy phép truy cập mở CC-BY
terms.core_definition: Creative Commons (CC) Licenses—formulated by Lawrence Lessig and the Creative Commons organization (2001)—are standardized legal copyright public licenses that grant the public permission to use, share, copy, distribute, and build upon a creator's intellectual work under specified legal conditions. In open-access academic publishing, the gold standard is CC-BY (Attribution, which allows unrestricted copying, distribution, remixing, and commercial use provided original authorship is credited), while CC-BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial) restricts reuse strictly to non-commercial educational and research purposes.
terms.seminal_citation: Lessig, L. (2001). The future of ideas: The fate of the commons in a connected world. Random House.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Creative Commons Licenses (CC-BY, CC-BY-NC) according to Lessig (2001).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The primary open-access academic licenses function through standardized legal modules:
1. CC-BY (Attribution): The most permissive license, mandated by Plan S and major funding agencies (cOAlition S, Wellcome Trust, NIH). Allows downstream users to distribute, remix, adapt, and build upon the article, even commercially, as long as full attribution is given to the original authors.
2. CC-BY-NC (Attribution-NonCommercial): Permits non-commercial reuse, adaptation, and sharing with attribution, while reserving commercial redistribution and monetization rights.
3. CC-BY-NC-ND (Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives): Highly restrictive; permits download and sharing with credit, but prohibits any adaptation, translation, or commercial exploitation.
4. CC0 (Public Domain Dedication): Waives all copyright worldwide; the international gold standard for open scientific research data and supplementary code.
terms.benchmarks:
Open Science and funder benchmarks (cOAlition S / Plan S, 2021; Budapest Open Access Initiative):
- Plan S Compliance: International research grants mandate CC-BY licensing for all published peer-reviewed journal articles; CC-BY-NC is generally rejected by major funders because it impedes computational text and data mining (TDM).
- Machine-Readable Metadata: CC licenses embed standardized RDF/XML metadata that allow automated web indexers to verify open-access reuse rights.
- Author Copyright Retention: Under pure CC-BY open access, authors retain 100% of their copyright, granting publishers only a non-exclusive license to publish.
terms.pitfalls:
Common copyright traps for academic authors:
1. Signing Away Copyright Under 'Open Access': Mistakenly signing traditional copyright assignment forms on hybrid open-access journals while paying an Article Processing Charge (APC).
2. Commercial Reuse Blockade Under CC-BY-NC: Choosing CC-BY-NC and subsequently discovering that fellow researchers cannot include figures in commercial academic textbooks or use automated text-mining pipelines.
3. Uncredited Figure Ingestion: Copying figures licensed under CC-BY into a new paper without including the mandatory verbatim attribution notice and link to the license.
terms.apa_reference: Creative Commons. (2020). About CC licenses: Want to know what the licenses do? Creative Commons Foundation. https://creativecommons.org/about/cclicenses/

terms.vietnamese: Tính Khả tín / Độ Chân thực (Tiêu chuẩn Credibility Định tính)
vietnamese_variants: Giá trị chân thực nội tại
terms.core_definition: Tiêu chí tương đương với 'Độ giá trị nội tại' (Internal Validity) trong nghiên cứu định tính theo khung Lincoln & Guba (1985). Credibility đo lường mức độ trùng khớp và tương thích (Congruence) giữa những kiến tạo thực tế trong tâm thức của những người tham gia nghiên cứu (Participants' lived reality) và cách thức nhà nghiên cứu diễn giải, tái hiện lại những thực tế đó trong báo cáo khoa học. Mục tiêu cốt lõi là đảm bảo phát hiện nghiên cứu là chân thực và có thể tin cậy được đối với chính những người trong cuộc.
terms.seminal_citation: Lincoln, Y. S., & Guba, E. G. (1985). Naturalistic inquiry. SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: Đã được biên tập và chuẩn hóa định nghĩa học thuật theo giáo trình kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Rigorous scholarly definition of Credibility according to established research methodology literature.
terms.benchmarks: Hệ thống 5 kỹ thuật thực thi bắt buộc theo Lincoln & Guba: (1) Tiếp cận thực địa kéo dài và quan sát bền bỉ (Prolonged Engagement & Persistent Observation); (2) Tam giác đạc đa nguồn (Triangulation); (3) Tham vấn chuyên gia phản biện ngang hàng (Peer Debriefing); (4) Phân tích các trường hợp ngoại lệ phủ định (Negative Case Analysis); (5) Kiểm chứng với đối tượng nghiên cứu (Member Checking - được coi là kỹ thuật quan trọng nhất).
terms.pitfalls: Áp đặt định kiến chủ quan của tác giả (Researcher bias) lên lời nói của người được phỏng vấn; bỏ qua các ý kiến trái chiều hoặc ngoại lệ; không tiến hành member checking để các đối tượng xác nhận tính chân thực của bản ghi chép.
terms.apa_reference: Lincoln, Y. S., & Guba, E. G. (1985). Naturalistic inquiry. SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Tính khả tín (Khung độ tin cậy Lincoln & Guba)
vietnamese_variants: Tính chân thực trong nghiên cứu định tính
terms.core_definition: Credibility is the foundational criterion of trustworthiness in qualitative and naturalistic inquiry, established by Yvonna S. Lincoln and Egon G. Guba (1985), serving as the naturalistic epistemological counterpart to quantitative internal validity. Credibility evaluates whether the researcher's reconstructed interpretations and theoretical findings represent a true, authentic, and believable reflection of the lived realities and multiple constructed viewpoints of the participants. Demonstrating credibility requires deploying rigorous field practices including prolonged engagement, persistent observation, triangulation, peer debriefing, negative case analysis, and member checking.
terms.seminal_citation: Lincoln, Y. S., & Guba, E. G. (1985). Naturalistic inquiry. SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #614
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Credibility (Lincoln & Guba) according to Lincoln & Guba (1985).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Lincoln and Guba delineate six operational techniques to establish credibility:
1. Prolonged Engagement: Substantial, extended immersion in the research site to understand cultural nuances, build trust, and detect distortions.
2. Persistent Observation: Identifying the pervasive characteristics and elements in the situation that are most relevant to the problem and focusing on them in depth.
3. Triangulation: Cross-checking data across multiple sources (informants), methods (interviews, observation, documents), and investigators.
4. Peer Debriefing: Engaging in regular, structured critical debriefing sessions with a knowledgeable non-investigator peer to expose blind spots and challenge emerging assumptions.
5. Negative Case Analysis: Continuously refining working hypotheses until they account for 100% of cases, actively seeking out and explaining deviant cases.
6. Member Checking: The most crucial technique—sharing raw transcripts, analytical summaries, and draft themes with participants for verification and correction.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological criteria (Lincoln & Guba, 1985; Creswell & Miller, 2000):
- Structural Corroboration: A minimum of three distinct credibility procedures must be transparently documented in the methodology section.
- Member Checking Protocol: Reporting the number of participants who reviewed draft findings and documenting specific adjustments made based on participant feedback.
- Thick Description Alignment: Pairing credibility techniques with rich narrative evidence that allows readers to judge truthfulness.
terms.pitfalls:
Common qualitative weaknesses in journal submissions:
1. Claiming Credibility Without Verifiable Practices: Asserting that findings are 'credible' while spending only 2 days in the field with zero member checking, peer debriefing, or triangulation.
2. Discarding Inconvenient Negative Cases: Omitting deviant cases to make the final model appear neat and unified, which destroys naturalistic credibility.
3. Confusing Member Checking with Polite Chat: Showing participants a final 300-page academic manuscript and interpreting their polite nod as rigorous member verification.
terms.apa_reference: Creswell, J. W., & Miller, D. L. (2000). Determining validity in qualitative inquiry. Theory Into Practice, 39(3), 124-130. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15430421tip3903_2

terms.term: Crisis of Representation in Social Science
terms.vietnamese: Khủng hoảng đại diện trong khoa học xã hội
terms.core_definition: The Crisis of Representation in Social Science is a profound epistemological, literary, and ethical rupture that emerged during the 'postmodern turn' of the mid-1980s, crystallized by anthropologists George E. Marcus and Michael M. J. Fischer (1986; Clifford & Marcus, 1986) and formalized into qualitative historical moments by Norman K. Denzin and Yvonna S. Lincoln (2005). The crisis challenged the foundational modernist assumption that a qualitative researcher can write a direct, objective, and transparent textual representation of another culture's or person's lived reality. It established that all academic writing is an inherently constructed, politically situated, and rhetorically crafted narrative infused with the author's own power, gender, class, and colonial biases.
terms.seminal_citation: Marcus, G. E., & Fischer, M. M. J. (1986). Anthropology as cultural critique: An experimental moment in the human sciences. University of Chicago Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Crisis of Representation in Social Science according to Denzin & Lincoln (2011), Bochner & Ellis (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The crisis transformed qualitative methodologies across four dimensions:
1. Deconstruction of the 'Authorial God Trick': Rejecting the invisible, omniscient, detached ethnographic narrator who claims to objectively document 'how the natives live'.
2. Polyvocality and Multi-Voiced Texts: Replacing single-authored authoritative accounts with collaborative texts where participant voices speak directly without heavy managerial editing by the academic.
3. Radical Reflexivity: Mandating that researchers interrogate and transparently disclose how their own biographical positionality, racial identity, and institutional power shape what they notice and write.
4. Experimental Writing Genres: Experimenting with autoethnography, poetic inquiry, performative ethnography, and narrative storytelling to reflect the ambiguity, emotion, and partiality of human knowledge.
terms.benchmarks:
Epistemological and methodological standards (Marcus & Fischer, 1986; Denzin & Lincoln, 2005):
- The Dual Crises: Coincided with the Crisis of Legitimation (challenging traditional criteria of validity and reliability) and Crisis of Praxis (questioning whether research actually changes the world).
- Positionality Transparency: High-quality qualitative scholarship mandates an explicit positioning statement locating the researcher in relation to the participants and institutional power structures.
- Ethical Humility: Acknowledging that scientific texts are always partial, provisional, and situated truths rather than universal representations.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design failures:
1. Ventriloquism / Representational Paternalism: Speaking · for · marginalized communities without their direct collaborative engagement, perpetuating colonial representational violence.
2. Paralyzing Navel-Gazing: Turning an empirical research article into a purely self-absorbed, narcissistic diary of the researcher's personal feelings, forgetting the participants and empirical problem entirely.
3. Complete Relativistic Abandonment: Concluding that because representation is imperfect, all scientific evidence is fiction and rigorous methodological standards are meaningless.
terms.apa_reference: Denzin, N. K., & Lincoln, Y. S. (2005). Introduction: The discipline and practice of qualitative research. In N. K. Denzin & Y. S. Lincoln (Eds.), The SAGE handbook of qualitative research (3rd ed., pp. 1-32). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích so sánh định tính tập sắc nét (csQCA)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật tập sắc nét QCA
terms.core_definition: Crisp-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (csQCA) is the foundational, set-theoretic comparative methodology introduced by Charles C. Ragin (1987) that bridges qualitative case-oriented inquiry and quantitative variable-oriented modeling using classical binary Boolean algebra. In csQCA, all causal conditions and the outcome are calibrated as crisp sets where membership is strictly dichotomous: 1 indicates full membership (presence of the condition) and 0 indicates full non-membership (absence of the condition). csQCA compiles cases into a formal binary Truth Table, using the Quine-McCluskey minimization algorithm to identify minimal Boolean combinations of necessary and sufficient conditions.
terms.seminal_citation: Ragin, C. C. (1987). The comparative method: Moving beyond qualitative and quantitative strategies. University of California Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Crisp-Set QCA (csQCA) according to Ragin (1987).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational execution of csQCA involves five sequential phases:
1. Dichotomous Calibration: Transforming raw case data into binary variables (0 or 1) based on explicit, theoretically anchored threshold criteria (e.g., Democracy = 1, Authoritarian = 0).
2. Truth Table Construction: Compiling all 2ᵏ possible logical combinations of k binary conditions. Empirical cases are assigned to truth table rows based on their specific configuration.
3. Resolving Contradictory Configurations: Identifying rows where identical combinations of conditions yield the outcome (Y=1) in some cases but non-outcome (Y=0) in others. Contradictions must be resolved by adding new causal conditions, re-examining calibration thresholds, or re-conceptualizing case boundaries.
4. Quine-McCluskey Minimization: Merging adjacent truth table rows that produce the same outcome and differ by only one condition (Boolean absorption: A · B + A · b = A).
5. Solution Presentation: Deriving prime implicants, reporting Consistency (≥ 0.80) and Coverage, and interpreting equifinal pathways.
terms.benchmarks:
Established csQCA benchmarks (Ragin, 1987; Rihoux & De Meur, 2009):
- Sample Sizing: Best suited for small-to-medium N studies (10 to 50 cases), where researchers retain intimate qualitative knowledge of individual cases.
- Condition-to-Case Ratio: To avoid the 'limited diversity' crisis (empty truth table rows), the number of causal conditions k must be strictly controlled (typically 4 to 6 conditions for 20–40 cases).
- Historical Baseline: While fuzzy-set QCA (fsQCA) accommodates continuous degrees of membership, csQCA remains the method of choice for inherently binary institutional, legal, or geopolitical events (e.g., war vs. peace, treaty ratified vs. rejected).
terms.pitfalls:
Common methodological traps in csQCA:
1. Artificial Dichotomization of Continuous Variables: Forcing continuous financial or psychological scales into binary 0/1 variables via median splits, throwing away valuable variance and distorting set memberships (fsQCA must be used instead).
2. Unresolved Contradictions in Truth Tables: Ignoring contradictory truth table rows, which halts Boolean minimization or yields invalid prime implicants.
3. Over-Fitting via Too Many Conditions: Including 8 conditions for 15 cases, generating 2⁸ = 256 truth table rows where 95% of rows are empty logical remainders.
terms.apa_reference: Rihoux, B., & De Meur, G. (2009). Crisp-set qualitative comparative analysis (csQCA). In B. Rihoux & C. C. Ragin (Eds.), Configurational comparative methods: Qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) and related techniques (pp. 33-68). SAGE Publications. https://doi.org/10.4135/9781452226569.n3

terms.vietnamese: Nền tảng Phân tích so sánh định tính tập sắc nét
vietnamese_variants: Lý thuyết tập sắc nét trong QCA
terms.core_definition: Crisp-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis Foundations encompasses the formal Boolean mathematical theorems, set-theoretic proofs, and case-oriented configurational logic codified by Charles C. Ragin (1987) and Benoît Rihoux and Gisèle De Meur (2009). Grounded in the philosophical stance that causality in social phenomena is complex, non-linear, conjunctural, and equifinal (multiple independent paths leading to the same outcome), the foundational csQCA architecture provides the mathematical apparatus for transforming multi-case qualitative evidence into formal truth tables, resolving causal asymmetry, and conducting systematic counterfactual analysis.
terms.seminal_citation: Ragin, C. C. (1987). The comparative method: Moving beyond qualitative and quantitative strategies. University of California Press.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Crisp-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis according to Xây dựng Bảng Chân lý (Truth Table) và giải mã bằng thuật toán tối thiểu hóa Quine-McCluskey..
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological criteria (Ragin, 1987; Rihoux & Ragin, 2009):
- Deterministic Logic with Probabilistic Benchmarks: While csQCA originated in deterministic Boolean logic, modern standards mandate reporting Consistency (≥ 0.80) to account for real-world empirical noise.
- Thick Case Knowledge Retained: Researchers must be able to return to individual named cases to explain why specific configurations produced the outcome.
- Solution Triad: Best practice requires reporting the complex, intermediate, and parsimonious solutions.
terms.operational_mechanism:
The axiomatic mathematical framework operates through three core Boolean structures:
1. Boolean Operators:
 - Logical AND (Conjunction, Multiplication): Condition A AND B (A · B or AB) requires membership in both sets simultaneously.
 - Logical OR (Equifinality, Addition): Condition A OR B (A + B) indicates alternative causal pathways.
 - Logical NOT (Negation): Lowercase letter (a) or tilde (~ A) indicates absence of membership (1 - A).
2. Causal Asymmetry Principle: The causal conditions explaining the presence of an outcome (Y=1) do NOT automatically explain its absence (y=0); the non-outcome must be modeled and minimized independently.
3. Counterfactual Analysis of Remainders: Managing truth table rows that lack empirical cases (logical remainders):
 - Easy Counterfactuals: Adding redundant conditions consistent with prior theory.
 - Difficult Counterfactuals: Counter-theoretical combinations.
4. Prime Implicant Chart: Selecting the minimal non-redundant set of configurations that covers all empirical cases producing the outcome.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design errors:
1. Symmetrical Thinking Fallacy: Assuming that if A · B → Y, then ~ A · ~ B → ~ Y; in set theory, absence of the cause does not imply absence of the effect.
2. Mechanistic Software Running: Relying entirely on automated minimization without qualitatively investigating the substantive plausibility of directional counterfactuals.
3. Indiscriminate Case Selection: Mixing radically heterogeneous cases that do not belong to the same overarching population or scope conditions.
terms.apa_reference: Rihoux, B., & Ragin, C. C. (Eds.). (2009). Configurational comparative methods: Qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) and related techniques. SAGE Publications. https://doi.org/10.4135/9781452226569

terms.vietnamese: Chương trình kỹ năng thẩm định phản biện (CASP)
vietnamese_variants: Bộ công cụ thẩm định CASP
terms.core_definition: The Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP), established in Oxford in 1993 and maintained by the CASP UK organisation (2018), is an internationally endorsed pedagogical framework and suite of standardized critical appraisal checklists designed to help researchers, clinicians, and evidence synthesizers systematically evaluate the methodological quality, trustworthiness, and applicability of published scientific studies. Encompassing eight dedicated checklists for distinct research designs—including Systematic Reviews, Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs), Qualitative Studies, Cohort Studies, Case-Control Studies, Diagnostic Studies, Economic Evaluations, and Clinical Prediction Rules—CASP serves as a premier quality-assessment tool in systematic reviews.
terms.seminal_citation: Critical Appraisal Skills Programme. (2018). CASP checklists: Oxford. CASP UK.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #622; nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Appraisal Skills Programme according to 10 câu hỏi cốt lõi sàng lọc tính giá trị kết quả, phương pháp luận chặt chẽ và khả năng áp dụng tại địa phương..
terms.operational_mechanism:
The CASP appraisal architecture operates across three overarching evaluative domains:
1. Section A: Is the basic study design valid? (Focuses on research question clarity, appropriate methodology, sampling strategy, and recruitment bias).
2. Section B: Was the study methodologically sound and rigorous? (Evaluates confounding control, data collection rigor, blinding, reflexivity in qualitative work, and data analysis completeness).
3. Section C: What are the results and will they help locally? (Assesses precision of effect estimates, confidence intervals, risk of bias, and external generalizability to the local clinical or organizational context).
4. Scoring Modality: Each checklist item is evaluated with standardized options: 'Yes', 'Can't tell', or 'No', supported by explicit qualitative justifications for each rating.
terms.benchmarks:
Systematic review standards (CASP, 2018; Cochrane Handbook):
- Transparent Risk-of-Bias Tabulation: High-impact systematic reviews publish full CASP appraisal summary tables detailing item-by-item ratings across all included studies.
- Dual Independent Appraisal: Quality appraisal must be conducted independently by at least two reviewers, with inter-rater agreement calculated (e.g., Cohen's κ κ) and discrepancies resolved via consensus or third-party adjudication.
- Avoid Sum Scores: CASP guidelines explicitly advise · against · calculating a simplistic aggregate percentage score (e.g., 'scored 8/10'); reviewers must evaluate domain-specific fatal flaws.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research synthesis errors:
1. Using Aggregate Numerical Quality Scores: Summing 'Yes' answers into a composite score (e.g., 7/10) and using it as a regression weight in meta-analysis, masking critical fatal flaws.
2. Applying Qualitative CASP to Quantitative Studies: Using the qualitative checklist to appraise mixed methods or survey studies without utilizing the correct design-specific tool.
3. Conflating Reporting Quality with Methodological Quality: Assuming a poorly reported study is methodologically flawed, or conversely assuming an eloquently written paper is free of severe operational bias.
terms.apa_reference: Long, H. A., French, D. P., & Brooks, J. M. (2020). Optimising the value of the critical appraisal skills programme (CASP) tool for quality appraisal in qualitative evidence synthesis. Research Methods in Medicine & Health Sciences, 1(1), 31-42. https://doi.org/10.1177/2632084320947559

terms.term: CASP Tool Framework for Qualitative and Mixed Evidence Syntheses
terms.vietnamese: Khung công cụ CASP trong tổng quan bằng chứng định tính và hỗn hợp
vietnamese_variants: Bộ công cụ CASP định tính
Khung đánh giá chất lượng CASP
terms.core_definition: The CASP Tool Framework for Qualitative and Mixed Evidence Syntheses represents the formal operational implementation of the 10-item CASP Qualitative Checklist, standardized by CASP (2018) and analyzed by Hannah A. Long et al. (2020), specifically designed to appraise qualitative research within systematic reviews and qualitative evidence syntheses (meta-ethnography, thematic synthesis). It evaluates whether qualitative studies meet criteria for clear research aims, appropriate qualitative methodology, justifiable research design, sound recruitment, rigorous data collection, explicit reflexivity (researcher-participant relationship), ethical consideration, data analysis rigor, clear statement of findings, and societal/practice value.
terms.seminal_citation: Critical Appraisal Skills Programme. (2018). CASP qualitative checklist. CASP UK.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #621
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) according to CASP UK (2018).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The 10-item operational screening unfolds in two sequential phases:
1. Phase 1: Two Foundational Screening Questions:
 - Item 1: Was there a clear statement of the aims of the research?
 - Item 2: Is a qualitative methodology appropriate?
 If the answer to both is 'Yes', the appraiser proceeds to the remaining 8 detailed questions.
2. Phase 2: Detailed Methodological Appraisal (Items 3–10):
 - Item 3: Was the research design appropriate to address the aims?
 - Item 4: Was the recruitment strategy appropriate?
 - Item 5: Was the data collected in a way that addressed the research issue?
 - Item 6: Has the relationship between researcher and participants been adequately considered (Reflexivity)?
 - Item 7: Have ethical issues been taken into consideration?
 - Item 8: Was the data analysis sufficiently rigorous?
 - Item 9: Is there a clear statement of findings?
 - Item 10: How valuable is the research?
3. Sensitivity Analysis in Qualitative Syntheses: Synthesizers test whether theoretical meta-themes remain robust when low-quality studies (flagged by CASP) are excluded.
terms.benchmarks:
Qualitative evidence synthesis standards (Long et al., 2020; Noyes et al., 2019 - GRADE-CERQual):
- Core Role in GRADE-CERQual: CASP serves as the primary input for evaluating the 'Methodological Limitations' component in GRADE-CERQual assessments of qualitative finding confidence.
- Qualitative Reflexivity Focus: Item 6 specifically targets whether the researcher examined their own biases and influence during formulation and fieldwork.
- Published Audit Trail: Publishing completed checklists in supplementary materials detailing verbatim textual evidence supporting each rating.
terms.pitfalls:
Common appraisal flaws in systematic review manuscripts:
1. Binary Dismissal of Reflexivity: Marking Item 6 'Yes' simply because the author listed their university affiliation, failing to evaluate whether genuine epistemological reflexivity was conducted.
2. Exclusion of Rich Studies Based on Page-Length Limits: Excluding older or brief qualitative papers that omitted administrative details due to journal word limits, discarding valuable substantive insights.
3. Single-Reviewer Appraisal: Conducting CASP quality appraisal with only a single reviewer, introducing severe subjective appraisal bias.
terms.apa_reference: Long, H. A., French, D. P., & Brooks, J. M. (2020). Optimising the value of the critical appraisal skills programme (CASP) tool for quality appraisal in qualitative evidence synthesis. Research Methods in Medicine & Health Sciences, 1(1), 31-42. https://doi.org/10.1177/2632084320947559

terms.vietnamese: Chọn mẫu trường hợp then chốt / Lấy mẫu tình huống quyết định
vietnamese_variants: Lấy mẫu trường hợp điển cứu quyết định
terms.core_definition: Critical Case Sampling (Chọn mẫu trường hợp then chốt) là chiến lược chọn mẫu có mục đích mang tính chiến lược cao của Patton (2015) và Bent Flyvbjerg (2006). Phương pháp này nhắm vào việc lựa chọn một trường hợp duy nhất (hoặc rất ít trường hợp) có tầm quan trọng chiến lược mang tính quyết định đối với vấn đề nghiên cứu, cho phép rút ra kết luận logic theo mệnh đề: 'Nếu hiện tượng không xảy ra ở đây thì nó sẽ không xảy ra ở bất kỳ đâu' hoặc ngược lại 'Nếu nhóm này thành công thì mọi nhóm khác đều sẽ thành công'.
terms.seminal_citation: Patton, M. Q. (2015). Qualitative Research & Evaluation Methods: Integrating Theory and Practice (4th ed.). SAGE Publications; Flyvbjerg, B. (2006). Five misunderstandings about case-study research. Qualitative Inquiry, 12(2), 219-245.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Case Sampling according to Patton (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quy trình triển khai: (1) Phân tích sâu sắc bản chất lý thuyết của hiện tượng; (2) Xác định vị trí trọng yếu có tính chất thử nghiệm đòn bẩy (crucial test); (3) Thu thập toàn diện dữ liệu đa nguồn tại trường hợp then chốt đó; (4) Vận dụng suy luận logic Modus Tollens hoặc Modus Ponens để khẳng định hoặc bác bỏ mệnh đề lý thuyết tổng quát.
benchmarks: Lập luận mệnh đề then chốt thuyết phục: Bắt buộc phải chứng minh bằng văn bản tại sao trường hợp này được coi là 'then chốt' (criticality justification).
Sức mạnh đòn bẩy thông tin tối đa: Giúp tiết kiệm chi phí và nguồn lực tối đa mà vẫn tạo ra tác động lý thuyết sâu rộng.
Kiểm toán độc lập quy trình: Do chỉ dựa trên 1-2 trường hợp mang tính quyết định, bằng chứng thực địa phải đạt độ tin cậy và minh bạch tuyệt đối.
pitfalls: Nhận định sai tính then chốt của trường hợp: Chọn một trường hợp thông thường nhưng cường điệu hóa thành trường hợp then chốt mà không có căn cứ thực tế.
Suy luận quá đà vượt khỏi logic đòn bẩy: Áp dụng suy luận khái quát hóa sang các bối cảnh hoàn toàn không liên quan về mặt cấu trúc.
Thiếu bằng chứng xác thực đa nguồn: Chỉ phỏng vấn một vài cá nhân rồi vội vàng tuyên bố bác bỏ một học thuyết khoa học lớn.
terms.apa_reference: Flyvbjerg, B. (2006). Five misunderstandings about case-study research. Qualitative Inquiry, 12(2), 219-245. https://doi.org/10.1177/1077800405284363

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích diễn ngôn phê phán (CDA)
vietnamese_variants: Phương pháp phân tích diễn ngôn phê phán
terms.core_definition: Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA)—pioneered by Norman Fairclough (1992, 1995) and Teun A. van Dijk (1993, 2008)—is an interdisciplinary qualitative and sociolinguistic research methodology that investigates how social power, dominance, ideological hegemony, and systemic inequality are enacted, reproduced, maintained, and resisted through spoken and written text. Unlike purely descriptive linguistic approaches that examine grammar or syntax in isolation, CDA treats language as a dialectical social practice, uncovering the hidden, taken-for-granted ideological assumptions embedded in institutional, political, corporate, and media discourse.
terms.seminal_citation: Fairclough, N. (1992). Discourse and social change. Polity Press.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Discourse Analysis according to Phân tích đa tầng theo mô hình 3 chiều của Fairclough: Văn bản (Text) → Thực hành diễn ngôn (Discursive practice) → Thực hành xã hội (Social practice)..
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological standards in CDA (Fairclough, 1995; Van Dijk, 1993; Wodak & Meyer, 2015):
- Emancipatory Objective: CDA is explicitly value-committed; it seeks not merely to describe language, but to unmask covert domination and contribute to social emancipation.
- Micro-Macro Linkage: Rigorous CDA must rigorously connect minute linguistic features (e.g., a specific pronoun or grammatical passive tense) to overarching structural power dynamics.
- Corpus Triangulation: Analyzing multi-genre textual corpuses (corporate annual reports, political speeches, internal memos, social media reactions) to demonstrate pervasive ideological patterns.
terms.operational_mechanism:
Fairclough's Three-Dimensional Model operationalizes CDA across three interrelated analytical layers:
1. Textual Analysis (Micro-Level): Detailed linguistic examination of the physical text, analyzing lexical choices, active vs. passive voice (agent deletion/nominalization, e.g., 'jobs were lost' vs. 'the CEO fired 500 workers'), metaphors, transitivity, and modality (assertive certainty vs. hesitation).
2. Discursive Practice Analysis (Meso-Level): Examining how the text is produced, distributed, and consumed within an institution; analyzing intertextuality (how the text borrows from or transforms other texts) and interdiscursivity (hybrid blending of distinct discourse genres).
3. Social Practice Analysis (Macro-Level): Situating the discourse within broader societal power relations, cultural ideologies, and political-economic structures (e.g., neoliberal marketization, state surveillance, racial hegemony).
4. Socio-Cognitive Approach (Van Dijk): Analyzing the 'discourse-cognition-society' triangle, examining how mental models and social representations mediate between text and power dominance.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research weaknesses criticized in CDA submissions:
1. Ideological Cherry-Picking (Confirmation Bias): Selecting isolated quotes that conveniently match the researcher's political biases, without conducting systematic corpus-wide linguistic coding.
2. Over-Interpretation of Trivial Syntax: Reading vast, nefarious political conspiracies into a single harmless grammatical typo, lacking textual evidence that readers or participants interpreted it that way.
3. Disregarding the Discursive Practice Layer: Jumping directly from word analysis to grand Marxist or post-colonial critique while completely omitting the meso-level institutional production processes.
terms.apa_reference: Van Dijk, T. A. (1993). Principles of critical discourse analysis. Discourse & Society, 4(2), 249-283. https://doi.org/10.1177/0957926593004002006

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật biến cố then chốt (CIT)
vietnamese_variants: Phương pháp sự kiện then chốt
terms.core_definition: The Critical Incident Technique (CIT) is a structured, empirical qualitative and exploratory research method formulated by John C. Flanagan (1954) during World War II aviation psychology studies. CIT systematically collects, analyzes, and categorizes direct firsthand human observations of specific, memorable behavioral events ('incidents') that made a decisive positive contribution ('effective incidents') or a decisive negative contribution ('ineffective incidents') to the success or failure of a specific activity, operational mission, or service encounter.
terms.seminal_citation: Flanagan, J. C. (1954). The critical incident technique. Psychological Bulletin, 51(4), 327-358. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0061470
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Incident Technique (CIT) according to Flanagan (1954).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Flanagan's classic five-step operational methodology unfolds as follows:
1. General Aim Specification: Explicitly defining the functional purpose of the activity (e.g., 'What is the objective of retail frontline service recovery?').
2. Plans and Specifications: Establishing strict criteria for what constitutes a valid incident (e.g., must be an actual firsthand observed event, occurring within a defined timeframe, with clear contextual antecedents, specific behaviors, and decisive outcomes).
3. Data Collection: Administering structured interviews or self-report incident logs asking informants three core prompts:
 - (a) What specific situation or context led up to the event?
 - (b) What exact behavioral actions did the focal person take?
 - (c) What was the precise outcome, and why was it perceived as exceptionally effective or ineffective?
4. Data Analysis & Inductive Category Formation: Parsing incidents into discrete behavioral units, grouping similar behaviors into sub-categories, and synthesizing them into overarching functional behavioral dimensions.
5. Interpretation and Reporting: Presenting category frequencies, operational descriptions, and critical behavioral competencies or design failure points.
terms.benchmarks:
Established empirical benchmarks (Flanagan, 1954; Gremler, 2004):
- Incident Saturation: Studies typically collect between 100 and 400 distinct critical incidents; data collection terminates when newly reported incidents fit cleanly into existing categories without generating novel behavioral themes.
- Inter-Judge Agreement: Independent judges categorize a random sub-sample of incidents (20%); inter-coder reliability must achieve κ ≥ 0.80 (or percentage agreement ≥ 85%).
- Extreme Encounter Focus: Investigating only memorable, highly impactful incidents (exceptional delight or acute disaster) rather than mundane, routine events.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design flaws in CIT applications:
1. Retrospective Memory Distortion: Asking respondents to recall incidents from 5 or 10 years ago, introducing severe recall bias, hindsight rationalization, and memory decay (incidents should be restricted to the past 6–12 months).
2. Collecting Vague Opinions Instead of Concrete Behaviors: Accepting abstract generalizations ('The manager was rude') rather than specific, observable behavioral actions ('The manager slammed the desk and pointed his finger').
3. Confusing Incidents with Informants: Misrepresenting a sample of 200 critical incidents as if it were 200 independent participants (one articulate informant often contributes 3–4 distinct incidents).
terms.apa_reference: Gremler, D. D. (2004). The critical incident technique in service research. Journal of Service Research, 7(1), 65-89. https://doi.org/10.1177/1094670504266138

terms.vietnamese: Tổng hợp diễn giải phê phán (CIS)
vietnamese_variants: Tổng hợp bằng chứng diễn giải phê phán
terms.core_definition: Critical Interpretive Synthesis (CIS) is an advanced, non-aggregative qualitative evidence synthesis methodology developed by Mary Dixon-Woods and colleagues (2006). Combining the rigorous, transparent auditing traditions of systematic reviews with the inductive theory-generating power of Noblit and Hare's meta-ethnography and grounded theory, CIS is designed to synthesize vast, highly diverse, and methodologically heterogeneous literature (quantitative trials, qualitative interviews, theoretical essays, policy reports). Rather than merely aggregating empirical findings, CIS conducts a critical critique of the underlying concepts, unexamined assumptions, and ideological framing of the literature, producing a transformative 'synthesizing argument' and new conceptual models.
terms.seminal_citation: Dixon-Woods, M., Cavers, D., Agarwal, S., Annandale, E., Arthur, A., Harvey, J., Hsu, R., Katbamna, S., Olsen, R., Smith, L., Riley, R., & Sutton, A. J. (2006). Conducting a critical interpretive synthesis of the literature on access to healthcare by vulnerable groups. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 6, Article 35. https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-6-35
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Interpretive Synthesis (CIS) according to Dixon-Woods et al. (2006).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational execution functions across four innovative stages:
1. Dynamic and Iterative Search Strategy: Replaces rigid, pre-locked search strings with iterative, organic searching (snowballing, citation chaining, and purposive conceptual sampling that evolves as new conceptual gaps emerge).
2. Broad Quality Appraisal (Conceptual Relevance over Methodological Flaws): Prioritizes the conceptual richness, theoretical contribution, and relevance of a paper over narrow methodological checklist scores; papers with minor technical flaws that offer profound conceptual insights are retained.
3. Inductive Coding and Thematic Generation: Constant comparative coding of findings, concepts, and author interpretations across studies.
4. Formulation of the Synthesizing Argument: Developing a coherent, grounded theoretical meta-framework that integrates contradictory evidence and challenges traditional policy assumptions (e.g., Dixon-Woods' landmark synthesis demonstrating how healthcare 'vulnerable groups' navigate barriers through informal competencies).
terms.benchmarks:
Qualitative synthesis standards (Dixon-Woods et al., 2006; Noyes et al., 2019):
- Interpretive over Aggregative: Output must be a novel conceptual model or synthesizing theoretical argument, NOT a superficial narrative summary of included studies.
- Heterogeneous Integration: Capable of synthesizing quantitative epidemiology, qualitative narratives, and philosophical theory under a unified framework.
- Audit Trail Transparency: Documenting the conceptual evolution of the search and synthesizing argument through detailed research memos.
terms.pitfalls:
Common methodological flaws in synthesis submissions:
1. Slipping into Passive Narrative Summary: Presenting a descriptive study-by-study recounting ('Author A found X, Author B found Y') without generating a transformative synthesizing argument.
2. Abandoning Systematic Search Auditing: Using the flexible nature of CIS as an excuse for chaotic, unrecorded, and non-replicable Google searches.
3. Rigid Checklisting: Ruthlessly discarding rich sociological and qualitative studies simply because they did not use randomized allocation concealment checklists.
terms.apa_reference: Dixon-Woods, M. (2011). Using framework-based synthesis for conducting reviews of thinking with diverse datasets. Qualitative Research in Organizations and Management, 6(2), 126-141. https://doi.org/10.1108/17465641111159125

terms.vietnamese: Sư phạm phê phán (Paulo Freire)
vietnamese_variants: Lý thuyết sư phạm phê phán
Giáo dục giải phóng Paulo Freire
terms.core_definition: Critical Pedagogy is a transformative philosophy of education and social research, formulated by Brazilian educator Paulo Freire (1970) in 'Pedagogy of the Oppressed' and expanded by Henry Giroux and bell hooks. Rejecting the traditional 'banking concept of education' (where passive students are treated as empty vessels into which authoritative teachers deposit knowledge), Critical Pedagogy posits that education and research are inherently political. It advocates for dialogical problem-posing education and critical research that fosters Conscientization (conscientização)—the process through which marginalized individuals develop critical awareness of their social, economic, and political oppression, empowering them to take transformative action (praxis: reflection and action) to liberate themselves.
terms.seminal_citation: Freire, P. (1970). Pedagogy of the oppressed. Herder and Herder.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Pedagogy (Paulo Freire) according to Freire (1970).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Freire's framework operates through four core pedagogical and methodological dynamics:
1. Dismantling the Banking Concept: Eliminating the hierarchical teacher-student (or researcher-subject) contradiction; establishing egalitarian relationships where 'the teacher-of-the-students and the students-of-the-teacher cease to exist and a new term emerges: teacher-student with students-teachers'.
2. Conscientization (Critical Consciousness): Guiding participants to transition from magical/naive consciousness (fatalistically accepting poverty as natural or divine will) to critical consciousness (uncovering the historical, structural, and political causes of systemic injustice).
3. Problem-Posing Education & Generative Themes: Conducting participatory fieldwork to identify 'generative themes'—emotionally charged, existential issues rooted in the community's daily struggles (e.g., land rights, wage exploitation, water access).
4. Praxis (Reflection and Action): Integrating critical reflection with concrete collective political and social action directed at transforming oppressive structures.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological and qualitative criteria (Freire, 1970; Giroux, 2011):
- Participatory Co-Investigation: Researchers do not research 'on' communities; they conduct research 'with' communities as co-investigators.
- Emancipatory Assessment: The success of an empirical critical pedagogy study is evaluated by whether it catalyzed tangible structural empowerment and community self-determination.
- Dialogical Method: Employing culture circles and open dialogue instead of top-down structured lectures or paternalistic surveys.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research misapplications:
1. Paternalistic Emancipation: Academics positioning themselves as 'enlightened saviors' descending upon a community to 'give them critical consciousness', reproducing the exact authoritarian banking dynamic Freire condemned.
2. Theoretical Jargon Without Praxis: Writing highly abstract, esoteric postmodern academic papers that are completely divorced from concrete grassroots struggles and community action.
3. Co-opting Generative Themes: Extracting community stories for academic publication without returning findings or creating educational resources for the community.
terms.apa_reference: Giroux, H. A. (2011). On critical pedagogy. Continuum International Publishing Group.

terms.term: Critical Realism in Social Science (Stratified Ontology & Retroduction)
terms.vietnamese: Thực tại luận phê phán trong khoa học xã hội (Bản thể học phân tầng & Hồi nghiệm)
terms.core_definition: Critical Realism in Social Science—pioneered by Roy Bhaskar (1975, 1979) and expanded by Margaret Archer (1998) and Philip Gorski (2013)—is a sophisticated philosophical paradigm that resolves the historic conflict between naive positivism (shallow empiricism) and postmodern constructivism (epistemic relativism). Critical realism establishes a realist ontology (an objective, stratified reality exists independently of human thought) alongside a relativist epistemology (human knowledge of that reality is socially constructed, fallible, and historically contingent). Its foundational contribution is the three-domain stratified ontology (the Empirical, the Actual, and the Real) and retroduction (reasoning backwards from observed events to uncover the generative causal mechanisms and structures that produced them).
terms.seminal_citation: Bhaskar, R. (1975). A realist theory of science. Leeds Books.
terms.expert_notes: thống nhất tên "Chủ nghĩa hiện thực phê phán" (đang lẫn "phản biện"/"phê phán" giữa #631 và #632) | Trùng #632, #633; lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Realism according to Saunders et al. (2019); Saunders (2019).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The critical realist framework operates through three core ontological and methodological pillars:
1. Three-Domain Stratified Ontology:
 - The Empirical: The subjective experiences, observations, and perceptions of human beings.
 - The Actual: The concrete events and occurrences that happen in time and space, whether observed by a scientist or not.
 - The Real: The underlying, unobservable generative structures, causal powers, enduring tendencies, and institutional mechanisms that have the capacity to generate events.
2. Generative Causality in Open Systems: Causality is not viewed as regular empirical succession (Humean constant conjunctions: 'whenever X, then Y'); in open social systems, causal mechanisms interact with contextual contingencies (C + M = O), meaning a generative mechanism can be active even if its effect is empirically neutralized by counteracting forces.
3. Retroduction (Abductive-Retroductive Logic): Asking the foundational retroductive question: 'What properties must the social world possess for this observed phenomenon to be possible?'
4. DREIC Model of Inquiry: Description of events → Retroduction to generative mechanisms → Elimination of rival explanations → Identification of the core mechanism → Correction of earlier theories.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological standards (Bhaskar, 1979; Archer et al., 1998; Danermark et al., 2002):
- Explanatory Depth: Critical realist papers prioritize deep mechanistic explanation over superficial statistical correlation or pure qualitative description.
- Contextual Contingency: Explicitly modeling how Context (C) activates or suppresses generative Mechanisms (M) to produce empirical Outcomes (O).
- Anti-Conflationism (Morphogenetic Approach): Maintaining the analytical separation between human agency and social structure over time (Archer, 1995).
terms.pitfalls:
Common philosophical errors in empirical manuscripts:
1. The Epistemic Fallacy: Reducing ontological reality to human knowledge of reality (e.g., arguing that because our knowledge of organizations is socially constructed, organizations have no independent real existence).
2. Confusing Humean Regularities with Realist Mechanisms: Reporting a statistical regression correlation and labeling the independent variable as a 'generative mechanism' without uncovering the structural causal powers.
3. Positivist Generalization Claims: Expecting critical realist mechanistic findings to produce universal, context-free predictive laws across open social systems.
terms.apa_reference: Archer, M., Bhaskar, R., Collier, A., Lawson, T., & Norrie, A. (Eds.). (1998). Critical realism: Essential readings. Routledge.

terms.vietnamese: Thực tại luận phê phán (Thực tại luận siêu nghiệm Bhaskar)
vietnamese_variants: Thực tại luận siêu nghiệm của Bhaskar
terms.core_definition: Critical Realism (Bhaskar's Transcendental Realism) refers to the foundational philosophical doctrine formulated by Roy Bhaskar in his seminal treatise 'A Realist Theory of Science' (1975). Utilizing a Kantian transcendental argument, Bhaskar deduced that the intelligibility and success of experimental scientific practice necessarily requires that the world consists of intransitive objects (real structures and generative mechanisms that exist and operate independently of human inquiry) distinct from transitive objects (the historically changing theories, concepts, and paradigms invented by humans to describe them). This dual demarcation refutes both positivist reductionism and radical postmodern skepticism.
terms.seminal_citation: Bhaskar, R. (1975). A realist theory of science. Leeds Books.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Critical Realism (Bhaskar) according to Bhaskar (1975/1979).
terms.operational_mechanism:
Bhaskar's transcendental realism is structured around four philosophical arguments:
1. The Transcendental Deduction from Experimentation: In a scientific experiment, scientists actively produce a closed system to isolate an event; if causal laws were merely constant conjunctions of observed events (Hume), then scientists would be creating the laws of nature. Because scientists create the · conditions · but not the · laws*, causal laws must reside in the unobservable generative mechanisms (the Intransitive Dimension).
2. The Transitive vs. Intransitive Dimensions:
 - Intransitive Dimension: Mind-independent reality, physical structures, causal powers, and tendencies.
 - Transitive Dimension: Socially produced scientific knowledge, theories, models, and measurement instruments.
3. The Epistemic Fallacy Rebuttal: Bhaskar proved that classical philosophy commits the epistemic fallacy by analyzing statements about · being · (ontology) as if they were statements about · knowing · (epistemology).
4. Concept of Tendency: Generative mechanisms do not produce rigid, invariant outcomes; they produce enduring 'tendencies' that manifest variably depending on open-system conditions.
terms.benchmarks:
Philosophical criteria (Bhaskar, 1975, 1979; Collier, 1994):
- Resolution of the Paradigm Wars: Provides a robust philosophical architecture that unites quantitative and qualitative methods under stratified ontology and retroduction.
- Realism Without Dogmatism: Maintains fallibilism (our current theories may be mistaken) while upholding truthlikeness and epistemic progress.
- Invariance in Depth: Truth is judged by penetrating into deeper strata of reality (from empirical appearances to deeper generative mechanisms).
terms.pitfalls:
Critical review hazards in philosophy chapters:
1. Conflating Transcendental Realism with Empirical Realism: Assuming Bhaskar supports naive positivism; Bhaskar's entire project is an attack on empirical realism for reducing the real to the observable.
2. Inappropriate Use of 'Mechanism': Using the term 'mechanism' as a generic synonym for 'variable' or 'algorithm', stripping it of Bhaskar's concept of intrinsic causal powers and liabilities.
3. Misinterpreting Open vs. Closed Systems: Treating real-world social environments as closed laboratory systems where experimental controls can produce invariant regularities.
terms.apa_reference: Collier, A. (1994). Critical realism: An introduction to Roy Bhaskar's philosophy. Verso.

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số tin cậy Cronbach's α
vietnamese_variants: Độ tin cậy tính nhất quán nội tại Alpha
terms.core_definition: Cronbach's α (α) is the most ubiquitous internal consistency reliability coefficient in psychometrics and social science measurement, formulated by Lee J. Cronbach (1951) as a generalized extension of the Kuder-Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20) for continuous and multi-point rating scales. Alpha estimates the proportion of variance in a composite scale score that is attributable to common variance among the constituent items. Under Classical Test Theory, Cronbach's α represents the lower bound of scale reliability, operating under the strict mathematical assumption of essential tau-equivalence (all items must have identical true score factor loadings).
terms.seminal_citation: Cronbach, L. J. (1951). Coefficient alpha and the internal structure of tests. Psychometrika, 16(3), 297-334. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02310555
terms.expert_notes: Đã được biên tập và chuẩn hóa định nghĩa học thuật theo giáo trình kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Rigorous scholarly definition of Cronbach's α according to established research methodology literature.
terms.benchmarks:
Established psychometric thresholds (Cronbach, 1951; Nunnally & Bernstein, 1994; Hair et al., 2019):
- Early Exploratory Research: α ≥ 0.70 is acceptable.
- Confirmatory / Applied Research: α ≥ 0.80 is desirable; α ≥ 0.90 is required for high-stakes individual assessment (clinical or certification).
- The 'Too High' Warning: α > 0.95 indicates extreme item redundancy (asking the exact same question in slightly different words), which wastes survey time and induces construct deficiency.
- Pruning Criterion: Items are pruned if their removal significantly elevates the overall scale alpha and their Corrected Item-Total Correlation is < 0.30.
terms.pitfalls:
Severe methodological criticisms in contemporary literature (Sijtsma, 2009; McNeish, 2018):
1. The Tau-Equivalence Violation: In real-world data, factor loadings are almost never equal. When tau-equivalence is violated, Cronbach's α systematically · underestimates · true scale reliability (McDonald's ω or Composite Reliability must be reported).
2. The Test-Length Inflation Artifact: Because alpha is a direct mathematical function of the number of items (k), adding 20 poorly correlated items will artificially drive alpha above 0.85, masking low item quality.
3. The Unidimensionality Myth: High alpha does NOT prove that a scale is unidimensional; a multidimensional scale consisting of two distinct, moderately correlated factors can easily achieve α > 0.85 (CFA must be run to test unidimensionality).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The algebraic formulation and computation unfold as follows:
1. Mathematical Formula: For a scale comprising k observed items with item variances σ_X_i² and total composite scale variance σ_S²:
α = [k / (k - 1)] · [1 - (∑_(i=1)^k σ_X_i²) / σ_S²]
2. Alternative Standardized Formulation: Expressed via average inter-item correlation (r̄):
α_standardized = (k · r̄) / [1 + (k - 1)r̄]
3. Core Mathematical Axiom (Essential Tau-Equivalence): Assumes that the single-factor confirmatory model fits the data with equal unstandardized factor loadings across all items (λ₁ = λ₂ = ... = λ_k).
4. Uncorrelated Errors Axiom: Assumes error terms across items are strictly uncorrelated (Cov(ε_i, ε_j) = 0). Violating this by adding correlated errors artificially inflates alpha.
terms.apa_reference: McNeish, D. (2018). Thanks coefficient alpha, we'll take it from here. Psychological Methods, 23(3), 412-433. https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000144

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích so sánh đa trường hợp (So sánh xuyên trường hợp)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật so sánh đối chiếu đa case
Cross-Case Analysis in Multiple Case Studies
domain_tags: Qualitative Research & Multiple Case Study Design
terms.core_definition: Cross-Case Comparative Analysis is an advanced qualitative and configurational analytical methodology, formalized by Robert K. Yin (2018) and Matthew B. Miles, A. Michael Huberman, and Johnny Saldaña (2014), applied in multiple-case study designs. Following an initial in-depth within-case analysis of each isolated case, cross-case analysis systematically compares patterns, processes, contexts, and outcomes across multiple bounded cases to identify cross-case similarities, differences, typologies, and generative causal mechanisms, enhancing both the theoretical generalizability and contextual robustness of qualitative findings.
terms.seminal_citation: Eisenhardt, K. M. (1989). Building theories from case study research. Academy of Management Review, 14(4), 532-550. https://doi.org/10.2307/258557
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Case Comparative Analysis according to Eisenhardt (1989), Yin (2018).
terms.category: Qualitative Research & Multiple Case Study Design
terms.operational_mechanism:
The operational execution functions across four structured analytical phases:
1. Thorough Within-Case Analysis: Conducting exhaustive case profiling, process tracing, and chronological coding for each case independently to understand its holistic internal dynamics before cross-case comparison begins.
2. Cross-Case Display Construction: Developing standardized visual display matrices (Miles et al., 2014):
 - Case-Ordered Descriptive Matrices: Sorting cases along a key dimension (e.g., firm size or performance).
 - Variable-by-Case Matrices: Cross-tabulating institutional conditions against strategic outcomes.
3. Replication Logic (Yin):
 - Literal Replication: Selecting cases that are predicted to produce similar results based on theoretical commonalities.
 - Theoretical Replication: Selecting cases that are predicted to produce contrasting results for predictable theoretical reasons.
4. Synthesis & Typology Generation: Inductively deriving overarching organizational archetypes, configuring causal pathways, and refining theoretical propositions.
terms.benchmarks:
Case study standards (Yin, 2018; Eisenhardt, 1989):
- Case Selection Cardinality: Eisenhardt recommends 4 to 10 cases; fewer than 4 cases makes empirical cross-case patterns difficult to ground, while more than 10 cases generates cognitive information overload.
- Theoretical vs. Sampling Selection: Cases must be chosen for theoretical reasons (revelatory, extreme, or polar types), NOT as a statistical representative sample.
- Chain of Evidence: Maintaining an auditable case study database that maps cross-case conclusions back to primary field evidence in each individual case.
terms.pitfalls:
Common research design defects identified by reviewers:
1. Premature Cross-Case Synthesis: Jumping immediately into comparing cases without completing thorough within-case analyses, resulting in superficial, shallow thematic comparisons.
2. Treating Cases as Quantitative Survey Respondents: Converting rich cases into a series of isolated variables and losing the holistic, contextual causal narrative that makes case study research powerful.
3. Unbalanced Within-Case Depth: Devoting 50 pages to Case 1 and 2 pages to Case 4, creating severe interpretive asymmetry.
terms.apa_reference: Miles, M. B., Huberman, A. M., & Saldaña, J. (2014). Qualitative data analysis: A methods sourcebook (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Tổng hợp xuyên trường hợp / Phân tích tổng hợp đa tình huống
vietnamese_variants: Phân tích so sánh đa trường hợp
Tổng hợp so sánh liên trường hợp
terms.core_definition: Cross-Case Synthesis là kỹ thuật phân tích dữ liệu chuyên biệt áp dụng riêng cho các thiết kế nghiên cứu đa trường hợp (từ 2 trường hợp trở lên) theo chuẩn mực của Robert K. Yin (2018). Kỹ thuật này đối chiếu các phát hiện độc lập từ từng trường hợp riêng lẻ nhằm phát hiện các mẫu hình chung (cross-case patterns), các điểm tương đồng hội tụ và các dị biệt có ý nghĩa lý thuyết, từ đó kiểm chứng logic nhân bản (replication logic) và xây dựng khung lý thuyết khái quát hóa cao hơn.
terms.seminal_citation: Yin, R. K. (2018). Case Study Research and Applications: Design and Methods (6th ed.). SAGE Publications; Miles, M. B., Huberman, A. M., & Saldaña, J. (2020). Qualitative Data Analysis: A Methods Sourcebook (4th ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: Đã cập nhật định nghĩa chuyên sâu từ tài liệu kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-case synthesis according to Yin (2014).
terms.operational_mechanism: Kỹ thuật thực hiện theo Yin (2018) và Miles, Huberman & Saldaña (2020): (1) Hoàn thiện báo cáo phân tích nội tại cho từng case riêng biệt (within-case narrative); (2) Xây dựng các ma trận xuyên trường hợp (cross-case word tables / meta-matrices) tóm lược các biến số hoặc mệnh đề lý thuyết trọng yếu; (3) Kiểm tra sự xuất hiện của các quy luật: Xác định xem các trường hợp có hành vi tương tự nhau (Literal replication) hay khác biệt theo đúng điều kiện dự đoán (Theoretical replication); (4) Phân tích các trường hợp ngoại lệ hoặc mâu thuẫn để điều chỉnh mệnh đề lý thuyết.
benchmarks: Điều kiện tiên quyết bắt buộc: Phải hoàn tất 100% phân tích Within-Case chi tiết trước khi tiến hành Cross-Case Synthesis.
Sử dụng bảng từ xuyên trường hợp (Cross-Case Word Tables): Trình bày minh bạch dữ liệu đối chiếu giữa các case theo từng biến cố hoặc chủ đề nghiên cứu.
Kiểm định đối chứng chặt chẽ: Phải có ít nhất 2 phương giải thích đối thủ (rival explanations) được xem xét và bác bỏ thông qua dữ liệu so sánh xuyên trường hợp.
pitfalls: Gộp dữ liệu thô (pooling data) kiểu thống kê: Trộn lẫn dữ liệu của tất cả các case lại để phân tích chung ngay từ đầu, phá vỡ bối cảnh toàn vẹn của từng trường hợp cụ thể.
So sánh bề mặt (superficial cross-case comparison): Chỉ liệt kê điểm giống và khác nhau mang tính hình thức bên ngoài mà không liên kết được với cơ chế lý thuyết nhân quả.
Bỏ qua các trường hợp không khớp mô hình: Cố tình lờ đi trường hợp có phát hiện trái ngược với các trường hợp còn lại để tạo ra một kết luận đồng thuận giả tạo.
terms.apa_reference: Yin, R. K. (2018). Case study research and applications: Design and methods (6th ed.). SAGE Publications, Inc.

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình trễ chéo hệ số chặn ngẫu nhiên với phần dư có cấu trúc
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình bảng trễ chéo tách biệt giữa và nội cá thể
terms.core_definition: Mô hình trễ chéo hệ số chặn ngẫu nhiên (RI-CLPM - Hamaker, Kuiper, & Grasman, 2015) là bước phát triển vượt bậc nhằm khắc phục sai sót nền tảng của CLPM truyền thống. Bằng cách bổ sung các biến tiềm ẩn hệ số chặn ngẫu nhiên (random intercepts) đại diện cho các đặc tính ổn định bất biến thời gian giữa các cá thể (between-person differences), RI-CLPM cho phép các hệ số trễ chéo phản ánh thuần túy các dao động nội tại cá thể (within-person fluctuations), đem lại kết luận nhân quả thực sự vững chắc.
terms.seminal_citation: Hamaker, Kuiper, & Grasman (2015)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Lagged Latent Curve Model with Structured Residuals according to Curran et al. (2014).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Phân tách mỗi biến quan sát y_it thành 2 thành phần độc lập: Hệ số chặn ngẫu nhiên RI_y_i (cấp độ giữa các cá thể, có hiệp phương sai với RI_x_i) và phần dư tiềm ẩn p_y_it (cấp độ nội tại cá thể theo thời gian). 2. Thiết lập cấu trúc tự hồi quy và trễ chéo hoàn toàn trên các phần dư tiềm ẩn: p_y_it = α · p_y_i,t-1 + β · p_x_i,t-1 + u_y_it. 3. Ước lượng qua Maximum Likelihood trong môi trường SEM (Mplus, lavaan).
terms.benchmarks: Đòi hỏi tối thiểu T ≥ 3 đợt sóng đo lường (waves) để định danh mô hình. So sánh chỉ số AIC/BIC và kiểm định Chi-bình phương chênh lệch (chi-square difference test) giữa CLPM và RI-CLPM; RI-CLPM hầu như luôn cho độ phù hợp vượt trội (CFI > 0.95, RMSEA < 0.05).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Chạy RI-CLPM với T = 2 (mô hình không thể định danh toán học trừ khi áp đặt các ràng buộc vô lý); không kiểm tra tính bất biến đo lường dọc (longitudinal measurement invariance) trước khi chạy mô hình khi các biến là biến tiềm ẩn đa chỉ báo.
terms.apa_reference: Hamaker, E. L., Kuiper, R. M., & Grasman, R. P. (2015). A critique of the cross-lagged panel model. Psychological Methods, 20(1), 102–116. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0038889

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình bảng trễ chéo truyền thống
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình hồi quy trễ chéo hai chiều
terms.core_definition: Mô hình bảng trễ chéo truyền thống (CLPM - Campbell & Stanley, 1963; Kenny, 1975) là kỹ thuật mô hình hóa cấu trúc tuyến tính (SEM) trên dữ liệu bảng dài hạn (longitudinal data) nhằm kiểm tra quan hệ nhân quả tương hỗ (reciprocal / bidirectional causal relations) giữa hai hoặc nhiều biến số qua ít nhất hai thời điểm đo lường.
terms.seminal_citation: Campbell & Stanley (1963); Kenny (1975); Hamaker et al. (2015)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Lagged Panel Model (CLPM) according to Kenny (1975).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Ước lượng đồng thời: Hệ số tự hồi quy (autoregressive paths: X_{t-1} → X_t và Y_{t-1} → Y_t đo lường tính ổn định theo thời gian). 2. Hệ số trễ chéo (cross-lagged paths: X_{t-1} → Y_t và Y_{t-1} → X_t đo lường ảnh hưởng dự báo nhân quả chéo sau khi đã kiểm soát quán tính của chính nó). 3. Hiệp phương sai đồng thời (synchronous covariances giữa sai số e_Xt và e_Yt tại mỗi thời điểm).
terms.benchmarks: Một biến X được xem là tiền đề dẫn dắt Y nếu hệ số trễ chéo X_{t-1} → Y_t có ý nghĩa thống kê (p < 0.05) trong khi chiều ngược lại Y_{t-1} → X_t không có ý nghĩa hoặc có độ lớn nhỏ hơn đáng kể. Các chỉ số độ phù hợp SEM toàn cục phải đạt: CFI/TLI ≥ 0.90, RMSEA ≤ 0.08, SRMR ≤ 0.08.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện kinh điển (Hamaker et al., 2015): CLPM truyền thống gộp chung (confounds) phương sai giữa các cá thể (between-person variance, mang tính bất biến thời gian) và phương sai nội tại cá thể (within-person variance, động lực biến thiên theo thời gian), dẫn đến các kết luận sai lệch nghiêm trọng về chiều nhân quả. Khuyến nghị chuẩn mực hiện nay là phải chuyển sang RI-CLPM.
terms.apa_reference: Hamaker, E. L., Kuiper, R. M., & Grasman, R. P. (2015). A critique of the cross-lagged panel model. Psychological Methods, 20(1), 102–116. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0038889

terms.vietnamese: Tương tác xuyên cấp trong mô hình đa cấp (HLM / MLM)
vietnamese_variants: Hiệu ứng tương tác xuyên cấp
Tương tác giữa các cấp độ
Cross-Level Moderation in Hierarchical Linear Modeling
terms.core_definition: A Cross-Level Interaction is an advanced moderation phenomenon in Multilevel Modeling (MLM) and Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM), formalized by Stephen W. Raudenbush and Anthony S. Bryk (2002; Snijders & Bosker, 2012), occurring when a higher-level macro variable (Level 2, e.g., departmental climate, school funding, national culture) moderates the relationship between a lower-level micro predictor (Level 1, e.g., employee commitment, student effort) and a lower-level outcome (Level 1, e.g., job performance, test scores). In essence, it models random slopes at Level 1 as predicted outcomes of Level 2 covariates.
terms.seminal_citation: Raudenbush, S. W., & Bryk, A. S. (2002). Hierarchical linear models: Applications and data analysis methods (2nd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-Level Interaction according to Aguinis et al. (2013).
terms.operational_mechanism:
The two-level mathematical architecture is specified as:
1. Level 1 (Individual Level) Equation:
Y_ij = β_0j + β_1j X_ij + e_ij, e_ij ~ N(0, σ²)
where Y_ij is outcome of individual i in group j, and β_1j is the group-specific slope.
2. Level 2 (Group Level) Equations:
β_0j = γ_00 + γ_01 W_j + u_0j
β_1j = γ_10 + γ_11 W_j + u_1j
where W_j is the Level 2 moderator, γ_11 is the cross-level interaction coefficient, and u_1j is the random slope disturbance.
3. Combined Mixed-Model Formulation:
Y_ij = ( γ_00 + γ_01 W_j + γ_10 X_ij + γ_11 (X_ij × W_j) + ( u_0j + u_1j X_ij + e_ij
4. Centering Decisions: Level 1 predictor X_ij must be Centered within Clusters (CWC / group-mean centering: X_ij - X̄_.j) to completely separate pure micro-level slope variance from macro-level contextual between-group variance.
terms.benchmarks:
Methodological benchmarks (Raudenbush & Bryk, 2002; Enders & Tofighi, 2007):
- Centering Rule: When testing cross-level interactions, Group-Mean Centering (CWC) of the Level 1 regressor is mandatory; using Grand-Mean Centering (CGM) conflates within-group and between-group effects, biasing γ_11.
- Sample Size Requirements: Detecting a cross-level interaction requires adequate Level 2 sample size (minimum 30 to 50 groups, with 5 to 20 individuals per group; 50/20 rule).
- Random Slope Verification: The Level 1 slope β_1j must exhibit significant residual variance (u_1j > 0 via likelihood ratio test) before modeling Level 2 cross-level predictors.
terms.pitfalls:
Critical multilevel modeling errors:
1. Conflating Centering Strategies: Using Grand-Mean Centering for X when interpreting cross-level interactions, resulting in an uninterpretable blend of individual and contextual influences.
2. Underpowered Level 2 Sample Sizes: Conducting multilevel cross-level moderation with only 10 or 12 organizations (J = 12), leading to severely inflated standard errors and high Type II error rates for γ_11.
3. Fixing Slopes to Invariance: Testing γ_11 while constraining the random slope variance to zero (u_1j = 0), which severely deflates standard errors and causes massive false-positive rejections (Type I errors).
terms.apa_reference: Enders, C. K., & Tofighi, D. (2007). Centering predictor variables in cross-sectional multilevel models: A new look at an old issue. Psychological Methods, 12(2), 121-138. https://doi.org/10.1037/1082-989X.12.2.121

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn hệ số tải chéo đánh giá giá trị phân biệt
terms.core_definition: Tiêu chuẩn hệ số tải chéo (Cross-Loadings Criterion - Chin, 1998) là phương pháp đánh giá giá trị phân biệt ở cấp độ biến quan sát (chỉ báo) trong mô hình SEM. Tiêu chuẩn yêu cầu hệ số tải nhân tố ngoài (outer loading) của một biến quan sát lên cấu trúc tiềm ẩn mà nó đại diện phải lớn hơn đáng kể so với tất cả các hệ số tải chéo của biến đó lên bất kỳ cấu trúc tiềm ẩn nào khác trong mô hình.
terms.seminal_citation: Chin (1998); Hair et al. (2022)
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Cross-loadings criterion according to Henseler et al. (2015); Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Xây dựng bảng ma trận hệ số tải chéo (Cross-loadings matrix) biểu diễn tương quan giữa tất cả các biến quan sát với toàn bộ điểm số biến tiềm ẩn (latent variable scores). 2. Kiểm tra điều kiện từng hàng: Hệ số tải chính λ_ii phải vượt trội hơn mọi hệ số tải chéo λ_ij (với j ≠ i). 3. Khoảng cách chênh lệch tối thiểu: Δ_lambda = λ_ii - max(λ_ij) phải đạt ngưỡng an toàn.
terms.benchmarks: Ngưỡng Chin (1998) & Hair et al. (2022): Hệ số tải chính phải ≥ 0.70. Khoảng cách giữa hệ số tải chính và hệ số tải chéo cao nhất tối thiểu phải đạt từ 0.10 đến 0.20 đơn vị. Nếu biến quan sát tải lên một cấu trúc khác với mức độ gần bằng cấu trúc gốc (Δ_lambda < 0.10), biến bị nghi ngờ có tính nhập nhằng (ambiguous item).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Chỉ dựa vào tiêu chuẩn Cross-loadings để bảo vệ giá trị phân biệt trên các tạp chí Q1. Nghiên cứu mô phỏng của Henseler et al. (2015) đã chứng minh rằng Cross-loadings có độ nhạy cực kỳ kém (tỷ lệ phát hiện sai sót dưới 50% trong nhiều kịch bản); bắt buộc phải báo cáo tiêu chuẩn HTMT song hành.
terms.apa_reference: Chin, W. W. (1998). The partial least squares approach to structural equation modeling. Modern Methods for Business Research, 295(2), 295–336.

terms.vietnamese: Nhận diện tải chéo trong phân tích nhân tố
terms.core_definition: Cross-Loadings Identification is an essential diagnostic procedure in Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), and PLS-SEM (Wynne W.
