terms.core_definition: Heteroskedasticity (frequently spelled heteroscedasticity) refers to the violation of the classical Gauss-Markov assumption of homoskedasticity in regression analysis, occurring when the variance of the error term conditional on the explanatory variables is not constant across observations: Var(epsilon_i | X) = sigma_i^2 != sigma^2. While Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) point estimates remain linear, unbiased, and consistent in the presence of heteroskedasticity, OLS is no longer efficient (ceasing to be BLUE), and standard OLS standard error formulas become severely biased, leading to invalid t-statistics, inflated Type I error rates, and unreliable confidence intervals.
terms.seminal_citation: White, H. (1980). A heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix estimator and a direct test for heteroskedasticity. Econometrica, 48(4), 817-838.
terms.expert_notes: Đã cập nhật định nghĩa chuyên sâu từ tài liệu kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Heteroskedasticity according to Wooldridge (2010).
terms.operational_mechanism: Diagnostic and remedial workflow: (1) Graphical inspection: Plotting OLS squared residuals hat{epsilon}_i^2 against fitted values hat{Y}_i or explanatory variables X_j; (2) Statistical testing: Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test (testing linear relationship between squared residuals and X) and White's General Test (incorporating squares and cross-products of regressors); (3) Remediation: If heteroskedasticity is present (p < 0.05), researchers must apply: (a) Huber-White Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors (HC0, HC1, HC2, or HC3); (b) Cluster-Robust Standard Errors for grouped data; or (c) Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS / WLS) to restore estimation efficiency.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Diagnostic and remedial workflow: (1) Graphical inspection: Plotting OLS squared residuals hat{epsilon}_i^2 against fitted values hat{Y}_i or explanatory variables X_j; (2) Statistical testing: Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test (testing linear relationship between squared residuals and X) and White's General Test (incorporating squares and cross-products of regressors); (3) Remediation: If heteroskedasticity is present (p < 0.05), researchers must apply: (a) Huber-White Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors (HC0, HC1, HC2, or HC3); (b) Cluster-Robust Standard Errors for grouped data; or (c) Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS / WLS) to restore estimation efficiency.
terms.benchmarks: Standard selection rules: (1) Breusch-Pagan or White test p < 0.05 indicates statistically significant heteroskedasticity; (2) Standard error estimator selection: Long and Ervin (2000) establish that HC3 standard errors should be the default in small samples (N < 250) due to superior finite-sample coverage; HC1 or HC2 for moderate samples; (3) Clustered standard errors (vce(cluster)) when observations are nested within firms or geographic clusters.
terms.pitfalls: Critical econometrics traps: (1) Erroneously claiming heteroskedasticity biases coefficient estimates (it biases standard errors and test statistics, not beta estimates); (2) Relying on standard OLS standard errors after a significant Breusch-Pagan test, leading to rejection in top economics and finance journals; and (3) Using log transformations blindly without verifying whether conditional variance on the log scale satisfies homoskedasticity.
terms.apa_reference: White, H. (1980). A heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix estimator and a direct test for heteroskedasticity. Econometrica, 48(4), 817–838. https://doi.org/10.2307/1912934

terms.vietnamese: Tương quan dị đặc tính - dị phương pháp
vietnamese_variants: Tương quan khác trait khác method
terms.core_definition: Heterotrait-Heteromethod (HTHM) Correlation is a critical diagnostic cell in the Multitrait-Multimethod (MTMM) Matrix formulated by Donald T. Campbell and Donald W. Fiske (1959). It measures the empirical correlation between two conceptually distinct traits measured using two different measurement methods (e.g., Trait A measured via self-report survey correlated with Trait B measured via supervisor evaluation). In construct validation, HTHM correlations represent the purest empirical baseline of trait divergence because they share neither trait variance nor common method variance.
terms.seminal_citation: Campbell, D. T., & Fiske, D. W. (1959). Convergent and discriminant validation by the multitrait-multimethod matrix. Psychological Bulletin, 56(2), 81-105.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Heterotrait-heteromethod correlation according to Henseler et al. (2015); Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: In an MTMM matrix evaluating T traits across M methods: (1) The Monotrait-Monomethod (MTMM) diagonal represents reliability; (2) Monotrait-Heteromethod (MTHM) represents convergent validity; (3) Heterotrait-Monomethod (HTMM) represents distinct traits sharing common method bias; (4) Heterotrait-Heteromethod (HTHM) represents distinct traits measured by distinct methods. For discriminant validity to hold, the validity diagonal (MTHM) must be substantially higher than the corresponding HTHM values, and HTHM values should ideally approximate zero.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: In an MTMM matrix evaluating T traits across M methods: (1) The Monotrait-Monomethod (MTMM) diagonal represents reliability; (2) Monotrait-Heteromethod (MTHM) represents convergent validity; (3) Heterotrait-Monomethod (HTMM) represents distinct traits sharing common method bias; (4) Heterotrait-Heteromethod (HTHM) represents distinct traits measured by distinct methods. For discriminant validity to hold, the validity diagonal (MTHM) must be substantially higher than the corresponding HTHM values, and HTHM values should ideally approximate zero.
terms.benchmarks: Campbell-Fiske MTMM validation rules: (1) HTHM correlations must be the lowest values in the entire matrix; (2) Discriminant validity requirement: MTHM (convergent validity) > HTHM; (3) The pattern of trait interrelationships should be consistent across both HTHM and HTMM sub-matrices; (4) Absolute HTHM values typically fall below r < 0.30.
terms.pitfalls: Common psychometric errors: (1) Misinterpreting high HTHM correlations (r > 0.50), which indicates that the two supposedly distinct theoretical constructs severely lack discriminant validity; (2) Conflating HTHM with HTMM—high HTMM correlations often reflect common method variance rather than genuine conceptual overlap; and (3) Abandoning MTMM verification in favor of simple exploratory factor analysis.
terms.apa_reference: Campbell, D. T., & Fiske, D. W. (1959). Convergent and discriminant validation by the multitrait-multimethod matrix. Psychological Bulletin, 56(2), 81–105. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0046016

terms.vietnamese: Tỷ số Tương quan Dị đặc tính - Đơn đặc tính (Chuẩn mực HTMT)
vietnamese_variants: Tiêu chuẩn thẩm định độ giá trị phân biệt HTMT
domain_tags: Mô hình Phương trình Cấu trúc (PLS-SEM & CB-SEM)
terms.core_definition: Tiêu chuẩn thẩm định Độ giá trị Phân biệt (Discriminant Validity) mang tính đột phá trong SEM do Jörg Henseler, Christian Ringle và Marko Sarstedt (2015) đề xuất, và được Roemer, Schuberth & Henseler (2021) hoàn thiện. HTMT là tỷ số giữa giá trị trung bình tương quan giữa các chỉ báo của hai khái niệm khác nhau (Heterotrait) so với trung bình nhân của tương quan giữa các chỉ báo trong cùng một khái niệm (Monotrait). Phương pháp mô phỏng Monte Carlo chứng minh HTMT đạt độ nhạy trên 97% trong việc phát hiện vi phạm độ giá trị phân biệt, khắc phục hoàn toàn điểm yếu thiếu nhạy bén của tiêu chuẩn cổ điển Fornell-Larcker (1981).
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8; Roemer, E., Schuberth, F., & Henseler, J. (2021). HTMT2–an improved criterion for assessing discriminant validity in structural equation modeling. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 121(12), 2637–2650. https://doi.org/10.1108/IMDS-02-2021-0082
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1189; lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Heterotrait-monotrait ratio of correlations (HTMT) according to Henseler et al. (2015); Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.benchmarks: Ngưỡng đánh giá tuyệt đối: HTMT ≤ 0.85 đối với các khái niệm có tính độc lập cao về mặt lý thuyết; HTMT ≤ 0.90 là ngưỡng tối đa chấp nhận đối với các khái niệm có sự tương đồng hoặc có mối quan hệ cấu trúc gần gũi. Kiểm định thống kê suy luận (HTMT Inference): Khoảng tin cậy một phía 90% (hoặc hai phía 95%) qua kỹ thuật Bootstrap KHÔNG ĐƯỢC CHỨA giá trị 1.0 (HTMT confidence interval does not include 1).
terms.pitfalls: Chỉ dựa vào tiêu chuẩn Fornell-Larcker và Cross-loadings để khẳng định đạt độ giá trị phân biệt khi các hệ số tải ngoài (Loadings) biến thiên không đồng đều (từ 0.60 đến 0.80). Tiếp tục duy trì mô hình khi HTMT vượt quá 0.90 mà không tiến hành sáp nhập khái niệm hoặc loại bỏ các chỉ báo có tương quan chéo quá cao.
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135.

terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp nghiên cứu phỏng đoán khám phá (Moustakas)
vietnamese_variants: Nghiên cứu suy nghiệm cá nhân
Phương pháp phỏng đoán hiện tượng học
terms.core_definition: Heuristic Inquiry is a qualitative, phenomenological research methodology developed by humanistic psychologist Clark Moustakas (1990) designed to investigate the nature and meaning of profound human experiences through direct personal immersion, self-reflection, and subjective awareness. Derived from the Greek word heuriskein (to discover or find), heuristic inquiry places the researcher's own lived experience, internal tacit knowing, and personal transformation at the core of the investigation, synthesizing personal insights with the lived experiences of co-researchers (participants).
terms.seminal_citation: Moustakas, C. (1990). Heuristic research: Design, methodology, and applications. SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Heuristic Inquiry according to Moustakas (1990).
terms.operational_mechanism: Moustakas delineated six systematic, sequential phases of heuristic inquiry: (1) Initial Engagement: Discovering an intense personal question or passion; (2) Immersion: Total engagement with the phenomenon in all waking life, dreams, and interactions; (3) Incubation: Retreating from active focus to allow unconscious tacit processing and intuitive synthesis; (4) Illumination: A breakthrough of conscious awareness, revealing new metaphors and meaning qualities; (5) Explication: Comprehensive, detailed examination of newly revealed meanings; and (6) Creative Synthesis: Articulating the essence through a rich narrative, poem, artistic composition, or overarching conceptual model.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Moustakas delineated six systematic, sequential phases of heuristic inquiry: (1) Initial Engagement: Discovering an intense personal question or passion; (2) Immersion: Total engagement with the phenomenon in all waking life, dreams, and interactions; (3) Incubation: Retreating from active focus to allow unconscious tacit processing and intuitive synthesis; (4) Illumination: A breakthrough of conscious awareness, revealing new metaphors and meaning qualities; (5) Explication: Comprehensive, detailed examination of newly revealed meanings; and (6) Creative Synthesis: Articulating the essence through a rich narrative, poem, artistic composition, or overarching conceptual model.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological credibility indicators: (1) Deep personal reflexivity and transparent autobiographical grounding; (2) Rigorous verbatim depiction of co-researchers' experiences through individual portraits, exemplary portraits, and a composite portrait; (3) Internal validation: Verifying that creative synthesis resonates profoundly with co-researchers (member checking).
terms.pitfalls: Common research weaknesses: (1) Descending into self-indulgent, undisciplined autobiography without systematic connection to co-researchers' accounts; (2) Skipping the incubation and explication phases, producing shallow descriptive summaries; and (3) Inadequate ethical safeguards when exploring intensely traumatic or vulnerable personal experiences.
terms.apa_reference: Moustakas, C. (1990). Heuristic research: Design, methodology, and applications. SAGE Publications. https://doi.org/10.4135/9781412995641

terms.vietnamese: Chương trình nghiên cứu phỏng đoán và thiên lệch nhận thức
vietnamese_variants: Lý thuyết Phỏng đoán và Thiên lệch
terms.core_definition: Chương trình nghiên cứu Phỏng đoán và Thiên lệch (Heuristics and Biases Program - Tversky & Kahneman, 1974; Kahneman, Slovic, & Tversky, 1982) là cuộc cách mạng nhận thức học đoạt giải Nobel Kinh tế, bác bỏ hoàn toàn giả định về con người duy lý hoàn hảo (Homo Economicus) trong lý thuyết kinh tế học cổ điển. Chương trình chứng minh rằng trong điều kiện bất định và phức tạp, con người dựa vào một số lượng hữu hạn các lối tắt tư duy phỏng đoán (heuristics) trực quan đơn giản để ra quyết định; mặc dù rất tiết kiệm thời gian, các phỏng đoán này dẫn đến các sai lệch nhận thức có tính quy luật, dự đoán được và lặp đi lặp lại một cách có hệ thống.
terms.seminal_citation: Tversky & Kahneman (1974); Kahneman, Slovic, & Tversky (1982)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Heuristics and Biases Program (Tversky & Kahneman) according to Tversky & Kahneman (1974).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Ba phỏng đoán nền tảng: (A) Phỏng đoán tính đại diện (Representativeness: đánh giá xác suất dựa trên mức độ tương đồng khuôn mẫu, bỏ qua xác suất tiên nghiệm Base-rate neglect); (B) Phỏng đoán tính sẵn có (Availability: đánh giá tần suất dựa trên mức độ dễ dàng gợi nhớ trong ký ức); (C) Phỏng đoán neo và hiệu chỉnh (Anchoring and Adjustment: đánh giá bị kéo lệch về phía con số khởi tạo ban đầu). 2. Phát triển thành Lý thuyết Triển vọng (Prospect Theory, 1979) giải thích hiện tượng ác cảm mất mát (Loss aversion) và định giá xác suất phi tuyến.
terms.benchmarks: Là lý thuyết nền tảng chi phối toàn bộ ngành Kinh tế học Hành vi (Behavioral Economics), Tài chính Hành vi, Marketing và Thiết kế Chính sách Công (Nudge Theory của Thaler & Sunstein).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Nhầm lẫn rằng 'phỏng đoán' luôn luôn là sai lầm hoặc tiêu cực. Gerd Gigerenzer (1999 - Fast and Frugal Heuristics) nhấn mạnh rằng trong môi trường bất định thực tế, phỏng đoán trực giác thường mang lại các quyết định chính xác và hiệu quả hơn các thuật toán tối ưu hóa toán học phức tạp.
terms.apa_reference: Tversky, A., & Kahneman, D. (1974). Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases. Science, 185(4157), 1124–1131. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình cấu trúc tính cách HEXACO
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình nhân cách 6 yếu tố HEXACO
terms.core_definition: The HEXACO Model of Personality Structure, formulated by Kibeom Lee and Michael C. Ashton (2004), is a six-dimensional psychometric taxonomy of human personality derived from comprehensive cross-cultural lexical studies. While the classical Big Five / Five-Factor Model (FFM) posits five broad traits, HEXACO demonstrates that a six-factor structure emerges consistently across European and Asian languages. Its signature theoretical contribution is the explicit identification of Honesty-Humility (H) as a distinct fundamental trait alongside Emotionality (E), Extraversion (X), Agreeableness (A), Conscientiousness (C), and Openness to Experience (O).
terms.seminal_citation: Ashton, M. C., & Lee, K. (2007). Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure. Personality and Social Psychology Review, 11(2), 150-166.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of HEXACO Model of Personality Structure according to Ashton & Lee (2007).
terms.operational_mechanism: HEXACO is operationalized via the HEXACO-PI-R inventory (available in 200, 100, and 60-item versions), assessing 6 domains each comprising 4 facets: (1) Honesty-Humility (Sincerity, Fairness, Greed Avoidance, Modesty); (2) Emotionality (Fearfulness, Anxiety, Dependence, Sentimentality); (3) Extraversion (Social Self-Esteem, Social Boldness, Sociability, Liveliness); (4) Agreeableness (Forgivingness, Gentleness, Flexibility, Patience); (5) Conscientiousness (Organization, Diligence, Perfectionism, Prudence); and (6) Openness to Experience (Aesthetic Appreciation, Inquisitiveness, Creativity, Unconventionality). Plus an interstitial facet: Altruism.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: HEXACO is operationalized via the HEXACO-PI-R inventory (available in 200, 100, and 60-item versions), assessing 6 domains each comprising 4 facets: (1) Honesty-Humility (Sincerity, Fairness, Greed Avoidance, Modesty); (2) Emotionality (Fearfulness, Anxiety, Dependence, Sentimentality); (3) Extraversion (Social Self-Esteem, Social Boldness, Sociability, Liveliness); (4) Agreeableness (Forgivingness, Gentleness, Flexibility, Patience); (5) Conscientiousness (Organization, Diligence, Perfectionism, Prudence); and (6) Openness to Experience (Aesthetic Appreciation, Inquisitiveness, Creativity, Unconventionality). Plus an interstitial facet: Altruism.
terms.benchmarks: Psychometric standards: (1) Internal consistency: Alpha >= 0.78 for broad domains, alpha >= 0.70 for facet scales; (2) CFA factor structure: Replicated cross-cultural structural invariance; (3) Criterion validity: Honesty-Humility uniquely explains substantial incremental variance (Delta R^2 = 10% to 25%) in predicting Counterproductive Work Behaviors (CWB), workplace theft, corporate fraud, unethical pro-organizational behavior, and Dark Triad traits beyond the Big Five.
terms.pitfalls: Common research pitfalls: (1) Treating Honesty-Humility as identical to Big Five Agreeableness (in HEXACO, Agreeableness captures patience versus anger, while Honesty-Humility captures fairness versus greed); (2) Using short 24-item brief scales for high-stakes employee selection where facet-level fidelity is lost; and (3) Overlooking social desirability bias on self-reported Honesty-Humility items (warranting observer/peer-ratings).
terms.apa_reference: Ashton, M. C., & Lee, K. (2007). Empirical, theoretical, and practical advantages of the HEXACO model of personality structure. Personality and Social Psychology Review, 11(2), 150–166. https://doi.org/10.1177/1088868306294907

terms.vietnamese: Phân cụm thứ bậc kết tụ
vietnamese_variants: Phân cụm phân cấp từ dưới lên
terms.core_definition: Phân cụm thứ bậc kết tụ (Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering - HAC - Ward, 1963; Sneath & Sokal, 1973) là phương pháp phân cụm từ dưới lên (bottom-up). Thuật toán khởi đầu bằng việc coi mỗi quan sát là một cụm đơn lẻ riêng biệt, sau đó tuần tự hợp nhất các cặp cụm có khoảng cách khoảng cách gần nhau nhất ở mỗi bước lặp cho đến khi toàn bộ dữ liệu hợp nhất thành một cụm duy nhất, tạo ra một cấu trúc cây thứ bậc hoàn chỉnh (Dendrogram).
terms.seminal_citation: Ward (1963); Sneath & Sokal (1973)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering according to Ward (1963).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Khởi tạo ma trận khoảng cách khoảng cách N × N. 2. Các phương pháp liên kết cụm (Linkage criteria): (A) Single linkage (khoảng cách khoảng cách nhỏ nhất - nhạy cảm với hiệu ứng xích chaining); (B) Complete linkage (khoảng cách khoảng cách lớn nhất - tạo cụm hình cầu chặt chẽ); (C) Average linkage (UPGMA - trung bình mọi cặp); (D) Phương pháp Ward (Ward's minimum variance - tối thiểu hóa mức tăng tổng bình phương sai số trong cụm). 3. Trực quan hóa cấu trúc lồng nhau qua biểu đồ cây Dendrogram.
terms.benchmarks: Phương pháp Ward là phương pháp liên kết được ưa chuộng nhất trong kinh tế và xã hội học vì nó tạo ra các cụm có quy mô cân đối và cấu trúc nội tại đồng nhất cao. Hệ số đồng hình (Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient > 0.75) chứng minh biểu đồ Dendrogram phản ánh trung thực ma trận khoảng cách khoảng cách gốc.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Độ phức tạp tính toán O(N²) hoặc O(N³) về bộ nhớ và thời gian, khiến HAC không thể chạy được trực tiếp trên các tập dữ liệu lớn (N > 10.000-50.000 quan sát) trừ khi áp dụng kỹ thuật lấy mẫu hoặc chuyển sang các thuật toán tối ưu như BIRCH.
terms.apa_reference: Ward, J. H., Jr. (1963). Hierarchical grouping to optimize an objective function. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 58(301), 236–244. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1963.10500845

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình tuyến tính phân tầng
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình hiệu ứng hỗn hợp (Linear Mixed-Effects)
terms.core_definition: Mô hình tuyến tính phân tầng (HLM / Multilevel Modeling) là kỹ thuật hồi quy tham số dành cho dữ liệu có cấu trúc lồng ghép thứ bậc (nested / hierarchical data như học sinh trong lớp, nhân viên trong công ty, thời điểm trong cá nhân). HLM khắc phục triệt để vi phạm giả định độc lập của sai số (vi phạm OLS i.i.d) bằng cách phân tách phương sai thành phần giữa các cấp độ (cấp 1 - cá nhân, cấp 2 - nhóm), cho phép cả hệ số chặn (random intercept) và hệ số góc (random slope) biến thiên ngẫu nhiên giữa các nhóm.
terms.seminal_citation: Raudenbush & Bryk (2002); Snijders & Bosker (2012)
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1197
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM) according to Raudenbush & Bryk (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Phương trình cấp 1 (Level 1): Y_ij = β_0j + β_1j · X_ij + e_ij với e_ij ~ N(0, σ²). 2. Phương trình cấp 2 (Level 2): β_0j = γ_00 + γ_01 · W_j + u_0j; β_1j = γ_10 + γ_11 · W_j + u_1j với (u_0j, u_1j) tuân theo phân phối chuẩn đa biến. 3. Ước lượng mô hình hợp nhất (Full Model) bằng Hợp lý cực đại hạn chế (Restricted Maximum Likelihood - REML) để đảm bảo ước lượng không chệch cho các thành phần phương sai.
terms.benchmarks: Hệ số tương quan nội lớp (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient - ICC): ICC = τ_00 / (τ_00 + σ²). Nếu ICC > 0.05 (hoặc > 0.10), cấu trúc đa cấp có ý nghĩa và việc áp dụng HLM là bắt buộc thay vì OLS thông thường. Kiểm định độ phù hợp mô hình: So sánh mô hình lồng nhau bằng Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT / Deviance test).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: (1) Quy mô mẫu cấp 2 quá nhỏ: Nếu số lượng nhóm ở Level 2 ít hơn 30-50 nhóm, ước lượng phương sai cấp 2 sẽ bị chệch và sai số chuẩn của các hệ số cấp 2 bị đánh giá thấp; (2) Không chuẩn hóa định tâm biến (centering): Cần phân biệt rõ định tâm theo trung bình tổng thể (Grand-Mean Centering) và định tâm theo trung bình nhóm (Group-Mean Centering) để tránh diễn giải sai các tác động giữa nhóm và nội nhóm.
terms.apa_reference: Raudenbush, S. W., & Bryk, A. S. (2002). Hierarchical linear models: Applications and data analysis methods (2nd ed.). Sage Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình hồi quy phân tầng (Kiểm định phương sai gia tăng)
vietnamese_variants: Hồi quy từng bước theo khối
Hồi quy phân cấp biến kiểm soát
terms.core_definition: Hierarchical Regression Modeling (also known as Sequential Regression or Block-Wise Regression) is a deductive quantitative modeling approach in which sets of predictor variables are entered into the regression equation in pre-determined, sequential blocks based on explicit theoretical logic. Distinct from Multilevel/Hierarchical Linear Modeling (which handles nested data structures), hierarchical regression is designed to assess incremental variance explained (Delta R^2) and evaluate whether a focal predictor or interaction term adds statistically significant predictive power beyond established demographic controls and alternative explanations.
terms.seminal_citation: Cohen, J., Cohen, P., West, S. G., & Aiken, L. S. (2003). Applied multiple regression/correlation analysis for the behavioral sciences (3rd ed.). Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hierarchical Regression Modeling according to Cohen et al. (2003).
terms.operational_mechanism: Sequential block entry protocol: (1) Block 1 (Controls): Baseline demographic and contextual covariates (e.g., age, firm size, industry fixed effects); (2) Block 2 (Main Predictors): Theoretical independent variables; (3) Block 3 (Interactions / Mediators): Product terms testing moderation (e.g., X * W) or psychological mechanisms. At each step k, the F-change statistic tests the null hypothesis that the newly added predictors have zero regression coefficients: F_{change} = [ (R_k^2 - R_{k-1}^2) / q ] / [ (1 - R_k^2) / (N - p_k - 1) ], where q is the number of added predictors and p_k is total predictors.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Sequential block entry protocol: (1) Block 1 (Controls): Baseline demographic and contextual covariates (e.g., age, firm size, industry fixed effects); (2) Block 2 (Main Predictors): Theoretical independent variables; (3) Block 3 (Interactions / Mediators): Product terms testing moderation (e.g., X * W) or psychological mechanisms. At each step k, the F-change statistic tests the null hypothesis that the newly added predictors have zero regression coefficients: F_{change} = [ (R_k^2 - R_{k-1}^2) / q ] / [ (1 - R_k^2) / (N - p_k - 1) ], where q is the number of added predictors and p_k is total predictors.
terms.benchmarks: Evaluation benchmarks in top management and psychology journals: (1) Delta R^2 statistical significance: F_{change} must yield p < 0.05 (or p < 0.01) to substantiate claims of incremental validity; (2) Moderation benchmarking: In field surveys, interaction terms typically yield Delta R^2 between 0.01 and 0.03 (1% to 3% additional variance), which is statistically and practically meaningful; (3) Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) should remain < 5.0 (strictly < 3.3) after mean-centering continuous interaction components.
terms.pitfalls: Common methodological errors: (1) Confusing hierarchical regression with automated stepwise regression (stepwise regression is purely algorithm-driven and data-dredged, which is widely condemned in top journals); (2) Entering focal predictors before controls, which obscures whether the focal variable possesses true incremental validity; and (3) Failing to report the F-change statistic and corresponding degrees of freedom.
terms.apa_reference: Cohen, J., Cohen, P., West, S. G., & Aiken, L. S. (2003). Applied multiple regression/correlation analysis for the behavioral sciences (3rd ed.). Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.

terms.vietnamese: Tổ chức có độ tin cậy cao (Lý thuyết HRO)
vietnamese_variants: Tổ chức vận hành siêu tin cậy
Lý thuyết quản trị rủi ro HRO
terms.core_definition: High Reliability Organizations (HRO) is an organizational theory framework developed by Karl E. Weick, Kathleen M. Sutcliffe, and Todd LaPorte to analyze organizations that operate continuously under extreme complexity, peak hazard, and rapid volatility (such as nuclear power stations, naval aircraft carriers, air traffic control towers, and intensive care units) yet experience remarkably fewer catastrophic accidents than predicted. HROs achieve extraordinary safety and performance through organizational mindfulness—a collective cognitive capability to continuously detect, intercept, and contain early weak signals of operational failure before they escalate into full-scale disasters.
terms.seminal_citation: Weick, K. E., & Sutcliffe, K. M. (2001). Managing the unexpected: Assuring high performance in an age of complexity. Jossey-Bass.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of High Reliability Organizations (HRO) according to Weick & Sutcliffe (2007).
terms.operational_mechanism: HRO theory articulates five signature operational principles divided into anticipation and containment: (1) Anticipation principles: (a) Preoccupation with failure (treating minor anomalies and near-misses as symptoms of systemic fragility); (b) Reluctance to simplify interpretations (rejecting tidy narratives and acknowledging situational complexity); (c) Sensitivity to operations (maintaining real-time frontline operational awareness); (2) Containment principles: (d) Commitment to resilience (rapid problem containment and error bounce-back); and (e) Deference to expertise (migrating decision authority during emergencies to the individuals with the deepest domain knowledge regardless of hierarchical rank).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: HRO theory articulates five signature operational principles divided into anticipation and containment: (1) Anticipation principles: (a) Preoccupation with failure (treating minor anomalies and near-misses as symptoms of systemic fragility); (b) Reluctance to simplify interpretations (rejecting tidy narratives and acknowledging situational complexity); (c) Sensitivity to operations (maintaining real-time frontline operational awareness); (2) Containment principles: (d) Commitment to resilience (rapid problem containment and error bounce-back); and (e) Deference to expertise (migrating decision authority during emergencies to the individuals with the deepest domain knowledge regardless of hierarchical rank).
terms.benchmarks: Empirical assessment metrics: (1) Near-miss reporting frequency: HROs display high reporting volume of micro-incidents without punitive retaliation; (2) Latent error containment speed: Time elapsed from anomaly emergence to systemic mitigation; (3) Structural decentralization during operational crises: Verification that frontline operators have explicit authority to halt production or operations without prior managerial approval.
terms.pitfalls: Common research misapplications: (1) Conflating formal bureaucratic compliance checklists with true HRO mindfulness (blind adherence to checklists can induce cognitive complacency); (2) Applying HRO principles superficially to standard low-hazard corporate environments without understanding core tension between efficiency and safety margins; and (3) Ignoring organizational culture and leadership psychological safety.
terms.apa_reference: Weick, K. E., & Sutcliffe, K. M. (2001). Managing the unexpected: Assuring high performance in an age of complexity. Jossey-Bass.

terms.vietnamese: Bài báo khoa học được trích dẫn cao (Top 1% ESI)
vietnamese_variants: Bài báo trích dẫn đỉnh cao ESI
Công trình nghiên cứu top 1% trích dẫn
terms.core_definition: A Highly Cited Paper in Clarivate's Essential Science Indicators (ESI) is an elite bibliometric designation awarded to a journal article or review indexed in Web of Science that has received sufficient cumulative citations to rank in the top 1% globally compared to all papers published in the same academic field and during the exact same publication year. By normalizing citation thresholds across 22 broad scientific disciplines and controlling for publication age (citing window), ESI Highly Cited status serves as a standardized global benchmark of breakthrough scientific impact and academic prestige.
terms.seminal_citation: Clarivate. (2024). Essential Science Indicators: Highly cited papers methodology and threshold definitions. Clarivate Analytics.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Highly Cited Paper (ESI Top 1%) according to Clarivate (2020).
terms.operational_mechanism: ESI computes citation percentiles through a structured protocol updated bi-monthly: (1) Classification: Assigns each indexed paper to one of 22 ESI scientific fields based on the journal's classification; (2) Age stratification: Partitions papers by publication year within a rolling 10-year citation window; (3) Threshold determination: Generates a citation frequency distribution and calculates the 99th percentile cutoff; (4) Dynamic qualification: Papers whose total citations equal or exceed the specific field-year threshold are awarded the Highly Cited Paper badge.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: ESI computes citation percentiles through a structured protocol updated bi-monthly: (1) Classification: Assigns each indexed paper to one of 22 ESI scientific fields based on the journal's classification; (2) Age stratification: Partitions papers by publication year within a rolling 10-year citation window; (3) Threshold determination: Generates a citation frequency distribution and calculates the 99th percentile cutoff; (4) Dynamic qualification: Papers whose total citations equal or exceed the specific field-year threshold are awarded the Highly Cited Paper badge.
terms.benchmarks: Field and age threshold dynamics: (1) Percentile requirement: Top 1.0% strictly within disciplinary cohort; (2) Citation thresholds vary dramatically: A 5-year-old Clinical Medicine paper may require > 250 citations, whereas a Mathematics paper of the same age may require ~40 citations to achieve the top 1% threshold; (3) Academic recognition: Essential component in international university rankings (e.g., Shanghai ARWU, Times Higher Education).
terms.pitfalls: Critical scientometric pitfalls: (1) Disciplinary misclassification: Articles published in multidisciplinary journals (e.g., Nature, Science, PNAS) reclassified at the article level can experience threshold distortion; (2) Vulnerability to citation stacking and predatory citation clubs organized to push specific papers over the 1% boundary; and (3) Equating high citations with methodological veracity (erroneous papers receiving numerous refutation citations can achieve top 1% status).
terms.apa_reference: Clarivate. (2024). Essential Science Indicators: Highly cited papers methodology and threshold definitions. Clarivate Analytics. https://clarivate.com/products/scientific-and-academic-research/research-discovery-and-workflow-solutions/essential-science-indicators/

terms.vietnamese: Mối Nguy cơ Lịch sử Đe dọa Độ giá trị Nội tại (Nguy cơ Campbell)
domain_tags: Độ giá trị Nội tại (Internal Validity)
terms.core_definition: Một trong những mối đe dọa kinh điển nhất đối với độ giá trị nội tại trong nghiên cứu thực nghiệm và đánh giá chính sách, do Donald T. Campbell và Julian Stanley (1963) định danh. Nguy cơ lịch sử xảy ra khi có các sự kiện bên ngoài bất ngờ xuất hiện đồng thời trong khoảng thời gian giữa lần đo trước can thiệp (Pre-test) và lần đo sau can thiệp (Post-test), và chính sự kiện bên ngoài này (chứ không phải can thiệp thực nghiệm) đã tạo ra sự thay đổi ở biến kết cục (ví dụ: đang thử nghiệm một chiến dịch quảng cáo thì đối thủ cạnh tranh bị khủng hoảng truyền thông hoặc nền kinh tế rơi vào suy thoái).
terms.seminal_citation: Campbell, D. T., & Stanley, J. C. (1963). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for research. Rand McNally; Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of History Threat according to Campbell & Stanley (1963).
terms.benchmarks: Biện pháp kiểm soát chuẩn mực phương pháp luận: (1) Thiết lập Nhóm đối chứng ngẫu nhiên tương đương (Randomized Control Group): Cả hai nhóm đều cùng trải qua sự kiện lịch sử bên ngoài như nhau, nhờ đó tác động của sự kiện lịch sử bị triệt tiêu khi so sánh hiệu số giữa hai nhóm; (2) Thiết kế Chuỗi thời gian ngắt quãng (Interrupted Time Series Design) với nhiều mốc đo lường trước và sau can thiệp để bóc tách bước nhảy đột ngột của sự kiện lịch sử.
terms.pitfalls: Sử dụng thiết kế một nhóm trước - sau can thiệp (One-group pretest-posttest design) rồi quy chụp 100% sự thay đổi là do can thiệp của mình mà hoàn toàn lờ đi các biến cố kinh tế vĩ mô diễn ra trong cùng kỳ.
terms.apa_reference: Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.

terms.vietnamese: Phương sai đồng nhất (Homoskedasticity)
vietnamese_variants: Hiện tượng phương sai sai số không đổi
Giả định phương sai đồng nhất
terms.core_definition: Homoskedasticity (often spelled homoscedasticity) is a foundational assumption of classical linear regression modeling and the Gauss-Markov theorem. It stipulates that the conditional variance of the disturbance term epsilon_i is constant across all values of the explanatory variables X: Var(epsilon_i | X) = sigma^2 for all i = 1, ..., N. Under homoskedasticity and strict exogeneity, the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimator achieves the minimum variance among all linear unbiased estimators, establishing the BLUE (Best Linear Unbiased Estimator) property and rendering standard OLS covariance matrix formulas exact.
terms.seminal_citation: Breusch, T. S., & Pagan, A. R. (1979). A simple test for heteroscedasticity and random coefficient variation. Econometrica, 47(5), 1287-1294.
terms.expert_notes: Đã cập nhật định nghĩa chuyên sâu từ tài liệu kinh điển.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Homoskedasticity according to Wooldridge (2010).
terms.operational_mechanism: Homoskedasticity specifies that the error variance-covariance matrix is scalar: Var(epsilon | X) = sigma^2 * I_N. When this assumption is tested empirically: (1) Residual scatter plots: Residuals e_i are plotted against fitted values hat{Y}_i (a horizontal band of random dispersion confirms homoskedasticity; a fanning or funnel shape indicates violation); (2) Formal statistical hypothesis tests: Null hypothesis H_0: sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = ... = sigma_N^2 = sigma^2. The Breusch-Pagan test regresses squared residuals e_i^2 on regressors X, yielding a test statistic distributed as Chi^2(p) under H_0; (3) Koenker's studentized Breusch-Pagan test is preferred when errors deviate from normality.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Homoskedasticity specifies that the error variance-covariance matrix is scalar: Var(epsilon | X) = sigma^2 * I_N. When this assumption is tested empirically: (1) Residual scatter plots: Residuals e_i are plotted against fitted values hat{Y}_i (a horizontal band of random dispersion confirms homoskedasticity; a fanning or funnel shape indicates violation); (2) Formal statistical hypothesis tests: Null hypothesis H_0: sigma_1^2 = sigma_2^2 = ... = sigma_N^2 = sigma^2. The Breusch-Pagan test regresses squared residuals e_i^2 on regressors X, yielding a test statistic distributed as Chi^2(p) under H_0; (3) Koenker's studentized Breusch-Pagan test is preferred when errors deviate from normality.
terms.benchmarks: Diagnostic criteria: (1) Breusch-Pagan / Cook-Weisberg test: p > 0.05 indicates failure to reject homoskedasticity; (2) White's test: p > 0.05; (3) When homoskedasticity is confirmed, standard OLS standard errors s.e.(hat{beta}) = sqrt(s^2 * (X'X)^{-1}_{jj}) are statistically efficient and optimal.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Assuming homoskedasticity holds without diagnostic verification, particularly in cross-sectional survey or firm-level financial datasets where heteroskedasticity is ubiquitous; (2) Erroneously believing homoskedasticity is required for unbiasedness (violating it causes inefficiency and standard error distortion, not coefficient bias); and (3) Failing to report robust standard errors when Breusch-Pagan p < 0.05.
terms.apa_reference: Breusch, T. S., & Pagan, A. R. (1979). A simple test for heteroscedasticity and random coefficient variation. Econometrica, 47(5), 1287–1294. https://doi.org/10.2307/1911963

terms.term: Hong Kong Principles for Assessing Researchers
terms.vietnamese: Các nguyên tắc Hồng Kông về đánh giá nhà nghiên cứu
vietnamese_variants: Tiêu chuẩn đánh giá nhà khoa học Hong Kong
Hong Kong Principles for Research Assessment
terms.core_definition: The Hong Kong Principles for Assessing Researchers (HKP), formulated at the 6th World Conference on Research Integrity (Moher et al., 2020), is an international declaration establishing five foundational principles to reform academic career evaluation and incentive structures. Designed to combat perverse academic incentives (such as 'publish or perish', journal impact factor obsession, and citation hyper-inflation) that foster questionable research practices, the HKP mandate that researchers must be evaluated based on behaviors that strengthen research integrity, rigor, and societal benefit.
terms.seminal_citation: Moher, D., Bouter, L., Kleinert, S., Glasziou, P., Shamoo, A. E., Barbour, V., Coriat, A. M., Foeger, N., & Dirnagl, U. (2020). The Hong Kong Principles for assessing researchers: Fostering research integrity. PLOS Biology, 18(7), Article e3000737.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hong Kong Principles for Assessing Researchers according to Moher et al. (2020).
terms.operational_mechanism: The framework articulates five actionable assessment principles: (1) Principle 1: Assess responsible research practices (rigorous design, transparent methodology, ethics approvals); (2) Principle 2: Value complete and transparent reporting (publishing null/negative findings, pre-registration); (3) Principle 3: Reward the practice of open science (depositing open data, code, and preprints); (4) Principle 4: Acknowledge a broad range of research activities (peer review contributions, replication studies, data curation); and (5) Principle 5: Recognize a wider range of research impacts (societal, educational, and policy impacts beyond raw citation counts).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The framework articulates five actionable assessment principles: (1) Principle 1: Assess responsible research practices (rigorous design, transparent methodology, ethics approvals); (2) Principle 2: Value complete and transparent reporting (publishing null/negative findings, pre-registration); (3) Principle 3: Reward the practice of open science (depositing open data, code, and preprints); (4) Principle 4: Acknowledge a broad range of research activities (peer review contributions, replication studies, data curation); and (5) Principle 5: Recognize a wider range of research impacts (societal, educational, and policy impacts beyond raw citation counts).
terms.benchmarks: Institutional implementation benchmarks: (1) Adoption in tenure, promotion, and grant funding criteria by universities and national research councils (e.g., European Research Council, NIH); (2) Decoupling promotion from simplistic journal impact factors (aligning with DORA - San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment); (3) Inclusion of Open Science Badges and data-sharing statements in promotion dossiers.
terms.pitfalls: Common institutional barriers: (1) Symbolic adoption: Formally endorsing the principles while departmental hiring committees continue using raw journal impact factors as informal cutoffs; (2) Neglecting the evaluation of peer review and data-sharing labors; and (3) Inadequate institutional infrastructure to verify open science contributions.
terms.apa_reference: Moher, D., Bouter, L., Kleinert, S., Glasziou, P., Shamoo, A. E., Barbour, V., Coriat, A. M., Foeger, N., & Dirnagl, U. (2020). The Hong Kong Principles for assessing researchers: Fostering research integrity. PLOS Biology, 18(7), Article e3000737. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3000737

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật móc cài câu Hook-and-Eye (Tính liên kết văn phong học thuật)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật liên kết câu đoạn Becker
Kỹ thuật móc xích câu từ học thuật
terms.core_definition: The Hook-and-Eye Technique is an academic writing and rhetorical cohesion diagnostic popularized by sociologists Howard S. Becker (1986) and writing theorists (e.g., Williams & Bizup, 2017). Designed to eliminate disjointed prose, abrupt thematic leaps, and cognitive friction in scholarly manuscripts, the technique requires that each sentence must contain a conceptual 'hook' (a key term, pronoun, or semantic referent) that links directly into the 'eye' of the immediately preceding sentence, ensuring unbroken, linear syntactic flow across paragraphs.
terms.seminal_citation: Becker, H. S. (1986). Writing for social scientists: How to start and finish your thesis, book, or article. University of Chicago Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hook-and-eye exercise according to Creswell & Creswell (2023).
terms.operational_mechanism: Executing the diagnostic procedure: (1) Manuscript printout: Print a draft paragraph with double spacing; (2) Highlighting: Draw a physical or digital loop around the grammatical subject or topic concept of sentence N; (3) Tracing backwards: Draw a connecting line to the concept or phrase in sentence N-1 that introduces or anchors that topic; (4) Diagnostic inspection: If a sentence lacks a connecting hook to the preceding sentence, a structural gap exists; (5) Revision: Rewrite sentence openings to employ the 'known-to-new' information principle (start sentences with familiar/established concepts, ending with new or complex theoretical information).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Executing the diagnostic procedure: (1) Manuscript printout: Print a draft paragraph with double spacing; (2) Highlighting: Draw a physical or digital loop around the grammatical subject or topic concept of sentence N; (3) Tracing backwards: Draw a connecting line to the concept or phrase in sentence N-1 that introduces or anchors that topic; (4) Diagnostic inspection: If a sentence lacks a connecting hook to the preceding sentence, a structural gap exists; (5) Revision: Rewrite sentence openings to employ the 'known-to-new' information principle (start sentences with familiar/established concepts, ending with new or complex theoretical information).
terms.benchmarks: Textual cohesion indicators in peer-reviewed drafting: (1) Zero unlinked sentences within body paragraphs; (2) Topic sentence continuity: Each paragraph's opening topic sentence must link directly to the overarching argument of the section; (3) Elimination of vague referents ('This proves that...' revised to 'This empirical divergence proves that...').
terms.pitfalls: Common academic writing flaws: (1) Over-relying on mechanical transitional adverbs ('Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'In addition') as artificial band-aids to mask deep structural gaps in argumentation; (2) Subject-verb separation: Inserting long qualifying clauses between the hook and the main verb; and (3) Introducing completely novel conceptual constructs in the final sentence of an empirical discussion without prior contextual grounding.
terms.apa_reference: Becker, H. S. (1986). Writing for social scientists: How to start and finish your thesis, book, or article. University of Chicago Press.

terms.vietnamese: Quy trình chân trời hóa dữ liệu hiện tượng học
vietnamese_variants: San phẳng chân trời dữ liệu
terms.core_definition: Horizonalization (Chân trời hóa) là bước nền tảng đầu tiên trong quy trình phân tích dữ liệu hiện tượng học siêu nghiệm (Transcendental Phenomenology) do Clark Moustakas (1994) chuẩn hóa. Trong bước này, nhà nghiên cứu rà soát toàn bộ các bản gỡ băng phỏng vấn (transcripts) và coi mỗi câu phát ngôn hoặc nhận định của đối tượng nghiên cứu đều có giá trị, trọng số và vị thế bình đẳng như nhau (equal weight/value) trong việc soi sáng hiện tượng. Khái niệm này ví dữ liệu như một đường chân trời trải rộng vô tận, nơi không có yếu tố nào ban đầu bị coi là thứ yếu hay nổi trội hơn yếu tố khác.
terms.seminal_citation: Moustakas, C. (1994). Phenomenological Research Methods. SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Horizonalization in Phenomenology according to Moustakas (1994).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quy trình thực hiện Horizonalization gồm 4 bước kỹ thuật: (1) Rà soát toàn bộ văn bản và trích xuất mọi phát ngôn liên quan đến trải nghiệm về hiện tượng; (2) Đặt tất cả các phát ngôn lên một mặt phẳng phân tích với trọng số ngang nhau (treat every statement as having equal value); (3) Áp dụng 2 tiêu chí kiểm định để chọn lọc 'yếu tố bất biến' (invariant constituents): (a) Phát ngôn có chứa đựng một khoảnh khắc ý nghĩa cốt lõi của trải nghiệm không? (b) Phát ngôn có thể được trừu tượng hóa và gán nhãn mà không làm mất đi nghĩa gốc không?; (4) Loại bỏ các phát ngôn trùng lặp, mơ hồ hoặc nằm ngoài phạm vi hiện tượng, giữ lại danh sách chân trời ý nghĩa chuẩn xác.
benchmarks: Tính bao quát tuyệt đối: Không được lược bỏ bất kỳ câu trần thuật nào trong giai đoạn sơ cấp trước khi thực hiện quy trình kiểm tra 2 tiêu chuẩn của Moustakas.
Tài liệu minh chứng kiểm toán: Phải lưu trữ bảng Horizonalization Matrix thể hiện trọn vẹn phát ngôn nguyên gốc, tiêu chí đánh giá giữ lại/loại bỏ, và đơn vị ý nghĩa tương ứng.
Nguyên tắc không thứ bậc ban đầu: Tuyệt đối không phân loại 'ý chính' hay 'ý phụ' dựa trên tần suất lặp lại ở bước này.
pitfalls: Chọn lọc thiên vị từ trước (cherry-picking): Nhà nghiên cứu chỉ nhặt ra những câu nói phù hợp với kỳ vọng hoặc giả thuyết cá nhân và bỏ qua các phát ngôn khác.
Loại bỏ dữ liệu quá sớm: Vội vàng gộp hoặc cắt tỉa dữ liệu ngay từ lần đọc đầu tiên khi chưa hiểu trọn vẹn ngữ cảnh của người tham gia.
Nhầm lẫn giữa Horizonalization và mã hóa định lượng: Đếm tần suất xuất hiện của từ ngữ thay vì đánh giá giá trị ý nghĩa hiện tượng học của phát ngôn.
terms.apa_reference: Moustakas, C. (1994). Phenomenological research methods. SAGE Publications, Inc. https://doi.org/10.4135/9781412995658

terms.vietnamese: Bài báo khoa học điểm nóng (Top 0.1% ESI)
vietnamese_variants: Công trình nghiên cứu đột phá ESI 0.1%
Bài báo trích dẫn cấp tốc ESI
terms.core_definition: An ESI Hot Paper is an elite, highly time-sensitive scientometric indicator generated by Clarivate Analytics' Essential Science Indicators (ESI). It recognizes a recent academic paper that has achieved an exceptional surge of international citations immediately following publication, ranking within the top 0.1% (top 1 in 1,000) of papers in the same scientific field. Unlike ESI Highly Cited Papers (which evaluate cumulative citations over a 10-year window), Hot Papers capture immediate, fast-breaking scientific breakthroughs published within the past two years and cited during the most recent two-month reporting bimonth.
terms.seminal_citation: Clarivate. (2024). Essential Science Indicators: Hot papers methodology and bimonthly threshold calculation. Clarivate Analytics.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hot Paper (ESI Top 0.1%) according to Clarivate (2020).
terms.operational_mechanism: Hot Paper determination follows a precise bi-monthly algorithmic protocol: (1) Time filter: Evaluates only articles published within the last two full calendar years; (2) Citing window: Examines citations accrued exclusively during the most recent two-month tracking bimonth (e.g., January-February); (3) Field benchmarking: Partitions papers across the 22 ESI scientific categories; (4) Percentile calculation: Determines the 99.9th percentile citation cutoff for each field-period cohort; (5) Designation: Papers meeting or exceeding this cutoff are designated as Hot Papers in Web of Science.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Hot Paper determination follows a precise bi-monthly algorithmic protocol: (1) Time filter: Evaluates only articles published within the last two full calendar years; (2) Citing window: Examines citations accrued exclusively during the most recent two-month tracking bimonth (e.g., January-February); (3) Field benchmarking: Partitions papers across the 22 ESI scientific categories; (4) Percentile calculation: Determines the 99.9th percentile citation cutoff for each field-period cohort; (5) Designation: Papers meeting or exceeding this cutoff are designated as Hot Papers in Web of Science.
terms.benchmarks: Scientometric parameters: (1) Percentile threshold: Top 0.1% globally; (2) Time-sensitivity: Hot status fluctuates dynamically every two months—a paper may be 'Hot' for one bimonthly cycle and lose that status in the next as citing velocity normalizes; (3) Indicates frontier research shifts, rapid paradigm adoptions, pandemic responses, or breakthrough methodological software releases.
terms.pitfalls: Common misinterpretations: (1) Confusing Hot Papers with Highly Cited Papers (Hot Papers reflect short-term citation velocity; Highly Cited reflects 10-year cumulative influence); (2) Vulnerability to short-term controversy—a flawed or retracted paper receiving a flood of critical refutation citations can temporarily achieve Hot Paper status; and (3) Citation gaming via organized self-citation spikes immediately upon online publication.
terms.apa_reference: Clarivate. (2024). Essential Science Indicators: Hot papers methodology and bimonthly threshold calculation. Clarivate Analytics. https://clarivate.com/products/scientific-and-academic-research/research-discovery-and-workflow-solutions/essential-science-indicators/

terms.vietnamese: Nội suy bốc thăm Hot-Deck
vietnamese_variants: Nội suy từ hồ sơ tương đồng
terms.core_definition: Nội suy bốc thăm Hot-Deck (Ford, 1983; Andridge & Little, 2010) là kỹ thuật điền thế dữ liệu khuyết thiếu phi tham số lịch sử trong các cuộc điều tra xã hội học và điều tra dân số lớn (như US Census). Phương pháp này thay thế giá trị bị khuyết của một quan sát (recipient) bằng giá trị thực tế quan sát được từ một cá thể khác trong cùng tập dữ liệu hiện tại (donor) có các đặc trưng nhân khẩu học/hành vi tương đồng nhất.
terms.seminal_citation: Ford (1983); Andridge & Little (2010)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hot-Deck Imputation according to Ford (1983).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Định nghĩa các ô điều chỉnh (Imputation classes / Adjustment cells) dựa trên các biến phân loại quan sát đầy đủ (ví dụ: cùng nhóm tuổi, cùng giới tính, cùng vùng địa lý). 2. Với mỗi quan sát bị khuyết trong một ô, chọn ngẫu nhiên một quan sát đầy đủ (donor) trong chính ô đó để sao chép giá trị sang ô bị khuyết. 3. Biến thể hiện đại: Hot-deck dựa trên Khoảng cách khoảng cách (Distance metric / Nearest-neighbor hot-deck).
terms.benchmarks: Ưu điểm lớn nhất là bảo toàn hoàn toàn miền giá trị thực tế (không tạo ra các giá trị lẻ phi lý như 2.4 con đối với biến đếm). Tuy nhiên, phương pháp làm đánh giá thấp sai số chuẩn nếu chỉ nội suy một lần duy nhất (Single imputation).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Sử dụng Hot-deck đơn lẻ mà không tính đến độ bất định của giá trị nội suy khi tính toán sai số chuẩn; bắt buộc phải kết hợp Hot-deck trong quy trình Multiple Imputation hoặc áp dụng kỹ thuật Bootstrap để hiệu chỉnh khoảng tin cậy.
terms.apa_reference: Andridge, R. R., & Little, R. J. (2010). A review of hot deck imputation for survey non-response. International Statistical Review, 78(1), 40–64. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1751-5823.2010.00103.x

terms.vietnamese: Phân phối T-bình phương Hotelling
terms.core_definition: Hotelling's T-squared (T^2) distribution, formulated by Harold Hotelling (1931), is the multivariate generalization of Student's t-distribution. It provides the exact sampling distribution for testing hypotheses regarding multivariate mean vectors of p continuous dependent variables across one or two independent samples when the population covariance matrix Sigma is unknown and estimated by sample covariance matrix S. Hotelling's T^2 controls the experimentwise Type I error rate across multiple correlated outcomes simultaneously, preventing the alpha inflation inherent in running multiple independent univariate t-tests.
terms.seminal_citation: Hotelling, H. (1931). The generalization of Student's ratio. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 2(3), 360-378.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hotelling's T-squared according to Hair et al. (2018).
terms.operational_mechanism: For a single sample of size N with sample mean vector bar{X} and sample covariance matrix S testing H_0: mu = mu_0: (1) T^2 statistic: T^2 = N * (bar{X} - mu_0)' S^{-1} (bar{X} - mu_0); (2) For two independent samples of sizes n_1, n_2 with pooled covariance S_p: T^2 = [ (n_1 * n_2) / (n_1 + n_2) ] * (bar{X}_1 - bar{X}_2)' S_p^{-1} (bar{X}_1 - bar{X}_2); (3) Exact F-transformation: Under multivariate normality, T^2 transforms directly to an exact F-statistic: F = [ (N - p) / (p * (N - 1)) ] * T^2 ~ F(p, N - p) for one-sample, or F = [ (n_1 + n_2 - p - 1) / (p * (n_1 + n_2 - 2)) ] * T^2 ~ F(p, n_1 + n_2 - p - 1) for two samples.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: For a single sample of size N with sample mean vector bar{X} and sample covariance matrix S testing H_0: mu = mu_0: (1) T^2 statistic: T^2 = N * (bar{X} - mu_0)' S^{-1} (bar{X} - mu_0); (2) For two independent samples of sizes n_1, n_2 with pooled covariance S_p: T^2 = [ (n_1 * n_2) / (n_1 + n_2) ] * (bar{X}_1 - bar{X}_2)' S_p^{-1} (bar{X}_1 - bar{X}_2); (3) Exact F-transformation: Under multivariate normality, T^2 transforms directly to an exact F-statistic: F = [ (N - p) / (p * (N - 1)) ] * T^2 ~ F(p, N - p) for one-sample, or F = [ (n_1 + n_2 - p - 1) / (p * (n_1 + n_2 - 2)) ] * T^2 ~ F(p, n_1 + n_2 - p - 1) for two samples.
terms.benchmarks: Assumptions and application criteria: (1) Multivariate normality of error vectors; (2) Homogeneity of covariance matrices (tested via Box's M test, p > 0.001); (3) Minimum sample size requirement: The total sample size minus the number of groups must exceed the number of dependent variables (N - k > p), otherwise the sample covariance matrix S is singular and cannot be inverted.
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors: (1) Running multiple univariate t-tests instead of Hotelling's T^2, causing severe Type I error inflation (familywise alpha = 1 - (1 - 0.05)^p); (2) Applying Hotelling's T^2 when multicollinearity among dependent variables is extreme (determinant |S| approx 0), which causes matrix inversion instability; and (3) Ignoring severe violations of multivariate normality in small samples, where non-parametric permutation tests should be substituted.
terms.apa_reference: Hotelling, H. (1931). The generalization of Student's ratio. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 2(3), 360–378. https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177732979

terms.vietnamese: Vết Hotelling (Vết Hotelling-Lawley trong MANOVA)
terms.core_definition: Hotelling's Trace (commonly termed the Hotelling-Lawley Trace, denoted T or V), developed by Harold Hotelling (1951) and Derek Lawley (1938), is one of the four classical omnibus test statistics used in Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) and Canonical Correlation Analysis (alongside Wilks' Lambda, Pillai's Trace, and Roy's Largest Root). It represents the sum of the eigenvalues of the matrix product H * E^{-1} (where H is the hypothesis / between-group sum of squares and cross-products matrix, and E is the error / within-group SSP matrix), measuring the total multivariate variance attributable to experimental group differences relative to error variance.
terms.seminal_citation: Hotelling, H. (1951). A generalized T test and measure of multivariate dispersion. Proceedings of the Second Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability, 23-41.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hotelling's Trace (Hotelling-Lawley Trace) according to Hotelling (1951).
terms.operational_mechanism: Computation proceeds through spectral decomposition: (1) Construct the between-group matrix H and within-group matrix E; (2) Solve the characteristic equation |H - lambda * E| = 0 to obtain the eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_s, where s = min(p, df_h); (3) Compute the Hotelling-Lawley Trace: T = sum_{i=1}^s lambda_i = tr(H * E^{-1}); (4) Approximate F-distribution: Hotelling's Trace is converted into an approximate F-statistic using the Rao or Pillai transformation to evaluate null hypothesis H_0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_k.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Computation proceeds through spectral decomposition: (1) Construct the between-group matrix H and within-group matrix E; (2) Solve the characteristic equation |H - lambda * E| = 0 to obtain the eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_s, where s = min(p, df_h); (3) Compute the Hotelling-Lawley Trace: T = sum_{i=1}^s lambda_i = tr(H * E^{-1}); (4) Approximate F-distribution: Hotelling's Trace is converted into an approximate F-statistic using the Rao or Pillai transformation to evaluate null hypothesis H_0: mu_1 = mu_2 = ... = mu_k.
terms.benchmarks: Comparative statistical behavior: (1) When group differences are concentrated along a single linear discriminant dimension (lambda_1 >> lambda_2), Hotelling's Trace and Roy's Largest Root exhibit the highest statistical power; (2) When group differences are dispersed across multiple dimensions, Pillai's Trace is more robust; (3) When sample sizes are large and multivariate assumptions are strictly met, all four MANOVA statistics yield nearly identical p-values.
terms.pitfalls: Critical review pitfalls: (1) Using Hotelling's Trace when Box's M test indicates severe violation of covariance homogeneity (in heteroskedastic MANOVA, Pillai's Trace is substantially more robust against Type I error inflation than Hotelling's Trace); (2) Misinterpreting the trace statistic directly without reporting the transformed F-statistic and degrees of freedom; and (3) Applying MANOVA when dependent variables are completely uncorrelated (where univariate ANOVAs with Bonferroni correction are more appropriate).
terms.apa_reference: Hotelling, H. (1951). A generalized T test and measure of multivariate dispersion. Proceedings of the Second Berkeley Symposium on Mathematical Statistics and Probability, 23–41.

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn HTMT.85 (Giá trị phân biệt trong PLS-SEM)
terms.core_definition: The HTMT.85 Criterion is a conservative methodological threshold for assessing discriminant validity in Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Covariance-Based SEM (CB-SEM), formulated by Jörg Henseler, Christian M. Ringle, and Marko Sarstedt (2015). Derived from the Heterotrait-Monotrait Ratio of Correlations (HTMT)—which estimates the true correlation between two latent constructs if they were measured with perfect, error-free reliability—the HTMT.85 criterion establishes that two conceptually distinct constructs must have an HTMT value strictly below 0.85. Values exceeding 0.85 indicate an unacceptable lack of discriminant validity.
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of HTMT_ 85 criterion according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: The HTMT ratio compares the average correlation between indicators measuring different constructs (heterotrait-heteromethod) to the geometric mean of the average correlations among indicators measuring the same construct (monotrait-heteromethod): HTMT_{ij} = [ (1 / (K_i * K_j)) * sum_{g=1}^{K_i} sum_{h=1}^{K_j} |r_{ig, jh}| ] / sqrt( [ (2 / (K_i(K_i - 1))) * sum_{g=1}^{K_i-1} sum_{h=g+1}^{K_i} r_{ig, ih} ] * [ (2 / (K_j(K_j - 1))) * sum_{g=1}^{K_j-1} sum_{h=g+1}^{K_j} r_{jg, jh} ] ). If HTMT_{ij} < 0.85, discriminant validity between construct i and construct j is established.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The HTMT ratio compares the average correlation between indicators measuring different constructs (heterotrait-heteromethod) to the geometric mean of the average correlations among indicators measuring the same construct (monotrait-heteromethod): HTMT_{ij} = [ (1 / (K_i * K_j)) * sum_{g=1}^{K_i} sum_{h=1}^{K_j} |r_{ig, jh}| ] / sqrt( [ (2 / (K_i(K_i - 1))) * sum_{g=1}^{K_i-1} sum_{h=g+1}^{K_i} r_{ig, ih} ] * [ (2 / (K_j(K_j - 1))) * sum_{g=1}^{K_j-1} sum_{h=g+1}^{K_j} r_{jg, jh} ] ). If HTMT_{ij} < 0.85, discriminant validity between construct i and construct j is established.
terms.benchmarks: Threshold rules (Henseler et al., 2015; Hair et al., 2022): (1) HTMT < 0.85: Strict, conservative cutoff recommended when constructs are conceptually distinct (e.g., Brand Loyalty vs. Perceived Price Fairness); (2) In Monte Carlo simulations, the HTMT.85 criterion achieves sensitivity rates of 97% to 99% in detecting discriminant validity violations, whereas the legacy Fornell-Larcker criterion fails to detect violations up to 50% of the time.
terms.pitfalls: Common research pitfalls: (1) Relying solely on the outdated Fornell-Larcker criterion (comparing square root of AVE to construct correlations) when modern Q1 journals explicitly require HTMT reporting; (2) Treating HTMT >= 0.85 as acceptable without examining item cross-loadings or merging redundant constructs; and (3) Using HTMT for formative measurement models (HTMT is mathematically valid only for reflective constructs).
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn HTMT.90 (Giá trị phân biệt trong PLS-SEM)
vietnamese_variants: Tiêu chuẩn HTMT.90 cho khái niệm tương đồng
terms.core_definition: The HTMT.90 Criterion is a liberal methodological cutoff proposed by Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2015) for evaluating discriminant validity in structural equation modeling when the latent constructs under investigation are conceptually very similar, overlapping, or represent sub-dimensions of a broader psychological construct (e.g., Affective Commitment vs. Continuance Commitment, or Customer Satisfaction vs. Perceived Value). Under this criterion, discriminant validity is substantiated if the HTMT ratio is strictly below 0.90, confirming that the two constructs share less than 81% of their true latent variance.
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #2
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of HTMT_ 90 criterion according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Operational application: (1) Compute the full HTMT correlation matrix across all reflective latent constructs in the measurement model; (2) Classify construct pairs: Determine whether pairs represent conceptually distinct domains (mandating HTMT < 0.85) or conceptually adjacent/sub-dimensional domains (permitting HTMT < 0.90); (3) Compare empirical HTMT estimates against 0.90; (4) If HTMT >= 0.90, the constructs fail discriminant validity, requiring the researcher to either eliminate cross-loading indicators or merge the two constructs into a single higher-order construct.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Operational application: (1) Compute the full HTMT correlation matrix across all reflective latent constructs in the measurement model; (2) Classify construct pairs: Determine whether pairs represent conceptually distinct domains (mandating HTMT < 0.85) or conceptually adjacent/sub-dimensional domains (permitting HTMT < 0.90); (3) Compare empirical HTMT estimates against 0.90; (4) If HTMT >= 0.90, the constructs fail discriminant validity, requiring the researcher to either eliminate cross-loading indicators or merge the two constructs into a single higher-order construct.
terms.benchmarks: Empirical cutoffs: (1) HTMT < 0.90: Permissible upper ceiling for closely related constructs; (2) HTMT >= 0.90: Clear indication of construct redundancy and multicollinearity; (3) Gold standard: Combining the HTMT.90 point estimate cutoff with bootstrapped confidence intervals (HTMT_inference).
terms.pitfalls: Critical reviewer pitfalls: (1) Applying the liberal 0.90 threshold universally to all constructs without theoretical justification for why the constructs should be treated as conceptually adjacent; (2) Reporting HTMT values between 0.86 and 0.89 without explicitly referencing Henseler et al. (2015) guidelines for conceptually related constructs; and (3) Ignoring severe multicollinearity in the structural model when two predictors exhibit HTMT > 0.88.
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8

terms.vietnamese: Suy diễn thống kê HTMT (Khoảng tin cậy Bootstrap)
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định suy diễn HTMT inference
Khoảng tin cậy HTMT qua bootstrap
terms.core_definition: HTMT Statistical Inference (HTMT_inference) is the inferential testing procedure introduced by Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2015) to evaluate discriminant validity in PLS-SEM and CB-SEM using non-parametric bootstrapping. Rather than relying exclusively on sample-specific point estimates (such as HTMT < 0.85 or < 0.90), HTMT_inference constructs a bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) or percentile bootstrap confidence interval for each pairwise HTMT value. Discriminant validity is formally established if the upper bound of the 90% or 95% one-sided (or 90% two-sided) confidence interval is strictly below the chosen threshold (0.85, 0.90, or the absolute conceptual ceiling of 1.0).
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135.
terms.expert_notes: khuyến nghị hiện nay: cận trên CI một phía < 0.85/0.90 (Franke & Sarstedt 2019), không chỉ "không chứa 1" | Trùng #3
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of HTMT_ text inference according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: The inferential protocol follows four steps: (1) Resampling: Generate B = 5,000 (or 10,000) bootstrap samples from original empirical data with replacement; (2) Estimation: Calculate the HTMT ratio for every construct pair across each bootstrap iteration; (3) Construct Confidence Intervals: Derive the 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI_{lower}, CI_{upper}] using percentile or BCa methods; (4) Hypothesis Testing: Evaluate the null hypothesis H_0: HTMT >= 1.0 against H_1: HTMT < 1.0 (or test against H_0: HTMT >= 0.85). If the upper limit of the confidence interval is strictly less than 1.0 (or 0.85/0.90), H_0 is rejected and discriminant validity is statistically established.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The inferential protocol follows four steps: (1) Resampling: Generate B = 5,000 (or 10,000) bootstrap samples from original empirical data with replacement; (2) Estimation: Calculate the HTMT ratio for every construct pair across each bootstrap iteration; (3) Construct Confidence Intervals: Derive the 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI_{lower}, CI_{upper}] using percentile or BCa methods; (4) Hypothesis Testing: Evaluate the null hypothesis H_0: HTMT >= 1.0 against H_1: HTMT < 1.0 (or test against H_0: HTMT >= 0.85). If the upper limit of the confidence interval is strictly less than 1.0 (or 0.85/0.90), H_0 is rejected and discriminant validity is statistically established.
terms.benchmarks: Inferential thresholds (Hair et al., 2022; Henseler et al., 2015): (1) HTMT_inference < 1.0: The 95% bootstrap confidence interval of HTMT must not include the value 1.0 (mandatory baseline); (2) HTMT_inference < 0.85: The upper confidence bound does not include 0.85 (conservative standard for distinct constructs); (3) Bootstrap settings: Minimum 5,000 resamples, no sign change, bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) confidence intervals.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Running bootstrap inference with too few resamples (e.g., B = 500), which produces unstable confidence interval bounds; (2) Failing to report the actual confidence interval bounds in manuscript discriminant validity tables; and (3) Concluding discriminant validity exists when the point estimate is 0.83 but the upper 95% CI bound reaches 0.91, overlapping the violation zone.
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8

terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số phát triển con người (HDI)
vietnamese_variants: Hệ số phát triển con người HDI
Thước đo phát triển toàn diện HDI
terms.core_definition: The Human Development Index (HDI) is a composite statistical index created by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq and Indian Nobel laureate Amartya Sen (1990) for the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). Formulated to challenge the hegemony of Gross National Product (GNP/GDP) as the sole metric of national development, the HDI operationalizes Sen's Capabilities Approach. It evaluates human development as the expansion of human freedoms and capabilities across three essential dimensions: a long and healthy life, access to knowledge, and a decent standard of living.
terms.seminal_citation: United Nations Development Programme. (1990). Human development report 1990: Concept and measurement of human development. Oxford University Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Human Development Index (HDI) according to Anand & Sen (1994), UNDP (1990).
terms.operational_mechanism: Since 2010, the UNDP computes HDI as the geometric mean of three normalized dimensional indices: HDI = (I_{Health} * I_{Education} * I_{Income})^{1/3}. (1) Health Dimension: Measured by life expectancy at birth, normalized as I_{Health} = (LE - 20) / (85 - 20); (2) Education Dimension: Arithmetic mean of Mean Years of Schooling (MYS) for adults >= 25 and Expected Years of Schooling (EYS) for school-age children: I_{Education} = (I_{MYS} + I_{EYS}) / 2; (3) Income Dimension: Measured by GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity (PPP $), log-transformed to reflect diminishing marginal utility of income: I_{Income} = (ln(GNIpc) - ln(100)) / (ln(75,000) - ln(100)).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Since 2010, the UNDP computes HDI as the geometric mean of three normalized dimensional indices: HDI = (I_{Health} * I_{Education} * I_{Income})^{1/3}. (1) Health Dimension: Measured by life expectancy at birth, normalized as I_{Health} = (LE - 20) / (85 - 20); (2) Education Dimension: Arithmetic mean of Mean Years of Schooling (MYS) for adults >= 25 and Expected Years of Schooling (EYS) for school-age children: I_{Education} = (I_{MYS} + I_{EYS}) / 2; (3) Income Dimension: Measured by GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity (PPP $), log-transformed to reflect diminishing marginal utility of income: I_{Income} = (ln(GNIpc) - ln(100)) / (ln(75,000) - ln(100)).
terms.benchmarks: UNDP Development Tiers: (1) Very High Human Development: HDI >= 0.800; (2) High Human Development: 0.700 <= HDI <= 0.799; (3) Medium Human Development: 0.550 <= HDI <= 0.699; (4) Low Human Development: HDI < 0.550; (5) Complementary indices: Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI), Gender Development Index (GDI), and Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI (PHDI).
terms.pitfalls: Methodological limitations: (1) Geometric aggregation assumes partial substitutability between health, education, and income, but cannot fully capture extreme deprivation; (2) Data quality discrepancies in national statistics and informal economic transactions; and (3) Ignoring intra-national economic inequality (resolved by adopting IHDI).
terms.apa_reference: United Nations Development Programme. (1990). Human development report 1990: Concept and measurement of human development. Oxford University Press.

terms.vietnamese: Dân tộc học không gian mạng nhân văn (Humanist Netnography)
vietnamese_variants: Dân tộc học kỹ thuật số nhân văn
terms.core_definition: Humanist Netnography is an interpretive, culturally attuned digital research methodology originated and evolved by Robert V. Kozinets (2015, 2020). Expanding beyond early utilitarian conceptions of netnography as mere online text-scraping or digital conversation monitoring, Humanist Netnography reclaims the anthropological soul of ethnography in technoculture. It investigates how human identity, emotions, interpersonal connections, rituals, and existential struggles are mediated, transformed, and experienced within immersive digital networks, social media platforms, virtual reality, and artificial intelligence environments.
terms.seminal_citation: Kozinets, R. V. (2020). Netnography: The essential guide to qualitative social media research (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Humanist Netnography according to Kozinets (2015), Bansal et al. (2024).
terms.operational_mechanism: Humanist Netnography combines four distinct digital data collection streams: (1) Archival Data: Naturally occurring online communications, videos, posts, and memes created without researcher intervention; (2) Elicited Data: Co-created digital narratives generated through online interviews, asynchronous video prompts, and digital focus groups; (3) Fieldnotes (Reflective Data): Detailed ethnographic notes recording the researcher's personal immersion and emotional sensations; (4) Immersive Data: Experiential engagement with algorithms, VR spaces, and algorithmic curation. Analysis employs 'hermeneutic recontextualization' and multimodal semiotic analysis.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Humanist Netnography combines four distinct digital data collection streams: (1) Archival Data: Naturally occurring online communications, videos, posts, and memes created without researcher intervention; (2) Elicited Data: Co-created digital narratives generated through online interviews, asynchronous video prompts, and digital focus groups; (3) Fieldnotes (Reflective Data): Detailed ethnographic notes recording the researcher's personal immersion and emotional sensations; (4) Immersive Data: Experiential engagement with algorithms, VR spaces, and algorithmic curation. Analysis employs 'hermeneutic recontextualization' and multimodal semiotic analysis.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards (Kozinets, 2020): (1) Deep cultural immersion: Sustained participant observation documented over months rather than one-off scraping; (2) Humanist ethical protocols: Procedural ethics addressing avatar privacy, informed consent in digital spaces, and non-commercial anonymization; (3) Multimodal synthesis: Integrating textual analysis with image, video, and audio data streams.
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors: (1) Passive data scraping masquerading as ethnography (scraping tweets or Reddit posts without researcher cultural immersion is automated content analysis, not netnography); (2) Ignoring platform algorithmic architecture—failing to account for how algorithms shape what content is visible; and (3) Violating online community trust by conducting covert lurker studies without ethical justification.
terms.apa_reference: Kozinets, R. V. (2020). Netnography: The essential guide to qualitative social media research (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình tam phân ba chiều của Marketing (Shelby Hunt)
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình 3 chiều phân đôi Hunt
Khung phân loại tiếp thị Shelby Hunt
terms.core_definition: Hunt's Three-Dichotomy Model of Marketing is a foundational metatheoretical framework articulated by marketing philosopher Shelby D. Hunt (1976) in 'The Nature and Scope of Marketing'.
