Designed to resolve long-standing debates regarding the academic boundaries, scientific legitimacy, and scope of marketing, the model cross-classifies all marketing phenomena and research inquiries across three fundamental dichotomies: Sector (Profit vs. Non-Profit), Micro vs. Macro, and Orientation (Positive vs. Normative), generating an eight-cell taxonomy defining the entire disciplinary scope of marketing science.
terms.seminal_citation: Hunt, S. D. (1976). The nature and scope of marketing. Journal of Marketing, 40(3), 17-28.
terms.expert_notes: Rác Markdown/bảng; mảnh trích
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hunt s 3-Dichotomy Model according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: The model partitions marketing inquiry across three orthogonal dichotomous axes: (1) Sector Dimension: Profit-oriented (business enterprises) versus Non-profit (universities, charities, public health campaigns); (2) Aggregation Dimension: Micro (individual consumers, single firms, specific transactions) versus Macro (aggregate industry systems, societal distribution mechanisms, public policy impacts); (3) Epistemological Dimension: Positive (descriptive, explanatory, and predictive inquiry: 'what is') versus Normative (prescriptive, evaluative, and moral guidance: 'what ought to be'). Cross-tabulating these three axes creates eight distinct analytical cells (e.g., Cell 1: Micro-Profit-Positive; Cell 8: Macro-Nonprofit-Normative).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The model partitions marketing inquiry across three orthogonal dichotomous axes: (1) Sector Dimension: Profit-oriented (business enterprises) versus Non-profit (universities, charities, public health campaigns); (2) Aggregation Dimension: Micro (individual consumers, single firms, specific transactions) versus Macro (aggregate industry systems, societal distribution mechanisms, public policy impacts); (3) Epistemological Dimension: Positive (descriptive, explanatory, and predictive inquiry: 'what is') versus Normative (prescriptive, evaluative, and moral guidance: 'what ought to be'). Cross-tabulating these three axes creates eight distinct analytical cells (e.g., Cell 1: Micro-Profit-Positive; Cell 8: Macro-Nonprofit-Normative).
terms.benchmarks: Philosophical demarcation benchmarks: (1) Hunt demonstrated that marketing is an authentic science primarily within the four Positive cells (Cells 1, 3, 5, 7), which adhere to the hypothetico-deductive method and empirical falsification; (2) The Normative cells (Cells 2, 4, 6, 8) represent applied art, engineering, and managerial practice; (3) Clear structural classification of any doctoral marketing research topic into its exact 3-dichotomy cell.
terms.pitfalls: Common scholarly errors: (1) Conflating Positive and Normative claims—deriving normative policy prescriptions directly from positive empirical findings without explicit value premises (violating Hume's guillotine); (2) Confining marketing research exclusively to the Micro-Profit domain, overlooking macro-marketing and public policy impacts; and (3) Dismissing non-profit marketing as non-legitimate marketing inquiry.
terms.apa_reference: Hunt, S. D. (1976). The nature and scope of marketing. Journal of Marketing, 40(3), 17–28. https://doi.org/10.1177/002224297604000304

terms.vietnamese: Hiệu chỉnh Epsilon Huynh-Feldt (Trong phân tích phương sai lặp lại)
terms.core_definition: The Huynh-Feldt Epsilon Correction, developed by Huynh Huynh and Leonard S. Feldt (1976), is an adjustment procedure for the degrees of freedom in Repeated Measures Analysis of Variance (RM-ANOVA) when the assumption of sphericity is violated. Designed as a less conservative alternative to the Greenhouse-Geisser correction, the Huynh-Feldt epsilon adjusts for the sample size bias present in Greenhouse-Geisser's estimate, providing higher statistical power and accurate Type I error control when departures from sphericity are moderate to mild (epsilon >= 0.75).
terms.seminal_citation: Huynh, H., & Feldt, L. S. (1976). Estimation of the Box correction for degrees of freedom from sample data in randomized block and split-plot designs. Journal of Educational Statistics, 1(1), 69-82.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Huynh-Feldt Epsilon Correction according to Huynh & Feldt (1976).
terms.operational_mechanism: Given a repeated measures design with k conditions and sample size N: (1) Compute the sample variance-covariance matrix among repeated measures and calculate the Greenhouse-Geisser epsilon hat{epsilon}_{GG}; (2) Calculate the Huynh-Feldt epsilon: tilde{epsilon}_{HF} = [ N * (k - 1) * hat{epsilon}_{GG} - 2 ] / [ (k - 1) * (N - 1 - (k - 1) * hat{epsilon}_{GG}) ]; (3) If tilde{epsilon}_{HF} exceeds 1.0 (a mathematical artifact that can occur when sphericity is nearly perfect), it is capped at 1.0; (4) Multiply numerator and denominator degrees of freedom by tilde{epsilon}_{HF}: df_1^* = tilde{epsilon}_{HF} * (k - 1) and df_2^* = tilde{epsilon}_{HF} * (k - 1)(N - 1); (5) Recalculate p-values using adjusted degrees of freedom.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Given a repeated measures design with k conditions and sample size N: (1) Compute the sample variance-covariance matrix among repeated measures and calculate the Greenhouse-Geisser epsilon hat{epsilon}_{GG}; (2) Calculate the Huynh-Feldt epsilon: tilde{epsilon}_{HF} = [ N * (k - 1) * hat{epsilon}_{GG} - 2 ] / [ (k - 1) * (N - 1 - (k - 1) * hat{epsilon}_{GG}) ]; (3) If tilde{epsilon}_{HF} exceeds 1.0 (a mathematical artifact that can occur when sphericity is nearly perfect), it is capped at 1.0; (4) Multiply numerator and denominator degrees of freedom by tilde{epsilon}_{HF}: df_1^* = tilde{epsilon}_{HF} * (k - 1) and df_2^* = tilde{epsilon}_{HF} * (k - 1)(N - 1); (5) Recalculate p-values using adjusted degrees of freedom.
terms.benchmarks: Decision framework (Girden, 1992; Howell, 2013): (1) When Mauchly's test of sphericity is significant (p < 0.05): If hat{epsilon}_{GG} > 0.75, apply the Huynh-Feldt correction (prevents overly conservative tests); (2) If hat{epsilon}_{GG} < 0.75 or if violation of sphericity is severe, apply the Greenhouse-Geisser correction; (3) In APA reporting format: F(df_1^*, df_2^*) = F_value, p = p_value, epsilon = tilde{epsilon}_{HF}.
terms.pitfalls: Common reporting traps: (1) Using Huynh-Feldt when hat{epsilon}_{GG} < 0.75, which fails to adequately guard against Type I error inflation; (2) Failing to cap tilde{epsilon}_{HF} at 1.0 when the formula yields a value greater than 1; and (3) Reporting original unadjusted degrees of freedom alongside corrected p-values.
terms.apa_reference: Huynh, H., & Feldt, L. S. (1976). Estimation of the Box correction for degrees of freedom from sample data in randomized block and split-plot designs. Journal of Educational Statistics, 1(1), 69–82. https://doi.org/10.3102/10769986001001069

terms.vietnamese: Chiết khấu hyperbol
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình chiết khấu phi nhất quán thời gian
terms.core_definition: Chiết khấu hyperbol (Hyperbolic Discounting, được George Ainslie phát hiện trong thực nghiệm tâm lý học năm 1975, 1992 và được David Laibson toán học hóa thành mô hình Chiết khấu Cận Hyperbol Quasi-Hyperbolic β-δ năm 1997) là mô hình kinh tế lượng hành vi giải thích sự Phi nhất quán theo thời gian (Time Inconsistency) trong các quyết định liên thời gian của con người (tiết kiệm, ăn kiêng, tập thể dục, cai thuốc lá, đầu tư giáo dục). Mô hình kinh tế cổ điển của Samuelson (1937) giả định Chiết khấu hàm mũ (Exponential Discounting): D(t) = δᵗ với tỷ lệ chiết khấu cố định không đổi theo thời gian, dẫn đến các kế hoạch lập ra cho tương lai luôn được thực thi nhất quán. Ngược lại, thực tế con người mắc phải Thiên kiến hiện tại (Present Bias): họ định giá cực kỳ cao cho các phần thưởng nhận được ngay tại thời điểm hiện tại và chiết khấu cực kỳ nặng nề các phần thưởng bị lùi lại một chút từ hiện tại, nhưng lại tỏ ra rất kiên nhẫn khi so sánh giữa hai thời điểm trong tương lai xa. Hàm chiết khấu hyperbol thực tế có dạng: D(t) = (1)/(1 + k t), có độ dốc ban đầu cực lớn và phẳng dần về sau.
terms.seminal_citation: Laibson, D. (1997). Golden eggs and hyperbolic discounting. The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 112(2), 443-478.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hyperbolic Discounting according to Laibson (1997).
terms.short_definition: Mô hình lựa chọn liên thời gian trong đó tỷ lệ chiết khấu giảm dần theo thời gian, giải thích hiện tượng thiên kiến hiện tại và mâu thuẫn ý chí nội tâm.
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Khung toán học Chiết khấu Cận Hyperbol (Mô hình Beta-Delta của Laibson, 1997):
 Thỏa dụng liên thời gian của cá nhân tại thời điểm t có dạng:
 U_t = u(c_t) + β ∑(τ=1 to T-t) δ^τ u(c_t+τ).
 - δ ∈ (0, 1): Hệ số kiên nhẫn dài hạn chuẩn tắc.
 - β ∈ (0, 1): Tham số thiên kiến hiện tại (Present-bias parameter). Mọi thỏa dụng trong tương lai (kể từ ngày mai) đều bị chiết khấu ngay lập tức bởi hệ số nhân β.
2. Phân loại cấu trúc nhận thức của người ra quyết định (O'Donoghue & Rabin, 1999):
 - Người ngây thơ (Naïve individuals): Hoàn toàn không biết mình bị thiên kiến hiện tại, luôn tin rằng ngày mai mình sẽ kiên nhẫn và tuân thủ kế hoạch tiết kiệm/ăn kiêng (dẫn đến thói quen trì hoãn mãn tính).
 - Người tinh tế (Sophisticated individuals): Nhận thức rõ ràng sự yếu mềm của ý chí trong tương lai, chủ động tìm kiếm các 'Công cụ cam kết cưỡng chế' (Commitment Devices - ví dụ: gửi tiền vào sổ tiết kiệm có kỳ hạn không được rút trước hạn, đăng ký thẻ tập gym có cam kết phạt).
3. Ước lượng thực nghiệm tham số β và δ: Thực hiện thực nghiệm đo lường lựa chọn liên thời gian (Time-dated trade-off tasks) sử dụng phương pháp Multiple Price Lists (MPL) hoặc Convex Time Budgets (Andreoni & Sprenger, 2012).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Tham số thiên kiến hiện tại β: Trong hầu hết các nghiên cứu kinh tế lượng thực nghiệm vi mô, giá trị β̂ dao động trong khoảng 0.65 - 0.85 (có ý nghĩa thống kê khác biệt hoàn toàn với giá trị 1.0 của mô hình hàm mũ tân cổ điển).
2. Tham số chiết khấu dài hạn δ: Thường xấp xỉ mức chiết khấu thông thường 0.95 - 0.99 tương ứng với mức lãi suất hàng năm 1 - 5%.
3. Hiện tượng Đảo chiều sở thích (Preference Reversal): Đa số mọi người chọn nhận 100 USD hôm nay thay vì 110 USD ngày mai; nhưng khi được hỏi lựa chọn giữa 100 USD sau 30 ngày và 110 USD sau 31 ngày, họ lại kiên nhẫn chọn 110 USD.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Đồng nhất độ trễ nhận thưởng với rủi ro vỡ nợ (Risk Confounding): Khi yêu cầu người tham gia thí nghiệm chọn nhận tiền trong tương lai, họ có thể từ chối không phải vì họ thiếu kiên nhẫn (chiết khấu cao) mà vì họ không tin tưởng nhà nghiên cứu sẽ quay lại trả tiền trong 1 tháng nữa. Phải thiết kế cơ chế đảm bảo độ tin cậy tuyệt đối để cô lập tham số β.
2. Giả định tính chất chiết khấu tĩnh trong suốt vòng đời: Thiên kiến hiện tại có thể thay đổi mạnh theo độ tuổi, tình trạng hôn nhân và các cú sốc sức khỏe/tài chính đột ngột.
3. Lạm dụng mô hình hàm mũ trong việc đánh giá các chính sách dài hạn: Sử dụng chiết khấu hàm mũ với tỷ lệ cao cho các vấn đề biến đổi khí hậu hoặc nợ công sẽ triệt tiêu hoàn toàn quyền lợi của các thế hệ mai sau trong phân tích chi phí - lợi ích (Cost-Benefit Analysis).
terms.apa_reference: Laibson, D. (1997). Golden eggs and hyperbolic discounting. The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 112(2), 443-478. https://doi.org/10.1162/003355397555253

terms.vietnamese: Giả thuyết khoa học
vietnamese_variants: Giả thuyết khoa học thực nghiệm
terms.core_definition: A Scientific Research Hypothesis is a formal, testable, and falsifiable proposition specifying an expected relationship, directional difference, or causal mechanism between two or more operationalized constructs or variables. Rooted in the hypothetico-deductive tradition (Popper, 1959; Hempel, 1966), a scientific hypothesis is not a casual conjecture or unsubstantiated speculation; rather, it is a theoretically derived proposition that logically bridges abstract conceptual frameworks with concrete empirical testing, establishing clear conditions under which it can be empirically refuted.
terms.seminal_citation: Popper, K. R. (1959). The logic of scientific discovery. Hutchinson & Co.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hypothesis according to Creswell & Creswell (2023).
terms.operational_mechanism: Hypothesis formulation follows a structured deductive progression: (1) Theoretical Grounding: Grounding the expected relationship in established theories (e.g., Social Exchange Theory, Resource-Based View); (2) Nomological Network: Specifying directionality (positive/negative), functional form (linear, curvilinear, threshold), and structural role (direct, mediating, moderating); (3) Operationalization: Translating latent constructs into empirically measurable variables; (4) Statistical Formulation: Translating the substantive research hypothesis (H_1) into an operational null hypothesis (H_0) subjected to significance testing (e.g., t-test, F-test, SEM path coefficient).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Hypothesis formulation follows a structured deductive progression: (1) Theoretical Grounding: Grounding the expected relationship in established theories (e.g., Social Exchange Theory, Resource-Based View); (2) Nomological Network: Specifying directionality (positive/negative), functional form (linear, curvilinear, threshold), and structural role (direct, mediating, moderating); (3) Operationalization: Translating latent constructs into empirically measurable variables; (4) Statistical Formulation: Translating the substantive research hypothesis (H_1) into an operational null hypothesis (H_0) subjected to significance testing (e.g., t-test, F-test, SEM path coefficient).
terms.benchmarks: Criteria for Q1-standard hypotheses: (1) Falsifiability: Clear empirical states of the world must exist that would refute the hypothesis; (2) Directionality: Hypotheses should be directional ('X increases Y') unless literature is fundamentally nascent or contradictory; (3) Parsimony and Precision: Avoiding complex compound propositions (double-barreled hypotheses combining multiple relationships into one statement).
terms.pitfalls: Common methodological traps: (1) Formulating non-falsifiable truisms or tautologies ('Effective leadership improves organizational outcomes'); (2) Double-barreled hypotheses ('X increases Y and Z'—if X increases Y but decreases Z, the hypothesis can neither be accepted nor rejected); and (3) Post-hoc hypothesizing (HARKing) to match serendipitous statistical patterns.
terms.apa_reference: Popper, K. R. (1959). The logic of scientific discovery. Hutchinson & Co.

terms.vietnamese: Ngụy tạo giả thuyết hậu nghiệm trong quản trị khoa học
vietnamese_variants: Biện minh giả thuyết sau thực nghiệm
terms.core_definition: Ngụy tạo giả thuyết hậu nghiệm là biểu hiện của Ngụy biện tay thiện xạ Texas (Texas Sharpshooter Fallacy) trong phương pháp luận khoa học: Bắn các phát đạn ngẫu nhiên lên tường trước (chạy dữ liệu), sau đó mới vẽ vòng tròn hồng tâm xung quanh các lỗ đạn dày nhất (đặt giả thuyết). Hành vi này vi phạm nguyên tắc cơ bản của phương pháp suy diễn giả thuyết Popper (Popperian hypothetico-deductive method), biến việc kiểm định giả thuyết thành một màn kịch diễn dịch giả mạo.
terms.seminal_citation: Kerr (1998); Gelman & Loken (2014)
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hypothesizing After the Results are Known according to Bị triệt tiêu khi bài báo thực hiện đăng ký trước thiết kế nghiên cứu (Preregistration) tại Open Science Framework..
terms.benchmarks: Các tạp chí hàng đầu (JAP, SMJ) yêu cầu tác giả phải phân định rõ ràng trong bài báo: Đâu là các phân tích kiểm định giả thuyết tiên nghiệm chính thức (Confirmatory / Planned analyses) và đâu là các phân tích khám phá hậu nghiệm bổ sung (Exploratory / Post-hoc analyses).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Sự khác biệt giữa Khám phá và Kiểm định: Trong nghiên cứu khám phá, việc sinh giả thuyết từ dữ liệu là hoàn toàn hợp pháp và đáng khuyến khích (Quy nạp/Loại suy). 2. Điểm phi chuẩn mực: Chỉ xảy ra khi tác giả ngụy trang quá trình khám phá đó thành kiểm định diễn dịch hình thức để đánh lừa người đọc về mức ý nghĩa thống kê của các kiểm định. 3. Thẩm định qua dấu vết kiểm toán (Audit trail) và thời gian biểu thu thập dữ liệu.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Trình bày các kết quả phân tích khám phá sau hồi quy như thể đó là các mục tiêu nghiên cứu ban đầu; phản biện sẽ chất vấn về nguy cơ bùng nổ sai số loại I và yêu cầu kiểm định chéo trên một tập dữ liệu độc lập.
terms.apa_reference: Gelman, A., & Loken, E. (2014). The statistical crisis in science: How array of data analysis choices leads to questionable research practices. American Scientist, 102(6), 460–465.

terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp giả thuyết - diễn dịch
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình giả thuyết - suy luận diễn dịch
Quy trình khoa học diễn dịch Popper
terms.core_definition: The Hypothetico-Deductive Method is the predominant epistemological framework of modern empirical science, formalized by Karl Popper, Carl Hempel, and Peter Medawar. It conceptualizes scientific progress not as the passive inductive accumulation of observations, but as an active, cyclical process of proposing bold theoretical hypotheses (conjectures), deductively deriving observable empirical implications from them, and subjecting those implications to rigorous empirical testing designed to refute or corroborate the theory (refutations).
terms.seminal_citation: Hempel, C. G. (1966). Philosophy of natural science. Prentice-Hall.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Hypothetico-Deductive Method according to Hempel (1966).
terms.operational_mechanism: The cycle proceeds through four distinct phases: (1) Theoretical Conception: Proposing an explanatory hypothesis to solve a theoretical puzzle or explain an unexplained phenomenon; (2) Deductive Implication: Logically deducing specific, operationalized observational predictions ('If hypothesis H is true, then under experimental conditions C, observation O must occur'); (3) Empirical Testing: Gathering systematic empirical data via controlled experiments, field surveys, or econometric modeling; (4) Appraisal and Feedback: If observation O fails to occur, the hypothesis is refuted via modus tollens; if O occurs, the hypothesis is corroborated (provisionally accepted, never permanently proven) and subjected to further stress-testing.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The cycle proceeds through four distinct phases: (1) Theoretical Conception: Proposing an explanatory hypothesis to solve a theoretical puzzle or explain an unexplained phenomenon; (2) Deductive Implication: Logically deducing specific, operationalized observational predictions ('If hypothesis H is true, then under experimental conditions C, observation O must occur'); (3) Empirical Testing: Gathering systematic empirical data via controlled experiments, field surveys, or econometric modeling; (4) Appraisal and Feedback: If observation O fails to occur, the hypothesis is refuted via modus tollens; if O occurs, the hypothesis is corroborated (provisionally accepted, never permanently proven) and subjected to further stress-testing.
terms.benchmarks: Epistemic appraisal criteria: (1) Modus tollens rigor: [(H -> O) and (not O)] -> not H; (2) Excess empirical content: Corroborated predictions must explain new, surprising phenomena beyond existing theories; (3) Complete documentation of failed predictions alongside successful ones.
terms.pitfalls: Critical philosophical errors: (1) The fallacy of affirming the consequent: Believing that because O occurred, hypothesis H is 'proven true' ([(H -> O) and O] does not prove H, because alternative rival hypotheses could also produce O); (2) Ad-hoc immunizing maneuvers modifying the hypothesis to evade negative results; and (3) Inductive data-mining masquerading as deductive testing.
terms.apa_reference: Hempel, C. G. (1966). Philosophy of natural science. Prentice-Hall.

terms.vietnamese: Thống kê I-bình phương (Mức độ không đồng nhất trong phân tích tổng hợp)
vietnamese_variants: Chỉ số không đồng nhất I2
terms.core_definition: The I-squared (I^2) statistic, developed by Julian P. T. Higgins and Simon G. Thompson (2002), is the standard quantitative metric used in meta-analyses to measure the proportion of total variation in observed effect sizes across studies that is attributable to true between-study heterogeneity rather than random sampling error (chance). Unlike Cochran's Q statistic (which tests the statistical existence of heterogeneity but depends heavily on the number of studies k), I^2 is an intuitive percentage metric that is largely independent of sample size and effect size scale.
terms.seminal_citation: Higgins, J. P., & Thompson, S. G. (2002). Quantifying heterogeneity in a meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 21(11), 1539-1558.
terms.expert_notes: ngưỡng 25/50/75% thuộc Higgins et al. (2003); trùng #1184
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of I-squared Statistic according to Higgins & Thompson (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism: The formula for I^2 is derived directly from Cochran's Q and degrees of freedom df = k - 1 (where k is the number of included studies): I^2 = max( 0, [ (Q - df) / Q ] * 100% ). When Cochran's Q is less than or equal to df, I^2 is set to 0%. In random-effects meta-analysis models, I^2 also reflects the ratio of between-study variance (tau^2) to total variance: I^2 = tau^2 / (tau^2 + s^2), where s^2 is the typical within-study sampling variance. Confidence intervals for I^2 are computed using Higgins and Thompson's test-based approach.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The formula for I^2 is derived directly from Cochran's Q and degrees of freedom df = k - 1 (where k is the number of included studies): I^2 = max( 0, [ (Q - df) / Q ] * 100% ). When Cochran's Q is less than or equal to df, I^2 is set to 0%. In random-effects meta-analysis models, I^2 also reflects the ratio of between-study variance (tau^2) to total variance: I^2 = tau^2 / (tau^2 + s^2), where s^2 is the typical within-study sampling variance. Confidence intervals for I^2 are computed using Higgins and Thompson's test-based approach.
terms.benchmarks: Empirical heterogeneity thresholds (Higgins et al., 2003; Cochrane Handbook): (1) 0% to 40%: Might not be important (low heterogeneity); (2) 30% to 60%: May represent moderate heterogeneity; (3) 50% to 90%: May represent substantial heterogeneity; (4) 75% to 100%: Considerable heterogeneity; (5) When I^2 > 50%, random-effects models are strictly required, and researchers must conduct subgroup analyses or meta-regressions to explore the sources of heterogeneity.
terms.pitfalls: Common meta-analytic pitfalls: (1) Treating I^2 as a measure of absolute dispersion (I^2 is a relative proportion, not an absolute spread of true effect sizes; reporting tau or the 95% Prediction Interval is essential for absolute dispersion); (2) Using fixed-effect models when I^2 > 50%; and (3) Ignoring wide confidence intervals of I^2 in small meta-analyses (k < 10 studies).
terms.apa_reference: Higgins, J. P., & Thompson, S. G. (2002). Quantifying heterogeneity in a meta-analysis. Statistics in Medicine, 21(11), 1539–1558. https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.1186

terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số i10 (Thước đo học thuật Google Scholar)
vietnamese_variants: Thước đo công trình trên 10 trích dẫn
terms.core_definition: The i10-index is a simple author-level bibliometric metric introduced by Google Scholar in 2011 to assess scholarly productivity and steady impact. It is formally defined as the total number of academic publications authored or co-authored by a researcher that have received at least 10 citations each. Google Scholar reports both an all-time i10-index and an i10-index over the most recent 5 calendar years (i10-index since year X), providing a direct indicator of whether an author's scholarly contributions maintain ongoing relevance.
terms.seminal_citation: Google. (2011). Google Scholar Citations open to all: Introducing the i10-index. Google Official Blog.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of i10-Index according to Google Scholar (2011).
terms.operational_mechanism: Calculation is straightforward: (1) Retrieve an author's complete publication list on Google Scholar Citations; (2) Count all individual publications where total citations c_i >= 10; (3) The count constitutes the all-time i10-index; (4) Repeat the calculation restricting citations to those accrued in the last 5 calendar years to yield the 5-year i10-index.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Calculation is straightforward: (1) Retrieve an author's complete publication list on Google Scholar Citations; (2) Count all individual publications where total citations c_i >= 10; (3) The count constitutes the all-time i10-index; (4) Repeat the calculation restricting citations to those accrued in the last 5 calendar years to yield the 5-year i10-index.
terms.benchmarks: Academic benchmarks: (1) Early-career researcher (postdoc / assistant professor): i10-index typically between 3 and 10; (2) Associate Professor: i10-index between 15 and 35; (3) Full Professor / Senior Chair: i10-index >= 50 (elite researchers often exceed 150 to 300); (4) Comparison: i10 >= h-index for authors whose top papers have more than 10 citations, but i10 can be less than h for highly productive authors with many papers cited between h and 10 times.
terms.pitfalls: Critical scientometric limitations: (1) Arbitrary threshold: The number 10 is mathematically arbitrary with no intrinsic ontological meaning; (2) Google Scholar data noise: Susceptibility to duplicate entries, student dissertations, non-peer-reviewed preprints, and automated citation scraping errors; and (3) Insensitivity to high impact: A paper with 10 citations and a paper with 10,000 citations count equally toward the i10-index.
terms.apa_reference: Google. (2011). Google Scholar Citations open to all: Introducing the i10-index. Google Official Blog. https://googleblog.blogspot.com/2011/11/google-scholar-citations-open-to-all.html

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn xác định tác giả ICMJE
vietnamese_variants: Bộ tiêu chí tác giả ICMJE
Quy chuẩn quyền tác giả ICMJE
Bốn tiêu chuẩn tác giả Vancouver
terms.core_definition: The ICMJE Authorship Criteria, established by the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors (originally the Vancouver Group), are the universally recognized global gold standard governing legitimate authorship attribution in biomedical, clinical, and increasingly broad multidisciplinary scientific research. Formulated to eliminate fraudulent authorship practices (such as guest, gift, and ghost authorship), the ICMJE explicitly mandates that authorship credit must be based on substantial intellectual contributions across four mandatory, non-negotiable criteria.
terms.seminal_citation: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors. (2023). Recommendations for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals. ICMJE.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of ICMJE Authorship Criteria according to ICMJE (2021).
terms.operational_mechanism: To qualify as an author, an individual must fulfill ALL FOUR of the following criteria simultaneously: (1) Substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND (2) Drafting the work or reviewing it critically for important intellectual content; AND (3) Final approval of the version to be published; AND (4) Agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved. Contributors who meet some but not all four criteria must be acknowledged in the Acknowledgments section, not listed on the byline.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: To qualify as an author, an individual must fulfill ALL FOUR of the following criteria simultaneously: (1) Substantial contributions to the conception or design of the work; or the acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of data for the work; AND (2) Drafting the work or reviewing it critically for important intellectual content; AND (3) Final approval of the version to be published; AND (4) Agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work in ensuring that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately investigated and resolved. Contributors who meet some but not all four criteria must be acknowledged in the Acknowledgments section, not listed on the byline.
terms.benchmarks: Compliance benchmarks: (1) All co-authors must sign an ICMJE disclosure form confirming satisfaction of all 4 criteria; (2) Clear distinction: Acquisition of funding, collection of routine data, or general administrative supervision alone DOES NOT justify authorship; (3) Mandatory reporting of detailed contributor roles via the CRediT taxonomy.
terms.pitfalls: Common ethical violations: (1) Adding senior laboratory directors who never reviewed the manuscript text (violating Criterion 2 and 3); (2) Omitting junior data analysts or doctoral students who drafted the manuscript (ghost authorship); and (3) Assuming that funding acquisition automatically grants authorship rights.
terms.apa_reference: International Committee of Medical Journal Editors. (2023). Recommendations for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals. ICMJE. http://www.icmje.org/recommendations/

terms.vietnamese: Kho lưu trữ dữ liệu nghiên cứu khoa học xã hội ICPSR
vietnamese_variants: Lưu trữ dữ liệu xã hội và chính trị ICPSR
terms.core_definition: The Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR), based at the Institute for Social Research at the University of Michigan since 1962, is the world's largest, oldest, and most authoritative curated digital data archive for social and behavioral science research. Maintaining an extensive repository of over 17,000 studies encompassing millions of variables, ICPSR provides standardized, preservation-grade access to raw microdata, cross-national surveys, census archives, and longitudinal datasets, serving as a primary infrastructure for open science, quantitative replication, and secondary empirical analysis.
terms.seminal_citation: Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research. (2024). Guide to social science data preparation and archiving: Best practice across the data life cycle (6th ed.). ICPSR, University of Michigan.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of ICPSR Data Archive according to ICPSR (1962).
terms.operational_mechanism: ICPSR curation and access workflows: (1) Professional Curation: Ingested datasets undergo rigorous expert curation, including comprehensive codebook verification, data cleaning, variable labeling, and automated disclosure risk analysis to ensure participant confidentiality; (2) Format Normalization: Proprietary formats are preserved in non-proprietary ASCII/XML and distributed in multiple formats (R, Stata, SPSS, SAS); (3) Tiered Access: Public open-access datasets, institutional member-access data, and secure Virtual Data Enclaves (VDE) for restricted sensitive microdata (e.g., criminal justice records, geocoded census data); (4) Persistent DOI assignment and comprehensive bibliographic citation indexing.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: ICPSR curation and access workflows: (1) Professional Curation: Ingested datasets undergo rigorous expert curation, including comprehensive codebook verification, data cleaning, variable labeling, and automated disclosure risk analysis to ensure participant confidentiality; (2) Format Normalization: Proprietary formats are preserved in non-proprietary ASCII/XML and distributed in multiple formats (R, Stata, SPSS, SAS); (3) Tiered Access: Public open-access datasets, institutional member-access data, and secure Virtual Data Enclaves (VDE) for restricted sensitive microdata (e.g., criminal justice records, geocoded census data); (4) Persistent DOI assignment and comprehensive bibliographic citation indexing.
terms.benchmarks: Secondary data research standards: (1) Use of official ICPSR study DOIs and formal data citations in manuscripts; (2) Application of complex survey sampling weights provided in ICPSR codebooks; (3) Compliance with ICPSR Restricted Data Use Agreements when accessing sensitive individual-level data.
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors in secondary data analysis: (1) Failing to apply provided probability weights (e.g., post-stratification weights), producing severely biased population estimates; (2) Treating repeated cross-sectional surveys archived in ICPSR as true longitudinal panel data; and (3) Citing ICPSR data informally in footnotes rather than providing formal data references in the bibliography.
terms.apa_reference: Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research. (2024). Guide to social science data preparation and archiving: Best practice across the data life cycle (6th ed.). ICPSR, University of Michigan. https://doi.org/10.3886/PREPAREARCHIVE.ED6

terms.term: Identification of Formative Measurement Models (2+ Rule)
terms.vietnamese: Định danh mô hình đo lường cấu thành (Quy tắc hai chỉ báo phát ra)
vietnamese_variants: Định danh biến tiềm ẩn formative
Identification of formative constructs in SEM
terms.core_definition: Identification of Formative Constructs refers to the mathematical and structural conditions required to estimate formative (cause) measurement models in Covariance-Based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM). Unlike reflective constructs where latent variables emit paths to indicators, a purely formative construct receives causal arrows from its indicators (x_i -> eta). Consequently, an isolated formative construct has no mathematical scale or unique covariance implications, making it structurally unidentified unless it emits paths to at least two reflective indicators or to two distinct endogenous latent constructs (the 'Two-Emitted-Paths Rule' or '2+ Rule'; Bollen & Davis, 2009).
terms.seminal_citation: Bollen, K. A., & Davis, W. R. (2009). Two rules of identification for structural equation models. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 16(3), 523-536.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Identification of formative constructs according to MacKenzie et al. (2011).
terms.operational_mechanism: To identify a formative construct eta = gamma_1 * x_1 + ... + gamma_k * x_k + zeta in CB-SEM: (1) The construct must have at least two emitted directed paths. Options include: (a) Pathing to two reflective indicators: eta -> y_1 and eta -> y_2 (MIMIC model: Multiple Indicators and Multiple Causes); (b) Pathing to two distinct endogenous latent constructs: eta -> xi_1 and eta -> xi_2; (c) Pathing to one reflective indicator and one endogenous construct; (2) Fixing the disturbance variance Var(zeta) or fixing one emitted path coefficient to 1.0 to assign metric scale; (3) In PLS-SEM, identification is achieved algorithmically via component weight estimation without requiring emitted reflective paths.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: To identify a formative construct eta = gamma_1 * x_1 + ... + gamma_k * x_k + zeta in CB-SEM: (1) The construct must have at least two emitted directed paths. Options include: (a) Pathing to two reflective indicators: eta -> y_1 and eta -> y_2 (MIMIC model: Multiple Indicators and Multiple Causes); (b) Pathing to two distinct endogenous latent constructs: eta -> xi_1 and eta -> xi_2; (c) Pathing to one reflective indicator and one endogenous construct; (2) Fixing the disturbance variance Var(zeta) or fixing one emitted path coefficient to 1.0 to assign metric scale; (3) In PLS-SEM, identification is achieved algorithmically via component weight estimation without requiring emitted reflective paths.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards (Bollen & Davis, 2009; Diamantopoulos et al., 2008): (1) In CB-SEM, failure to include at least two emitted paths results in non-positive definite matrices and failure of model convergence; (2) In PLS-SEM, redundancy analysis must be conducted: Formative construct must predict a single-item global reflective measure with path coefficient beta >= 0.70 (R^2 >= 0.50) to establish convergent validity.
terms.pitfalls: Critical reviewer rejection traps: (1) Specifying a formative construct in AMOS or LISREL without emitted paths, leading to fatal identification errors; (2) Confusing formative indicators with reflective indicators in CB-SEM, causing severe model misspecification; and (3) Failing to evaluate multicollinearity among formative indicators (Variance Inflation Factor / VIF must be < 3.3 or strictly < 5.0).
terms.apa_reference: Bollen, K. A., & Davis, W. R. (2009). Two rules of identification for structural equation models. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 16(3), 523–536. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510903008298

terms.vietnamese: Thư viện số IEEE Xplore
vietnamese_variants: Cơ sở dữ liệu IEEE Xplore
Thư viện học thuật IEEE Xplore
terms.core_definition: The IEEE Xplore Digital Library is the premier authoritative scholarly database and digital discovery platform for electrical engineering, computer science, telecommunications, robotics, biomedical engineering, and computational methodology, maintained by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) and the Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET). Indexing over 6 million peer-reviewed journal articles, international conference proceedings, technical standards, and computational tutorials, it serves as an indispensable source for systematic literature reviews, state-of-the-art benchmarking, and technological patent landscaping.
terms.seminal_citation: IEEE. (2024). IEEE Xplore digital library: Search algorithms, metadata indexing, and standards documentation. Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of IEEE Xplore Digital Library according to IEEE (2000).
terms.operational_mechanism: Systematic search capabilities in IEEE Xplore: (1) Advanced Search: Nested Boolean logic (AND, OR, NOT), proximity operators (NEAR/n, ONEAR/n), and field-specific indexing (e.g., Abstract, Index Terms, Document Title); (2) Controlled Vocabulary: Search indexing via IEEE Thesaurus and Inspec Controlled Terms; (3) Bibliographic export: Automated export of formatted references and BibTeX files containing DOIs, accession numbers, and author affiliation metadata; (4) Systematic review integration: Full compliance with PRISMA guidelines for electronic database search strings.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Systematic search capabilities in IEEE Xplore: (1) Advanced Search: Nested Boolean logic (AND, OR, NOT), proximity operators (NEAR/n, ONEAR/n), and field-specific indexing (e.g., Abstract, Index Terms, Document Title); (2) Controlled Vocabulary: Search indexing via IEEE Thesaurus and Inspec Controlled Terms; (3) Bibliographic export: Automated export of formatted references and BibTeX files containing DOIs, accession numbers, and author affiliation metadata; (4) Systematic review integration: Full compliance with PRISMA guidelines for electronic database search strings.
terms.benchmarks: Systematic review standards (Kitchenham & Charters, 2007 for software/engineering reviews): (1) Fully documented search syntax including exact operator formatting; (2) Deduplication against Web of Science, Scopus, and ACM Digital Library; (3) Inclusion of both peer-reviewed IEEE Transactions and premier IEEE flagship conferences (e.g., CVPR, ICCV, ICSE).
terms.pitfalls: Common systematic search errors: (1) Running unstructured, natural-language search strings rather than structured Boolean queries; (2) Overlooking that IEEE Xplore limits search queries to a maximum of 40 search terms; and (3) Neglecting to export complete metadata fields needed for PRISMA flowchart accounting.
terms.apa_reference: IEEE. (2024). IEEE Xplore digital library: Search algorithms, metadata indexing, and standards documentation. Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/

terms.term: Item Information Function (IIF in Item Response Theory)
terms.vietnamese: Hàm thông tin câu hỏi (Hàm IIF trong lý thuyết ứng đáp câu hỏi)
vietnamese_variants: Hàm thông tin mục hỏi IIF
Đường cong thông tin câu hỏi
terms.core_definition: The Item Information Function (IIF), denoted I_i(theta), is a foundational mathematical concept in Item Response Theory (IRT) formulated by Frederic M. Lord and Allan Birnbaum (1968). It quantifies the psychometric precision and measurement reliability that an individual test or survey item provides at any specific point along the continuous latent trait continuum (theta). In sharp contrast to Classical Test Theory (which assumes measurement error is constant across all examinees), IRT recognizes that an item's precision varies depending on the examinee's ability level, with IIF peaking near the item's difficulty threshold.
terms.seminal_citation: Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee's ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick (Eds.), Statistical theories of mental test scores (pp. 397-479). Addison-Wesley.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of IIF according to Thông tin cực đại tại ngưỡng độ khó của câu hỏi: I(theta) = a² * P · (1-P)..
terms.benchmarks: Psychometric evaluation standards: (1) High information: Peak I_i(theta) >= 0.50 (driven by discrimination a_i >= 1.4); (2) Maximum information location: Peaks exactly at theta = b_i (item difficulty); (3) Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT): Algorithms select the next administered item to maximize IIF at the test-taker's current ability estimate hat{theta}.
terms.operational_mechanism: In a 2-Parameter Logistic (2PL) IRT model, the Item Information Function is mathematically defined as: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * Q_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * (1 - P_i(theta)), where a_i is the item discrimination parameter and P_i(theta) is the probability of a correct response. In the 3-Parameter Logistic (3PL) model accounting for guessing c_i: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * [ (P_i(theta) - c_i)^2 / (1 - c_i)^2 ] * [ Q_i(theta) / P_i(theta) ]. Summing IIFs across all test items yields the Test Information Function: TIF(theta) = sum_{i=1}^n I_i(theta), where the standard error of measurement is directly related as: SE(theta) = 1 / sqrt(TIF(theta)).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: In a 2-Parameter Logistic (2PL) IRT model, the Item Information Function is mathematically defined as: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * Q_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * (1 - P_i(theta)), where a_i is the item discrimination parameter and P_i(theta) is the probability of a correct response. In the 3-Parameter Logistic (3PL) model accounting for guessing c_i: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * [ (P_i(theta) - c_i)^2 / (1 - c_i)^2 ] * [ Q_i(theta) / P_i(theta) ]. Summing IIFs across all test items yields the Test Information Function: TIF(theta) = sum_{i=1}^n I_i(theta), where the standard error of measurement is directly related as: SE(theta) = 1 / sqrt(TIF(theta)).
terms.pitfalls: Common psychometric errors: (1) Assuming an item provides equal precision across all ability levels; (2) Retaining items with flat or near-zero IIF curves across the target trait range (indicative of low discrimination a_i < 0.50); and (3) Confusing IIF with the Item Characteristic Curve (ICC)—ICC displays probability, whereas IIF displays Fisher information / statistical precision.
terms.apa_reference: Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee's ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick (Eds.), Statistical theories of mental test scores (pp. 397–479). Addison-Wesley.

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định nghiệm đơn vị dữ liệu bảng Im-Pesaran-Shin
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định Im-Pesaran-Shin (IPS - Im, Pesaran, & Shin, 2003) là phép kiểm định nghiệm đơn vị trên dữ liệu bảng thuộc thế hệ thứ nhất, cho phép tính không đồng nhất (heterogeneity) trong hệ số tự hồi quy giữa các thực thể cá thể. Đây là cải tiến vượt bậc so với kiểm định Levin-Lin-Chu (LLC) vốn giả định cứng nhắc rằng tất cả các cá thể đều có cùng một hệ số nghiệm đơn vị.
terms.seminal_citation: Im, Pesaran, & Shin (2003)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Im-Pesaran-Shin Panel Unit Root Test (IPS) according to Im, Pesaran & Shin (2003).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Chạy hồi quy Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) riêng biệt cho từng thực thể i: Delta y_it = α_i + β_i · y_{i,t-1} + ∑ [γ_ij · Delta y_{i,t-j}] + e_it. 2. Trích xuất thống kê t-bar là trung bình cộng của các giá trị t-statistic cá thể t_i: t_bar = (1/N) · sum_i t_i. 3. Chuẩn hóa thống kê t_bar thành thống kê W_tbar tuân theo phân phối chuẩn tắc N(0, 1) khi N và T tiến ra vô cùng.
terms.benchmarks: Giả thuyết H0: Tất cả các chuỗi cá thể đều có nghiệm đơn vị (H0: β_i = 0 với mọi i). Giả thuyết H1: Tồn tại một tỷ lệ cá thể có chuỗi dừng (β_i < 0 với ít nhất một số i). Nếu p-value < 0.05: Bác bỏ H0, kết luận chuỗi dữ liệu bảng có tính dừng.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: IPS là kiểm định thế hệ 1, giả định tính độc lập chéo giữa các thực thể (cross-sectional independence). Nếu dữ liệu bảng có hiện tượng phụ thuộc chéo (cross-sectional dependence do cú sốc toàn cầu hoặc tương tác kinh tế), kiểm định IPS sẽ bị phóng đại sai lầm loại I (phát hiện dừng giả tạo); khi đó bắt buộc phải chuyển sang kiểm định thế hệ thứ hai CIPS của Pesaran (2007).
terms.apa_reference: Im, K. S., Pesaran, M. H., & Shin, Y. (2003). Testing for unit roots in heterogeneous panels. Journal of Econometrics, 115(1), 53–74. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(03)00092-7

terms.vietnamese: Thiên lệch thời gian bất tử
vietnamese_variants: Thiên lệch thời gian sống bất tử
Immortal Time Bias in Cohort Studies
terms.core_definition: Thiên lệch thời gian bất tử (Immortal Time Bias - Suissa, 2007, 2008) là dạng thiên lệch kinh tế lượng dọc nguy hiểm xảy ra trong các nghiên cứu đoàn hệ (cohort studies) và phân tích sống sót. Thiên lệch xuất hiện khi khoảng thời gian từ khi đối tượng bắt đầu được theo dõi đến khi họ thực sự tiếp nhận can thiệp/điều trị (khoảng thời gian 'bất tử' vì đối tượng bắt buộc phải sống sót thì mới tiếp nhận được can thiệp) bị phân loại sai vào nhóm được can thiệp, dẫn đến việc phóng đại nhân tạo lợi ích sống sót hoặc làm sai lệch tỷ số rủi ro (Hazard Ratio).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Immortal Time Bias according to Suissa (2008).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Khoảng thời gian bất tử (T_0 đến T_1): Giai đoạn cá thể đã vào nghiên cứu nhưng chưa dùng thuốc. Trong giai đoạn này, theo định nghĩa, biến cố tử vong không thể xảy ra đối với nhóm can thiệp (vì nếu chết thì họ đã không đủ điều kiện vào nhóm can thiệp). 2. Nếu gán toàn bộ thời gian theo dõi từ T_0 vào nhóm can thiệp, tỷ lệ biến cố trên một đơn vị thời gian của nhóm can thiệp sẽ bị pha loãng giảm xuống giả tạo. 3. Hiệu chỉnh chuẩn mực: Sử dụng Mô hình hồi quy Cox với Biến số can thiệp thay đổi theo thời gian (Time-varying covariate Cox model) hoặc Thiết kế thử nghiệm mục tiêu mô phỏng (Target Trial Emulation).
terms.benchmarks: Là tiêu chuẩn kiểm định nghiêm ngặt trên các tạp chí y học và kinh tế y tế hàng đầu (NEJM, Lancet, BMJ). Tỷ số rủi ro HR bị thiên lệch thường tạo cảm giác can thiệp có tác dụng bảo vệ thần kỳ (HR < 0.70 giả tạo) trong khi thực chất can thiệp có thể không có tác dụng hoặc thậm chí gây hại.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Phân loại đối tượng vào nhóm can thiệp dựa trên hành vi trong tương lai của họ (Future-looking classification). Mọi thiết kế nghiên cứu đoàn hệ bắt buộc phải xử lý thời gian tiếp nhận can thiệp bằng time-dependent covariates để triệt tiêu thời gian bất tử.
terms.apa_reference: Suissa, S. (2008). Immortal time bias in pharmacoepidemiology. American Journal of Epidemiology, 167(4), 492–499. https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwm324

terms.vietnamese: Nguồn lực kém tính linh động (Trong lý thuyết dựa trên nguồn lực)
vietnamese_variants: Tài nguyên bất động một phần
terms.core_definition: Imperfectly Mobile Resources is one of the two foundational structural assumptions—alongside resource heterogeneity—underpinning the Resource-Based View (RBV) of the firm, articulated by Jay Barney (1991) and Margaret Peteraf (1993). It stipulates that strategic, rent-yielding assets, capabilities, human capital, and routines cannot be easily, rapidly, or costlessly bought, sold, or transferred across competing firms in factor markets. Because valuable resources are socially complex, path-dependent, or relationally co-specialized, their immobility prevents rivals from bidding them away or copying them instantly, securing sustained competitive advantage.
terms.seminal_citation: Peteraf, M. A. (1993). The cornerstones of competitive advantage: A resource-based view. Strategic Management Journal, 14(3), 179-191.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Imperfectly mobile resources according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Resource immobility stems from four distinct structural isolation mechanisms: (1) Asset co-specialization: The resource has substantially higher value within the specific firm's idiosyncratic network of assets than in alternative employment; (2) Path dependency: Resources developed over decades through unique historical trajectories (Dierickx & Cool, 1989 time compression diseconomies); (3) Causal ambiguity: Neither rivals nor internal managers fully comprehend the precise link between capabilities and sustained performance; and (4) Social complexity: Tacit organizational culture and relational trust networks.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Resource immobility stems from four distinct structural isolation mechanisms: (1) Asset co-specialization: The resource has substantially higher value within the specific firm's idiosyncratic network of assets than in alternative employment; (2) Path dependency: Resources developed over decades through unique historical trajectories (Dierickx & Cool, 1989 time compression diseconomies); (3) Causal ambiguity: Neither rivals nor internal managers fully comprehend the precise link between capabilities and sustained performance; and (4) Social complexity: Tacit organizational culture and relational trust networks.
terms.benchmarks: Strategic assessment benchmarks (Barney's VRIO framework): (1) Inimitability and Non-substitutability tests confirming that factor market trade cannot duplicate the resource; (2) Wage premium tests: Demonstrating that key employees earn economic rents shared with the firm rather than extracting 100% of the rent via labor market mobility; (3) Qualitative process tracing documenting firm-specific organizational integration.
terms.pitfalls: Common research misapplications: (1) Treating generic, commodity assets (e.g., standard enterprise software, leased office buildings) as imperfectly mobile resources; (2) Overlooking resource mobility triggers—ignoring how corporate poaching, employee spin-offs, or open-source disruptions can rapidly commoditize previously immobile assets; and (3) Assuming resource immobility guarantees value without demonstrating market relevance (Value in VRIO).
terms.apa_reference: Peteraf, M. A. (1993). The cornerstones of competitive advantage: A resource-based view. Strategic Management Journal, 14(3), 179–191. https://doi.org/10.1002/smj.4250140303

terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp luận khoa học triển khai
vietnamese_variants: Khoa học thực thi nghiên cứu
Phương pháp nghiên cứu ứng dụng thực tiễn
terms.core_definition: Implementation Science Methodology is a rigorous, multidisciplinary scientific framework dedicated to the systematic study of methods and strategies that promote the systematic uptake of evidence-based interventions, clinical practices, and management policies into routine organizational and community practice (Eccles & Mittman, 2006). Designed to bridge the notorious '17-year research-to-practice pipeline gap', implementation science focuses not on testing whether an intervention works (clinical efficacy), but on understanding the contextual mechanisms, organizational barriers, and implementation strategies that determine how well it is adopted, implemented, and sustained in real-world settings.
terms.seminal_citation: Proctor, E., Silmere, H., Raghavan, R., Hovmand, P., Aarons, G., Bunger, A., Griffey, R., & Hensley, M. (2011). Outcomes for implementation research: Conceptual distinctions, measurement challenges, and research agenda. Administration and Policy in Mental Health and Mental Health Services Research, 38(2), 65-76.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Implementation Science Methodology according to Eccles & Mittman (2006).
terms.operational_mechanism: Implementation research operates through three foundational pillars: (1) Determinant Frameworks: Assessing multi-level organizational barriers and facilitators (e.g., CFIR - Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research: Outer Setting, Inner Setting, Characteristics of Individuals, Innovation Characteristics, and Implementation Process); (2) Implementation Strategies: Explicitly specifying discrete actions (e.g., ERIC taxonomy: training, champion recruitment, audit and feedback); (3) Implementation Outcomes: Evaluating Proctor et al. (2011) distinct outcomes: Acceptability, Adoption, Appropriateness, Costs, Feasibility, Fidelity, Penetration, and Sustainability; (4) Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation Trial Designs (Types 1, 2, and 3).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Implementation research operates through three foundational pillars: (1) Determinant Frameworks: Assessing multi-level organizational barriers and facilitators (e.g., CFIR - Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research: Outer Setting, Inner Setting, Characteristics of Individuals, Innovation Characteristics, and Implementation Process); (2) Implementation Strategies: Explicitly specifying discrete actions (e.g., ERIC taxonomy: training, champion recruitment, audit and feedback); (3) Implementation Outcomes: Evaluating Proctor et al. (2011) distinct outcomes: Acceptability, Adoption, Appropriateness, Costs, Feasibility, Fidelity, Penetration, and Sustainability; (4) Hybrid Effectiveness-Implementation Trial Designs (Types 1, 2, and 3).
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards: (1) Complete specification of implementation strategies following StaRI (Standards for Reporting Implementation Studies) guidelines; (2) Clear separation between intervention outcomes (e.g., patient health, sales revenue) and implementation outcomes (e.g., staff adoption rate, fidelity); (3) Use of validated measurement scales (e.g., AIM - Acceptability of Intervention Measure, IAM - Intervention Appropriateness Measure, FIM - Feasibility of Intervention Measure).
terms.pitfalls: Common research flaws: (1) The 'type 3 error'—concluding an intervention failed when it was actually never implemented with adequate fidelity; (2) Describing implementation strategies in vague terms without specifying the actor, action, target, temporality, dose, and theoretical justification; and (3) Treating implementation context as static rather than dynamically evolving during roll-out.
terms.apa_reference: Proctor, E., Silmere, H., Raghavan, R., Hovmand, P., Aarons, G., Bunger, A., Griffey, R., & Hensley, M. (2011). Outcomes for implementation research: Conceptual distinctions, measurement challenges, and research agenda. Administration and Policy in Mental Health and Mental Health Services Research, 38(2), 65–76. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10488-010-0319-7

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích biểu đồ tầm quan trọng - hiệu suất (IPMA trong PLS-SEM)
vietnamese_variants: Biểu đồ ma trận ưu tiên IPMA
terms.core_definition: Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA, also termed Importance-Performance Matrix Analysis), developed in PLS-SEM by Christian M. Ringle and Marko Sarstedt (2016) based on Martilla and James's (1977) foundational concept, is an advanced analytical procedure that extends standard structural equation modeling results by combining the total structural effects (importance) of predecessor constructs with their average rescaled latent variable scores (performance). By contrasting importance on the horizontal axis with performance on the vertical axis, IPMA identifies strategic, high-leverage priority areas for managerial intervention.
terms.seminal_citation: Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2016). Gain more insight from your PLS-SEM results: The importance-performance map analysis. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 116(9), 1865-1886.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Importance-Performance Map Analysis according to Xác định các yếu tố nằm ở góc 'Tầm quan trọng cao nhưng Hiệu quả thấp' (High importance, Low performance) là ưu tiên hành động số 1..
terms.benchmarks: Managerial interpretation rules (Ringle & Sarstedt, 2016): (1) Priority Area for Improvement (High Importance, Low Performance): The highest managerial priority where investments yield maximum marginal improvement in the target construct; (2) Maintain Performance (High Importance, High Performance); (3) Low Priority (Low Importance, Low Performance); (4) Potential Overkill (Low Importance, High Performance); (5) Prerequisites: Endogenous construct scale must have a clear metric direction; indicator coding must be positive.
terms.operational_mechanism: IPMA execution follows a rigorous three-step protocol: (1) Rescaling: Latent variable scores and manifest indicators (typically on 1-to-5 or 1-to-7 Likert scales) are rescaled linearly to a standardized 0-to-100 performance scale: Y_i^{rescaled} = [ (Y_i - min(Y)) / (max(Y) - min(Y)) ] * 100; (2) Calculating Importance: Deriving the total effect (direct path coefficient plus sum of all indirect paths) of each predecessor construct on the focal endogenous target construct; (3) Constructing the Map: Plotting total effects on the X-axis (Importance) against mean rescaled scores on the Y-axis (Performance), partitioned into four strategic quadrants by cross-hairs set at sample average importance and performance values.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: IPMA execution follows a rigorous three-step protocol: (1) Rescaling: Latent variable scores and manifest indicators (typically on 1-to-5 or 1-to-7 Likert scales) are rescaled linearly to a standardized 0-to-100 performance scale: Y_i^{rescaled} = [ (Y_i - min(Y)) / (max(Y) - min(Y)) ] * 100; (2) Calculating Importance: Deriving the total effect (direct path coefficient plus sum of all indirect paths) of each predecessor construct on the focal endogenous target construct; (3) Constructing the Map: Plotting total effects on the X-axis (Importance) against mean rescaled scores on the Y-axis (Performance), partitioned into four strategic quadrants by cross-hairs set at sample average importance and performance values.
terms.pitfalls: Common analytical errors: (1) Using direct path coefficients instead of total effects (direct effects ignore crucial indirect mediating mechanisms, distorting true importance); (2) Applying IPMA without ensuring all indicator scales are aligned in the same directional orientation (reverse-coded items must be inverted before rescaling); and (3) Conducting IPMA when the target construct R^2 is very low, rendering structural importance estimates unreliable.
terms.apa_reference: Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2016). Gain more insight from your PLS-SEM results: The importance-performance map analysis. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 116(9), 1865–1886. https://doi.org/10.1108/IMDS-10-2015-0429

terms.vietnamese: Hàm Phản ứng Đẩy (Hàm Đáp ứng Xung Lực IRF)
vietnamese_variants: Đáp ứng cú sốc hệ thống VAR
terms.core_definition: Kỹ thuật mô phỏng động lực cốt lõi trong phân tích VAR/VECM do Sims (1980) sáng tạo. IRF theo dõi quỹ đạo phản ứng theo thời gian (Time path) của từng biến nội sinh trong hệ thống trước một cú sốc bất ngờ có độ lớn bằng một độ lệch chuẩn (One-standard-deviation innovation shock) đánh vào một biến số cụ thể, trong điều kiện giả định các cú sốc khác giữ nguyên. IRF giúp giải mã bức tranh trực quan về độ lớn, thời gian trễ và độ kéo dài của tác động chính sách kinh tế.
terms.seminal_citation: Sims, C. A. (1980). Macroeconomics and reality. Econometrica, 48(1), 1–48; Lütkepohl, H. (2005). New introduction to multiple time series analysis. Springer.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Impulse Response Function (IRF) according to Lütkepohl (2005).
terms.benchmarks: Bắt buộc báo cáo dải khoảng tin cậy Bootstrap 95% (Confidence Bands / Error Bands) bao quanh đường phản ứng trung tâm: Nếu dải tin cậy 95% không chứa đường trục 0, phản ứng của hệ thống đạt ý nghĩa thống kê tại thời kỳ đó. Lựa chọn kỹ thuật trực giao hóa cú sốc: Phân rã Cholesky (yêu cầu sắp xếp thứ tự biến từ ngoại sinh nhất đến nội sinh nhất) hoặc Structural VAR (SVAR) dựa trên các ràng buộc kinh tế ngắn hạn và dài hạn (Blanchard & Quah, 1989).
terms.pitfalls: Sắp xếp thứ tự biến tùy tiện trong phân rã Cholesky khi ma trận hiệp phương sai của phần dư có tương quan cao, dẫn đến đồ thị phản ứng bị biến đổi hoàn toàn khi đảo thứ tự biến; chỉ báo cáo đường trung bình mà không hiển thị dải khoảng tin cậy bootstrap.
terms.apa_reference: Sims, C. A. (1980). Macroeconomics and reality. Econometrica, 48(1), 1–48.

terms.vietnamese: Mã hóa In-Vivo / Mã hóa sử dụng nguyên văn ngôn từ đối tượng
vietnamese_variants: Mã hóa ngôn ngữ tự nhiên
terms.core_definition: In-Vivo Coding (mã hóa nguyên văn thực địa, bắt nguồn từ thuật ngữ tiếng Latin 'in vivo' - trong cơ thể sống) là một phương pháp mã hóa định tính chu kỳ một (First Cycle coding) mang tính nhân văn sâu sắc, trong đó nhãn mã (code) được trích xuất nguyên văn từng từ hoặc cụm từ ngắn từ chính lời ăn tiếng nói, tiếng lóng, ẩn dụ hoặc thuật ngữ đặc thù của người tham gia nghiên cứu (Saldaña, 2021; Charmaz, 2014). Phương pháp này ưu tiên tối thượng việc bảo tồn tiếng nói nguyên bản, hệ tư tưởng và thế giới quan của đối tượng nghiên cứu.
terms.seminal_citation: Saldaña, J. (2021). The Coding Manual for Qualitative Researchers (4th ed.). SAGE Publications; Charmaz, K. (2014). Constructing Grounded Theory (2nd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of In-Vivo Coding according to Saldaña (2021).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quy trình thực hiện: (1) Đọc kỹ lưỡng bản gỡ băng phỏng vấn hoặc ghi chép thực địa; (2) Khoanh vùng các từ ngữ đặc sắc, giàu hình ảnh, chứa đựng cảm xúc mạnh mẽ hoặc mang tính thuật ngữ nội bộ (indigenous terms / insider jargon) mà đối tượng tự sử dụng để mô tả thế giới của họ; (3) Đặt từ ngữ đó trong dấu ngoặc kép để làm tên mã chính thức (ví dụ: 'sống sót qua ngày', 'cháy sạch năng lượng', 'cắn răng chịu trận'); (4) Sử dụng các mã In-Vivo này làm hạt giống để kích hoạt phân tích lý thuyết ở các chu kỳ sau.
benchmarks: Đặt trong dấu ngoặc kép minh bạch: Tất cả các mã In-Vivo phải được định dạng chuẩn mực trong ngoặc kép để phân biệt với mã do nghiên cứu viên tự đặt.
Ưu tiên cho các nhóm đối tượng đặc thù: Cực kỳ phù hợp cho nghiên cứu về trẻ em, thanh thiếu niên, các tiểu văn hóa ngầm, cộng đồng yếm thế hoặc các nhóm nghề nghiệp có tiếng lóng chuyên biệt.
Cầu nối sang khái niệm lý thuyết: Các mã In-Vivo ở chu kỳ 1 phải được nâng cấp và liên kết với các phạm trù phân tích trừu tượng hơn ở chu kỳ 2.
pitfalls: Lạm dụng biến mã thành câu trích dẫn dài: Cắt nguyên cả một câu văn dài phức tạp làm mã thay vì chắt lọc 1-3 từ khóa đắt giá nhất.
Dừng lại ở bề mặt ngôn từ mà không khái niệm hóa: Để nguyên hàng trăm mã In-Vivo rời rạc mà không phân tích ý nghĩa ẩn dụ và cấu trúc lý thuyết đằng sau ngôn từ đó.
Bắt chước ngôn ngữ đối tượng một cách kệch cỡm: Sử dụng mã In-Vivo sai ngữ cảnh văn hóa khiến phân tích trở nên phản cảm hoặc thiếu tôn trọng người tham gia.
terms.apa_reference: Saldaña, J. (2021). The coding manual for qualitative researchers (4th ed.). SAGE Publications, Inc.

terms.vietnamese: Tỷ lệ mới mắc và tỷ lệ hiện mắc
vietnamese_variants: Tần suất mới phát và hiện có
Incidence và prevalence trong dịch tễ học
Tỷ số phát sinh và tỷ lệ lưu hành
terms.core_definition: Incidence vs. Prevalence represents the fundamental conceptual and mathematical distinction in epidemiology, biostatistics, and health economics regarding the measurement of disease occurrence. Incidence quantifies the rate of occurrence of new cases of a disease or condition arising within a specified population at risk over a defined period (measuring disease risk and speed of onset). In contrast, Prevalence quantifies the proportion of a population that has the disease or condition at a specific point in time or over a period, encompassing both newly diagnosed and pre-existing surviving cases (measuring total disease burden).
terms.seminal_citation: Rothman, K. J., Greenland, S., & Lash, T. L. (2008). Modern epidemiology (3rd ed.). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Incidence vs. Prevalence according to Rothman, Greenland & Lash (2008).
terms.operational_mechanism: Mathematical formulation and dynamics: (1) Cumulative Incidence: CI = (Number of new cases during period) / (Number of disease-free individuals at risk at start of period); (2) Incidence Rate (Incidence Density): IR = (Number of new cases) / (Total person-time of observation); (3) Point Prevalence: P = (Total existing cases at time t) / (Total population at time t); (4) Steady-State Relationship: In a stable population with low incidence and constant duration, Prevalence approximates the product of Incidence Rate and average disease duration D: P approx IR * D. Treatments that prolong survival without curing increase prevalence despite unchanged incidence.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Mathematical formulation and dynamics: (1) Cumulative Incidence: CI = (Number of new cases during period) / (Number of disease-free individuals at risk at start of period); (2) Incidence Rate (Incidence Density): IR = (Number of new cases) / (Total person-time of observation); (3) Point Prevalence: P = (Total existing cases at time t) / (Total population at time t); (4) Steady-State Relationship: In a stable population with low incidence and constant duration, Prevalence approximates the product of Incidence Rate and average disease duration D: P approx IR * D. Treatments that prolong survival without curing increase prevalence despite unchanged incidence.
terms.benchmarks: Epidemiological application rules: (1) Cohort studies and randomized controlled trials directly measure Incidence (and Relative Risk / Incidence Rate Ratio); (2) Cross-sectional surveys and census studies measure Prevalence (and Prevalence Odds Ratio); (3) Case-control studies cannot directly calculate incidence or prevalence, estimating the Odds Ratio (OR) as a proxy for the Relative Risk under the rare disease assumption (prevalence < 5% to 10%).
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Confusing prevalence with incidence in cross-sectional studies, incorrectly inferring risk factors or causal etiology from prevalent surviving cases (Neyman's bias / incidence-prevalence bias); (2) Including individuals who already have the disease in the denominator when calculating incidence; and (3) Interpreting an increase in prevalence as a failure of healthcare, when it may actually reflect improved medical survival.
terms.apa_reference: Rothman, K. J., Greenland, S., & Lash, T. L. (2008). Modern epidemiology (3rd ed.). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins.

terms.vietnamese: Tính bất khả so sánh (Bất khả thông ước Kuhn)
vietnamese_variants: Tính bất tương thích hệ hình
Khái niệm bất khả thông ước Kuhn
terms.core_definition: Incommensurability is a revolutionary epistemological concept introduced to the philosophy of science independently by Thomas S. Kuhn (1962) in 'The Structure of Scientific Revolutions' and Paul Feyerabend. Borrowed from Greek mathematics (where lines have no common unit of measurement), incommensurability asserts that competing scientific paradigms cannot be directly compared, evaluated, or judged against an objective, neutral, paradigm-independent standard of rationality or empirical fact. Because rival paradigms embody distinct ontological worldviews, conceptual vocabularies, and standards of evidence, proponents of different paradigms 'practice their trade in different worlds.'
terms.seminal_citation: Kuhn, T. S. (1962). The structure of scientific revolutions. University of Chicago Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Incommensurability according to Kuhn (1962).
terms.operational_mechanism: Kuhn articulated incommensurability across three interconnected levels: (1) Semantic Incommensurability (Taxonomic Incommensurability): Meaning change across conceptual networks (e.g., 'mass' in Newtonian mechanics is invariant, whereas in relativistic Einsteinian physics it varies with velocity); (2) Observational Incommensurability (Theory-Ladenness of Observation): Scientists viewing the same empirical data through different paradigms perceive different visual-conceptual realities (Gestalt switch); (3) Methodological Incommensurability (Kuhn-Loss): Competing paradigms disagree on what constitutes a legitimate problem, acceptable evidence, and scientific explanation.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Kuhn articulated incommensurability across three interconnected levels: (1) Semantic Incommensurability (Taxonomic Incommensurability): Meaning change across conceptual networks (e.g., 'mass' in Newtonian mechanics is invariant, whereas in relativistic Einsteinian physics it varies with velocity); (2) Observational Incommensurability (Theory-Ladenness of Observation): Scientists viewing the same empirical data through different paradigms perceive different visual-conceptual realities (Gestalt switch); (3) Methodological Incommensurability (Kuhn-Loss): Competing paradigms disagree on what constitutes a legitimate problem, acceptable evidence, and scientific explanation.
terms.benchmarks: Epistemic appraisal criteria: (1) Incommensurability does not mean incomparability—Kuhn emphasized that paradigms can be compared via shared meta-theoretical values (accuracy, consistency, scope, simplicity, fruitfulness), though scientists weigh these values differently; (2) Translation failure: Scientific revolutions involve untranslatable semantic shifts rather than cumulative preservation.
terms.pitfalls: Common philosophical distortions: (1) Equating incommensurability with radical relativism or irrationalism (Kuhn explicitly rejected irrationalism, arguing paradigm debate is rational persuasion, not coercive proof); (2) Applying incommensurability indiscriminately to everyday incremental differences between theories within normal science; and (3) Assuming rival scientists cannot communicate at all (communication is possible via bilingual translation).
terms.apa_reference: Kuhn, T. S. (1962). The structure of scientific revolutions. University of Chicago Press.

terms.vietnamese: Sự bất khả quy chiếu giữa các hệ hình nghiên cứu
vietnamese_variants: Tính bất khả thông ước giữa các paradigm
Sự bất tương thích hệ hình phương pháp luận
terms.core_definition: Incommensurability of Paradigms refers to the thesis within social sciences and research methodology (Burrell & Morgan, 1979; Guba & Lincoln, 1994) asserting that alternative philosophical research paradigms—namely Positivism, Post-Positivism, Constructivism/Interpretivism, and Critical Theory—are fundamentally incompatible and mutually exclusive. Because each paradigm is founded on contradictory ontological assumptions (e.g., objective singular reality vs. multiple subjective constructed realities) and epistemological stances (dualist detachment vs. transactional co-creation), purists argue they cannot be logically synthesized or combined within a single research design.
terms.seminal_citation: Guba, E. G., & Lincoln, Y. S. (1994). Competing paradigms in qualitative research. In N. K. Denzin & Y. S. Lincoln (Eds.), Handbook of qualitative research (pp. 105-117). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Incommensurability of Paradigms according to Kuhn (1962).
terms.operational_mechanism: The paradigm debate operates along four core metatheoretical dimensions (Guba & Lincoln): (1) Ontology: What is the nature of reality? (Realism vs. Relativism); (2) Epistemology: What is the relationship between the knower and what can be known? (Objectivist vs. Subjectivist); (3) Methodology: How does the researcher discover knowledge? (Experimental/Deductive vs. Hermeneutic/Dialectical); and (4) Axiology: What is the role of values? (Value-free vs. Value-bound). In mixed methods research, the 'incompatibility thesis' argues paradigms cannot mix, whereas 'dialectical pluralism' and 'pragmatism' (Teddlie & Tashakkori; Creswell) resolve this tension by prioritizing research questions over metaphysical purism.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The paradigm debate operates along four core metatheoretical dimensions (Guba & Lincoln): (1) Ontology: What is the nature of reality? (Realism vs. Relativism); (2) Epistemology: What is the relationship between the knower and what can be known? (Objectivist vs. Subjectivist); (3) Methodology: How does the researcher discover knowledge? (Experimental/Deductive vs. Hermeneutic/Dialectical); and (4) Axiology: What is the role of values? (Value-free vs. Value-bound). In mixed methods research, the 'incompatibility thesis' argues paradigms cannot mix, whereas 'dialectical pluralism' and 'pragmatism' (Teddlie & Tashakkori; Creswell) resolve this tension by prioritizing research questions over metaphysical purism.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological positioning in doctoral proposals: (1) Philosophical transparency: Chapter 1/3 must explicitly declare the study's paradigm stance; (2) Dialectical justification: If mixing qualitative and quantitative paradigms, researchers must justify their epistemological bridge (e.g., Pragmatism, Critical Realism); (3) Consistent alignment between ontology, epistemology, and method.
terms.pitfalls: Common research flaws: (1) Epistemological schizophrenia—claiming a radical constructivist ontology while employing rigid positivist confirmatory factor analysis without theoretical reconciliation; (2) Using pragmatism as an uncritical excuse for sloppy, unprincipled mixing of methods; and (3) Ignoring paradigm tensions in mixed methods joint displays.
terms.apa_reference: Guba, E. G., & Lincoln, Y. S. (1994). Competing paradigms in qualitative research. In N. K. Denzin & Y. S. Lincoln (Eds.), Handbook of qualitative research (pp. 105–117). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Luận đề bất khả thông ước
vietnamese_variants: Luận điểm bất khả so sánh
Giả thuyết bất tương thích lý thuyết
terms.core_definition: The Incommensurability Thesis is the formal philosophical proposition, central to the post-positivist turn in philosophy of science (Paul Feyerabend, 1962; Thomas Kuhn, 1962), asserting that successive or rival comprehensive scientific theories lack a common measure of meaning and evaluation. Grounded in semantic holism (the thesis that the meaning of a scientific term is determined by its relationships within the entire theoretical network), the thesis rejects the cumulative model of science, demonstrating that theoretical transition involves meaning variance (radical semantic displacement) rather than cumulative preservation.
terms.seminal_citation: Feyerabend, P. K. (1962). Explanation, reduction, and empiricism. In H. Feigl & G. Maxwell (Eds.), Scientific explanation, space, and time (pp. 28-97). University of Minnesota Press.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Incommensurability thesis according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: The thesis operates across three primary arguments: (1) Radical Meaning Shift: When moving from Theory T1 to T2, the core terms undergo radical reconceptualization such that assertions in T1 cannot be cleanly stated in T2's language; (2) Rejection of Neutral Observation Language: There is no theory-neutral observation language capable of adjudicating between T1 and T2; (3) Rational Underdetermination: Empirical evidence alone is insufficient to logically compel the adoption of one theory over another without invoking non-algorithmic epistemic values.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The thesis operates across three primary arguments: (1) Radical Meaning Shift: When moving from Theory T1 to T2, the core terms undergo radical reconceptualization such that assertions in T1 cannot be cleanly stated in T2's language; (2) Rejection of Neutral Observation Language: There is no theory-neutral observation language capable of adjudicating between T1 and T2; (3) Rational Underdetermination: Empirical evidence alone is insufficient to logically compel the adoption of one theory over another without invoking non-algorithmic epistemic values.
terms.benchmarks: Philosophical evaluation criteria: (1) Local vs. Global Incommensurability: Modern philosophy of science (Kuhn's later works, 1983) restricts incommensurability to 'local incommensurability' (taxonomic untranslatability among a small cluster of interdefined terms), refuting radical global cognitive disconnect; (2) Translation hermeneutics: Demonstrating how scientific communities overcome semantic barriers through historical re-learning.
terms.pitfalls: Common philosophical pitfalls: (1) Caricaturing the thesis as claiming rival scientists speak gibberish to one another; (2) Conflating incommensurability with incomparability; and (3) Assuming that because theories are incommensurable, scientific progress is impossible (progress occurs in problem-solving efficacy).
terms.apa_reference: Feyerabend, P. K. (1962). Explanation, reduction, and empiricism. In H. Feigl & G. Maxwell (Eds.), Scientific explanation, space, and time (pp. 28–97). University of Minnesota Press.

terms.vietnamese: Tỷ số chi phí - hiệu quả gia tăng (ICER)
vietnamese_variants: Tỷ suất chi phí hiệu quả tăng thêm
terms.core_definition: The Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) is the standard quantitative summary metric in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, and public policy used to evaluate the economic value of a new health intervention compared to an existing standard of care. Representing the additional economic cost per unit of health benefit gained, ICER provides a mathematical decision rule for resource allocation, assessing whether a novel clinical treatment or public health policy represents an efficient use of scarce budgetary resources.
terms.seminal_citation: Drummond, M. F., Sculpher, M. J., Claxton, K., Stoddart, G. L., & Torrance, G. W. (2015). Methods for the economic evaluation of health care programmes (4th ed.). Oxford University Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratio (ICER) according to Drummond et al. (2015).
