terms.benchmarks: Koo and Li (2016) clinical and psychometric benchmarks: (1) ICC < 0.50: Poor reliability; (2) 0.50 <= ICC < 0.75: Moderate reliability; (3) 0.75 <= ICC < 0.90: Good reliability; (4) ICC >= 0.90: Excellent reliability; (5) Multilevel Modeling benchmark: ICC >= 0.05 confirms non-ignorable clustering, requiring HLM or cluster-robust standard errors.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Reporting 'the ICC' without explicitly specifying the exact model type (e.g., ICC(2,1) vs. ICC(3,k)), which prevents replication; (2) Using a consistency model when absolute agreement is required for clinical decision cutoffs; and (3) Applying Pearson's r instead of ICC for test-retest reliability (Pearson ignores systematic mean differences between test occasions).
terms.apa_reference: Shrout, P. E., & Fleiss, J. L. (1979). Intraclass correlations: Uses in assessing rater reliability. Psychological Bulletin, 86(2), 420–428. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.86.2.420

terms.vietnamese: Tỷ số Mills nghịch đảo (Hệ số Lambda Heckman)
vietnamese_variants: Hệ số điều chỉnh thiên lệch chọn mẫu Heckman
terms.core_definition: The Inverse Mills Ratio (IMR, denoted lambda), formulated by Nobel laureate James Heckman (1979) in his landmark Two-Step Selection Correction framework, is an econometric correction term used to eliminate sample selection bias in non-randomly selected observational samples (e.g., wage offers observed only for employed individuals, export performance observed only for firms that choose to export). Derived from the hazard function of the standard normal distribution, the IMR represents the expected value of the truncated error term conditional on an observation being selected into the sample.
terms.seminal_citation: Heckman, J. J. (1979). Sample selection bias as a specification error. Econometrica, 47(1), 153-161.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Inverse Mills Ratio (Lambda) according to Heckman (1979).
terms.operational_mechanism: Heckman's Two-Step Procedure: (1) First-Stage Probit Selection Model: Estimate a binary probit regression predicting sample selection probability: Pr(s_i = 1 | Z_i) = Phi(Z_i' * gamma), where Z_i includes all explanatory variables plus at least one valid Exclusion Restriction (an instrument affecting selection but not the outcome); (2) Computing IMR: For each selected observation (s_i = 1), compute lambda_i = phi(Z_i' * hat{gamma}) / Phi(Z_i' * hat{gamma}), where phi is the standard normal PDF and Phi is the CDF; (3) Second-Stage OLS Outcome Model: Regress outcome Y_i on regressors X_i and the computed lambda_i: Y_i = X_i' * beta + beta_lambda * lambda_i + e_i; (4) Hypothesis test: If beta_lambda = rho * sigma_e is statistically significant (p < 0.05), sample selection bias is present, and its inclusion purges the selection bias from beta.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Heckman's Two-Step Procedure: (1) First-Stage Probit Selection Model: Estimate a binary probit regression predicting sample selection probability: Pr(s_i = 1 | Z_i) = Phi(Z_i' * gamma), where Z_i includes all explanatory variables plus at least one valid Exclusion Restriction (an instrument affecting selection but not the outcome); (2) Computing IMR: For each selected observation (s_i = 1), compute lambda_i = phi(Z_i' * hat{gamma}) / Phi(Z_i' * hat{gamma}), where phi is the standard normal PDF and Phi is the CDF; (3) Second-Stage OLS Outcome Model: Regress outcome Y_i on regressors X_i and the computed lambda_i: Y_i = X_i' * beta + beta_lambda * lambda_i + e_i; (4) Hypothesis test: If beta_lambda = rho * sigma_e is statistically significant (p < 0.05), sample selection bias is present, and its inclusion purges the selection bias from beta.
terms.benchmarks: Econometric standards: (1) Identification requires an Exclusion Restriction: Z must contain at least one instrumental variable that strongly predicts selection (s_i = 1) but has no direct effect on outcome Y_i; (2) Significance of lambda: beta_lambda p < 0.05 confirms selection bias and validates the Heckman correction; (3) Robust standard errors: Standard OLS standard errors in step 2 are invalid; Heckman asymptotic standard errors or bootstrapping must be reported.
terms.pitfalls: Fatal econometrics errors in top journals: (1) Estimating the Heckman model without an exclusion restriction (relying solely on non-linear functional form identification, which induces severe collinearity between lambda and X, inflating standard errors); (2) Retaining lambda when it is non-significant without checking whether collinearity masked its effect; and (3) Confusing Heckman selection with treatment effects (Heckman selection models incident outcome truncation, not binary treatment assignment).
terms.apa_reference: Heckman, J. J. (1979). Sample selection bias as a specification error. Econometrica, 47(1), 153–161. https://doi.org/10.2307/1912352

terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp gán trọng số nghịch đảo xác suất (IPW)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật gán trọng số xu hướng IPW
terms.core_definition: Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW), grounded in the Horvitz-Thompson survey sampling estimator and adapted for causal inference by Paul Rosenbaum and Donald Rubin (1983), is a semi-parametric causal estimation technique used in observational studies to remove confounding and estimate Average Treatment Effects (ATE). By weighting each participant by the inverse of their estimated probability of receiving the treatment they actually received (their propensity score), IPW creates a synthetic, pseudo-population where treatment assignment is statistically independent of observed baseline covariates.
terms.seminal_citation: Rosenbaum, P. R., & Rubin, D. B. (1983). The central role of the propensity score in observational studies for causal effects. Biometrika, 70(1), 41-55.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Inverse Probability Weighting according to Kết hợp với mô hình kết quả tạo thành 'Ước lượng Vững kép' (Doubly Robust Estimator: chỉ cần một trong hai mô hình đúng thì ước lượng nhân quả vẫn không chệch)..
terms.benchmarks: Covariate balance benchmarks (Austin & Stuart, 2015): (1) Standardized Mean Difference (SMD) across all covariates in the weighted pseudo-population must be < 0.10 (strictly < 0.05); (2) Variance ratio of continuous covariates between 0.80 and 1.25; (3) Weight distribution inspection: Extreme weights (w_i > 20 or > 50) must be trimmed (weight trimming/truncation at 1st and 99th percentiles) or stabilized.
terms.operational_mechanism: IPW estimation proceeds in three steps: (1) Propensity Score Estimation: Fit a logistic or probit regression predicting treatment assignment T in {0, 1} from baseline covariates X, yielding e(X) = Pr(T = 1 | X); (2) Construct Weights: For Average Treatment Effect (ATE): w_i = T_i / e(X_i) + (1 - T_i) / (1 - e(X_i)); For Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT): w_i = T_i + (1 - T_i) * e(X_i) / (1 - e(X_i)); (3) Weighted Outcome Regression: Estimate a weighted linear or generalized linear regression of outcome Y on treatment T using weights w_i. Stabilized weights are used to prevent extreme variance: sw_i = T_i * Pr(T=1) / e(X_i) + (1 - T_i) * Pr(T=0) / (1 - e(X_i)).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: IPW estimation proceeds in three steps: (1) Propensity Score Estimation: Fit a logistic or probit regression predicting treatment assignment T in {0, 1} from baseline covariates X, yielding e(X) = Pr(T = 1 | X); (2) Construct Weights: For Average Treatment Effect (ATE): w_i = T_i / e(X_i) + (1 - T_i) / (1 - e(X_i)); For Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT): w_i = T_i + (1 - T_i) * e(X_i) / (1 - e(X_i)); (3) Weighted Outcome Regression: Estimate a weighted linear or generalized linear regression of outcome Y on treatment T using weights w_i. Stabilized weights are used to prevent extreme variance: sw_i = T_i * Pr(T=1) / e(X_i) + (1 - T_i) * Pr(T=0) / (1 - e(X_i)).
terms.pitfalls: Critical methodological traps: (1) Positivity violation: When certain subjects have propensity scores near 0 or 1, their inverse weights explode to infinity, destabilizing the estimator; (2) Treating IPW as fixing unmeasured confounding (IPW relies strictly on the unconfoundedness / conditional independence assumption); and (3) Using robust sandwich variance estimators or bootstrapping to account for the first-stage estimation of propensity scores.
terms.apa_reference: Rosenbaum, P. R., & Rubin, D. B. (1983). The central role of the propensity score in observational studies for causal effects. Biometrika, 70(1), 41–55. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/70.1.41

terms.vietnamese: Ước lượng nhân quả bằng trọng số nghịch đảo xác suất điều trị
vietnamese_variants: Ước lượng IPW chuẩn xác suất
Kỹ thuật IPTW trong suy diễn nhân quả
terms.core_definition: Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW Causal Estimation, also designated Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting / IPTW) is the rigorous operational implementation of propensity score weighting within epidemiological, biomedical, and econometric causal inference. By reweighting observational cohort data, IPW mimics a randomized trial by ensuring that the distribution of confounding covariates is balanced between treated and untreated groups, allowing for unconfounded estimation of risk ratios, hazard ratios, and causal treatment differences.
terms.seminal_citation: Hernán, M. A., & Robins, J. M. (2020). Causal inference: What if. Chapman & Hall/CRC.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1385
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) according to Robins et al. (2000).
terms.operational_mechanism: Implementation protocol: (1) Identification of the Confounder Set: Constructing a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to select the minimally sufficient adjustment set of non-colliders; (2) Propensity score modeling via logistic regression, generalized boosted modeling (GBM), or Super Learner; (3) Calculation of stabilized weights sw_i; (4) Covariate balance diagnostic: Generating Love plots displaying pre- and post-weighting Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs); (5) Marginal Structural Model (MSM) estimation: Fitting weighted generalized estimating equations (GEE) with robust Huber-White sandwich standard errors.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Implementation protocol: (1) Identification of the Confounder Set: Constructing a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to select the minimally sufficient adjustment set of non-colliders; (2) Propensity score modeling via logistic regression, generalized boosted modeling (GBM), or Super Learner; (3) Calculation of stabilized weights sw_i; (4) Covariate balance diagnostic: Generating Love plots displaying pre- and post-weighting Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs); (5) Marginal Structural Model (MSM) estimation: Fitting weighted generalized estimating equations (GEE) with robust Huber-White sandwich standard errors.
terms.benchmarks: Diagnostic cutoffs: (1) Post-weighting SMD < 0.10 for all baseline covariates; (2) Overlap / Positivity check: Overlapping propensity score distributions across treatment groups; (3) Doubly Robust Estimation: Combining IPW with outcome regression (AIPW - Augmented IPW) provides consistency if EITHER the propensity model OR the outcome model is correctly specified.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Failing to report the distribution of weights (mean of stabilized weights should approximate 1.0); (2) Omitting robust sandwich standard errors (standard errors will be artificially small if weight uncertainty is ignored); and (3) Weighting on post-treatment colliders or mediators, which introduces collider stratification bias.
terms.apa_reference: Hernán, M. A., & Robins, J. M. (2020). Causal inference: What if. Chapman & Hall/CRC.

terms.vietnamese: Mối quan hệ hình chữ U ngược (Hiệu ứng phi tuyến bậc hai)
terms.core_definition: An Inverted-U Shaped Relationship is a non-linear, quadratic curvilinear effect in which an independent variable (X) initially exerts a positive effect on an outcome (Y), reaches an optimal inflection turning point (zenith), and subsequently exerts a negative effect beyond that point (the 'Too-Much-of-a-Good-Thing' effect / TMGT, Pierce & Aguinis, 2013). Ubiquitous in strategic management, organizational behavior, and behavioral economics (e.g., stress and performance / Yerkes-Dodson law; executive tenure and firm innovation; employee autonomy and job satisfaction), it demonstrates that optimal outcomes occur at intermediate, balanced levels of the focal construct.
terms.seminal_citation: Lind, J. T., & Mehlum, H. (2010). With or without U? The appropriate test for a U-shaped relationship. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 72(1), 109-118.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Inverted-U Shaped Relationship according to Haans, Pieters & He (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quadratic polynomial regression equation: Y = beta_0 + beta_1 * X + beta_2 * X^2 + Controls + epsilon. For an authentic inverted-U shape: (1) beta_1 must be positive and statistically significant (beta_1 > 0, p < 0.05); (2) The quadratic coefficient beta_2 must be negative and statistically significant (beta_2 < 0, p < 0.05); (3) Inflection point calculation: The turning point is calculated by setting the first derivative to zero: dY/dX = beta_1 + 2 * beta_2 * X = 0 -> X_{inflection} = - beta_1 / (2 * beta_2); (4) Lind and Mehlum (2010) Three-Step Test: (a) beta_2 is negative; (b) The simple slope is positive and significant at low values of X (X_{min}); (c) The simple slope is negative and significant at high values of X (X_{max}).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Quadratic polynomial regression equation: Y = beta_0 + beta_1 * X + beta_2 * X^2 + Controls + epsilon. For an authentic inverted-U shape: (1) beta_1 must be positive and statistically significant (beta_1 > 0, p < 0.05); (2) The quadratic coefficient beta_2 must be negative and statistically significant (beta_2 < 0, p < 0.05); (3) Inflection point calculation: The turning point is calculated by setting the first derivative to zero: dY/dX = beta_1 + 2 * beta_2 * X = 0 -> X_{inflection} = - beta_1 / (2 * beta_2); (4) Lind and Mehlum (2010) Three-Step Test: (a) beta_2 is negative; (b) The simple slope is positive and significant at low values of X (X_{min}); (c) The simple slope is negative and significant at high values of X (X_{max}).
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards in top journals (AMJ, SMJ, JAP): (1) The inflection point X_{inflection} must lie well within the empirical range of the data [X_{min}, X_{max}] (typically within the 10th to 90th percentile), rather than outside observed boundaries; (2) Lind and Mehlum's 'utest' must reject the null hypothesis of a monotonic relationship (p < 0.05); (3) Both X and X^2 must be entered simultaneously, with continuous predictors mean-centered.
terms.pitfalls: Critical review rejection traps: (1) Concluding an inverted-U exists solely because beta_2 is negative and significant, without verifying that the inflection point lies inside the data range (often the turning point is beyond X_{max}, meaning the true relationship is merely concave deceleration, not inverted-U); (2) Omitting the linear term beta_1 * X while including X^2; and (3) Failing to test whether a cubic or spline model better fits the data.
terms.apa_reference: Lind, J. T., & Mehlum, H. (2010). With or without U? The appropriate test for a U-shaped relationship. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 72(1), 109–118. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0084.2009.00569.x

terms.vietnamese: Câu hỏi điều tra (Thứ bậc câu hỏi nghiên cứu Cooper & Schindler)
vietnamese_variants: Câu hỏi điều tra trung gian
Thứ bậc câu hỏi điều tra thực nghiệm
terms.core_definition: An Investigative Question is an intermediate operational tier within the classical Hierarchy of Research Questions formulated by Donald R. Cooper and Pamela S. Schindler (2014). Situated directly between broad high-level Research Questions and specific, granular Measurement Questions (survey questionnaire items), investigative questions delineate the specific factual, behavioral, attitudinal, or process dimensions that the researcher must empirically examine in order to satisfactorily answer the central overarching research question.
terms.seminal_citation: Cooper, D. R., & Schindler, P. S. (2014). Business research methods (12th ed.). McGraw-Hill Education.
terms.expert_notes: Rác Markdown/bảng; mảnh trích
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Investigative Question according to Schindler (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism: The hierarchy operates through five deductive levels: (1) Management/Theoretical Dilemma: The overarching organizational challenge or scholarly problem; (2) Management Question: Restating dilemma as an action-oriented query; (3) Research Question: Academic translation into a scientific inquiry; (4) Investigative Questions: Breaking the research question into specific operational sub-inquiries (e.g., 'What are the current adoption barriers?', 'How do performance expectations vary by department?'); (5) Measurement Questions: The final, precise items administered to respondents on a survey or interview guide.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The hierarchy operates through five deductive levels: (1) Management/Theoretical Dilemma: The overarching organizational challenge or scholarly problem; (2) Management Question: Restating dilemma as an action-oriented query; (3) Research Question: Academic translation into a scientific inquiry; (4) Investigative Questions: Breaking the research question into specific operational sub-inquiries (e.g., 'What are the current adoption barriers?', 'How do performance expectations vary by department?'); (5) Measurement Questions: The final, precise items administered to respondents on a survey or interview guide.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological consistency standards: (1) Exhaustiveness: The set of investigative questions must collectively cover 100% of the conceptual scope defined by the primary research question; (2) Mutual exclusivity: Minimal thematic overlap between distinct investigative questions; (3) Direct traceability: Every survey item in the measurement instrument must link back to at least one specific investigative question.
terms.pitfalls: Common research design errors: (1) Skipping the investigative question tier and jumping directly from a broad abstract research question to 50 disconnected survey items, resulting in fragmented data; (2) Confusing investigative questions with survey questions (investigative questions guide researcher thinking, while survey questions are phrased for respondent comprehension); and (3) Posing investigative questions that cannot be empirically measured.
terms.apa_reference: Cooper, D. R., & Schindler, P. S. (2014). Business research methods (12th ed.). McGraw-Hill Education.

terms.vietnamese: Tam giác đạc nhà nghiên cứu (Đa dạng hóa người nghiên cứu theo Denzin)
vietnamese_variants: Tam giác đạc người nghiên cứu
Kiểm chứng chéo đa điều tra viên
terms.core_definition: Investigator Triangulation is one of the four foundational forms of triangulation conceptualized by sociologist Norman K. Denzin (1970, 1978), alongside Data, Theory, and Methodological triangulation. It involves deploying two or more independent researchers, ethnographers, or qualitative coders to observe, collect, analyze, and interpret the exact same empirical phenomenon or dataset. By cross-comparing independent analytical interpretations, investigator triangulation minimizes individual researcher confirmation bias, idiosyncratic perceptual blind spots, and interpretive solipsism.
terms.seminal_citation: Denzin, N. K. (1978). The research act: A theoretical introduction to sociological methods (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.
terms.expert_notes: Mảnh trích; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Investigator Triangulation (Tam giác đạc Nhà nghiên cứu) according to Denzin (1978).
terms.operational_mechanism: Execution follows a structured multi-investigator protocol: (1) Independent fieldwork / analysis: Two or more researchers independently code raw transcripts or conduct field observations; (2) Blind coding comparison: Calculating formal inter-coder agreement indices (e.g., Cohen's Kappa, Krippendorff's Alpha) on a subset of data; (3) Consensus reconciliation meetings: Conducting structured dialectical debates to discuss divergent interpretations and anomalies; (4) Multi-perspective synthesis: Incorporating researchers from complementary disciplinary backgrounds (e.g., an economist paired with a qualitative sociologist) to broaden theoretical interpretation.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Execution follows a structured multi-investigator protocol: (1) Independent fieldwork / analysis: Two or more researchers independently code raw transcripts or conduct field observations; (2) Blind coding comparison: Calculating formal inter-coder agreement indices (e.g., Cohen's Kappa, Krippendorff's Alpha) on a subset of data; (3) Consensus reconciliation meetings: Conducting structured dialectical debates to discuss divergent interpretations and anomalies; (4) Multi-perspective synthesis: Incorporating researchers from complementary disciplinary backgrounds (e.g., an economist paired with a qualitative sociologist) to broaden theoretical interpretation.
terms.benchmarks: Credibility benchmarks: (1) Detailed documentation in method sections specifying the number of coders, their academic backgrounds, and independent coding procedures; (2) Explicit audit trail of negotiated coding consensus; (3) Transparent reporting of initial inter-coder discrepancies and how theoretical differences were resolved.
terms.pitfalls: Common research weaknesses: (1) Superficial tokenism—having a second researcher glance at a codebook for 10 minutes and claiming 'investigator triangulation'; (2) Groupthink—junior researchers merely deferring uncritically to the interpretation of a senior principal investigator; and (3) Assuming investigator triangulation produces absolute positivist certainty (its goal is interpretive depth and credibility, not mechanical consensus).
terms.apa_reference: Denzin, N. K. (1978). The research act: A theoretical introduction to sociological methods (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.

terms.vietnamese: Quy trình Tam giác đạc Nhà nghiên cứu (Mã hóa Độc lập Nhiều Người)
vietnamese_variants: Tam giác đạc nhà nghiên cứu
domain_tags: Mã hóa & Phân tích Dữ liệu
terms.core_definition: Hình thức tam giác đạc sử dụng từ hai nhà nghiên cứu trở lên tham gia độc lập vào cùng một quá trình thu thập, quan sát hoặc mã hóa phân tích dữ liệu (Denzin 1978). Mục tiêu cốt tử là triệt tiêu thiên kiến nhận thức cá nhân (Individual cognitive bias) của một tác giả đơn lẻ, đảm bảo các chủ đề và mô hình khái niệm không bị chi phối bởi lăng kính chủ quan của một người duy nhất.
terms.seminal_citation: Denzin, N. K. (1978). The research act: A theoretical introduction to sociological methods (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill; Armstrong, D., Gosling, A., Weinman, J., & Marteau, T. (1997). The place of inter-rater reliability in qualitative research: An empirical study. Sociology, 31(3), 597–606.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Investigator Triangulation Protocol according to Denzin (1978).
terms.benchmarks: Quy trình thực thi chuẩn: (1) Mã hóa độc lập (Independent coding): Ít nhất 2 nhà nghiên cứu mã hóa riêng rẽ trên một tập mẫu dữ liệu (thường 10–20% tổng dung lượng bản gỡ băng); (2) Đánh giá độ tin cậy đồng thuận: Tính toán chỉ số Cohen's κ hoặc Holsti Index (yêu cầu κ ≥ 0.70 hoặc % agreement ≥ 80%); (3) Tổ chức thảo luận phân giải các điểm bất đồng (Consensus meeting) để thống nhất cây mã hóa cuối cùng.
terms.pitfalls: Chỉ một người mã hóa toàn bộ dữ liệu rồi đưa cho người thứ hai đọc lướt qua ký tên đồng ý; không báo cáo chỉ số đồng thuận giữa các người mã hóa (Inter-coder agreement).
terms.apa_reference: Denzin, N. K. (1978). The research act: A theoretical introduction to sociological methods (2nd ed.). McGraw-Hill.

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích tổng hợp dữ liệu từng cá thể (IPD Meta-Analysis)
vietnamese_variants: Meta-analysis dữ liệu cấp bệnh nhân
terms.core_definition: An Individual Participant Data (IPD) Meta-Analysis is universally recognized as the gold standard of evidence synthesis in clinical medicine, epidemiology, and quantitative social science. Rather than extracting summary aggregate statistics (e.g., mean differences, odds ratios) from published journal articles, the IPD approach involves obtaining, standardizing, and pooling the original, raw individual-level participant datasets directly from the principal investigators of all eligible randomized controlled trials or observational cohorts.
terms.seminal_citation: Stewart, L. A., & Parmar, M. K. (1993). Meta-analysis of the literature or of individual patient data: Is there a difference?. The Lancet, 341(8842), 418-422.
terms.expert_notes: "loại bỏ hoàn toàn" quá mức; trùng #1284 | Nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of IPD according to Loại bỏ hoàn toàn thiên lệch sinh thái (Ecological fallacy) và cho phép phân tích tương tác điều tiết ở cấp độ cá thể chính xác 100%..
terms.operational_mechanism: IPD workflow proceeds through five stages: (1) International consortium establishment: Reaching out to trialists worldwide to share de-identified raw patient data; (2) Data cleaning and standardization: Recoding variables, checking consistency, and re-running original study analyses to verify data integrity; (3) One-Stage vs. Two-Stage Modeling: (a) Two-stage IPD: Analyze IPD in each trial separately, then pool effect estimates via standard random-effects meta-analysis; (b) One-stage IPD: Fit a single hierarchical multilevel mixed-effects model directly to the pooled individual-level database, accounting for clustering within trials; (4) Subgroup interaction testing: Directly estimating individual-level treatment-by-covariate interactions without ecological bias.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: IPD workflow proceeds through five stages: (1) International consortium establishment: Reaching out to trialists worldwide to share de-identified raw patient data; (2) Data cleaning and standardization: Recoding variables, checking consistency, and re-running original study analyses to verify data integrity; (3) One-Stage vs. Two-Stage Modeling: (a) Two-stage IPD: Analyze IPD in each trial separately, then pool effect estimates via standard random-effects meta-analysis; (b) One-stage IPD: Fit a single hierarchical multilevel mixed-effects model directly to the pooled individual-level database, accounting for clustering within trials; (4) Subgroup interaction testing: Directly estimating individual-level treatment-by-covariate interactions without ecological bias.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards (PRISMA-IPD guidelines): (1) Retrieval rate: Securing raw data for >= 80% to 90% of all identified eligible trial participants; (2) Ability to analyze time-to-event outcomes with exact Cox proportional hazards and survival curves; (3) Complete elimination of outcome reporting bias and publication bias (by accessing unpublished endpoints).
terms.pitfalls: Common research obstacles: (1) Data retrieval failure—failure of investigators to share raw data due to institutional legal restrictions, loss of older files, or competitive reluctance; (2) Extreme resource and time intensity (typically requiring 2 to 4 years to complete); and (3) Inconsistent variable definitions across trials requiring complex harmonization.
terms.apa_reference: Stewart, L. A., & Parmar, M. K. (1993). Meta-analysis of the literature or of individual patient data: Is there a difference?. The Lancet, 341(8842), 418–422. https://doi.org/10.1016/0140-6736(93)93004-K

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích biểu đồ tầm quan trọng - hiệu suất (Lưới ưu tiên IPMA)
vietnamese_variants: Ma trận phân tích tầm quan trọng và hiệu suất
Lưới ưu tiên chiến lược IPMA
terms.core_definition: Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA Priority Grid), formalized in PLS-SEM methodology by Ringle and Sarstedt (2016), is an advanced graphical and analytical tool that extends structural model path coefficients into actionable managerial priorities. By contrasting the total structural effect (importance) of predecessor latent constructs on an endogenous target variable against their average rescaled latent performance scores (performance on a 0-100 scale), IPMA identifies high-impact, low-performing operational drivers that yield maximum marginal returns on investment.
terms.seminal_citation: Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2016). Gain more insight from your PLS-SEM results: The importance-performance map analysis. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 116(9), 1865-1886.
terms.expert_notes: Nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of IPMA according to Xác định các yếu tố nằm ở góc 'Tầm quan trọng cao nhưng Hiệu quả thấp' (High importance, Low performance) là ưu tiên hành động số 1..
terms.operational_mechanism: IPMA execution involves: (1) Rescaling manifest indicators and latent scores into a standardized 0 to 100 range: Y_i^{rescaled} = [ (Y_i - min(Y)) / (max(Y) - min(Y)) ] * 100; (2) Deriving Total Structural Effects: Summing direct and indirect path coefficients to determine total importance on the focal target construct; (3) Two-dimensional grid plotting: Constructing a scatterplot with Total Effect (Importance) on the X-axis and Mean Rescaled Score (Performance) on the Y-axis; (4) Indicator-level IPMA: Zooming into individual items of high-importance constructs to isolate specific actionable operational levers.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: IPMA execution involves: (1) Rescaling manifest indicators and latent scores into a standardized 0 to 100 range: Y_i^{rescaled} = [ (Y_i - min(Y)) / (max(Y) - min(Y)) ] * 100; (2) Deriving Total Structural Effects: Summing direct and indirect path coefficients to determine total importance on the focal target construct; (3) Two-dimensional grid plotting: Constructing a scatterplot with Total Effect (Importance) on the X-axis and Mean Rescaled Score (Performance) on the Y-axis; (4) Indicator-level IPMA: Zooming into individual items of high-importance constructs to isolate specific actionable operational levers.
terms.benchmarks: Decision grid benchmarks: (1) Quadrant I (High Importance, Low Performance): The highest strategic priority for resource allocation; (2) Quadrant II (High Importance, High Performance): Competitive strengths to maintain; (3) Quadrant III (Low Importance, Low Performance): Secondary priority; (4) Quadrant IV (Low Importance, High Performance): Potential overkill / resource misallocation; (5) Statistical significance: Target construct R^2 must be substantial (R^2 >= 0.20) for reliable IPMA interpretation.
terms.pitfalls: Common analytical mistakes: (1) Conflating direct path coefficients with total effects (ignoring indirect mediating paths severely underestimates construct importance); (2) Interpreting IPMA when construct indicators have reverse coding that was not properly inverted prior to 0-100 rescaling; and (3) Conducting IPMA on formative constructs without checking multicollinearity.
terms.apa_reference: Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2016). Gain more insight from your PLS-SEM results: The importance-performance map analysis. Industrial Management & Data Systems, 116(9), 1865–1886. https://doi.org/10.1108/IMDS-10-2015-0429

terms.term: Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW / IPW)
terms.vietnamese: Gán trọng số nghịch đảo xác suất điều trị (IPTW)
vietnamese_variants: Trọng số xu hướng nghịch đảo IPTW
Inverse probability of treatment weighting in epidemiology
terms.core_definition: Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW, commonly abbreviated as IPW) is an epidemiological and biostatistical causal inference method utilizing the propensity score to estimate unconfounded causal effects in observational studies. Grounded in counterfactual logic, IPTW assigns each subject a weight inversely proportional to their probability of receiving their observed treatment conditional on baseline confounders, thereby simulating a randomized clinical trial by mathematically eliminating confounding associations between treatment and observed covariates.
terms.seminal_citation: Robins, J. M., Hernán, M. Á., & Brumback, B. (2000). Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology, 11(5), 550-560.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of IPW according to Kết hợp với mô hình kết quả tạo thành 'Ước lượng Vững kép' (Doubly Robust Estimator: chỉ cần một trong hai mô hình đúng thì ước lượng nhân quả vẫn không chệch)..
terms.benchmarks: Balance and diagnostic standards: (1) Balance criterion: Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs) across all baseline covariates in the weighted sample must fall below 0.10 (strictly < 0.05); (2) Mean of stabilized weights sw_i must approximate 1.0 (e.g., between 0.98 and 1.02); (3) Weight truncation / trimming: Trimming extreme weights at the 1st and 99th percentiles if extreme outliers are detected.
terms.operational_mechanism: IPTW execution follows four distinct steps: (1) Propensity score modeling via logistic regression: e_i = Pr(A_i = 1 | L_i); (2) Calculation of unstabilized weights: w_i = A_i / e_i + (1 - A_i) / (1 - e_i); (3) Calculation of stabilized weights: sw_i = A_i * Pr(A=1) / e_i + (1 - A_i) * Pr(A=0) / (1 - e_i), which prevents extreme weights from inflating variance; (4) Marginal Structural Model estimation: Regressing outcome Y on treatment A using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with robust sandwich covariance matrices.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: IPTW execution follows four distinct steps: (1) Propensity score modeling via logistic regression: e_i = Pr(A_i = 1 | L_i); (2) Calculation of unstabilized weights: w_i = A_i / e_i + (1 - A_i) / (1 - e_i); (3) Calculation of stabilized weights: sw_i = A_i * Pr(A=1) / e_i + (1 - A_i) * Pr(A=0) / (1 - e_i), which prevents extreme weights from inflating variance; (4) Marginal Structural Model estimation: Regressing outcome Y on treatment A using generalized estimating equations (GEE) with robust sandwich covariance matrices.
terms.pitfalls: Critical biostatistical traps: (1) Positivity violations: Extreme weights arising from subjects with propensity scores near 0 or 1, which causes massive variance inflation; (2) Weighting on post-treatment variables or mediators, which induces collider stratification bias; and (3) Failing to use robust sandwich standard errors, leading to artificially narrow confidence intervals.
terms.apa_reference: Robins, J. M., Hernán, M. Á., & Brumback, B. (2000). Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology, 11(5), 550–560. https://doi.org/10.1097/00001648-200009000-00011

terms.vietnamese: Đường đặc trưng câu hỏi (Đường cong ICC trong IRT)
vietnamese_variants: Đường đặc tuyến câu hỏi ICC
Đường cong ứng đáp câu hỏi
terms.core_definition: The Item Characteristic Curve (ICC, also termed Item Response Function / IRF or Trace Line) is the central mathematical and graphical representation of an individual item in Item Response Theory (IRT). Plotted as an S-shaped (sigmoidal) logistic curve, the ICC depicts the non-linear relationship between an examinee's underlying continuous latent ability or trait level (theta, on the horizontal axis) and the conditional probability of endorsing or correctly answering the item (P(theta), on the vertical axis).
terms.seminal_citation: Lord, F. M. (1980). Applications of item response theory to practical testing problems. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Characteristic Curve according to Đường cong dốc hơn thể hiện câu hỏi có độ phân biệt cao hơn; vị trí dịch sang phải thể hiện câu hỏi khó hơn..
terms.benchmarks: Parameter evaluation standards: (1) Difficulty parameter b_i: Typically spans between -3.0 (very easy) and +3.0 (very difficult); (2) Discrimination parameter a_i: Values >= 1.35 are high, >= 1.70 very high (values < 0.65 indicate inadequate discrimination); (3) Guessing parameter c_i: Should approximate 1/k for k-choice multiple-choice items (e.g., c approx 0.20 for 5-choice items).
terms.operational_mechanism: In the general 3-Parameter Logistic (3PL) IRT model, the ICC is mathematically expressed as: P_i(theta) = c_i + (1 - c_i) / [ 1 + exp( -1.7 * a_i * (theta - b_i) ) ], where: (1) Parameter b_i (Difficulty / Threshold): The trait level where the probability of endorsement is midway between c_i and 1.0 (horizontal inflection point); (2) Parameter a_i (Discrimination): The slope of the curve at inflection point b_i (steeper slope indicates higher discrimination); (3) Parameter c_i (Pseudo-guessing): The lower asymptote reflecting the probability of a correct response by examinees with extremely low ability.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: In the general 3-Parameter Logistic (3PL) IRT model, the ICC is mathematically expressed as: P_i(theta) = c_i + (1 - c_i) / [ 1 + exp( -1.7 * a_i * (theta - b_i) ) ], where: (1) Parameter b_i (Difficulty / Threshold): The trait level where the probability of endorsement is midway between c_i and 1.0 (horizontal inflection point); (2) Parameter a_i (Discrimination): The slope of the curve at inflection point b_i (steeper slope indicates higher discrimination); (3) Parameter c_i (Pseudo-guessing): The lower asymptote reflecting the probability of a correct response by examinees with extremely low ability.
terms.pitfalls: Common psychometric errors: (1) Retaining items with negative discrimination slopes (a_i < 0), which implies that higher-ability participants perform worse than lower-ability participants, signaling flawed item keying; (2) Violating the unidimensionality assumption of IRT; and (3) Confusing the ICC with the Item Information Function (IIF)—ICC plots probability, while IIF plots statistical precision.
terms.apa_reference: Lord, F. M. (1980). Applications of item response theory to practical testing problems. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.

terms.term: Item Characteristic Curve (Trace Line in Item Response Theory)
terms.vietnamese: Đường đặc tuyến ứng đáp câu hỏi trong lý thuyết IRT
vietnamese_variants: Đường cong tham số hóa câu hỏi
terms.core_definition: The Item Characteristic Curve (Trace Line in Item Response Theory) is the mathematical function mapping the progression of latent trait theta to observed response probabilities across 1PL (Rasch), 2PL, 3PL, and polytomous IRT models (Graded Response Model, Partial Credit Model). Serving as the foundational unit of test assembly, computer adaptive testing (CAT), and Differential Item Functioning (DIF) detection, trace lines provide an invariant characterization of item performance independent of specific test-taking sample distributions.
terms.seminal_citation: Hambleton, R. K., Swaminathan, H., & Rogers, H. J. (1991). Fundamentals of item response theory. SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1404
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Characteristic Curve (ICC) according to Embretson & Reise (2000).
terms.operational_mechanism: Comparative model trace lines: (1) 1PL / Rasch Model: Assumes all items have equal discrimination (a_i = 1) and zero guessing (c_i = 0), varying only in difficulty b_i: P(theta) = 1 / [1 + exp(-(theta - b_i))]; (2) 2PL Model: Freely estimates discrimination a_i and difficulty b_i; (3) Polytomous trace lines (Samejima Graded Response Model): Multiple cumulative curves P^*_{ik}(theta) for ordered Likert categories; (4) Differential Item Functioning (DIF): Occurs when the trace line for an item differs significantly between demographic groups (e.g., gender, ethnicity) after matching on latent trait theta.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Comparative model trace lines: (1) 1PL / Rasch Model: Assumes all items have equal discrimination (a_i = 1) and zero guessing (c_i = 0), varying only in difficulty b_i: P(theta) = 1 / [1 + exp(-(theta - b_i))]; (2) 2PL Model: Freely estimates discrimination a_i and difficulty b_i; (3) Polytomous trace lines (Samejima Graded Response Model): Multiple cumulative curves P^*_{ik}(theta) for ordered Likert categories; (4) Differential Item Functioning (DIF): Occurs when the trace line for an item differs significantly between demographic groups (e.g., gender, ethnicity) after matching on latent trait theta.
terms.benchmarks: Psychometric modeling standards: (1) Model fit: Item-level goodness of fit evaluated via Orlando-Thissen S-X^2 or Yen's Q_1 statistic (p > 0.05 indicates good fit); (2) Invariance test: Non-significant DIF across demographic subgroups; (3) Item Information: Curve steepness directly determines the maximum height of the Item Information Function.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Forcing a 1PL/Rasch model onto empirical data where item discriminations vary substantially without testing model fit; (2) Neglecting local item independence (residual correlations among items after partialling out theta); and (3) Misinterpreting trace lines in software with non-standard scaling constants (D = 1.0 vs. D = 1.702).
terms.apa_reference: Hambleton, R. K., Swaminathan, H., & Rogers, H. J. (1991). Fundamentals of item response theory. SAGE Publications.

terms.term: Item Difficulty Index (p-value / Facility Value in Testing)
terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số độ khó câu hỏi / Giá trị độ dễ p-value trong trắc nghiệm
terms.core_definition: Item Difficulty Index (ký hiệu là p hoặc p-value trong lý thuyết đo lường cổ điển CTT) là tỷ lệ phần trăm số thí sinh trả lời đúng một câu hỏi trắc nghiệm trên tổng số thí sinh tham gia làm bài (Ebel & Frisbie, 1991; Crocker & Algina, 1986). Cần đặc biệt lưu ý: trong trắc nghiệm học thuật, p là một 'chỉ số độ dễ' (facility index) - giá trị p càng cao thì câu hỏi càng dễ, và giá trị p càng thấp thì câu hỏi càng khó, hoàn toàn khác biệt với khái niệm p-value (mức ý nghĩa thống kê) trong kiểm định giả thuyết.
terms.seminal_citation: Ebel, R. L., & Frisbie, D. A. (1991). Essentials of Educational Measurement (5th ed.). Prentice-Hall; Crocker, L., & Algina, J. (1986). Introduction to Classical and Modern Test Theory. Holt, Rinehart and Winston.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Difficulty Index (p-value in Testing) according to Wood (1960).
terms.operational_mechanism: Công thức toán học: p = R / N, trong đó R là số lượng thí sinh trả lời đúng câu hỏi và N là tổng số thí sinh trong mẫu kiểm tra. Đối với thang đo chỉnh sửa loại trừ đoán mò (corrected for guessing): p_corrected = (p - 1/k) / (1 - 1/k), với k là số lượng phương án lựa chọn.
benchmarks: Độ khó tối ưu cho trắc nghiệm 4 phương án (k = 4): p tối ưu = (1.0 + 0.25) / 2 = 0.625 (thường dao động lý tưởng từ 0.50 đến 0.70 để tối đa hóa phương sai bài thi).
Phân loại độ khó chuẩn mực: p > 0.85: Câu hỏi quá dễ; 0.70 < p ≤ 0.85: Câu hỏi dễ; 0.30 ≤ p ≤ 0.70: Câu hỏi trung bình (đạt chuẩn tốt nhất); 0.15 ≤ p < 0.30: Câu hỏi khó; p < 0.15: Câu hỏi quá khó.
Độ khó trung bình toàn bài thi: Thường nên duy trì ở mức p_mean = 0.50 - 0.60 để đạt đường phân phối chuẩn đối xứng.
pitfalls: Nhầm lẫn ký hiệu p-value độ khó với p-value kiểm định ý nghĩa: Viết báo cáo nhầm rằng 'câu hỏi có ý nghĩa thống kê p < 0.05' trong khi thực tế câu hỏi có độ khó cực cao chỉ 5% người làm đúng.
Đề thi toàn câu hỏi quá khó (p < 0.20): Làm giảm phương sai bài thi, khiến điểm số bị dồn cục ở cận dưới (floor effect) và không thể phân loại được thí sinh trung bình.
Đề thi toàn câu hỏi quá dễ (p > 0.90): Gây ra hiện tượng trần (ceiling effect), không thể phát hiện được những học sinh xuất sắc.
terms.apa_reference: Ebel, R. L., & Frisbie, D. A. (1991). Essentials of educational measurement (5th ed.). Prentice-Hall.

terms.term: Item Discrimination Index (D-Index / Upper-Lower 27% Rule - Kelley)
terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số độ phân biệt câu hỏi / Quy tắc phân nhóm 27% Truman Kelley
terms.core_definition: Item Discrimination Index (ký hiệu là D) là chỉ số đo lường năng lực của một câu hỏi trắc nghiệm trong việc phân biệt rạch ròi giữa những thí sinh có năng lực cao (nhóm điểm cao) và những thí sinh có năng lực thấp (nhóm điểm thấp) trên tổng thể bài kiểm tra (Kelley, 1939; Ebel & Frisbie, 1991). Một câu hỏi có độ phân biệt tốt là câu hỏi mà phần lớn thí sinh giỏi trả lời đúng, trong khi phần lớn thí sinh yếu trả lời sai. Nếu một câu hỏi có chỉ số D âm, câu hỏi đó mang khiếm khuyết nghiêm trọng (thí sinh yếu làm đúng nhiều hơn thí sinh giỏi) và bắt buộc phải bị loại bỏ ngay lập tức.
terms.seminal_citation: Kelley, T. L. (1939). The selection of upper and lower groups for the validation of test items. Journal of Educational Psychology, 30(1), 17-24; Ebel, R. L., & Frisbie, D. A. (1991). Essentials of Educational Measurement (5th ed.). Prentice-Hall.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Discrimination Index (D) according to Ebel (1954).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quy tắc 27% của Truman Kelley (1939): (1) Sắp xếp điểm tổng toàn bài thi của tất cả thí sinh từ cao nhất đến thấp nhất; (2) Trích xuất 27% số thí sinh có điểm cao nhất làm Nhóm Cao (Upper group - U) và 27% số thí sinh có điểm thấp nhất làm Nhóm Thấp (Lower group - L); (3) Tính toán chỉ số phân biệt D theo công thức: D = (R_U - R_L) / n, trong đó R_U là số thí sinh nhóm Cao làm đúng, R_L là số thí sinh nhóm Thấp làm đúng, và n là số thí sinh trong mỗi nhóm (n = 0.27 · N).
benchmarks: Thang đánh giá chuẩn của Robert Ebel (1991): D ≥ 0.40: Câu hỏi xuất sắc (Very good item - giữ lại hoàn toàn); 0.30 ≤ D ≤ 0.39: Câu hỏi tốt (Reasonably good - có thể chỉnh sửa nhỏ); 0.20 ≤ D ≤ 0.29: Câu hỏi biên (Marginal item - cần đại tu chỉnh sửa); D < 0.20: Câu hỏi kém (Poor item - loại bỏ hoặc viết lại toàn bộ).
Giá trị D âm (D < 0): Bắt buộc kiểm tra đáp án ngay; đây là dấu hiệu đáp án bị chấm sai hoặc câu hỏi có bẫy ngôn từ đánh lừa học sinh giỏi.
Tối ưu hóa độ phân biệt: Câu hỏi có độ khó trung bình (p = 0.50) có tiềm năng toán học đạt chỉ số phân biệt D cao nhất.
pitfalls: Giữ lại câu hỏi có D < 0.15: Làm giảm độ tin cậy Cronbach's α của toàn bài kiểm tra.
Chia nhóm tùy tiện không theo quy tắc 27%: Kelley (1939) đã chứng minh tỷ lệ 27% ở hai đầu mút là tỷ lệ tối ưu nhất về mặt toán học để cân bằng giữa độ tin cậy và sự khác biệt phương sai.
Bỏ qua phân tích các phương án nhiễu (distractor analysis): Chỉ xem chỉ số D mà không kiểm tra xem các đáp án sai có thu hút được thí sinh nhóm Thấp hay không.
terms.apa_reference: Kelley, T. L. (1939). The selection of upper and lower groups for the validation of test items. Journal of Educational Psychology, 30(1), 17-24. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0057123

terms.vietnamese: Hàm thông tin câu hỏi (Độ chính xác đo lường IIF)
vietnamese_variants: Hàm đo lường độ chính xác IIF
Hàm lượng thông tin câu hỏi
terms.core_definition: The Item Information Function (IIF) is a core mathematical function in Item Response Theory that quantifies the amount of psychometric information—and therefore the exact statistical measurement precision—contributed by an individual test or survey item at any specific point along the latent trait continuum theta. Derived from Fisher's information concept, the IIF demonstrates that measurement reliability is not a uniform, static single number across all examinees (as assumed by Classical Test Theory), but a dynamic function that varies across trait levels.
terms.seminal_citation: Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee's ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick (Eds.), Statistical theories of mental test scores (pp. 397-479). Addison-Wesley.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Information Function according to Thông tin cực đại tại ngưỡng độ khó của câu hỏi: I(theta) = a² * P · (1-P)..
terms.benchmarks: Precision evaluation standards: (1) High-stakes cutoffs: Target TIF(theta) >= 16 (yielding SE(theta) <= 0.25) across critical decision zones (e.g., certification cut-scores); (2) General research scale: TIF(theta) >= 10 (SE(theta) <= 0.316, corresponding to reliability approx 0.90); (3) Targeted test assembly: Selecting items whose IIF peaks coincide with key decision thresholds.
terms.operational_mechanism: Under the 2PL IRT model: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * (1 - P_i(theta)). The function reveals three fundamental mathematical properties: (1) Information is proportional to the square of discrimination a_i^2 (items with higher discrimination provide exponentially greater measurement precision); (2) Maximum information occurs at theta = b_i (item difficulty), where P_i(theta) = 0.50; (3) Information is strictly additive: Test Information Function TIF(theta) = sum_{i=1}^n I_i(theta), directly yielding conditional Standard Error of Measurement: SE(theta) = 1 / sqrt(TIF(theta)).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Under the 2PL IRT model: I_i(theta) = a_i^2 * P_i(theta) * (1 - P_i(theta)). The function reveals three fundamental mathematical properties: (1) Information is proportional to the square of discrimination a_i^2 (items with higher discrimination provide exponentially greater measurement precision); (2) Maximum information occurs at theta = b_i (item difficulty), where P_i(theta) = 0.50; (3) Information is strictly additive: Test Information Function TIF(theta) = sum_{i=1}^n I_i(theta), directly yielding conditional Standard Error of Measurement: SE(theta) = 1 / sqrt(TIF(theta)).
terms.pitfalls: Common psychometric errors: (1) Assembling tests using items whose IIFs all peak around the population mean (theta = 0), leaving extreme high and low performers measured with very high error (low information); (2) Conflating item discrimination with difficulty; and (3) Ignoring the guessing parameter penalty in 3PL models, which depresses information in lower ability regions.
terms.apa_reference: Birnbaum, A. (1968). Some latent trait models and their use in inferring an examinee's ability. In F. M. Lord & M. R. Novick (Eds.), Statistical theories of mental test scores (pp. 397–479). Addison-Wesley.

terms.vietnamese: Đường cong toán học hàm thông tin câu hỏi (IIF)
vietnamese_variants: Đồ thị hàm thông tin IIF
Đường cong thông tin mục hỏi
terms.core_definition: The Item Information Function (IIF Mathematical Curve) is the bell-shaped graphical curve depicting Fisher information across latent ability theta for a specific psychometric item. In computerized adaptive testing (CAT) and scale construction, plotting and comparing IIF curves enables test developers to identify which items maximally differentiate candidates at honors cutoffs, clinical depression diagnostic thresholds, or baseline literacy floors.
terms.seminal_citation: Baker, F. B. (2001). The basics of item response theory (2nd ed.). ERIC Clearinghouse on Assessment and Evaluation.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item information function (IIF) according to DeVellis (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism: Curve properties: (1) Peak Height: Governed by the discrimination parameter a_i; (2) Peak Location: Governed by the difficulty threshold b_i; (3) Curve Spread / Width: Narrow, sharp peaks provide intense precision within a restricted trait band, while wider curves distribute moderate precision across a broader continuum; (4) Polytomous IIF: In Likert-scale items (GRM), the IIF curve is the sum of category information functions, producing wider, multi-peaked information plateaus.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Curve properties: (1) Peak Height: Governed by the discrimination parameter a_i; (2) Peak Location: Governed by the difficulty threshold b_i; (3) Curve Spread / Width: Narrow, sharp peaks provide intense precision within a restricted trait band, while wider curves distribute moderate precision across a broader continuum; (4) Polytomous IIF: In Likert-scale items (GRM), the IIF curve is the sum of category information functions, producing wider, multi-peaked information plateaus.
terms.benchmarks: Curve appraisal criteria: (1) Useful information threshold: Peak I_i(theta) >= 0.50; (2) Information overlap: Verifying that composite test information covers the entire target population spectrum (-2.5 <= theta <= +2.5); (3) Item trimming: Items whose peak IIF < 0.20 contribute almost purely random noise and should be excised.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Relying on Classical Test Theory item-total correlations without examining the latent trait region where the item actually provides precision; (2) Believing an item provides 'high reliability' universally; and (3) Failing to evaluate conditional standard errors across marginalized subgroups.
terms.apa_reference: Baker, F. B. (2001). The basics of item response theory (2nd ed.). ERIC Clearinghouse on Assessment and Evaluation.

terms.term: Item Response Theory (IRT - Modern Psychometric Measurement)
terms.vietnamese: Lý thuyết ứng đáp câu hỏi / Lý thuyết đo lường tâm lý học hiện đại
vietnamese_variants: Lý thuyết phản hồi câu hỏi
Lý thuyết trắc nghiệm hiện đại IRT
terms.core_definition: Item Response Theory (IRT, còn gọi là Lý thuyết nét tiềm ẩn - Latent Trait Theory) là một mô hình toán học và đo lường tâm lý học hiện đại (Lord, 1980; Embretson & Reise, 2000), ra đời để khắc phục các giới hạn cố hữu của Lý thuyết đo lường cổ điển (Classical Test Theory - CTT). IRT mô hình hóa xác suất một cá nhân trả lời đúng hoặc tán thành một câu hỏi cụ thể như một hàm phi tuyến tính của Năng lực tiềm ẩn của cá nhân đó (ký hiệu là Theta) và các thuộc tính đặc trưng của chính câu hỏi đó (Độ khó b, Độ phân biệt a, và Độ đoán mò c). Điểm ưu việt tuyệt đối của IRT là tính 'bất biến tham số' (parameter invariance) - tham số câu hỏi không phụ thuộc vào mẫu làm bài và điểm năng lực người làm không phụ thuộc vào đề thi cụ thể.
terms.seminal_citation: Lord, F. M. (1980). Applications of Item Response Theory to Practical Testing Problems. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates; Embretson, S. E., & Reise, S. P. (2000). Item Response Theory for Psychologists. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1410
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Item Response Theory (IRT) according to Lord (1980).
terms.operational_mechanism: Đường cong đặc trưng câu hỏi (Item Characteristic Curve - ICC): Hàm toán học logistic liên kết Theta với xác suất P(Theta): P(Y=1|Theta) = c + (1 - c) / (1 + exp(-D · a · (Theta - b))). Ba mô hình IRT tiêu chuẩn: (1) Mô hình 1 tham số (1PL / Rasch Model): Chỉ chứa tham số Độ khó b; (2) Mô hình 2 tham số (2PL Model): Chứa Độ khó b và Độ phân biệt a; (3) Mô hình 3 tham số (3PL Model): Bổ sung tham số Đoán mò ngẫu nhiên c (Pseudo-guessing parameter).
benchmarks: Quy mô mẫu lớn bắt buộc: Khác với CTT, IRT đòi hỏi cỡ mẫu lớn để ước lượng tham số ổn định (1PL tối thiểu N ≥ 200-300; 2PL N ≥ 500; 3PL N ≥ 1,000).
Giả định Một chiều (Unidimensionality): Tập hợp câu hỏi phải đo lường duy nhất một chiều kích năng lực tiềm ẩn (kiểm định qua EFA/CFA).
Giả định Độc lập cục bộ (Local Independence): Khi đã kiểm soát năng lực Theta, các câu trả lời cho các câu hỏi khác nhau phải hoàn toàn độc lập với nhau.
Hàm thông tin câu hỏi (Item Information Function - IIF): Đo lường chính xác câu hỏi cung cấp độ chính xác đo lường tối đa tại dải năng lực nào.
pitfalls: Áp dụng mô hình 3PL cho cỡ mẫu nhỏ (N = 100-200): Dẫn đến hiện tượng các tham số không thể hội tụ hoặc sai số chuẩn khổng lồ.
Vi phạm giả định một chiều: Cố tình chạy IRT trên một thang đo đa chiều phức tạp mà không kiểm định tính đơn chiều trước.
Đánh đồng điểm tổng CTT thô với năng lực Theta của IRT: Bỏ qua lợi ích của việc tính điểm năng lực thích ứng trong thi trắc nghiệm trên máy tính (Computerized Adaptive Testing - CAT).
terms.apa_reference: Embretson, S. E., & Reise, S. P. (2000). Item response theory for psychologists. Lawrence Erlbaum Associates Publishers.

terms.vietnamese: Chuỗi thời gian ngắt quãng (Thiết kế bán thực nghiệm ITS)
vietnamese_variants: Phương pháp bán thực nghiệm ITS
terms.core_definition: Interrupted Time Series (ITS) is an elite quasi-experimental research framework utilized when randomized controlled trials are logistically, politically, or ethically impossible (e.g., evaluating national tobacco taxation, mandatory seatbelt legislation, corporate mergers). By tracking a long series of pre-intervention observations, ITS models the underlying secular trend and projects the unobserved counterfactual, allowing for rigorous causal attribution of observed post-intervention shifts to the focal intervention.
terms.seminal_citation: Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of ITS according to Cần tối thiểu 10-15 điểm quan sát trước và sau can thiệp; kiểm soát tự tương quan qua mô hình ARIMA / Newey-West..
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards: (1) Sufficient time points: Minimum 12 observations before and 12 after intervention (ideally >= 24 per phase); (2) Correction of autocorrelation via ARIMA, generalized least squares, or Prais-Winsten estimation; (3) Falsification tests using control outcome variables that should not be affected by the intervention.
terms.operational_mechanism: ITS design architecture: (1) Temporal series compilation: High-frequency longitudinal tracking (e.g., monthly observations over 5 years); (2) Identification of intervention date T_0; (3) Statistical specification: Segmented regression with level and trend change parameters; (4) Methodological enhancements: Adding a non-equivalent control group (Comparative ITS / CITS) to eliminate concurrent historical events, or incorporating multiple switch-on/switch-off intervention points (ABA or ABAB designs).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: ITS design architecture: (1) Temporal series compilation: High-frequency longitudinal tracking (e.g., monthly observations over 5 years); (2) Identification of intervention date T_0; (3) Statistical specification: Segmented regression with level and trend change parameters; (4) Methodological enhancements: Adding a non-equivalent control group (Comparative ITS / CITS) to eliminate concurrent historical events, or incorporating multiple switch-on/switch-off intervention points (ABA or ABAB designs).
terms.pitfalls: Common design vulnerabilities: (1) History confounders—an unmeasured economic or social event occurring simultaneously with the intervention; (2) Gradual implementation: Interventions that take years to phase in, making the exact point of interruption ambiguous; and (3) High attrition or changes in data definition across the time series.
terms.apa_reference: Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật tái lấy mẫu Jackknife
vietnamese_variants: Tái chọn mẫu rút từng quan sát
terms.core_definition: Kỹ thuật tái lấy mẫu Jackknife (Quenouille, 1949, 1956; Tukey, 1958) là phương pháp thống kê phi tham số tiên phong dùng để ước lượng độ chệch (bias) và phương sai sai số chuẩn (standard error) của một tham số ước lượng mà không cần đặt bất kỳ giả định nào về phân phối của dữ liệu. Jackknife hoạt động bằng cách tính toán lại tham số trên n mẫu con, mỗi mẫu con được tạo ra bằng cách loại bỏ tuần tự đúng một quan sát (leave-one-out).
terms.seminal_citation: Quenouille (1949, 1956); Tukey (1958)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Jackknife Resampling according to Quenouille (1949), Tukey (1958).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Cho mẫu ban đầu kích thước n. Tạo n mẫu con kích thước (n - 1) bằng cách lần lượt bỏ đi quan sát thứ i (i = 1...n), thu được n ước lượng tham số theta_(-i). 2. Ước lượng Jackknife cho độ chệch: Bias_jack = (n - 1) · (theta_bar_jack - θ_hat). 3. Ước lượng tham số hiệu chỉnh chệch: θ_jack = n * θ_hat - (n - 1) · theta_bar_jack. 4. Ước lượng phương sai Jackknife: Var_jack = [(n - 1) / n] * ∑ [ (theta_(-i) - theta_bar_jack)² ].
terms.benchmarks: Được áp dụng rộng rãi để hiệu chỉnh chệch trong các ước lượng hợp lý cực đại phi tuyến tính, tính toán hệ số gia tốc trong BCa bootstrap, và chẩn đoán các quan sát có tầm ảnh hưởng lớn (influential observations).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Áp dụng Jackknife cho các tham số phi trơn (non-smooth parameters như Trung vị Median hoặc các phân vị). Phép tính Jackknife hoàn toàn thất bại và cho phương sai không nhất quán khi áp dụng cho hàm trung vị (trong trường hợp này Bootstrap là bắt buộc).
terms.apa_reference: Tukey, J. W. (1958). Bias and confidence in not-quite large samples. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 29(2), 614–623.

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định phân phối chuẩn Jarque-Bera
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định Jarque-Bera (Jarque & Bera, 1980, 1987) là phép kiểm định goodness-of-fit tiệm cận dùng để kiểm tra xem sai số ngẫu nhiên hoặc chuỗi dữ liệu có tuân theo phân phối chuẩn (normal distribution) hay không, dựa trên độ lệch (skewness S) và độ nhọn (kurtosis K) của mẫu.
terms.seminal_citation: Jarque & Bera (1980, 1987)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Jarque-Bera Test according to Jarque & Bera (1987).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Tính toán hệ số bất đối xứng (skewness S) và hệ số độ nhọn (kurtosis K) của mẫu. 2. Trong phân phối chuẩn lý tưởng, S = 0 và K = 3 (hoặc excess kurtosis = K - 3 = 0). 3. Thống kê kiểm định JB: JB = (N/6) * [S² + ((K - 3)²) / 4]. 4. Thống kê JB tuân theo phân phối Chi-bình phương với 2 bậc tự do (df = 2) khi quy mô mẫu N tiến ra vô cùng.
terms.benchmarks: Giả thuyết H0: Dữ liệu tuân theo phân phối chuẩn (S = 0, K = 3). Nếu p-value ≥ 0.05: Không thể bác bỏ H0, giả định phân phối chuẩn được thỏa mãn. Nếu p-value < 0.05: Bác bỏ H0, dữ liệu có hiện tượng lệch hoặc đuôi béo (leptokurtic).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: (1) Sử dụng JB cho mẫu nhỏ (N < 50): Phân phối tiệm cận Chi-bình phương của JB bị chệch nặng ở mẫu nhỏ, làm tăng tỷ lệ bác bỏ sai lầm (nên dùng Shapiro-Wilk cho mẫu nhỏ); (2) Bác bỏ kết quả OLS khi JB có p < 0.05 trên mẫu lớn: Theo Định lý Giới hạn Trung tâm (CLT), khi N lớn, các ước lượng OLS vẫn tiệm cận chuẩn bất kể phân phối của phần dư.
terms.apa_reference: Jarque, C. M., & Bera, A. K. (1987). A test for normality of observations and regression residuals. International Statistical Review, 55(2), 163–172. https://doi.org/10.2307/1403192

terms.vietnamese: Hệ thống phiên âm Jefferson (Phân tích hội thoại)
vietnamese_variants: Hệ thống ký hiệu Gail Jefferson
terms.core_definition: The Jeffersonian Transcription System, developed by Gail Jefferson (1984, 2004) alongside Harvey Sacks and Emanuel Schegloff, is the internationally standardized notation system used in Conversation Analysis (CA) and ethnomethodology to transcribe naturally occurring spoken interaction. Recognizing that how something is said is as crucial to social action as what is said, the system captures micro-details of speech delivery—including exact pause lengths in tenths of a second, overlapping speech, pitch shifts, volume, elongation, breathiness, and laughter particles.
terms.seminal_citation: Jefferson, G. (2004). Glossary of transcript symbols with an introduction. In G. H. Lerner (Ed.), Conversation analysis: Studies from the first generation (pp. 13-31). John Benjamins Publishing.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Jeffersonian Transcription System according to Silverman (2016); Silverman (2016).
terms.operational_mechanism: Key Jeffersonian transcription symbols: (1) Pauses: Timed in seconds and tenths in parentheses, e.g., (0.4) for a four-tenth second silence; (.) denotes a micro-pause under 0.2 seconds; (2) Overlaps: Left brackets [ indicate the exact onset of simultaneous speech, right brackets ] indicate where overlap ends; (3) Intonation: Period (.) indicates falling contour, question mark (?) indicates rising contour, comma (,) indicates continuing contour; (4) Delivery dynamics: Underlining indicates stress or emphasis; ALL CAPS indicates loud volume; degree signs o...o indicate whispered speech; colons (:::) indicate sound stretching/elongation; greater/less than symbols (>...<) indicate hurried speech; arrows (uparrow, downarrow) indicate sudden pitch jumps.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Key Jeffersonian transcription symbols: (1) Pauses: Timed in seconds and tenths in parentheses, e.g., (0.4) for a four-tenth second silence; (.) denotes a micro-pause under 0.2 seconds; (2) Overlaps: Left brackets [ indicate the exact onset of simultaneous speech, right brackets ] indicate where overlap ends; (3) Intonation: Period (.) indicates falling contour, question mark (?) indicates rising contour, comma (,) indicates continuing contour; (4) Delivery dynamics: Underlining indicates stress or emphasis; ALL CAPS indicates loud volume; degree signs o...o indicate whispered speech; colons (:::) indicate sound stretching/elongation; greater/less than symbols (>...<) indicate hurried speech; arrows (uparrow, downarrow) indicate sudden pitch jumps.
terms.benchmarks: Conversation analytic standards: (1) Micro-analytic fidelity: Verbatim transcription strictly preserving hesitations, repairs, non-lexical tokens ('uh', 'um'), and colloquial pronunciations without grammatical sanitization; (2) Time-aligned multi-pass listening using specialized software (e.g., Praat, ELAN); (3) Standard line numbering accompanying all transcript excerpts in published manuscripts.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Standardizing or 'cleaning up' speech into formal written grammar, which destroys the empirical interactional mechanics; (2) Guessing pause lengths rather than measuring them using digital acoustic spectrograms; and (3) Imposing researcher psychological assumptions (e.g., 'he was angry') rather than describing the interactional acoustic delivery.
terms.apa_reference: Jefferson, G. (2004). Glossary of transcript symbols with an introduction. In G. H. Lerner (Ed.), Conversation analysis: Studies from the first generation (pp. 13–31). John Benjamins Publishing. https://doi.org/10.1075/pbns.125.02jef

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số ảnh hưởng của tạp chí (Chỉ số JIF Clarivate)
vietnamese_variants: Journal Impact Factor Web of Science
terms.core_definition: The Journal Impact Factor (JIF), devised by Eugene Garfield (1955, 1972) and published annually in Clarivate's Journal Citation Reports (JCR), is the world's most widely recognized bibliometric indicator of academic journal prestige and citation velocity. It measures the average frequency with which peer-reviewed articles published in a specific journal during the preceding two calendar years were cited in indexed Web of Science journals during the focal evaluation year.
terms.seminal_citation: Garfield, E. (1972). Citation analysis as a tool in journal evaluation. Science, 178(4060), 471-479.
terms.expert_notes: Nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of JIF according to Tính bằng: Tổng số trích dẫn trong năm hiện tại cho các bài báo xuất bản trong 2 năm trước chia cho tổng số bài báo có thể trích dẫn được xuất bản trong 2 năm đó..
terms.operational_mechanism: Calculation formula for year Y: JIF_Y = (Citations in year Y to items published in year Y-1 and Y-2) / (Total citable items published in year Y-1 and Y-2). 'Citable items' are strictly defined as substantive scholarly contributions: research articles and review papers. Letters, editorials, news items, and book reviews are excluded from the denominator, though any citations they receive are included in the numerator. Clarivate also provides a 5-Year Impact Factor and the Journal Citation Indicator (JCI).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Calculation formula for year Y: JIF_Y = (Citations in year Y to items published in year Y-1 and Y-2) / (Total citable items published in year Y-1 and Y-2). 'Citable items' are strictly defined as substantive scholarly contributions: research articles and review papers. Letters, editorials, news items, and book reviews are excluded from the denominator, though any citations they receive are included in the numerator. Clarivate also provides a 5-Year Impact Factor and the Journal Citation Indicator (JCI).
terms.benchmarks: JCR quartile benchmarking: (1) Quartile 1 (Q1): Journals ranking in the top 25% of their specific Web of Science category; Q2 (25%-50%), Q3 (50%-75%), Q4 (bottom 25%); (2) Disciplinary variations: JIF values are non-comparable across disciplines (a JIF of 3.5 is elite in Pure Mathematics or History, but modest in Molecular Biology); (3) DORA compliance: San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment mandates that JIF must not be used as a proxy for individual article or researcher quality.
terms.pitfalls: Critical bibliometric distortions: (1) Numerator-denominator asymmetry: Journal editors negotiating classification of articles to depress the denominator while capturing citations in the numerator; (2) Citation skewness: ~80% of a journal's JIF is typically driven by only 20% of its published papers; and (3) Coercive citation: Editors pressuring submitting authors to cite the journal to artificially inflate JIF.
terms.apa_reference: Garfield, E. (1972). Citation analysis as a tool in journal evaluation. Science, 178(4060), 471–479. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.178.4060.471

terms.vietnamese: Lý thuyết kiến tạo công việc (Wrzesniewski & Dutton)
vietnamese_variants: Kiến tạo công việc chủ động
Lý thuyết thiết kế lại công việc từ dưới lên
terms.core_definition: Job Crafting Theory, formulated by Amy Wrzesniewski and Jane E. Dutton (2001), is an influential organizational behavior framework conceptualizing employee agency and bottom-up job redesign. In sharp contrast to traditional top-down job design theories (e.g., Hackman & Oldham) which view employees as passive recipients of predetermined job descriptions, Job Crafting captures the proactive, self-initiated physical, cognitive, and relational boundaries employees alter to reshape their work identity, psychological meaningfulness, and professional engagement.
terms.seminal_citation: Wrzesniewski, A., & Dutton, J. E. (2001). Crafting a job: Revisioning employees as active crafters of their work. Academy of Management Review, 26(2), 179-201.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Job Crafting Theory (Wrzesniewski & Dutton) according to Wrzesniewski & Dutton (2001).
terms.operational_mechanism: Wrzesniewski and Dutton delineated three primary forms of job crafting: (1) Task Crafting: Altering the number, scope, type, or execution of daily work tasks (e.g., introducing a new digital tool); (2) Relational Crafting: Reshaping the frequency, nature, and depth of interpersonal interactions with colleagues, clients, and mentors; (3) Cognitive Crafting: Reframing cognitive perspectives regarding the social value and purpose of one's work (e.g., a hospital cleaner viewing their work as healing patients rather than cleaning floors). In quantitative research, measured via the Job Crafting Questionnaire (JCQ; Slemp & Vella-Brodrick) or the Dutch Job Crafting Scale (Tims et al., based on the JD-R model).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Wrzesniewski and Dutton delineated three primary forms of job crafting: (1) Task Crafting: Altering the number, scope, type, or execution of daily work tasks (e.g., introducing a new digital tool); (2) Relational Crafting: Reshaping the frequency, nature, and depth of interpersonal interactions with colleagues, clients, and mentors; (3) Cognitive Crafting: Reframing cognitive perspectives regarding the social value and purpose of one's work (e.g., a hospital cleaner viewing their work as healing patients rather than cleaning floors). In quantitative research, measured via the Job Crafting Questionnaire (JCQ; Slemp & Vella-Brodrick) or the Dutch Job Crafting Scale (Tims et al., based on the JD-R model).
terms.benchmarks: Psychometric and empirical standards: (1) Construct validity: Job crafting uniquely predicts work engagement, job performance, and psychological well-being beyond formal job demands and personality traits (Delta R^2 = 5% to 15%); (2) Scale reliability: Alpha >= 0.80 across task, relational, and cognitive subscales; (3) Longitudinal cross-lagged panels showing reciprocal gains between job crafting and personal resources.
terms.pitfalls: Common research pitfalls: (1) Conflating job crafting with organizational citizenship behavior (OCB)—OCB is other-oriented extra-role behavior, while job crafting is self-directed task and identity reframing; (2) Ignoring organizational constraints—failing to examine how toxic supervision or excessive surveillance restricts job crafting opportunities; and (3) Assuming job crafting is always positive (unaligned task crafting can undermine organizational goals).
terms.apa_reference: Wrzesniewski, A., & Dutton, J. E. (2001). Crafting a job: Revisioning employees as active crafters of their work. Academy of Management Review, 26(2), 179–201. https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.2001.4378011

terms.vietnamese: Mô hình yêu cầu và nguồn lực công việc (Mô hình JD-R)
vietnamese_variants: Khung phân tích kiệt sức và gắn kết JD-R
terms.core_definition: The Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Model, formulated by Arnold B. Bakker and Evangelia Demerouti (2001, 2007), is an overarching, flexible occupational health psychology framework positing that regardless of industry or job type, all working conditions can be classified into two broad categories: Job Demands and Job Resources. The model articulates two distinct, simultaneous psychological processes: an energetic Health Impairment Process (excessive demands leading to chronic exhaustion, strain, and burnout) and a motivational Motivational Process (abundant resources fostering work engagement, organizational commitment, and superior performance).
terms.seminal_citation: Bakker, A. B., & Demerouti, E. (2007). The job demands-resources model: State of the art. Journal of Managerial Psychology, 22(3), 309-328.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Job Demands-Resources Model (JD-R) according to Demerouti et al. (2001), Bakker & Demerouti (2007).
terms.operational_mechanism: The JD-R model operates via dual main effects and two key interaction hypotheses: (1) Health Impairment Process: Chronic Job Demands (work overload, emotional demands, role conflict) drain energetic reserves, triggering burnout and somatic illness; (2) Motivational Process: Job Resources (autonomy, supervisor support, feedback, developmental opportunities) satisfy basic psychological needs (Deci & Ryan), driving work engagement; (3) Buffering Hypothesis: Job resources buffer the negative impact of job demands on strain; (4) Coping Hypothesis: Job demands amplify the positive impact of job resources on engagement (resources become most valuable under high demand conditions). Evaluated via structural equation modeling (SEM) and longitudinal cross-lagged panel models.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The JD-R model operates via dual main effects and two key interaction hypotheses: (1) Health Impairment Process: Chronic Job Demands (work overload, emotional demands, role conflict) drain energetic reserves, triggering burnout and somatic illness; (2) Motivational Process: Job Resources (autonomy, supervisor support, feedback, developmental opportunities) satisfy basic psychological needs (Deci & Ryan), driving work engagement; (3) Buffering Hypothesis: Job resources buffer the negative impact of job demands on strain; (4) Coping Hypothesis: Job demands amplify the positive impact of job resources on engagement (resources become most valuable under high demand conditions). Evaluated via structural equation modeling (SEM) and longitudinal cross-lagged panel models.
terms.benchmarks: Empirical testing standards: (1) Dual-process structural paths: Demands -> Burnout path beta >= 0.30 (p < 0.001); Resources -> Engagement path beta >= 0.40 (p < 0.001); (2) Moderation interaction terms (Demands x Resources) achieving statistically significant Delta R^2; (3) Measurement scales: Evaluated using the Maslach Burnout Inventory (MBI) or Oldenburg Burnout Inventory (OLBI) alongside the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale (UWES).
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Assuming the JD-R model requires fixed, universal scales rather than tailoring demands and resources to the specific professional context; (2) Conflating Challenge Demands (which can promote engagement) with Hindrance Demands (which strictly deplete health); and (3) Testing the model using purely cross-sectional surveys without controlling for common method bias.
terms.apa_reference: Bakker, A. B., & Demerouti, E. (2007). The job demands-resources model: State of the art. Journal of Managerial Psychology, 22(3), 309–328. https://doi.org/10.1108/02683940710733115

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định Đồng liên kết Johansen (Kiểm định Trace và Max-Eigenvalue)
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định đồng liên kết hệ thống VAR
domain_tags: Kinh tế lượng Chuỗi thời gian
Quan hệ Cân bằng Dài hạn
terms.core_definition: Phương pháp kiểm định đồng liên kết đa biến dựa trên mô hình tự hồi quy vectơ (VAR) do Søren Johansen (1988, 1990) phát triển. Khác với phương pháp 2 bước Engle-Granger (chỉ tìm được tối đa một vectơ đồng liên kết duy nhất), Johansen cho phép kiểm định và ước lượng TOÀN BỘ các mối quan hệ cân bằng dài hạn độc lập tồn tại giữa một hệ thống gồm k chuỗi thời gian không dừng có cùng bậc tích hợp I(1).
terms.seminal_citation: Johansen, S. (1988). Statistical analysis of cointegration vectors. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control, 12(2–3), 231–254; Johansen, S., & Juselius, K. (1990). Maximum likelihood estimation and inference on cointegration—with applications to the demand for money. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 52(2), 169–210.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Johansen Cointegration Test according to Johansen (1991).
terms.benchmarks: Hai phép kiểm định thống kê bắt buộc: (1) Kiểm định vết ma trận (Trace Test λ_trace): Kiểm định giả thuyết có tối đa r vectơ đồng liên kết đối kháng với giả thuyết có nhiều hơn r vectơ; (2) Kiểm định giá trị riêng cực đại (Maximum Eigenvalue Test λ_max): Kiểm định giả thuyết có đúng r vectơ so với r+1 vectơ. Nếu giá trị thống kê lớn hơn giá trị tới hạn ở mức 5% (p < 0.05), bác bỏ H0. Khi tồn tại đồng liên kết (r ≥ 1), bắt buộc phải chuyển từ mô hình VAR sai phân sang mô hình Vector Error Correction Model (VECM).
terms.pitfalls: Áp dụng Johansen khi các chuỗi có bậc tích hợp hỗn hợp (vừa có I(0) vừa có I(1) - trường hợp này bắt buộc phải dùng ARDL Bounds Test của Pesaran et al. 2001); chọn sai bậc trễ của mô hình VAR cơ sở làm sai lệch phân phối tiệm cận của bài kiểm định Trace và Max-Eigenvalue; không xác định đúng cấu trúc xu thế (Trend assumption) trong phương trình đồng liên kết.
terms.apa_reference: Johansen, S., & Juselius, K. (1990). Maximum likelihood estimation and inference on cointegration—with applications to the demand for money. Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics, 52(2), 169–210.

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật Johnson-Neyman (Phân tích điều tiết chiếu rọi Floodlight)
