vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật J-N trong điều tiết
terms.core_definition: The Johnson-Neyman (J-N) Technique, developed by Palmer O. Johnson and Jerzy Neyman (1936) and popularized in behavioral sciences by Andrew Hayes (PROCESS macro) and Spiller et al. (2013), is an advanced mathematical procedure for probing interaction effects in regression and ANCOVA. In contrast to the traditional 'pick-a-point' / spotlight approach (which arbitrarily evaluates simple slopes at mean +/- 1 SD of the moderator), the J-N technique functions as a 'floodlight' analysis, mathematically solving for the exact boundary values (regions of significance) across the entire continuous spectrum of the moderator where the focal predictor's conditional effect transitions between statistical significance and non-significance.
terms.seminal_citation: Johnson, P. O., & Neyman, J. (1936). Tests of certain linear hypotheses and their application to some educational problems. Statistical Research Memoirs, 1, 57-93.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1428
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Johnson-Neyman Technique according to Hayes (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism: Given the moderation equation Y = beta_0 + beta_1 X + beta_2 W + beta_3 (X * W) + epsilon, the conditional effect (simple slope) of X on Y is theta_{X->Y} = beta_1 + beta_3 * W, with conditional standard error s.e.(theta) = sqrt( Var(hat{beta}_1) + W^2 * Var(hat{beta}_3) + 2 * W * Cov(hat{beta}_1, hat{beta}_3) ). The Johnson-Neyman technique sets the t-ratio t = theta / s.e.(theta) equal to the critical two-tailed t-value (t_{crit} = 1.96 for alpha = 0.05) and solves the quadratic equation for W, deriving the exact numerical roots W_{lower} and W_{upper} that define the thresholds of significance.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Given the moderation equation Y = beta_0 + beta_1 X + beta_2 W + beta_3 (X * W) + epsilon, the conditional effect (simple slope) of X on Y is theta_{X->Y} = beta_1 + beta_3 * W, with conditional standard error s.e.(theta) = sqrt( Var(hat{beta}_1) + W^2 * Var(hat{beta}_3) + 2 * W * Cov(hat{beta}_1, hat{beta}_3) ). The Johnson-Neyman technique sets the t-ratio t = theta / s.e.(theta) equal to the critical two-tailed t-value (t_{crit} = 1.96 for alpha = 0.05) and solves the quadratic equation for W, deriving the exact numerical roots W_{lower} and W_{upper} that define the thresholds of significance.
terms.benchmarks: Reporting standards in top journals (JCR, JMR, JAP): (1) Mandatory J-N plot displaying the continuous conditional effect curve with 95% confidence bands plotted against the complete range of moderator W; (2) Reporting exact boundary values and the percentage of sample observations falling inside vs. outside the region of significance (e.g., 'The effect of X on Y is positive and significant only when W > 3.42, which represents 42.6% of the sample'); (3) Superiority: Banning artificial median splits and arbitrary spotlighting.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Failing to report the percentage of sample cases situated within the significance region (a mathematically significant boundary that lies outside the empirical range of observed data is practically meaningless); (2) Reporting J-N roots when the interaction term itself (beta_3) is non-significant; and (3) Forgetting that J-N assumptions mirror OLS regression assumptions regarding homoscedasticity and normality.
terms.apa_reference: Johnson, P. O., & Neyman, J. (1936). Tests of certain linear hypotheses and their application to some educational problems. Statistical Research Memoirs, 1, 57–93.

terms.term: Joint Display in Mixed Methods Research
terms.vietnamese: Bảng hiển thị tích hợp phương pháp hỗn hợp
vietnamese_variants: Ma trận tích hợp dữ liệu
Bảng so sánh định lượng - định tính
domain_tags: Nghiên cứu Phương pháp Hỗn hợp
terms.core_definition: Bảng trực quan hóa tích hợp cấp cao trong nghiên cứu phương pháp hỗn hợp (Mixed Methods Research) do Fetters, Curry & Creswell (2013) và Guetterman et al. (2015) đề xuất. Bảng này đặt song song các phát hiện thống kê định lượng và trích dẫn bằng chứng định tính theo từng mục tiêu nghiên cứu cụ thể, từ đó tạo ra sự kết nối và tương tác sâu sắc (Integration through joint display) nhằm tạo ra "nhiều hơn tổng số các phần" (the whole is greater than the ∑ of its parts).
terms.seminal_citation: Fetters, M. D., Curry, L. A., & Creswell, J. W. (2013). Achieving integration in mixed methods designs—principles and practices. Health Services Research, 48(6pt2), 2134–2156. https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6773.12117; Guetterman, T. C., Fetters, M. D., & Creswell, J. W. (2015). Integrating quantitative and qualitative results in health science mixed methods research through joint displays. Annals of Family Medicine, 13(6), 554–561. https://doi.org/10.1370/afm.1865
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Joint display according to Creswell & Creswell (2023).
terms.benchmarks: Cấu trúc bảng chuẩn mực phải gồm 4 cột bắt buộc: (1) Khái niệm hoặc Câu hỏi nghiên cứu cụ thể; (2) Kết quả định lượng (Hệ số hồi quy, p-value, tỷ lệ %); (3) Minh chứng định tính (Các trích dẫn nguyên văn mang tính đại diện cao - Verbatim quotes); (4) Diễn giải tích hợp (Meta-inferences: chỉ rõ kết quả hai nhánh là Khẳng định lẫn nhau - Convergent, Bổ trợ cho nhau - Complementary, hay Mâu thuẫn - Discordant).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy "Tách rời giả tạo" (Side-by-side without integration): Đặt dữ liệu định lượng và định tính cạnh nhau nhưng không có cột phân tích tích hợp (Meta-inferences). Bẫy "Bỏ qua mâu thuẫn" (Confirmation bias): Chỉ trình bày những phát hiện định tính ủng hộ kết quả định lượng mà che giấu các mâu thuẫn hoặc điểm dị biệt giữa hai luồng dữ liệu.
terms.apa_reference: Guetterman, T. C., Fetters, M. D., & Creswell, J. W. (2015). Integrating quantitative and qualitative results in health science mixed methods research through joint displays. Annals of Family Medicine, 13(6), 554–561.

terms.term: Joint Display in Mixed Methods Research
terms.vietnamese: Bảng trình bày chung trong nghiên cứu phương pháp hỗn hợp
vietnamese_variants: Ma trận trình bày chung Joint Display
Khung tích hợp thị giác joint display
terms.core_definition: A Joint Display in Mixed Methods Research is a structured visual table, matrix, or graphic diagram that simultaneously juxtaposes qualitative findings (themes, narratives, direct quotes) and quantitative results (statistical coefficients, effect sizes, p-values) side-by-side (Guetterman, Fetters, & Creswell, 2015). Widely recognized as the premier operational tool for achieving authentic methodological integration, joint displays provide a transparent evidentiary platform to compare, contrast, and synthesize both data strands, enabling the generation and validation of overarching 'meta-inferences'.
terms.seminal_citation: Guetterman, T. C., Fetters, M. D., & Creswell, J. W. (2015). Integrating quantitative and qualitative results in health science mixed methods research through joint displays. The Annals of Family Medicine, 13(6), 554-561.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Joint Display in Mixed Methods according to Guetterman et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Constructing a joint display involves a systematic visual architecture: (1) Column 1: Substantive theoretical construct or research question; (2) Column 2: Quantitative statistical results (e.g., odds ratios, path coefficients, mean scores, sample sizes); (3) Column 3: Qualitative findings (e.g., major themes, representative verbatim quotes, ethnographic context); (4) Column 4: Integrated Meta-Inferences (explicit synthesis explaining how the two sources confirm, expand, or contradict one another); (5) Column 5 (Optional): Actionable managerial or clinical implications.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Constructing a joint display involves a systematic visual architecture: (1) Column 1: Substantive theoretical construct or research question; (2) Column 2: Quantitative statistical results (e.g., odds ratios, path coefficients, mean scores, sample sizes); (3) Column 3: Qualitative findings (e.g., major themes, representative verbatim quotes, ethnographic context); (4) Column 4: Integrated Meta-Inferences (explicit synthesis explaining how the two sources confirm, expand, or contradict one another); (5) Column 5 (Optional): Actionable managerial or clinical implications.
terms.benchmarks: Methodological standards in Q1 mixed methods publishing: (1) Inclusion of at least one comprehensive joint display matrix in the results or discussion section; (2) Clear classification of integration outcomes: Confirmation (convergent findings), Expansion (divergent insights covering different facets), or Discordance (conflicting findings); (3) Traceability linking individual participant quotes directly to quantitative subgroup quartiles.
terms.pitfalls: Common reporting pitfalls: (1) 'Pseudosynthesis'—creating a table that simply lists numbers and quotes without including an explicit column synthesizing meta-inferences; (2) Cherry-picking only qualitative quotes that agree with quantitative hypotheses while concealing contradictory narratives; and (3) Cluttered, unreadable tables exceeding journal page limits.
terms.apa_reference: Guetterman, T. C., Fetters, M. D., & Creswell, J. W. (2015). Integrating quantitative and qualitative results in health science mixed methods research through joint displays. The Annals of Family Medicine, 13(6), 554–561. https://doi.org/10.1370/afm.1865

terms.vietnamese: Ma trận trình bày chung (Khung tích hợp dữ liệu thị giác)
vietnamese_variants: Ma trận joint display hỗn hợp
Khung ma trận tích hợp kết quả
terms.core_definition: A Joint Display Matrix is a specific methodological matrix framework designed to structure and publish complex integrated multi-strand data in mixed methods investigations. Functioning as a cognitive organizer for peer reviewers and readers, the matrix systematically maps disparate data modalities onto common analytical coordinates, demonstrating how statistical patterns and ethnographic narratives reinforce one another to solve complex research questions.
terms.seminal_citation: Fetters, M. D., Curry, L. A., & Creswell, J. W. (2013). Achieving integration in mixed methods designs—principles and practices. Health Services Research, 48(6pt2), 2134-2156.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Joint Display Matrix according to Guetterman et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Execution across mixed methods designs: (1) Convergent Designs: Side-by-side comparison matrix evaluating convergence; (2) Sequential Explanatory Designs: Quantitative results in row 1, followed by specific qualitative explanatory mechanisms in row 2; (3) Sequential Exploratory Designs: Qualitative themes in column 1 mapped to newly developed quantitative scale items in column 2, followed by psychometric validation statistics in column 3; (4) Advanced Case-Based Displays: Arraying qualitative case profiles against quantitative outcome scores.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Execution across mixed methods designs: (1) Convergent Designs: Side-by-side comparison matrix evaluating convergence; (2) Sequential Explanatory Designs: Quantitative results in row 1, followed by specific qualitative explanatory mechanisms in row 2; (3) Sequential Exploratory Designs: Qualitative themes in column 1 mapped to newly developed quantitative scale items in column 2, followed by psychometric validation statistics in column 3; (4) Advanced Case-Based Displays: Arraying qualitative case profiles against quantitative outcome scores.
terms.benchmarks: Design-specific benchmarks: (1) Gramms compliance: Alignment with Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study guidelines; (2) Complete conceptual coverage: Every stated mixed methods sub-question must be represented in the matrix; (3) Reader accessibility: Clear row headers and intuitive layout.
terms.pitfalls: Common methodological flaws: (1) Displaying qualitative and quantitative data at incompatible levels of analysis (e.g., individual quotes juxtaposed with country-level macro indicators); (2) Omitting participant sample identifiers; and (3) Treating the matrix as an optional decorative exhibit rather than the central analytical engine of the paper.
terms.apa_reference: Fetters, M. D., Curry, L. A., & Creswell, J. W. (2013). Achieving integration in mixed methods designs—principles and practices. Health Services Research, 48(6pt2), 2134–2156. https://doi.org/10.1111/1475-6773.12117

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định Jonckheere-Terpstra (Kiểm định xu hướng các nhóm có thứ tự)
terms.core_definition: The Jonckheere-Terpstra Test (J-T test), developed independently by A.R. Jonckheere (1954) and T.J. Terpstra (1952), is a non-parametric statistical hypothesis test used to determine whether there is a statistically significant monotonic trend among k independent, ordered groups. While the standard Kruskal-Wallis test evaluates whether ANY group differences exist without regard to ordering, the Jonckheere-Terpstra test explicitly tests an a priori ordered alternative hypothesis: H_1: theta_1 <= theta_2 <= ... <= theta_k (with at least one strict inequality), providing substantially higher statistical power when investigating dose-response relationships or ordered ordinal categories.
terms.seminal_citation: Jonckheere, A. R. (1954). A distribution-free k-sample test against ordered alternatives. Biometrika, 41(1/2), 133-145.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Jonckheere-Terpstra Test according to Jonckheere (1954).
terms.operational_mechanism: Calculation is based on the sum of Mann-Whitney U counts across all ordered group pairs: (1) Arrange k groups in hypothesized theoretical order: Group 1, Group 2, ..., Group k; (2) For every pair of groups (i, j) where i < j, compute the count U_{ij} of instances where an observation in group j exceeds an observation in group i; (3) Compute the total J-T test statistic: J = sum_{i=1}^{k-1} sum_{j=i+1}^k U_{ij}; (4) Large-sample normal approximation: Compute standardized z-score: z = (J - E[J]) / sqrt(Var(J)), where E[J] = (N^2 - sum n_i^2) / 4, adjusting for tied observations.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Calculation is based on the sum of Mann-Whitney U counts across all ordered group pairs: (1) Arrange k groups in hypothesized theoretical order: Group 1, Group 2, ..., Group k; (2) For every pair of groups (i, j) where i < j, compute the count U_{ij} of instances where an observation in group j exceeds an observation in group i; (3) Compute the total J-T test statistic: J = sum_{i=1}^{k-1} sum_{j=i+1}^k U_{ij}; (4) Large-sample normal approximation: Compute standardized z-score: z = (J - E[J]) / sqrt(Var(J)), where E[J] = (N^2 - sum n_i^2) / 4, adjusting for tied observations.
terms.benchmarks: Statistical power benchmarks: (1) Superior power: When an a priori monotonic trend is hypothesized (e.g., drug dosage: placebo < low < medium < high; or corporate hierarchy: junior < mid < senior), the J-T test possesses substantially greater power (15% to 35% higher) than the unordered Kruskal-Wallis omnibus test; (2) Statistical significance: Two-tailed or one-tailed z-score p < 0.05 rejecting the null hypothesis of equal group medians.
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors: (1) Using the Jonckheere-Terpstra test when there is no theoretical basis for an ordered monotonic trend across groups (in which case Kruskal-Wallis must be used); (2) Applying the test post-hoc after inspecting the data to determine the ordering of groups, invalidating the test's Type I error rate; and (3) Failing to adjust for extensive ties in discrete ordinal data.
terms.apa_reference: Jonckheere, A. R. (1954). A distribution-free k-sample test against ordered alternatives. Biometrika, 41(1/2), 133–145. https://doi.org/10.2307/2333011

terms.vietnamese: Báo cáo trích dẫn tạp chí khoa học (Hệ thống JCR Clarivate)
vietnamese_variants: Cơ sở dữ liệu Journal Citation Reports
terms.core_definition: Journal Citation Reports (JCR) is the premier, authoritative annual bibliometric reporting database published by Clarivate Analytics, evaluating over 21,000 academic journals across 250+ scientific disciplines indexed in Web of Science (Science Citation Index Expanded / SCIE, Social Sciences Citation Index / SSCI, Arts & Humanities Citation Index / AHCI, and Emerging Sources Citation Index / ESCI). JCR serves as the global institutional benchmark for journal impact factors, quartile rankings, and citation network analytics.
terms.seminal_citation: Clarivate. (2024). Journal Citation Reports: Reference guide and metric definitions. Clarivate Analytics.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Journal Citation Reports (JCR) according to Clarivate (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism: JCR provides a comprehensive suite of journal-level citation metrics: (1) Journal Impact Factor (JIF) and 5-Year Impact Factor; (2) Journal Citation Indicator (JCI): Field-normalized citation impact; (3) Quartile (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) and Percentile Rankings within specific subject categories; (4) Immediacy Index: Frequency of citations in the exact year of publication; (5) Cited Half-Life and Citing Half-Life: Measuring the longevity and recency of journal citation obsolescence; (6) Eigenfactor Score and Article Influence Score (AIS): PageRank-like algorithms weighting citations by the prestige of the citing journal.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: JCR provides a comprehensive suite of journal-level citation metrics: (1) Journal Impact Factor (JIF) and 5-Year Impact Factor; (2) Journal Citation Indicator (JCI): Field-normalized citation impact; (3) Quartile (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) and Percentile Rankings within specific subject categories; (4) Immediacy Index: Frequency of citations in the exact year of publication; (5) Cited Half-Life and Citing Half-Life: Measuring the longevity and recency of journal citation obsolescence; (6) Eigenfactor Score and Article Influence Score (AIS): PageRank-like algorithms weighting citations by the prestige of the citing journal.
terms.benchmarks: Institutional evaluation benchmarks: (1) Quartile 1 (Q1) status (top 25th percentile by JIF or JCI in its category) serves as the primary criterion for international tenure, doctoral graduation requirements, and university ranking methodologies; (2) Suppression protocols: Clarivate annually suppresses journals exhibiting abnormal citation stacking or extreme anomalous self-citation (> 50%).
terms.pitfalls: Common administrative misuses: (1) Cross-category comparison: Directly comparing raw JIF values between vastly different disciplinary categories without referencing JCR quartile rankings; (2) Using JCR journal rankings as an uncritical proxy for individual article quality (violating DORA principles); and (3) Overlooking that predatory journals fabricate false 'JCR impact factor' claims on unverified websites.
terms.apa_reference: Clarivate. (2024). Journal Citation Reports: Reference guide and metric definitions. Clarivate Analytics. https://clarivate.com/products/scientific-and-academic-research/research-discovery-and-workflow-solutions/journal-citation-reports/

terms.core_definition: The Journal Impact Factor (Two-Year Citation Metric) is the standard quantitative formula developed by Eugene Garfield to measure the short-term citation velocity of scholarly journals. It is mathematically defined as the ratio of all citations received in a target year by articles published in that journal during the two preceding calendar years, divided by the total number of citable articles and reviews published by that journal in those same two years.
terms.seminal_citation: Garfield, E. (1999). Journal impact factor: A brief review. Canadian Medical Association Journal, 161(8), 979-980.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Journal Impact Factor according to Tính bằng: Tổng số trích dẫn trong năm hiện tại cho các bài báo xuất bản trong 2 năm trước chia cho tổng số bài báo có thể trích dẫn được xuất bản trong 2 năm đó..
terms.benchmarks: Scientometric benchmarks: (1) Median JIF varies widely across disciplines: ~1.5 to 2.5 in Mathematics, ~3.0 to 5.0 in Business and Management, ~6.0 to 12.0 in Molecular Biology; (2) 5-Year Impact Factor is preferred in social sciences and humanities where literature matures slowly over a 5 to 10 year citing window.
terms.operational_mechanism: The canonical mathematical equation: JIF_t = C_{t} / (A_{t-1} + A_{t-2}), where C_t is the number of citations in year t to items published in years t-1 and t-2, and A represents citable papers. By restricting the citation window to two preceding years, JIF reflects rapid citation uptake and immediate relevance, which benefits rapidly moving biomedical and physical sciences.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The canonical mathematical equation: JIF_t = C_{t} / (A_{t-1} + A_{t-2}), where C_t is the number of citations in year t to items published in years t-1 and t-2, and A represents citable papers. By restricting the citation window to two preceding years, JIF reflects rapid citation uptake and immediate relevance, which benefits rapidly moving biomedical and physical sciences.
terms.pitfalls: Critical limitations: (1) Two-year citing window penalty: Heavily penalizes fields with long publication lag times and slow citation half-lives (e.g., economics, sociology, mathematics); (2) Extreme skewness: A handful of blockbuster papers or methodological reviews artificially inflate the journal's JIF while the median paper receives few or zero citations; and (3) Editorial gaming via request for self-citations.
terms.apa_reference: Garfield, E. (1999). Journal impact factor: A brief review. Canadian Medical Association Journal, 161(8), 979–980.

terms.core_definition: Journal Impact Factor (JIF Calculation & Limitations) examines the technical algorithms, systemic distortions, and ethical critiques surrounding the use of JIF in academic research evaluation. Highlighted by the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) and the Leiden Manifesto (Hicks et al., 2015), scholarly consensus strongly condemns the misuse of JIF as a surrogate metric for individual research quality, hiring, funding, or tenure decisions, emphasizing its vulnerability to citation skewness, gaming, and disciplinary biases.
terms.seminal_citation: Hicks, D., Wouters, P., Waltman, L., de Rijcke, S., & Rafols, I. (2015). Bibliometrics: The Leiden Manifesto for research metrics. Nature, 520(7548), 429-431.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1435
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Journal Impact Factor (JIF) according to Garfield (1972).
terms.operational_mechanism: Technical analysis of JIF calculation and flaws: (1) Skewed distribution: Citations within journals follow a heavy-tailed power-law distribution; using the arithmetic mean (JIF) to summarize a non-normal distribution is statistically flawed (the median citation count is typically 50% lower than the JIF); (2) Editorial gaming strategies: Publishing extensive review articles (which cite heavily), issuing advance online publications to widen citation windows, or requesting citation of recent journal papers in revisions; (3) Alternative metrics: Eigenfactor (PageRank algorithm removing self-citations), Source Normalized Impact per Paper (SNIP), and Scimago Journal Rank (SJR).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Technical analysis of JIF calculation and flaws: (1) Skewed distribution: Citations within journals follow a heavy-tailed power-law distribution; using the arithmetic mean (JIF) to summarize a non-normal distribution is statistically flawed (the median citation count is typically 50% lower than the JIF); (2) Editorial gaming strategies: Publishing extensive review articles (which cite heavily), issuing advance online publications to widen citation windows, or requesting citation of recent journal papers in revisions; (3) Alternative metrics: Eigenfactor (PageRank algorithm removing self-citations), Source Normalized Impact per Paper (SNIP), and Scimago Journal Rank (SJR).
terms.benchmarks: Responsible research assessment criteria (Leiden Manifesto, 2015): (1) Principle 1: Quantitative evaluation should support, not supplant, qualitative expert peer review; (2) Principle 2: Measure performance against the research missions of the institution; (3) Principle 6: Account for variation by field in citation practices (field-normalized metrics); (4) Absolute ban on evaluating individual papers based on the host journal's JIF.
terms.pitfalls: Common institutional errors: (1) Denying tenure to an author who published a groundbreaking paper in a lower-JIF journal; (2) Rewarding authors who publish superficial papers in high-JIF journals purely for institutional prestige; and (3) Failing to evaluate paper-level normalized citations (e.g., Field-Weighted Citation Impact / FWCI).
terms.apa_reference: Hicks, D., Wouters, P., Waltman, L., de Rijcke, S., & Rafols, I. (2015). Bibliometrics: The Leiden Manifesto for research metrics. Nature, 520(7548), 429–431. https://doi.org/10.1038/520429a

terms.vietnamese: Kho lưu trữ số học thuật JSTOR
vietnamese_variants: Cơ sở dữ liệu số JSTOR
terms.core_definition: JSTOR (short for Journal Storage) is a premier digital library and archival repository established in 1995 by William G. Bowen (Ithaka Harbors). Originally created to solve physical library space constraints by digitizing complete retrospective back-runs of core academic journals, JSTOR now indexes over 12 million academic journal articles, books, and primary source historical documents across 75 disciplines, serving as an indispensable foundation for longitudinal historiography, systematic literature reviews, and philosophical analysis.
terms.seminal_citation: Bowen, W. G. (1995). JSTOR and the academic library of the future. Information Technology and Libraries, 14(4), 238-243.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of JSTOR Digital Archive according to Bowen (1995).
terms.operational_mechanism: Archival and discovery mechanisms: (1) Moving Wall: A defined time window (typically 3 to 5 years) between a journal's most recent issue and the issues available on JSTOR, preserving commercial publisher revenue while ensuring permanent archival access; (2) Complete Historical Runs: High-resolution full-text digitization from Volume 1, Issue 1 (often dating back to the 17th and 18th centuries); (3) Advanced Boolean and proximity search syntax; (4) Text & Data Mining (TDM): Automated text analysis via the Constellate platform for digital humanities and computational social science.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Archival and discovery mechanisms: (1) Moving Wall: A defined time window (typically 3 to 5 years) between a journal's most recent issue and the issues available on JSTOR, preserving commercial publisher revenue while ensuring permanent archival access; (2) Complete Historical Runs: High-resolution full-text digitization from Volume 1, Issue 1 (often dating back to the 17th and 18th centuries); (3) Advanced Boolean and proximity search syntax; (4) Text & Data Mining (TDM): Automated text analysis via the Constellate platform for digital humanities and computational social science.
terms.benchmarks: Systematic search standards: (1) Documented search strings with exact date delimiters; (2) Inclusion in PRISMA flowcharts when conducting historical, sociological, or business history reviews; (3) Cross-referencing against Web of Science and Scopus.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Relying exclusively on JSTOR for current, frontier research (overlooking the 'moving wall' delay of 3-5 years); (2) Unstructured keyword queries missing seminal historical foundational papers; and (3) Inadequate export of bibliographic metadata for citation management.
terms.apa_reference: Bowen, W. G. (1995). JSTOR and the academic library of the future. Information Technology and Libraries, 14(4), 238–243.

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định chéo K-lớp phân tầng
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định chéo K-lớp phân tầng (Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation - Kohavi, 1995; Kuhn & Johnson, 2013) là kỹ thuật đánh giá hiệu năng mô hình ngoài mẫu (out-of-sample performance) chuẩn mực nhất trong học máy và kinh tế lượng dự báo. Phương pháp chia tập dữ liệu thành K phần (folds) có kích thước bằng nhau, với ràng buộc bắt buộc là tỷ lệ phân bổ của các lớp nhãn mục tiêu (hoặc các nhóm biến phụ thuộc) trong mỗi fold phải được bảo toàn giống hệt như tỷ lệ trong toàn bộ tập dữ liệu gốc.
terms.seminal_citation: Kohavi (1995); Kuhn & Johnson (2013)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of K-Fold Stratified Cross-Validation according to Kohavi (1995).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Phân tầng và chia dữ liệu thành K phần (thường K = 5 hoặc K = 10). 2. Lặp lại K vòng: Tại mỗi vòng k, sử dụng K - 1 phần làm tập huấn luyện (training set) và 1 phần còn lại làm tập kiểm tra độc lập (validation/test set). 3. Đánh giá chỉ số hiệu năng (Accuracy, AUC, F1, RMSE) trên tập kiểm tra. 4. Tính trung bình và độ lệch chuẩn của chỉ số hiệu năng qua toàn bộ K vòng lặp.
terms.benchmarks: Tiêu chuẩn chuẩn mực Kohavi (1995): 10-fold Stratified Cross-Validation là cấu hình tối ưu nhất giúp cân bằng hoàn hảo giữa độ chệch và phương sai của ước lượng hiệu năng. Bắt buộc áp dụng khi dữ liệu có hiện tượng mất cân bằng nhãn (imbalanced classes) để đảm bảo mỗi fold đều có đủ các ca biến cố dương tính.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy rò rỉ dữ liệu (Data Leakage): Thực hiện các bước tiền xử lý dữ liệu (như chuẩn hóa Scale, điền dữ liệu khuyết Imputation, hoặc chọn lọc biến Feature Selection) trên toàn bộ tập dữ liệu TRƯỚC KHI chia K-fold. Tất cả các bước tiền xử lý bắt buộc phải được đóng gói bên trong quy trình đường ống (Pipeline) và chỉ được học trên tập train của từng fold.
terms.apa_reference: Kohavi, R. (1995). A study of cross-validation and bootstrap for accuracy estimation and model selection. In Proceedings of the 14th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Vol. 2, pp. 1137–1143).

terms.vietnamese: Thuật toán phân cụm K-Means
terms.core_definition: Thuật toán phân cụm K-Means (MacQueen, 1967; Lloyd, 1982) là thuật toán phân hoạch không giám sát kinh điển nhất, nhằm phân chia N quan sát vào K cụm xác định trước sao cho tổng bình phương khoảng cách khoảng cách từ mỗi điểm dữ liệu đến trọng tâm cụm tương ứng (Within-Cluster Sum of Squares - WCSS / Inertia) đạt giá trị cực tiểu toàn cục.
terms.seminal_citation: MacQueen (1967); Lloyd (1982); Arthur & Vassilvitskii (2007)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of K-Means Clustering Algorithm according to MacQueen (1967).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Khởi tạo K trọng tâm ban đầu (nên dùng thuật toán K-Means++ của Arthur & Vassilvitskii, 2007 để tối ưu hóa vị trí khởi tạo). 2. Bước gán (Assignment step): Gán từng quan sát vào cụm có khoảng cách khoảng cách Euclidean đến trọng tâm là nhỏ nhất. 3. Bước cập nhật (Update step): Tính toán lại tọa độ trọng tâm mới bằng giá trị trung bình tọa độ của tất cả các điểm thuộc cụm đó. 4. Lặp lại bước 2 và 3 cho đến khi các trọng tâm hội tụ và không còn sự dịch chuyển nhãn cụm.
terms.benchmarks: Xác định số lượng cụm K tối ưu: Dựa trên Phương pháp điểm gãy biểu đồ khuỷu tay (Elbow method: điểm uốn của đường cong WCSS), Chỉ số Silhouette trung bình, và Thống kê khoảng trống (Gap Statistic của Tibshirani et al., 2001).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Áp dụng K-Means cho dữ liệu có các cụm có hình dạng phi cầu (non-spherical shapes như hình bán nguyệt, hình elip kéo dài) hoặc có quy mô và mật độ chênh lệch quá lớn. K-Means giả định ngầm rằng các cụm có dạng hình cầu đồng phương sai; khi giả định này sai, K-Means sẽ chia cắt các cụm tự nhiên thành các mảnh vụn sai lệch (khắc phục bằng Gaussian Mixture Models hoặc DBSCAN).
terms.apa_reference: Lloyd, S. (1982). Least squares quantization in PCM. IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 28(2), 129–137. https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1982.1056489

terms.vietnamese: Nội suy theo K láng giềng gần nhất
vietnamese_variants: Điền khuyết bằng thuật toán KNN
terms.core_definition: Nội suy theo K láng giềng gần nhất (KNN Imputation - Troyanskaya et al., 2001; Batista & Monard, 2002) là thuật toán học máy phi tham số dùng để điền thế dữ liệu khuyết thiếu. Với mỗi mẫu có giá trị khuyết, thuật toán tìm kiếm k quan sát hoàn chỉnh khác có khoảng cách khoảng cách tương đồng gần nhất trong không gian đa chiều của các biến không bị khuyết, sau đó gán giá trị nội suy bằng trung bình cộng (hoặc trung vị có trọng số) của k láng giềng đó.
terms.seminal_citation: Troyanskaya et al. (2001); Batista & Monard (2002)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of K-Nearest Neighbors Imputation (KNN) according to Batista & Monard (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Đo lường khoảng cách khoảng cách đa biến: Sử dụng khoảng cách khoảng cách Euclidean chuẩn hóa (đối với biến liên tục) hoặc khoảng cách khoảng cách Gower (cho dữ liệu hỗn hợp cả định lượng lẫn định tính). 2. Xác định k láng giềng gần nhất (thường chọn k = 5 đến 10). 3. Điền giá trị: Đối với biến liên tục, tính trung bình có trọng số nghịch đảo khoảng cách; đối với biến phân loại, lấy nhãn có tần suất xuất hiện nhiều nhất (Majority vote).
terms.benchmarks: Ưu việt tuyệt đối so với các phương pháp tham số tuyến tính khi dữ liệu có cấu trúc phi tuyến phức tạp hoặc cấu trúc phân cụm đa chiều. Thường được tối ưu hóa siêu tham số k thông qua phương pháp kiểm định chéo (Cross-validation).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: (1) Nhạy cảm với thang đo của biến: Nếu không chuẩn hóa dữ liệu (Z-score normalization) trước khi tính khoảng cách khoảng cách, các biến có độ biến thiên số học lớn sẽ chi phối toàn bộ khoảng cách khoảng cách và làm sai lệch việc chọn láng giềng; (2) Không hiệu quả khi tỷ lệ dữ liệu khuyết quá cao trên nhiều biến đồng thời.
terms.apa_reference: Troyanskaya, O., Cantor, M., Sherlock, G., Brown, P., Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., Botstein, D., & Altman, R. B. (2001). Missing value estimation methods for DNA microarrays. Bioinformatics, 17(6), 520–525. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/17.6.520

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số Thích hợp Mẫu Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (Chỉ số KMO)
domain_tags: Phân tích Nhân tố Khám phá (EFA)
terms.core_definition: Chỉ số thống kê do Henry Kaiser (1970, 1974) và Rice phát triển nhằm đánh giá mức độ thích hợp của dữ liệu mẫu cho việc thực hiện Phân tích Nhân tố (EFA/CFA). KMO so sánh độ lớn của các hệ số tương quan quan sát được giữa các cặp biến với các hệ số tương quan riêng phần (Partial correlations). Nếu các biến thực sự chia sẻ các nhân tố chung tiềm ẩn, tương quan riêng phần sẽ nhỏ và chỉ số KMO sẽ tiến gần về 1.0.
terms.seminal_citation: Kaiser, H. F. (1970). A second generation little jiffy. Psychometrika, 35(4), 401–415. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02291817; Kaiser, H. F. (1974). An index of factorial simplicity. Psychometrika, 39(1), 31–36. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02291575
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) according to Hair et al. (2018); Hair et al. (2018); Kaiser (1974); Hair et al. (2018).
terms.benchmarks: Thang đo đánh giá KMO của Kaiser (1974): (1) KMO ≥ 0.90: Rất tuyệt vời (Marvelous); (2) 0.80 ≤ KMO < 0.90: Tốt (Meritorious); (3) 0.70 ≤ KMO < 0.80: Trung bình khá (Middling); (4) 0.60 ≤ KMO < 0.70: Tạm chấp nhận (Mediocre); (5) 0.50 ≤ KMO < 0.60: Đáng thất vọng (Miserable); (6) KMO < 0.50: Không thể chấp nhận (Unacceptable - cấm chạy EFA). Bắt buộc KMO ≥ 0.60 (lý tưởng ≥ 0.70).
terms.pitfalls: Chạy EFA khi KMO < 0.50 dẫn đến việc trích xuất các nhân tố giả tạo từ ma trận tương quan rời rạc; chỉ báo cáo KMO toàn thể mà không kiểm tra chỉ số KMO cho từng biến riêng lẻ trên đường chéo của ma trận phản hình ảnh (Anti-image correlation matrix MSA phải ≥ 0.50).
terms.apa_reference: Kaiser, H. F. (1974). An index of factorial simplicity. Psychometrika, 39(1), 31–36.

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số đo lường độ phù hợp mẫu Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO)
vietnamese_variants: Chỉ số KMO trong phân tích nhân tố
terms.core_definition: The Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) Measure of Sampling Adequacy, formulated by Henry F. Kaiser (1970, 1974) based on work with Rice and Meyer, is an essential diagnostic statistic computed prior to conducting Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) or Principal Component Analysis (PCA). It quantifies the proportion of variance among observed variables that might be common variance caused by underlying latent factors, as opposed to unique error variance. KMO evaluates whether the pattern of pairwise correlations and partial correlations among variables justifies factoring.
terms.seminal_citation: Kaiser, H. F. (1974). An index of factorial simplicity. Psychometrika, 39(1), 31-36.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin Measure (KMO) according to Kaiser (1974).
terms.operational_mechanism: The overall KMO index is calculated using bivariate correlation coefficients r_{ij} and partial correlation coefficients a_{ij} (controlling for all other variables): KMO = [ sum_{i != j} r_{ij}^2 ] / [ sum_{i != j} r_{ij}^2 + sum_{i != j} a_{ij}^2 ]. When latent common factors exist, the partial correlations a_{ij} approximate zero because common factor variance has been partialled out, driving the ratio KMO toward 1.0. Individual KMO values for each variable (diagonal elements of anti-image correlation matrix) are also evaluated.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The overall KMO index is calculated using bivariate correlation coefficients r_{ij} and partial correlation coefficients a_{ij} (controlling for all other variables): KMO = [ sum_{i != j} r_{ij}^2 ] / [ sum_{i != j} r_{ij}^2 + sum_{i != j} a_{ij}^2 ]. When latent common factors exist, the partial correlations a_{ij} approximate zero because common factor variance has been partialled out, driving the ratio KMO toward 1.0. Individual KMO values for each variable (diagonal elements of anti-image correlation matrix) are also evaluated.
terms.benchmarks: Kaiser's (1974) canonical evaluation scale: (1) KMO >= 0.90: Marvelous; (2) 0.80 <= KMO < 0.90: Meritorious (highly adequate); (3) 0.70 <= KMO < 0.80: Middling (acceptable); (4) 0.60 <= KMO < 0.70: Mediocre (marginal); (5) 0.50 <= KMO < 0.60: Miserable; (6) KMO < 0.50: Unacceptable (factor analysis should NOT be conducted); (7) Individual item anti-image correlations must exceed 0.50 (items with KMO_i < 0.50 must be eliminated).
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Running factor analysis when KMO < 0.60, producing uninterpretable factor solutions; (2) Reporting overall KMO without inspecting anti-image correlation diagonals for problematic individual items; and (3) Relying solely on Bartlett's Test of Sphericity (which is hypersensitive to large samples) without confirming adequate KMO.
terms.apa_reference: Kaiser, H. F. (1974). An index of factorial simplicity. Psychometrika, 39(1), 31–36. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02291575

terms.vietnamese: Thuật toán lọc Kalman (Mô hình chuỗi thời gian không gian trạng thái)
vietnamese_variants: Thuật toán ước lượng Kalman filter
Lọc hồi quy trạng thái Kalman
terms.core_definition: The Kalman Filter, formulated by Rudolf E. Kálmán (1960), is an optimal recursive mathematical algorithm used in time-series econometrics, quantitative finance, and aerospace engineering to estimate unobservable, latent dynamic state variables from noisy, observed time-series measurements. Formulated within a State-Space representation, the Kalman filter operates through a continuous predict-update cycle, generating the Best Linear Unbiased Estimate (BLUE) of the underlying state under Gaussian error distributions.
terms.seminal_citation: Kalman, R. E. (1960). A new approach to linear filtering and prediction problems. Journal of Basic Engineering, 82(1), 35-45.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kalman Filter Algorithm according to Kalman (1960).
terms.operational_mechanism: The State-Space system is specified by two equations: (1) State Equation (Transition): alpha_t = T_t * alpha_{t-1} + R_t * eta_t, where eta_t ~ N(0, Q_t); (2) Measurement Equation (Observation): y_t = Z_t * alpha_t + d_t + epsilon_t, where epsilon_t ~ N(0, H_t). The algorithm executes recursively: (a) Time Update (Predict): Project the state forward a_{t|t-1} = T_t * a_{t-1} and compute projected covariance P_{t|t-1}; (b) Measurement Update (Correct): Calculate prediction error v_t = y_t - Z_t * a_{t|t-1} and Kalman Gain K_t = P_{t|t-1} * Z_t' * F_t^{-1}; (c) Update state estimate a_{t|t} = a_{t|t-1} + K_t * v_t and covariance P_{t|t}.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The State-Space system is specified by two equations: (1) State Equation (Transition): alpha_t = T_t * alpha_{t-1} + R_t * eta_t, where eta_t ~ N(0, Q_t); (2) Measurement Equation (Observation): y_t = Z_t * alpha_t + d_t + epsilon_t, where epsilon_t ~ N(0, H_t). The algorithm executes recursively: (a) Time Update (Predict): Project the state forward a_{t|t-1} = T_t * a_{t-1} and compute projected covariance P_{t|t-1}; (b) Measurement Update (Correct): Calculate prediction error v_t = y_t - Z_t * a_{t|t-1} and Kalman Gain K_t = P_{t|t-1} * Z_t' * F_t^{-1}; (c) Update state estimate a_{t|t} = a_{t|t-1} + K_t * v_t and covariance P_{t|t}.
terms.benchmarks: Econometric applications: (1) Estimating unobserved macro concepts: Natural rate of interest (r*), Time-Varying Non-Accelerating Inflation Rate of Unemployment (NAIRU), and time-varying CAPM betas; (2) Hyperparameters estimated via Maximum Likelihood using the prediction error decomposition; (3) Convergence: Kalman gain stabilizes to a steady state in stationary systems.
terms.pitfalls: Common econometric errors: (1) Applying the standard linear Kalman filter to non-linear dynamic models without transitioning to the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) or Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF); (2) Severe sensitivity to poor initial priors (a_0, P_0) in short time series; and (3) Violating the assumption of mutually uncorrelated measurement and transition errors.
terms.apa_reference: Kalman, R. E. (1960). A new approach to linear filtering and prediction problems. Journal of Basic Engineering, 82(1), 35–45. https://doi.org/10.1115/1.3662552

terms.vietnamese: Đường cong sinh tồn Kaplan-Meier (Ước lượng tích số giới hạn)
terms.core_definition: The Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve, developed by Edward L. Kaplan and Paul Meier (1958), is a non-parametric statistic used to estimate the survival function S(t)—the probability of surviving past time t—from time-to-event longitudinal data. Its transformative breakthrough is the mathematical accommodation of right-censoring (when subjects drop out, are lost to follow-up, or remain event-free when the study ends), providing an unconfounded, stepwise graphical trajectory of survival probability over time.
terms.seminal_citation: Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 53(282), 457-481.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kaplan-Meier Curve according to Kaplan & Meier (1958).
terms.operational_mechanism: The Kaplan-Meier product-limit formula calculates survival as the cumulative product of conditional survival probabilities at each discrete event time t_i: hat{S}(t) = prod_{t_i <= t} [ 1 - (d_i / n_i) ], where d_i is the number of events (deaths, failures, customer churns) occurring at time t_i, and n_i is the number of subjects at risk just prior to t_i (excluding individuals previously censored or experienced event). Plotted as a declining step function with vertical ticks representing censored observations. Between-group differences are statistically evaluated via the non-parametric Log-Rank Test.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The Kaplan-Meier product-limit formula calculates survival as the cumulative product of conditional survival probabilities at each discrete event time t_i: hat{S}(t) = prod_{t_i <= t} [ 1 - (d_i / n_i) ], where d_i is the number of events (deaths, failures, customer churns) occurring at time t_i, and n_i is the number of subjects at risk just prior to t_i (excluding individuals previously censored or experienced event). Plotted as a declining step function with vertical ticks representing censored observations. Between-group differences are statistically evaluated via the non-parametric Log-Rank Test.
terms.benchmarks: Biostatistical and reporting standards (CONSORT): (1) Displaying a 'Number at Risk' table positioned beneath the horizontal time axis at key intervals (e.g., Year 1, 2, 3); (2) Reporting Median Survival Time with 95% Greenwood confidence intervals; (3) Log-rank test p < 0.05 confirming statistically significant survival divergence between treatment arms.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Violating the uninformative censoring assumption (assuming censored patients have the same survival prognosis as continuing patients; if frail patients drop out, Kaplan-Meier overestimates survival); (2) Truncating curves at very long follow-up times when few patients remain at risk (n_i < 10), creating deceptive wide steps; and (3) Using Kaplan-Meier to adjust for continuous covariates (which requires Cox proportional hazards modeling).
terms.apa_reference: Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 53(282), 457–481. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452

terms.vietnamese: Ước lượng Kaplan-Meier
vietnamese_variants: Ước lượng tích số giới hạn
terms.core_definition: Ước lượng Kaplan-Meier (Kaplan & Meier, 1958) là phương pháp phi tham số chuẩn mực để ước lượng hàm xác suất sống sót S(t) theo thời gian trong dữ liệu thời gian dẫn đến biến cố (time-to-event). Phương pháp này xử lý tối ưu hiện tượng kiểm duyệt phải (right-censoring) — tình trạng một số cá thể rời bỏ nghiên cứu hoặc chưa gặp biến cố tại thời điểm kết thúc quan sát — mà không cần đặt bất kỳ giả định nào về phân phối thời gian.
terms.seminal_citation: Kaplan & Meier (1958)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kaplan-Meier Estimator according to Kaplan & Meier (1958).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Sắp xếp các thời điểm xảy ra biến cố theo thứ tự tăng dần: t_1 < t_2 < ... < t_k. 2. Tại mỗi thời điểm t_i, ghi nhận số lượng đối tượng có nguy cơ (risk set) n_i và số lượng biến cố thực tế d_i. 3. Xác suất sống sót có điều kiện tại t_i là (1 - d_i / n_i). 4. Hàm sống sót tích lũy S(t) là tích của các xác suất sống sót điều kiện tại mọi thời điểm t_i ≤ t: S_hat(t) = prod_{t_i ≤ t} (1 - d_i / n_i).
terms.benchmarks: Được hiển thị trực quan qua đường cong sống sót Kaplan-Meier bậc thang (step-function survival curve). So sánh giữa hai hoặc nhiều nhóm độc lập bằng kiểm định Log-Rank (Mantel-Cox test); sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê khi p-value < 0.05. Báo cáo trung vị thời gian sống sót (Median Survival Time) kèm khoảng tin cậy 95% theo công thức Greenwood.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: (1) Diễn giải sai về số lượng đối tượng ở đuôi đường cong: Khi thời gian càng dài, số lượng đối tượng có nguy cơ n_i giảm mạnh khiến sai số chuẩn bùng nổ; (2) Giả định kiểm duyệt độc lập (informative censoring): Nếu việc rời bỏ nghiên cứu có liên quan đến nguy cơ gặp biến cố, ước lượng Kaplan-Meier sẽ bị chệch tham số.
terms.apa_reference: Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 53(282), 457–481. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số tương quan hạng Kendall's Tau (Tau-b và Tau-c)
terms.core_definition: Hệ số tương quan hạng Kendall's Tau (Kendall, 1938) là thước đo phi tham số đo lường mức độ liên kết thứ bậc giữa hai biến số dựa trên số lượng các cặp quan sát thuận hòa (concordant pairs) và nghịch hòa (discordant pairs). So với Spearman's Rho, Kendall's Tau có các thuộc tính thống kê vượt trội hơn: Phân phối mẫu tiệm cận chuẩn nhanh hơn nhiều và diễn giải xác suất trực tiếp hơn (hiệu số xác suất đồng thuận trừ bất đồng thuận).
terms.seminal_citation: Kendall (1938); Stuart (1953)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kendall's Tau (Tau-b & Tau-c) according to Kendall (1938).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Xét toàn bộ n · (n - 1)/2 cặp quan sát: Cặp là thuận hòa nếu (x_i - x_j) · (y_i - y_j) > 0; là nghịch hòa nếu < 0. 2. Tau-a: Dùng khi không có hạng buộc: Τ_a = (C - D) / [n · (n-1)/2]. 3. Tau-b: Hiệu chỉnh cho ma trận vuông có hạng buộc (ties): Τ_b = (C - D) / √((C + D + T_x) · (C + D + T_y)). 4. Tau-c (Stuart-Kendall Tau-c): Dùng riêng cho các bảng chéo kích thước hình chữ nhật (m × r với m ≠ r).
terms.benchmarks: Giá trị Tau nằm trong khoảng [-1, 1]. Thông thường, giá trị số tuyệt đối của Kendall's Tau nhỏ hơn Spearman's Rho từ 20-30% trên cùng một tập dữ liệu (ví dụ τ = 0.40 thường tương đương Spearman = 0.55-0.60). Bác bỏ H0 khi p-value < 0.05.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Sử dụng Tau-b cho bảng chéo hình chữ nhật không vuông (ví dụ biến X có 3 mức, biến Y có 5 mức). Khi bảng không vuông, Tau-b không bao giờ đạt được giá trị cực đại +/-1.0; trường hợp này bắt buộc phải sử dụng Tau-c của Stuart (1953).
terms.apa_reference: Kendall, M. G. (1938). A new measure of rank correlation. Biometrika, 30(1/2), 81–93. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/30.1-2.81

terms.vietnamese: Ước lượng mật độ hàm nhân (Phương pháp làm mịn phi tham số KDE)
vietnamese_variants: Ước lượng mật độ phi tham số
terms.core_definition: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE), pioneered by Murray Rosenblatt (1956) and Emanuel Parzen (1962), is a foundational non-parametric statistical technique used to estimate the continuous probability density function (PDF) of a random variable from discrete sample data. Overcoming the severe discretization flaws of classical histograms (which depend arbitrarily on bin widths and bin origin points), KDE produces a smooth, continuous, and mathematically differentiable density curve that exposes underlying multimodality, skewness, and heavy-tailed distribution structures.
terms.seminal_citation: Parzen, E. (1962). On estimation of a probability density function and mode. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 33(3), 1065-1076.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) according to Rosenblatt (1956), Parzen (1962).
terms.operational_mechanism: Given a sample of n observations x_1, x_2, ..., x_n, the kernel density estimate at any point x is defined as: hat{f}_h(x) = [1 / (n * h)] * sum_{i=1}^n K( (x - x_i) / h ), where K(u) is a non-negative, symmetric kernel function integrating to 1 (e.g., Gaussian, Epanechnikov, Triangular), and h > 0 is the bandwidth (smoothing parameter). The choice of bandwidth h is mathematically decisive: small h creates undersmoothed, noisy spikes; large h causes oversmoothing that masks true bimodal peaks. Optimal bandwidth is chosen via Silverman's rule of thumb or plug-in cross-validation methods.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Given a sample of n observations x_1, x_2, ..., x_n, the kernel density estimate at any point x is defined as: hat{f}_h(x) = [1 / (n * h)] * sum_{i=1}^n K( (x - x_i) / h ), where K(u) is a non-negative, symmetric kernel function integrating to 1 (e.g., Gaussian, Epanechnikov, Triangular), and h > 0 is the bandwidth (smoothing parameter). The choice of bandwidth h is mathematically decisive: small h creates undersmoothed, noisy spikes; large h causes oversmoothing that masks true bimodal peaks. Optimal bandwidth is chosen via Silverman's rule of thumb or plug-in cross-validation methods.
terms.benchmarks: Technical evaluation standards: (1) Epanechnikov kernel minimizes mean integrated squared error (MISE), though the Gaussian kernel is universally preferred for visual smoothness; (2) Bandwidth selection: Silverman's rule h = 0.9 * min(s, IQR/1.34) * n^{-1/5} serves as standard baseline; (3) Multimodality testing via Silverman's bootstrap test.
terms.pitfalls: Common analytical traps: (1) Boundary bias: KDE smears probability mass across natural boundaries when data are strictly positive (e.g., income > 0), requiring log transformation or boundary kernel adjustments; (2) Subjective manual bandwidth tweaking to force a desired multi-peaked appearance; and (3) Overlooking that sample size n affects bandwidth shrinkage rate.
terms.apa_reference: Parzen, E. (1962). On estimation of a probability density function and mode. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 33(3), 1065–1076. https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177704472

terms.vietnamese: Ghi nhận thao tác gõ phím (Nghiên cứu tiến trình viết học thuật)
vietnamese_variants: Theo dõi tiến trình gõ phím
terms.core_definition: Keystroke Logging is an unobtrusive digital research methodology in cognitive linguistics, translation studies, and academic writing research that records the precise temporal micro-actions of a writer during text production. Using specialized background software (such as Inputlog or ScriptLog), keystroke logging captures every individual keystroke, mouse click, cursor movement, revision event, deletion, and cognitive pause length in milliseconds, transforming writing from an invisible private process into an empirically measurable behavioral sequence.
terms.seminal_citation: Leijten, M., & Van Waes, L. (2013). Keystroke logging in writing research: Using Inputlog to analyze and visualize writing processes. Written Communication, 30(3), 358-392.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Keystroke logging according to Wiley / Beatty & Willis (2020); Wiley (2020).
terms.operational_mechanism: Execution follows four analytical dimensions (Leijten & Van Waes, 2013): (1) Temporal Logging: Recording precise timestamps of key presses and releases; (2) Pause Analysis: Detecting cognitive pauses exceeding pre-defined thresholds (e.g., 200ms for motor pauses, 1,000ms to 2,000ms for cognitive planning/formulation pauses); (3) Linear vs. Non-linear Revision: Distinguishing immediate local revisions (backspacing) from distant structural revisions throughout the document; (4) Triangulation: Synchronizing keystroke logs with eye-tracking gaze fixation data and retrospective cued think-aloud protocols.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Execution follows four analytical dimensions (Leijten & Van Waes, 2013): (1) Temporal Logging: Recording precise timestamps of key presses and releases; (2) Pause Analysis: Detecting cognitive pauses exceeding pre-defined thresholds (e.g., 200ms for motor pauses, 1,000ms to 2,000ms for cognitive planning/formulation pauses); (3) Linear vs. Non-linear Revision: Distinguishing immediate local revisions (backspacing) from distant structural revisions throughout the document; (4) Triangulation: Synchronizing keystroke logs with eye-tracking gaze fixation data and retrospective cued think-aloud protocols.
terms.benchmarks: Empirical standards: (1) Cognitive load indicators: Pauses located at sentence and paragraph boundaries reflect macro-level planning, whereas frequent mid-word pauses signal lexical retrieval difficulties or working memory overload; (2) S-burst metric: Measuring the length of fluent text production bursts between pauses; (3) Non-intrusive setup: Ensuring software introduces zero visible latency to participant typing.
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Setting arbitrary pause thresholds without cognitive theoretical justification; (2) Analyzing massive quantitative log dumps without qualitative textual context; and (3) Failing to secure explicit ethical informed consent for capturing participant keystrokes (which can capture passwords or sensitive personal communications).
terms.apa_reference: Leijten, M., & Van Waes, L. (2013). Keystroke logging in writing research: Using Inputlog to analyze and visualize writing processes. Written Communication, 30(3), 358–392. https://doi.org/10.1177/0741088313491692

terms.term: Methodological Limitations of Baron & Kenny (1986) 4-Step Mediation
terms.vietnamese: Khắc phục hạn chế của phương pháp trung gian 4 bước Baron & Kenny (1986)
vietnamese_variants: Phê phán mô hình Baron and Kenny
Modern mediation alternatives to Baron & Kenny
terms.core_definition: The Methodological Limitations of Baron and Kenny's (1986) 4-Step Mediation Approach encompasses the critical econometric, mathematical, and power flaws identified by modern methodologists (Preacher & Hayes, 2004, 2008; Zhao, Lynch, & Chen, 2010; Hayes, 2022). Once the standard framework for testing mediation, the Baron and Kenny approach is now widely considered outdated and obsolete in top Q1 journals due to its reliance on underpowered causal steps, its erroneous requirement of a significant total effect (Step 1), and its vulnerability to severe Type II errors.
terms.seminal_citation: Zhao, X., Lynch, J. G., & Chen, Q. (2010). Reconsidering Baron and Kenny: Myths and truths about mediation analysis. Journal of Consumer Research, 37(2), 197-206.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Khắc phục hạn chế của phương pháp 4 bước Baron & Kenny (1986) according to Hayes (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism: Three fatal flaws and modern solutions: (1) The Step 1 Fallacy: Baron & Kenny mandate that the total effect of X on Y (path c) must be statistically significant. Zhao et al. (2010) prove that when competitive mediation occurs (where direct and indirect effects have opposite signs, e.g., a * b is positive while c' is negative), the total effect can be exactly zero, causing Baron & Kenny to falsely conclude zero mediation; (2) Low Statistical Power: Testing mediation through a series of discrete significance gates multiplies Type II error rates; (3) The Sobel Test Flaw: The Sobel test assumes the sampling distribution of the indirect effect (a * b) is normal, whereas the product of two normal variables is heavily skewed and leptokurtic. Modern standard: Non-parametric bootstrapping (5,000+ resamples) directly evaluating the indirect effect a * b.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Three fatal flaws and modern solutions: (1) The Step 1 Fallacy: Baron & Kenny mandate that the total effect of X on Y (path c) must be statistically significant. Zhao et al. (2010) prove that when competitive mediation occurs (where direct and indirect effects have opposite signs, e.g., a * b is positive while c' is negative), the total effect can be exactly zero, causing Baron & Kenny to falsely conclude zero mediation; (2) Low Statistical Power: Testing mediation through a series of discrete significance gates multiplies Type II error rates; (3) The Sobel Test Flaw: The Sobel test assumes the sampling distribution of the indirect effect (a * b) is normal, whereas the product of two normal variables is heavily skewed and leptokurtic. Modern standard: Non-parametric bootstrapping (5,000+ resamples) directly evaluating the indirect effect a * b.
terms.benchmarks: Modern editorial benchmarks (JAP, JCR, AMJ): (1) Mandatory replacement of Baron & Kenny with bootstrapped indirect effect testing (e.g., Hayes' PROCESS macro, lavaan in R, or SEM); (2) Reporting 95% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals for the indirect effect; (3) Rejection of manuscripts using the 4-step approach without bootstrapping.
terms.pitfalls: Critical reviewer rejection traps: (1) Claiming 'no mediation exists' simply because path c was non-significant in Step 1; (2) Reporting Sobel test p-values instead of bootstrapped confidence intervals; and (3) Asserting 'full mediation' without testing alternative indirect pathways or omitted confounders.
terms.apa_reference: Zhao, X., Lynch, J. G., & Chen, Q. (2010). Reconsidering Baron and Kenny: Myths and truths about mediation analysis. Journal of Consumer Research, 37(2), 197–206. https://doi.org/10.1086/651257

terms.vietnamese: Khung 4 loại độ giá trị nghiên cứu (Shadish, Cook & Campbell)
vietnamese_variants: Bộ tứ độ giá trị SCC
Bốn loại tính hợp lệ trong nghiên cứu
terms.core_definition: The Four Validities Typology is the authoritative meta-theoretical framework for evaluating the truth-value and inferential rigor of empirical social science investigations, formulated by Donald T. Campbell and systematically synthesized by William R. Shadish, Thomas D. Cook, and Donald T. Campbell (2002). Rather than viewing 'validity' as a vague monolithic concept, the typology partitions research quality across four distinct, interrelated, and often competing dimensions: Statistical Conclusion Validity, Internal Validity, Construct Validity, and External Validity.
terms.seminal_citation: Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.
terms.expert_notes: Tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Khung 4 Loại Tính Hợp lệ (The 4 Validities Typology) according to Shadish, Cook & Campbell (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism: The four distinct validity tiers operate as follows: (1) Statistical Conclusion Validity: Is there a statistically significant covariation between the presumed cause and effect, and how large is it? (Focuses on statistical power, fishing, and assumption violations); (2) Internal Validity: Is the observed covariation causally unconfounded, or could it be produced by rival extraneous threats? (Focuses on history, maturation, selection, attrition); (3) Construct Validity: Do the operationalized manipulations and measurement instruments genuinely represent the theoretical concepts they claim to embody? (Focuses on mono-operation bias, confounding constructs); (4) External Validity: Can the causal relationship generalize across different persons, settings, treatment variations, and historical times?
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The four distinct validity tiers operate as follows: (1) Statistical Conclusion Validity: Is there a statistically significant covariation between the presumed cause and effect, and how large is it? (Focuses on statistical power, fishing, and assumption violations); (2) Internal Validity: Is the observed covariation causally unconfounded, or could it be produced by rival extraneous threats? (Focuses on history, maturation, selection, attrition); (3) Construct Validity: Do the operationalized manipulations and measurement instruments genuinely represent the theoretical concepts they claim to embody? (Focuses on mono-operation bias, confounding constructs); (4) External Validity: Can the causal relationship generalize across different persons, settings, treatment variations, and historical times?
terms.benchmarks: Methodological trade-off standards: (1) Inevitable Trade-offs: Tightly controlled laboratory experiments maximize Internal Validity at the expense of External Validity; naturalistic field studies maximize External Validity while compromising Internal Validity; (2) Programmatic research sequences: Beginning with high internal validity laboratory designs to isolate mechanisms, followed by field quasi-experiments to establish external generalizability.
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors: (1) Conflating Internal Validity with Construct Validity (a study can prove X caused Y with zero confounding, yet completely mislabel what psychological construct X actually represents); (2) Claiming broad external validity from a single unrepresentative student sample; and (3) Overlooking statistical conclusion validity threats such as uncorrected multiple testing.
terms.apa_reference: Shadish, W. R., Cook, T. D., & Campbell, D. T. (2002). Experimental and quasi-experimental designs for generalized causal inference. Houghton Mifflin.

terms.term: Measurement Invariance Testing (Configural, Metric, Scalar Invariance)
terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định bất biến đo lường (Bất biến cấu hình, Hệ số tải, Điểm chặn)
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định tính bất biến đo lường
Bất biến đo lường đa nhóm MGCFA
terms.core_definition: Measurement Invariance Testing (or Measurement Equivalence) is a mandatory psychometric procedure in structural equation modeling (Multi-Group Confirmatory Factor Analysis / MGCFA, or MICOM in PLS-SEM) used to verify whether a measurement instrument assesses the exact same latent construct in the exact same mathematical metric across different demographic groups (e.g., gender, nationality, cultures) or across multiple longitudinal time points. Without establishing measurement invariance, observed group differences in scale scores cannot be interpreted as genuine differences in the underlying construct, but may merely reflect cultural response bias or translation artifacts.
terms.seminal_citation: Vandenberg, R. J., & Lance, C. E. (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for organizational research. Organizational Research Methods, 3(1), 4-70.
terms.expert_notes: Tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kiểm định Bất biến Đo lường (Measurement Invariance) according to MacKenzie et al. (2011).
terms.operational_mechanism: Testing proceeds through a hierarchical sequence of nested model comparisons with increasingly restrictive parameter equality constraints: (1) Configural Invariance: Verifies that the same pattern of factor loadings exists across groups (same basic factor structure without equality constraints); (2) Metric Invariance (Weak Invariance): Constrains factor loadings to be equal across groups (Lambda_1 = Lambda_2); required to validly compare regression slopes and structural relationships across groups; (3) Scalar Invariance (Strong Invariance): Constrains both factor loadings AND indicator intercepts (tau_1 = tau_2) to be equal; MANDATORY before comparing latent factor means across groups; (4) Strict Invariance: Constrains residual error variances to be equal.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Testing proceeds through a hierarchical sequence of nested model comparisons with increasingly restrictive parameter equality constraints: (1) Configural Invariance: Verifies that the same pattern of factor loadings exists across groups (same basic factor structure without equality constraints); (2) Metric Invariance (Weak Invariance): Constrains factor loadings to be equal across groups (Lambda_1 = Lambda_2); required to validly compare regression slopes and structural relationships across groups; (3) Scalar Invariance (Strong Invariance): Constrains both factor loadings AND indicator intercepts (tau_1 = tau_2) to be equal; MANDATORY before comparing latent factor means across groups; (4) Strict Invariance: Constrains residual error variances to be equal.
terms.benchmarks: Cheung and Rensvold (2002) and Chen (2007) model evaluation cutoffs: Because the chi-square difference test (Delta Chi^2) is overly sensitive in large samples, invariance is established if: (1) Metric Invariance: Change in CFI <= 0.010, paired with change in RMSEA <= 0.015 or change in SRMR <= 0.030; (2) Scalar Invariance: Change in CFI <= 0.010, paired with change in RMSEA <= 0.015 or change in SRMR <= 0.015; (3) Partial Invariance: If full scalar invariance fails, at least two items per construct must retain invariant loadings and intercepts.
terms.pitfalls: Fatal cross-cultural errors: (1) Comparing latent or observed group means (e.g., cross-country cultural comparisons) after establishing only metric invariance, which is mathematically invalid and triggers immediate rejection; (2) Relying exclusively on Delta Chi^2 in samples N > 500; and (3) Ignoring partial invariance when only one non-essential item violates intercept equality.
terms.apa_reference: Vandenberg, R. J., & Lance, C. E. (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for organizational research. Organizational Research Methods, 3(1), 4–70. https://doi.org/10.1177/109442810031002

terms.term: HTMT Statistical Inference Test (Bootstrapped Discriminant Validity)
terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định suy luận thống kê HTMT (Độ giá trị phân biệt qua Bootstrap)
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định suy diễn HTMT inference
Kiểm định khoảng tin cậy HTMT
terms.core_definition: The HTMT Statistical Inference Test (HTMT_inference) is the formal inferential procedure developed by Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2015) to statistically test the null hypothesis that the true correlation between two latent constructs is equal to 1.0 (H_0: HTMT >= 1.0) using non-parametric bootstrap resampling. By generating empirical confidence intervals for each pairwise Heterotrait-Monotrait ratio, the test provides statistical proof that two constructs are empirically distinct rather than relying solely on sample-specific point estimates.
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kiểm định Suy luận Thống kê (HTMT inference test) according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism: Testing protocol: (1) Resample the original empirical dataset B = 5,000 to 10,000 times with replacement; (2) Compute the HTMT correlation ratio for every pair of reflective constructs in each bootstrap draw; (3) Construct a 95% one-sided or 90% two-sided bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence interval [CI_{lower}, CI_{upper}]; (4) Decision rule: If the upper confidence interval bound CI_{upper} is strictly less than 1.0 (or less than the conservative 0.85 / 0.90 thresholds), the null hypothesis of construct identity is rejected, and discriminant validity is statistically established.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: Testing protocol: (1) Resample the original empirical dataset B = 5,000 to 10,000 times with replacement; (2) Compute the HTMT correlation ratio for every pair of reflective constructs in each bootstrap draw; (3) Construct a 95% one-sided or 90% two-sided bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap confidence interval [CI_{lower}, CI_{upper}]; (4) Decision rule: If the upper confidence interval bound CI_{upper} is strictly less than 1.0 (or less than the conservative 0.85 / 0.90 thresholds), the null hypothesis of construct identity is rejected, and discriminant validity is statistically established.
terms.benchmarks: Inferential cutoffs (Hair et al., 2022): (1) Baseline requirement: Upper bound of the 95% bootstrap CI must not include the value 1.0; (2) Conservative standard: Upper bound does not exceed 0.85 for conceptually distinct constructs; (3) Liberal standard: Upper bound does not exceed 0.90 for conceptually related constructs; (4) Reporting table: Displaying both the HTMT point estimate and the [CI_{lower}, CI_{upper}] interval for every construct pair.
terms.pitfalls: Common reporting errors: (1) Concluding discriminant validity is supported when the point estimate is 0.82 but the upper 95% CI bound reaches 0.92; (2) Running bootstrap inference with fewer than 5,000 resamples; and (3) Applying HTMT inference to formative constructs.
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115–135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8

terms.vietnamese: Thống kê rk LM của Kleibergen-Paap (Kiểm định thiếu định danh)
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định hạng ma trận công cụ Kleibergen-Paap
terms.core_definition: The Kleibergen-Paap rk LM Statistic, developed by Frank Kleibergen and Richard Paap (2006), is an econometric diagnostic test for underidentification in Instrumental Variables (IV / 2SLS) and Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimation when error disturbances are heteroscedastic, serially correlated, or clustered. Testing the null hypothesis that the matrix of reduced-form coefficients on the excluded instruments has rank deficiency (rank(Pi) = K - 1), a statistically significant statistic (p < 0.05) proves that the model is identified—meaning the instruments are relevant and correlate with the endogenous regressors even under non-spherical error conditions.
terms.seminal_citation: Kleibergen, F., & Paap, R. (2006). Generalized reduced rank tests using the singular value decomposition. Journal of Econometrics, 133(1), 97-126.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kleibergen-Paap rk LM Statistic according to Kleibergen & Paap (2006).
terms.operational_mechanism: In the linear IV model with K endogenous regressors and L excluded instruments (L >= K): (1) The first-stage equation matrix is X = Z * Pi + V; (2) Under homoscedasticity, underidentification is tested via Anderson's canonical correlations LM test; (3) When errors are non-spherical (clustered, heteroscedastic), Anderson's test is invalid, and the Kleibergen-Paap rk statistic generalizes the test by using a singular value decomposition (SVD) of the rank-deficient parameter matrix with a heteroskedasticity-robust covariance estimator; (4) The resulting rk LM test statistic is distributed asymptotically as Chi^2 with degrees of freedom df = (L - K + 1).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: In the linear IV model with K endogenous regressors and L excluded instruments (L >= K): (1) The first-stage equation matrix is X = Z * Pi + V; (2) Under homoscedasticity, underidentification is tested via Anderson's canonical correlations LM test; (3) When errors are non-spherical (clustered, heteroscedastic), Anderson's test is invalid, and the Kleibergen-Paap rk statistic generalizes the test by using a singular value decomposition (SVD) of the rank-deficient parameter matrix with a heteroskedasticity-robust covariance estimator; (4) The resulting rk LM test statistic is distributed asymptotically as Chi^2 with degrees of freedom df = (L - K + 1).
terms.benchmarks: Diagnostic standards in top economics and finance journals: (1) Rejection of null hypothesis: p < 0.05 (preferably p < 0.01) confirming that the model satisfies identification (rank condition is fulfilled); (2) Companion test: Must be paired with the Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F-statistic for weak instrument testing (benchmarked against Stock-Yogo critical values); (3) Standard output in Stata 'ivreg2' and R 'ivmodel'.
terms.pitfalls: Common econometric errors: (1) Reporting Anderson's LM test instead of Kleibergen-Paap when using robust or clustered standard errors (Anderson assumes homoscedasticity); (2) Confusing underidentification (instruments have zero correlation with regressors) with weak identification (instruments have weak correlation); and (3) Failing to report the Kleibergen-Paap statistic in 2SLS regression tables.
terms.apa_reference: Kleibergen, F., & Paap, R. (2006). Generalized reduced rank tests using the singular value decomposition. Journal of Econometrics, 133(1), 97–126. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.02.011

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định Kolmogorov-Smirnov
vietnamese_variants: Kiểm định hàm phân phối thực nghiệm
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định Kolmogorov-Smirnov (Kolmogorov, 1933; Smirnov, 1948) là phép kiểm định phi tham số kinh điển dùng để so sánh hàm phân phối tích lũy thực nghiệm (Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function - ECDF) của một mẫu dữ liệu với một phân phối lý thuyết xác định (One-sample K-S), hoặc so sánh ECDF giữa hai mẫu độc lập (Two-sample K-S).
terms.seminal_citation: Kolmogorov (1933); Smirnov (1948); Lilliefors (1967)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test according to Smirnov (1948).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Xây dựng hàm phân phối tích lũy thực nghiệm F_n(x) = (số lượng quan sát ≤ x) / n. 2. Thống kê kiểm định D là khoảng cách khoảng cách thẳng đứng lớn nhất (supremum distance) giữa F_n(x) và hàm phân phối lý thuyết F_0(x): D = sup_x |F_n(x) - F_0(x)|. 3. So sánh D với phân phối Kolmogorov để tính p-value.
terms.benchmarks: Giả thuyết H0: Mẫu dữ liệu tuân theo phân phối lý thuyết xác định (hoặc hai mẫu độc lập có cùng phân phối quần thể). Nếu p-value ≥ 0.05: Không thể bác bỏ H0, khẳng định hai phân phối tương đồng. Nếu p-value < 0.05: Bác bỏ H0, hai phân phối có sự khác biệt có ý nghĩa thống kê.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Sử dụng kiểm định K-S một mẫu chuẩn để kiểm định phân phối chuẩn khi các tham số trung bình và phương sai được ước lượng từ chính mẫu dữ liệu. Khi đó, kiểm định K-S chuẩn trở nên cực kỳ bảo thủ (p-value bị phóng đại quá mức); bắt buộc phải sử dụng hiệu chỉnh Lilliefors Test.
terms.apa_reference: Lilliefors, H. W. (1967). On the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for normality with mean and variance unknown. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 62(318), 399–402. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1967.10482916

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định Tính Dừng KPSS (Kiểm định Đối nghịch Nghiệm Đơn vị)
domain_tags: Kinh tế lượng Chuỗi thời gian
terms.core_definition: Phép kiểm định tính dừng đột phá trong kinh tế lượng chuỗi thời gian do Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt & Shin (1992) đề xuất. Điểm khác biệt mang tính cách mạng của KPSS so với ADF và Phillips-Perron là việc ĐẢO NGƯỢC GIẢ THUYẾT: Giả thuyết vô hiệu H0 của KPSS là 'Chuỗi thời gian là chuỗi dừng (Stationary xung quanh hằng số hoặc xu thế)', trong khi giả thuyết đối H1 là 'Chuỗi có nghiệm đơn vị (Không dừng / I(1))'. KPSS được sử dụng như một phép kiểm tra đối chứng chéo (Confirmatory Analysis) để phân giải những trường hợp ADF/PP đưa ra kết quả không dứt khoát do độ mạnh thống kê yếu.
terms.seminal_citation: Kwiatkowski, D., Phillips, P. C. B., Schmidt, P., & Shin, Y. (1992). Testing the null hypothesis of stationarity against the alternative of a unit root. Journal of Econometrics, 54(1–3), 159–178. https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076(92)90104-Y
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of KPSS according to P-value > 0.05: Không thể bác bỏ H0, xác nhận chuỗi thời gian dừng. Kết hợp ADF và KPSS giúp kiểm định chéo độ tin cậy..
terms.benchmarks: Đánh giá qua giá trị thống kê LM (Lagrange Multiplier): Nếu LM_stat > Critical Value ở mức 5% (hoặc 1%), nhà nghiên cứu BÁC BỎ giả thuyết H0 và kết luận chuỗi không dừng. Nếu LM_stat < Critical Value (p > 0.05), chưa đủ bằng chứng bác bỏ H0, kết luận chuỗi dừng. Phối hợp kết quả chuẩn mực: (1) ADF bác bỏ H0 VÀ KPSS không bác bỏ H0 → Khẳng định tuyệt đối chuỗi là dừng I(0); (2) ADF không bác bỏ H0 VÀ KPSS bác bỏ H0 → Khẳng định tuyệt đối chuỗi không dừng I(1).
terms.pitfalls: Nhầm lẫn giả thuyết H0 của KPSS với ADF (vội vàng kết luận chuỗi dừng khi p < 0.05 trong khi thực chất p < 0.05 của KPSS là bác bỏ tính dừng); không xác định đúng kiểm định dừng quanh mức trung bình (Level stationarity) hay dừng quanh xu thế (Trend stationarity).
terms.apa_reference: Kwiatkowski, D., Phillips, P. C. B., Schmidt, P., & Shin, Y. (1992). Testing the null hypothesis of stationarity against the alternative of a unit root. Journal of Econometrics, 54(1–3), 159–178.

terms.vietnamese: Hệ số Alpha của Krippendorff (Độ tin cậy trong phân tích nội dung)
vietnamese_variants: Hệ số tin cậy mã hóa Krippendorff
terms.core_definition: Krippendorff's Alpha, formulated by Klaus Krippendorff (1970, 2018), is the universally endorsed, most rigorous non-parametric inter-coder reliability statistic for content analysis, text mining, and behavioral observation.
