Far superior to simple percentage agreement and Cohen's Kappa, Krippendorff's alpha seamlessly accommodates any number of coders (from two to hundreds), handles missing data systematically, and generalizes mathematically across nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio, and circular metric scales.
terms.seminal_citation: Krippendorff, K. (2018). Content analysis: An introduction to its methodology (4th ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Krippendorff's Alpha according to Krippendorff (2018).
terms.operational_mechanism: The mathematical formula is: alpha = 1 - (D_o / D_e), where D_o is the observed disagreement among coders and D_e is the expected disagreement by chance. Computation utilizes a coincidence matrix rather than a contingency matrix, pooling all paired comparisons: D_o = (1 / n) * sum_{c} sum_{k} o_{ck} * delta^2(c, k), where delta^2(c, k) is a metric difference function specific to the measurement level (e.g., delta^2 = 1 for nominal difference; delta^2 = (c - k)^2 for interval scales). When agreement is perfect, D_o = 0 and alpha = 1.0; when agreement equals chance, D_o = D_e and alpha = 0.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The mathematical formula is: alpha = 1 - (D_o / D_e), where D_o is the observed disagreement among coders and D_e is the expected disagreement by chance. Computation utilizes a coincidence matrix rather than a contingency matrix, pooling all paired comparisons: D_o = (1 / n) * sum_{c} sum_{k} o_{ck} * delta^2(c, k), where delta^2(c, k) is a metric difference function specific to the measurement level (e.g., delta^2 = 1 for nominal difference; delta^2 = (c - k)^2 for interval scales). When agreement is perfect, D_o = 0 and alpha = 1.0; when agreement equals chance, D_o = D_e and alpha = 0.
terms.benchmarks: Krippendorff's standard thresholds (2018): (1) Customary benchmark for high reliability: alpha >= 0.800 (data are fully dependable for publication); (2) Tentative conclusion threshold: 0.667 <= alpha < 0.800 (acceptable only for exploratory research); (3) Rejection threshold: alpha < 0.667 requires immediate discarding of data, revision of the codebook, and retraining of coders; (4) Minimum pilot sample: At least 10% to 20% of the total dataset independently double-coded.
terms.pitfalls: Critical review rejection traps: (1) Reporting raw percentage agreement instead of Krippendorff's alpha; (2) Treating alpha as a correlation coefficient (alpha measures absolute agreement, not correlation); and (3) Ignoring scale metrics (e.g., treating ordinal Likert codes as nominal categories, which discards ordered distance information).
terms.apa_reference: Krippendorff, K. (2018). Content analysis: An introduction to its methodology (4th ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định Kruskal-Wallis H
vietnamese_variants: ANOVA một yếu tố phi tham số
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định Kruskal-Wallis H (Kruskal & Wallis, 1952) là phép kiểm định phi tham số mở rộng của kiểm định Mann-Whitney U cho trường hợp so sánh từ ba nhóm độc lập trở lên (k ≥ 3). Đây là giải pháp thay thế hoàn hảo cho Phân tích phương sai một yếu tố (One-way ANOVA) khi các giả định về phân phối chuẩn hoặc tính đồng nhất của phương sai bị vi phạm.
terms.seminal_citation: Kruskal & Wallis (1952); Dunn (1964)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kruskal-Wallis H Test according to Kruskal & Wallis (1952).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Gộp toàn bộ N quan sát của k nhóm và xếp hạng chung từ 1 đến N. 2. Tính tổng thứ hạng R_j cho từng nhóm j (với quy mô n_j). 3. Thống kê H: H = [12 / (N · (N + 1))] * ∑_(j=1)ᵏ [R²_j / n_j] - 3 · (N + 1). 4. Hiệu chỉnh hạng buộc: H_adj = H / [ 1 - ∑(t³ - t) / (N³ - N) ]. 5. Thống kê H tuân theo phân phối Chi-bình phương với (k - 1) bậc tự do khi quy mô mẫu đủ lớn (n_j ≥ 5).
terms.benchmarks: Giả thuyết H0: Tất cả k nhóm xuất phát từ cùng một phân phối quần thể. Bác bỏ H0 khi p-value < 0.05. Nếu p < 0.05, bắt buộc tiến hành Phân tích so sánh hậu kiểm (Post-hoc test) bằng Kiểm định Dunn (Dunn's test, 1964) hoặc Conover-Iman kèm hiệu chỉnh đa kiểm định Bonferroni hoặc Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR). Kích thước hiệu ứng Epsilon-bình phương (ε² = (H - k + 1) / (N - k)).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Chạy hàng loạt kiểm định Mann-Whitney U từng cặp sau khi Kruskal-Wallis có ý nghĩa mà không hiệu chỉnh tỷ lệ sai lầm loại I (Family-Wise Error Rate), làm sai lệch kết luận thống kê nghiêm trọng.
terms.apa_reference: Kruskal, W. H., & Wallis, W. A. (1952). Use of ranks in one-criterion variance analysis. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 47(260), 583–621. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1952.10483441

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích phương sai một yếu tố phi tham số
terms.core_definition: Phân tích phương sai một yếu tố phi tham số Kruskal-Wallis là thủ tục kiểm định tương đương với F-test trong ANOVA nhưng vận hành hoàn toàn trên ma trận thứ hạng. Thủ tục kiểm tra xem sự biến thiên của tổng thứ hạng giữa các nhóm có vượt trội một cách có ý nghĩa thống kê so với sự biến thiên ngẫu nhiên bên trong nội bộ các nhóm hay không.
terms.seminal_citation: Kruskal & Wallis (1952); Tomczak & Tomczak (2014)
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kruskal-Wallis one-way ANOVA according to Schindler (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Kiểm tra điều kiện tiên quyết: Biến phụ thuộc là biến liên tục hoặc thứ bậc; biến độc lập gồm ≥ 3 nhóm phân loại; các quan sát hoàn toàn độc lập giữa các nhóm. 2. Nếu các nhóm có phân phối cùng dạng hình học (độ lệch và độ trải rộng tương đương), phép kiểm định trở thành phép so sánh trung vị chính xác giữa các nhóm. 3. Tính toán Eta-bình phương phi tham số: η²_H = (H - k + 1) / (N - k).
terms.benchmarks: Quy tắc ngưỡng Cohen cho η²_H: 0.01 (hiệu ứng nhỏ), 0.06 (hiệu ứng vừa), 0.14 (hiệu ứng lớn). Báo cáo kèm theo giá trị trung vị (Median) và Khoảng tứ phân vị (IQR) cho từng nhóm thay vì báo cáo Mean và SD.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Vẫn báo cáo Mean và SD khi đã dùng Kruskal-Wallis. Khi dữ liệu vi phạm phân phối chuẩn buộc phải dùng ANOVA phi tham số, việc báo cáo giá trị trung bình (Mean) là mâu thuẫn nhận thức luận vì Mean bị bóp méo bởi các ngoại lai; chuẩn mực là phải báo cáo Median và IQR.
terms.apa_reference: Tomczak, M., & Tomczak, E. (2014). The need to report effect size estimates revisited. An overview of some recommended measures of effect size. Trends in Sport Sciences, 1(21), 19–25.

terms.vietnamese: Chuyển dịch hệ hình theo Kuhn (Các cuộc cách mạng khoa học)
vietnamese_variants: Cách mạng khoa học Thomas Kuhn
terms.core_definition: A Kuhnian Paradigm Shift is the revolutionary, non-cumulative transformation of scientific knowledge formulated by historian and philosopher of science Thomas S. Kuhn (1962) in 'The Structure of Scientific Revolutions'. Challenging the logical positivist orthodoxy that science progresses through continuous, linear accumulation of facts, Kuhn demonstrated that science proceeds through episodic cycles: periods of puzzle-solving 'Normal Science' governed by an established paradigm, punctuated by crisis when anomalies accumulate, culminating in a revolutionary 'Paradigm Shift' where the scientific community abandons the old paradigm in favor of an incommensurable new one.
terms.seminal_citation: Kuhn, T. S. (1962). The structure of scientific revolutions. University of Chicago Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kuhnian Paradigm Shift according to Kuhn (1962).
terms.operational_mechanism: The Kuhnian cycle unfolds across five distinct stages: (1) Pre-Paradigmatic Phase: Disorganized, competing schools with no shared foundational consensus; (2) Normal Science: A dominant paradigm crystallizes, guiding puzzle-solving research within an unquestioned disciplinary matrix; (3) Anomalies: Empirical findings emerge that persistently resist explanation within paradigm rules; (4) Crisis: Anomalies multiply and resist resolution, triggering loss of faith and intense meta-theoretical debate; (5) Scientific Revolution (Paradigm Shift): A rival paradigm emerges, offering a novel worldview that resolves the core crisis, adopted through community persuasion and generational turnover (Planck's principle).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The Kuhnian cycle unfolds across five distinct stages: (1) Pre-Paradigmatic Phase: Disorganized, competing schools with no shared foundational consensus; (2) Normal Science: A dominant paradigm crystallizes, guiding puzzle-solving research within an unquestioned disciplinary matrix; (3) Anomalies: Empirical findings emerge that persistently resist explanation within paradigm rules; (4) Crisis: Anomalies multiply and resist resolution, triggering loss of faith and intense meta-theoretical debate; (5) Scientific Revolution (Paradigm Shift): A rival paradigm emerges, offering a novel worldview that resolves the core crisis, adopted through community persuasion and generational turnover (Planck's principle).
terms.benchmarks: Historical and philosophical benchmarks: (1) Classic examples: Copernican revolution (geocentric to heliocentric astronomy), Newtonian to Einsteinian relativistic physics, Lavoisier's oxygen chemistry superseding phlogiston theory, and the behavioral economics revolution superseding rational homo economicus; (2) Incommensurability: The new paradigm cannot be logically reduced to the old.
terms.pitfalls: Common scholarly abuses: (1) Trivialization—labeling minor incremental theoretical updates or technological iterations as 'paradigm shifts'; (2) Misinterpreting Kuhn as claiming science is irrational (paradigm change is governed by epistemic values like accuracy and scope, not irrational whim); and (3) Forgetting that during Normal Science, paradigms actively suppress novelties that threaten their foundations.
terms.apa_reference: Kuhn, T. S. (1962). The structure of scientific revolutions. University of Chicago Press.

terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định tính dừng KPSS
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định KPSS (Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt, & Shin, 1992) là phép kiểm định tính dừng chuỗi thời gian mang tính bổ trợ chiến lược cho kiểm định ADF. Điểm đặc biệt của KPSS là đảo ngược hoàn toàn cấu trúc giả thuyết so với Dickey-Fuller: Giả thuyết vô hiệu H0 của KPSS là chuỗi có tính dừng (stationary quanh một hằng số hoặc xu hướng), còn H1 là chuỗi có nghiệm đơn vị (không dừng).
terms.seminal_citation: Kwiatkowski et al. (1992)
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin Test according to P-value > 0.05: Không thể bác bỏ H0, xác nhận chuỗi thời gian dừng. Kết hợp ADF và KPSS giúp kiểm định chéo độ tin cậy..
terms.benchmarks: Nếu LM_stat < Critical Value (tương đương p-value > 0.05): Không thể bác bỏ H0, kết luận chuỗi là dừng. Nếu LM_stat > Critical Value (p-value < 0.05): Bác bỏ H0, khẳng định chuỗi không dừng. Chiến lược kiểm định kép (Joint Testing): Khi cả ADF bác bỏ nghiệm đơn vị VÀ KPSS không bác bỏ tính dừng, khẳng định chuỗi dừng là tuyệt đối chắc chắn.
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Phân rã chuỗi: y_t = xi · t + r_t + ε_t, trong đó r_t = r_{t-1} + u_t là một bước ngẫu nhiên (random walk) với phương sai σ_u². 2. Giả thuyết H0: σ_u² = 0 (thành phần bước ngẫu nhiên biến mất, chuỗi dừng quanh xu hướng hoặc mức). 3. Thống kê kiểm định LM: LM = ∑ (S²_t) / (T² * s²(l)), trong đó S_t là tổng tích lũy phần dư OLS và s²(l) là ước lượng phương sai dài hạn vững Newey-West.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Hiểu nhầm chiều giả thuyết của KPSS giống như ADF. Nhiều tác giả thấy p-value < 0.05 của KPSS đã vội vã tuyên bố chuỗi dừng, trong khi thực chất p < 0.05 của KPSS nghĩa là BÁC BỎ tính dừng (tức chuỗi không dừng).
terms.apa_reference: Kwiatkowski, D., Phillips, P. C. B., Schmidt, P., & Shin, Y. (1992). Testing the null hypothesis of stationarity against the alternative of a unit root: How sure are we that economic time series have a unit root?. Journal of Econometrics, 54(1–3), 159–178. https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-4076(92)90104-Y

terms.vietnamese: Độ lệch tuyệt đối nhỏ nhất (Hồi quy trung vị LAD)
vietnamese_variants: Ước lượng sai số tuyệt đối tối thiểu
terms.core_definition: Least Absolute Deviations (LAD, also known as L_1-norm regression or Median Regression), originally formulated by Roger Joseph Boscovich (1757) and Pierre-Simon Laplace (1793), is a robust econometric estimation method that models the conditional median of the dependent variable as a linear function of explanatory variables. While Ordinary Least Squares (OLS / L_2-norm) minimizes the sum of squared residuals, LAD minimizes the sum of absolute residuals, making it exceptionally resilient against extreme outliers and heavy-tailed non-Gaussian error distributions.
terms.seminal_citation: Koenker, R., & Bassett, G. (1978). Regression quantiles. Econometrica, 46(1), 33-50.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of LAD according to Rất vững trước các điểm ngoại lai (outliers) cực đoan và phân phối đuôi dày (heavy-tailed distributions)..
terms.benchmarks: Comparative statistical behavior: (1) Robustness: When errors follow heavy-tailed distributions (e.g., Cauchy, Laplace, Student-t with df < 3) or contain severe vertical outliers, LAD is asymptotically more efficient than OLS; (2) Efficiency tradeoff: If errors are perfectly Gaussian N(0, sigma^2), LAD is ~36% less efficient asymptotically than OLS (asymptotic relative efficiency = 2/pi approx 0.637); (3) Median prediction: Estimates conditional median changes rather than mean changes.
terms.operational_mechanism: For the linear model Y_i = X_i' * beta + epsilon_i, the LAD estimator solves the non-differentiable optimization problem: hat{beta}_{LAD} = argmin_{beta} sum_{i=1}^n |Y_i - X_i' * beta|. Because the objective function contains sharp absolute value kinks, it cannot be solved via calculus (no closed-form matrix solution like OLS); instead, it is solved using linear programming via the Simplex method or interior point algorithms (Koenker & Bassett, 1978). LAD represents the special 50th percentile (tau = 0.50) case of general Quantile Regression. Standard errors are derived via non-parametric bootstrapping or kernel density estimation of the error density at the median f(0).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: For the linear model Y_i = X_i' * beta + epsilon_i, the LAD estimator solves the non-differentiable optimization problem: hat{beta}_{LAD} = argmin_{beta} sum_{i=1}^n |Y_i - X_i' * beta|. Because the objective function contains sharp absolute value kinks, it cannot be solved via calculus (no closed-form matrix solution like OLS); instead, it is solved using linear programming via the Simplex method or interior point algorithms (Koenker & Bassett, 1978). LAD represents the special 50th percentile (tau = 0.50) case of general Quantile Regression. Standard errors are derived via non-parametric bootstrapping or kernel density estimation of the error density at the median f(0).
terms.pitfalls: Common research errors: (1) Interpreting LAD coefficients as marginal effects on the conditional mean (LAD estimates shifts in conditional medians); (2) Using standard OLS standard error formulas; and (3) Overlooking that LAD is robust to vertical outliers in Y, but remains sensitive to high-leverage outliers in the X space (requiring robust bounded-influence estimators like Huber or Tukey biweight).
terms.apa_reference: Koenker, R., & Bassett, G. (1978). Regression quantiles. Econometrica, 46(1), 33–50. https://doi.org/10.2307/1913643

terms.term: Lagrange Multiplier Test (LM / Rao Score Test)
terms.vietnamese: Kiểm định nhân tử Lagrange (Kiểm định Score Rao)
terms.core_definition: Kiểm định nhân tử Lagrange (LM test - Aitchison & Silvey, 1958) hay kiểm định Score (Rao, 1948) là một trong ba trụ cột kiểm định giả thuyết tiệm cận cổ điển (cùng với Wald test và Likelihood Ratio test). Điểm ưu việt tuyệt đối của kiểm định LM là nó chỉ yêu cầu ước lượng mô hình dưới giả thuyết vô hiệu có ràng buộc (Restricted model), giúp tiết kiệm chi phí tính toán tối đa khi mô hình không ràng buộc quá phức tạp hoặc khó hội tụ.
terms.seminal_citation: Rao (1948); Aitchison & Silvey (1958); Engle (1984)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Lagrange Multiplier Test (LM / Score Test) according to Rao (1948), Silvey (1959).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Ước lượng mô hình dưới các ràng buộc của H0 (Restricted Model), thu được ước lượng tham số θ_tilde. 2. Đánh giá vector Score (đạo hàm bậc nhất của hàm log-hợp lý s(theta) = d ln L / d theta) tại θ_tilde. Theo nguyên lý, nếu H0 đúng thì vector Score phải tiệm cận về 0. 3. Thống kê kiểm định LM: LM = s(θ_tilde)' * I⁻¹(θ_tilde) · s(θ_tilde), trong đó I là ma trận thông tin Fisher. 4. Thống kê LM tuân theo phân phối Chi-bình phương với bậc tự do bằng số ràng buộc r.
terms.benchmarks: Bất đẳng thức bộ ba kiểm định (Trinity of tests) trong mô hình tuyến tính: Wald ≥ LR ≥ LM. Do đó, kiểm định LM là kiểm định thận trọng/bảo thủ nhất trong việc bác bỏ H0. Nếu p-value < 0.05: Bác bỏ H0, khẳng định ràng buộc bị vi phạm và việc mở rộng mô hình là có cơ sở khoa học.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Nhầm lẫn giữa Wald test và LM test trong thiết kế nghiên cứu. Nếu việc ước lượng mô hình đầy đủ (unrestricted) gặp trục trặc hội tụ toán học, việc cố chấp dùng Wald test sẽ thất bại; phương án chuẩn xác nhất là chuyển sang LM test trên mô hình rút gọn.
terms.apa_reference: Engle, R. F. (1984). Wald, likelihood ratio, and Lagrange multiplier tests in econometrics. Handbook of Econometrics, 2, 775–826. https://doi.org/10.1016/S1573-4412(84)02005-5

terms.vietnamese: Các chương trình nghiên cứu khoa học theo Lakatos
vietnamese_variants: Phương pháp luận chương trình nghiên cứu Lakatos
terms.core_definition: Lakatosian Research Programmes (Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes / MSRP) is an influential philosophy of science framework formulated by Imre Lakatos (1970). Synthesizing Karl Popper's normative demarcation of falsificationism with Thomas Kuhn's historical sociologism, Lakatos argued that the basic unit of scientific appraisal is not an isolated theory subjected to a single crucial experiment, but a dynamic, evolving Research Programme structured into an irrefutable Hard Core surrounded by a flexible Protective Belt of auxiliary hypotheses.
terms.seminal_citation: Lakatos, I. (1978). The methodology of scientific research programmes: Philosophical papers (Vol. 1, J. Worrall & G. Currie, Eds.). Cambridge University Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Lakatosian Research Programmes according to Lakatos (1970).
terms.operational_mechanism: A scientific research programme consists of three essential elements: (1) Hard Core (Negative Heuristic): Foundational metaphysical and theoretical assumptions that scientists methodologically protect from falsification (e.g., three laws of motion in Newtonian physics; rational utility maximization in neoclassical economics); (2) Protective Belt: Auxiliary hypotheses, observational models, and boundary conditions adjusted to absorb empirical anomalies; (3) Positive Heuristic: A partially articulated set of problem-solving techniques guiding how to modify the protective belt; (4) Programme Shift: Classified as Progressive if theoretical shifts lead to novel empirical predictions that are corroborated, or Degenerating if shifts are purely ad-hoc semantic excuses.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: A scientific research programme consists of three essential elements: (1) Hard Core (Negative Heuristic): Foundational metaphysical and theoretical assumptions that scientists methodologically protect from falsification (e.g., three laws of motion in Newtonian physics; rational utility maximization in neoclassical economics); (2) Protective Belt: Auxiliary hypotheses, observational models, and boundary conditions adjusted to absorb empirical anomalies; (3) Positive Heuristic: A partially articulated set of problem-solving techniques guiding how to modify the protective belt; (4) Programme Shift: Classified as Progressive if theoretical shifts lead to novel empirical predictions that are corroborated, or Degenerating if shifts are purely ad-hoc semantic excuses.
terms.benchmarks: Epistemic appraisal criteria: (1) Continuous growth of empirical content: Every theoretical adjustment must predict new, unanticipated facts; (2) Excess empirical corroboration: At least some novel predictions must be verified; (3) Rational supersession: A degenerating programme is rationally superseded when a progressive rival programme emerges that accounts for both the previous programme's successes and its anomalies.
terms.pitfalls: Common philosophical misunderstandings: (1) Conflating MSRP with naive Popperian falsification (Lakatos proved that no experiment immediately kills a theory; theories are protected by their auxiliary belts); (2) Using Lakatos to defend dogmatic persistence in degenerating programmes indefinitely; and (3) Failing to articulate what constitutes the core vs. auxiliary belt in doctoral conceptual frameworks.
terms.apa_reference: Lakatos, I. (1978). The methodology of scientific research programmes: Philosophical papers (Vol. 1, J. Worrall & G. Currie, Eds.). Cambridge University Press.

terms.term: LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator)
terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp LASSO (Hồi quy điều chuẩn chuẩn L1)
vietnamese_variants: Chọn lựa biến tự động LASSO
terms.core_definition: Hồi quy LASSO (Tibshirani, 1996) là phương pháp hồi quy điều chuẩn (regularization) mang tính cách mạng, bổ sung hình phạt dựa trên chuẩn L1 (tổng giá trị tuyệt đối của các hệ số hồi quy) vào hàm mục tiêu OLS. Nhờ tính chất hình học đặc thù của hình phạt L1 (hình thoi với các đỉnh nhọn chạm vào các trục tọa độ), LASSO có khả năng co cụm (shrink) chính xác một số hệ số hồi quy về đúng bằng 0, đồng thời thực hiện cả hai nhiệm vụ: Ước lượng tham số và Chọn lọc biến tự động (Sparsity / Feature Selection).
terms.seminal_citation: Tibshirani (1996); Belloni, Chernozhukov, & Hansen (2014)
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of LASSO according to Tham số phạt λ được tinh chỉnh tối ưu thông qua k-fold Cross-Validation nhằm tối thiểu hóa sai số dự báo..
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Bài toán tối ưu hóa: Min_beta { ∑_(i=1)ⁿ (y_i - X_i · beta)² + λ * ∑_(j=1)^p |β_j| }. 2. Siêu tham số điều chuẩn λ ≥ 0: Khi λ = 0, LASSO trùng khớp với OLS; khi lambda tiến ra vô cùng, tất cả các hệ số đều bị triệt tiêu về 0. 3. Lựa chọn giá trị tối ưu λ * thông qua kiểm định chéo K-fold (Cross-validation: λ_min hoặc quy tắc an toàn 1-SE rule λ_1se). 4. Giải bài toán tối ưu bằng thuật toán Coordinate Descent (Friedman et al., 2010).
terms.benchmarks: Được áp dụng chuẩn mực trong kinh tế lượng dữ liệu lớn chiều cao (High-dimensional data: khi số biến p lớn hơn kích thước mẫu n, p >> n) và trong suy luận nhân quả học máy hiện đại (Belloni, Chernozhukov, & Hansen, 2014 - Double Selection LASSO để chọn biến kiểm soát cho mô hình nhân quả).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Khi các biến giải thích có tương quan rất cao với nhau (nhóm biến cộng tuyến), LASSO có xu hướng chọn bừa một biến duy nhất trong nhóm và triệt tiêu toàn bộ các biến còn lại về 0, bỏ qua cấu trúc đa cộng tuyến thực tế (khắc phục bằng Elastic Net); (2) Các hệ số ước lượng của LASSO bị chệch về phía 0 (shrinkage bias), bắt buộc phải chạy Post-LASSO OLS để khôi phục độ lớn không chệch.
terms.apa_reference: Tibshirani, R. (1996). Regression shrinkage and selection via the lasso. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 58(1), 267–288. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1996.tb02080.x

terms.vietnamese: Hồi quy LASSO (Kỹ thuật Co cụm và Lựa chọn Biến L1 Tibshirani)
domain_tags: Lựa chọn Mô hình & Thuộc tính
terms.core_definition: Phương pháp học máy và kinh tế lượng mang tính bước ngoặt do Robert Tibshirani (1996) phát minh (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator - LASSO). Khác với Ridge (phạt bình phương L2), LASSO áp đặt hình phạt L1 dựa trên tổng giá trị tuyệt đối của các hệ số hồi quy: λ * ∑(|β_j|). Nhờ hình học đặc thù của hình đa diện L1 (các đỉnh nhọn tiếp xúc với trục tọa độ), khi tham số phạt lambda đủ lớn, LASSO sẽ ÉP CHÍNH XÁC CÁC HỆ SỐ CỦA CÁC BIẾN KHÔNG QUAN TRỌNG VỀ ĐÚNG BẰNG 0. Nhờ đó, LASSO đồng thời thực hiện cả hai nhiệm vụ: Co cụm ước lượng và Lựa chọn tập biến tối ưu (Feature selection).
terms.seminal_citation: Tibshirani, R. (1996). Regression shrinkage and selection via the lasso. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 58(1), 267–288. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1996.tb02080.x; Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., & Wainwright, M. (2015). Statistical learning with sparsity: The lasso and generalizations. CRC Press.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of LASSO Regression (L1 Regularization) according to Tibshirani (1996).
terms.benchmarks: Quy chuẩn lựa chọn lambda: Sử dụng 10-fold Cross-Validation và đối chiếu giữa hai tiêu chuẩn: (1) λ_min (giá trị lambda tối thiểu hóa sai số CV); (2) λ_1se (quy tắc 1 sai số chuẩn: chọn mô hình tiết kiệm nhất có sai số nằm trong vòng 1 sai số chuẩn của mức tối thiểu). Bắt buộc chuẩn hóa toàn bộ các biến độc lập trước khi ước lượng. Áp dụng Post-LASSO OLS (chạy lại OLS trên tập các biến được LASSO giữ lại) để loại bỏ độ chệch co cụm đối với các hệ số quan trọng.
terms.pitfalls: Khi có một nhóm biến có tương quan rất cao với nhau (Collinear group), LASSO có xu hướng chỉ chọn ngẫu nhiên một biến duy nhất trong nhóm và loại bỏ toàn bộ các biến còn lại (để giải quyết vấn đề này, bắt buộc dùng Elastic Net); khi số biến p lớn hơn nhiều cỡ mẫu n, LASSO chỉ chọn được tối đa n biến.
terms.apa_reference: Tibshirani, R. (1996). Regression shrinkage and selection via the lasso. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 58(1), 267–288.

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích lớp tiềm ẩn (Mô hình hỗn hợp LCA)
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình phân lớp tiềm ẩn
Phân tích cấu trúc phân nhóm tiềm ẩn
terms.core_definition: Latent Class Analysis (LCA), formulated by Paul Lazarsfeld and Neil Henry (1968) and modernized by Leo Goodman (1974), is a person-centered, model-based finite mixture modeling technique used to identify unobserved, mutually exclusive subgroups (latent classes) within a population based on observed multivariate categorical or binary indicators. In contrast to variable-centered methods (e.g., factor analysis) which assume a continuous latent trait, LCA is person-centered: it classifies individuals into discrete behavioral or psychological typology profiles based on conditional response probability patterns.
terms.seminal_citation: Goodman, L. A. (1974). Exploratory latent structure analysis using both identifiable and unidentifiable models. Biometrika, 61(2), 215-231.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Class Analysis (LCA) according to Lazarsfeld & Henry (1968).
terms.operational_mechanism: LCA estimates two sets of parameters via Maximum Likelihood using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm: (1) Latent Class Prevalences (gamma_c): The proportion of the population belonging to latent class c (sum gamma_c = 1.0); (2) Item-Response Probabilities (rho_{j,r|c}): The conditional probability that an individual in class c endorses response category r on item j; (3) Joint probability formula: Pr(Y = y) = sum_{c=1}^C gamma_c * prod_{j=1}^J rho_{j, y_j | c}, assuming local independence (indicators are mutually independent conditional on class membership); (4) Posterior class assignment: Assigning individuals to the class with the highest posterior probability via Bayes' rule.
terms.operational_mechanism_en: LCA estimates two sets of parameters via Maximum Likelihood using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm: (1) Latent Class Prevalences (gamma_c): The proportion of the population belonging to latent class c (sum gamma_c = 1.0); (2) Item-Response Probabilities (rho_{j,r|c}): The conditional probability that an individual in class c endorses response category r on item j; (3) Joint probability formula: Pr(Y = y) = sum_{c=1}^C gamma_c * prod_{j=1}^J rho_{j, y_j | c}, assuming local independence (indicators are mutually independent conditional on class membership); (4) Posterior class assignment: Assigning individuals to the class with the highest posterior probability via Bayes' rule.
terms.benchmarks: Class enumeration decision criteria (Nylund et al., 2007): (1) Information Criteria: Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), Sample-Size Adjusted BIC (SABIC), and AIC—lower values indicate superior trade-off between fit and parsimony (BIC is the most reliable criterion); (2) Likelihood Ratio Tests: Lo-Mendell-Rubin adjusted LRT (LMR-LRT) and Bootstrap Likelihood Ratio Test (BLRT) p < 0.05 indicating that a k-class model fits significantly better than a (k - 1)-class model; (3) Classification Quality: Entropy >= 0.80 (values > 0.80 indicate sharp classification clarity); (4) Class size: Smallest class should contain at least 5% of the total sample.
terms.pitfalls: Common research pitfalls: (1) Selecting the number of classes purely based on AIC without checking BIC and BLRT; (2) Local maxima entrapment—running LCA with too few random start values (minimum 500 to 1,000 random starts required to ensure global maximum identification); and (3) Violating the local independence assumption without modeling residual direct effects between items.
terms.apa_reference: Goodman, L. A. (1974). Exploratory latent structure analysis using both identifiable and unidentifiable models. Biometrika, 61(2), 215–231. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/61.2.215

terms.vietnamese: Phân bổ Dirichlet tiềm ẩn (Mô hình hóa chủ đề văn bản LDA)

terms.core_definition: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), formulated by David Blei, Andrew Ng, and Michael I. Jordan (2003), is an unsupervised, three-level generative probabilistic Bayesian model for discrete text corpora. In computational social science, management, and scientometrics, LDA discovers latent thematic structures ('topics') across massive text collections by positing that documents are represented as random mixtures over latent topics, and each topic is characterized by a discrete Dirichlet probability distribution over words.
terms.seminal_citation: Blei, D. M., Ng, A. Y., & Jordan, M. I. (2003). Latent Dirichlet allocation. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 3, 993-1022.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Dirichlet Allocation according to Đánh giá chất lượng chủ đề qua chỉ số Topic Coherence (Cv score > 0.50) và Perplexity..
terms.benchmarks: Computational evaluation standards: (1) Topic Coherence Metrics: C_v or UMass coherence scores (higher coherence indicates semantically interpretable, non-chirographic word clusters); (2) Perplexity / Held-out log-likelihood evaluation across varying numbers of topics K to prevent under- or over-fitting; (3) Qualitative validation: Independent human coding checks (word intrusion tests and topic intrusion tests; Chang et al., 2009).
terms.operational_mechanism: The generative process for each document d in corpus D: (1) Sample document topic proportions theta_d ~ Dirichlet(alpha); (2) For each of the N_d words in document d: (a) Sample a specific topic assignment z_{dn} ~ Multinomial(theta_d); (b) Sample an observed word w_{dn} ~ Multinomial(beta_{z_{dn}}), where beta_k ~ Dirichlet(eta) represents topic k's word distribution. Parameter estimation is executed via Collapsed Gibbs Sampling or Variational Expectation-Maximization (VEM) to infer the unobserved posterior distributions of topic-word distributions (beta) and document-topic distributions (theta).
terms.operational_mechanism_en: The generative process for each document d in corpus D: (1) Sample document topic proportions theta_d ~ Dirichlet(alpha); (2) For each of the N_d words in document d: (a) Sample a specific topic assignment z_{dn} ~ Multinomial(theta_d); (b) Sample an observed word w_{dn} ~ Multinomial(beta_{z_{dn}}), where beta_k ~ Dirichlet(eta) represents topic k's word distribution. Parameter estimation is executed via Collapsed Gibbs Sampling or Variational Expectation-Maximization (VEM) to infer the unobserved posterior distributions of topic-word distributions (beta) and document-topic distributions (theta).
terms.pitfalls: Common research mistakes: (1) Treating raw LDA topics as self-evident theoretical truths without rigorous human domain expert validation; (2) Inadequate text pre-processing (failing to remove domain-specific stop words, numbers, and uninformative high-frequency terms, which contaminates topics); and (3) Running LDA with an arbitrary number of topics K without running coherence and perplexity grid searches.
terms.apa_reference: Blei, D. M., Ng, A. Y., & Jordan, M. I. (2003). Latent Dirichlet allocation. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 3, 993–1022.

terms.core_definition: Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGCM) is an advanced structural equation modeling (SEM) technique used to estimate intra-individual changes over repeated measurements (trajectories over time) and inter-individual differences in these trajectories. Unlike repeated-measures ANOVA or simple linear growth models, LGCM operationalizes longitudinal change via continuous latent factors—typically an intercept factor (representing baseline status or initial level) and a slope factor (representing the systematic rate of change over time), each characterized by a mean and a variance.
terms.seminal_citation: Meredith, W., & Tisak, J. (1990). Latent curve analysis. Psychometrika, 55(1), 107-122.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1478
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGCM) according to Duncan et al. (2006).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Model Specification: Define repeated manifest indicators Y_1, Y_2, ..., Y_T across T measurement waves.
2. Factor Loading Constraints: Fix the factor loadings of the latent Intercept factor (eta_0) to 1.0 across all waves (lambda_0t = 1). For the latent Slope factor (eta_1), fix factor loadings according to time intervals (e.g., 0, 1, 2, ..., T-1 for linear change with baseline at t=1, or freely estimate specific loadings for nonlinear/unspecified trajectories).
3. Parameter Estimation: Estimate the latent mean vector (mean intercept alpha_0, mean slope alpha_1), latent variances (psi_00 for intercept heterogeneity, psi_11 for growth rate heterogeneity), and covariance (psi_01 linking baseline level to growth rate), alongside wave-specific residual error variances (theta_t).
4. Software Execution: Estimate via Maximum Likelihood (FIML to handle attrition/missing data) in Mplus, lavaan (R), or Amos.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Time Points: Minimum T >= 3 waves for linear growth models; T >= 4 waves recommended for quadratic or freely estimated non-linear functional forms.
2. Sample Size: Minimum N >= 150-200 for simple linear LGCM; N >= 300-500 when adding time-invariant covariates (conditional LGCM) or distal outcomes.
3. Model Fit Standards: Standard SEM global fit indices apply: CFI/TLI >= 0.95, RMSEA <= 0.06 (or <= 0.08 with 90% CI upper bound < 0.10), SRMR <= 0.08.
4. Variance Significance: A statistically significant slope variance (psi_11, p < 0.05) justifies testing conditional predictors of growth.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Measurement Invariance Violation: Failing to test longitudinal measurement invariance (configural, metric, scalar) across waves prior to estimating latent trajectories, leading to confound between true growth and instrument recalibration.
2. Residual Structure Misspecification: Inappropriately forcing time-specific residuals to be equal and uncorrelated when autocorrelation or heteroscedasticity across waves exists.
3. Overfitting Functional Form: Imposing quadratic or cubic polynomials without theoretical rationale or sufficient waves, yielding multicollinearity and non-convergence.
terms.apa_reference: Meredith, W., & Tisak, J. (1990). Latent curve analysis. Psychometrika, 55(1), 107-122. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02294745

terms.core_definition: Latent Growth Modeling (LGM) represents the broader structural equation framework for capturing intra-individual developmental trajectories and inter-individual variation across longitudinal panel waves. Extending standard univariate growth curve analysis, LGM encompasses multivariate parallel-process models (assessing joint trajectories of two or more constructs), piece-wise linear growth models (accounting for institutional policy shifts or developmental turning points), and accelerated longitudinal cohorts.
terms.seminal_citation: Bollen, K. A., & Curran, P. J. (2006). Latent curve models: A structural equation perspective. John Wiley & Sons.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1477; lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGM) according to Kline (2023); Kline (2023).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Trajectory Formulation: Formulate individual growth paths as y_it = eta_0i + lambda_t * eta_1i + epsilon_it, where eta_0i is individual i's baseline level and eta_1i is the developmental slope.
2. Conditional / Explanatory Structuring: Introduce time-invariant covariates (Z_i) to explain between-person variance in intercept and slope (eta_0i = gamma_00 + gamma_01 * Z_i + zeta_0i; eta_1i = gamma_10 + gamma_11 * Z_i + zeta_1i), and time-varying covariates (X_it) to account for wave-specific fluctuations.
3. Multivariate Parallel Process: Model cross-domain growth by allowing covariances between latent intercepts and slopes of multiple simultaneous developmental processes (e.g., employee burnout and turnover intention).
4. Computation: Implemented using Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML) or robust estimators (MLR) to account for missingness and multivariate non-normality.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Measurement Occasions: Minimum 3 distinct occasions, spaced at meaningful temporal intervals aligned with theoretical change processes.
2. Covariance Stability: Covariance between initial level and growth rate (Cov(eta_0, eta_1)) must be substantively interpreted (e.g., negative covariance indicating 'fan-spread' convergence or ceiling effects).
3. Model Comparison: Nested comparisons between intercept-only, linear, and non-linear/piece-wise models using Delta chi^2 (Satorra-Bentler scaled if MLR) and Delta CFI < 0.010.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Ignoring Attrition Mechanisms: Failing to evaluate whether longitudinal drop-out is Missing at Random (MAR) or Missing Not at Random (MNAR), leading to biased trajectory parameters.
2. Unbalanced Time Intervals: Incorrectly treating unequal spacing between measurement waves as equal integer steps in slope loading matrices.
3. Failure to Differentiate Within vs. Between-Person Dynamics: Conflating cross-sectional differences with genuine developmental growth mechanisms.
terms.apa_reference: Bollen, K. A., & Curran, P. J. (2006). Latent curve models: A structural equation perspective. John Wiley & Sons. https://doi.org/10.1002/0471746096

terms.core_definition: Latent Moderated Structural Equations (LMS) is a distribution-analytic approach developed by Klein and Moosbrugger (2000) for estimating interaction and quadratic effects between continuous latent variables directly within SEM. Unlike product-indicator methods (e.g., Marsh, Ping, Kenny-Judd) which require constructing noisy manifest products of indicators, LMS models the non-normality induced by the latent interaction term using a finite mixture of conditional normal distributions without requiring any product indicators.
terms.seminal_citation: Klein, A., & Moosbrugger, H. (2000). Maximum likelihood estimation of latent interaction effects with the LMS method. Psychometrika, 65(4), 457-474.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Moderated Structural Equations (LMS) according to Klein & Moosbrugger (2000).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Latent Equation Specification: Specify the structural equation eta = gamma_1 * xi_1 + gamma_2 * xi_2 + gamma_3 * (xi_1 * xi_2) + zeta, where xi_1 is the focal predictor, xi_2 is the moderator, and (xi_1 * xi_2) is their latent interaction.
2. Numerical Integration: Since the product of two normal latent variables is non-normal, LMS maximizes the log-likelihood function via Gauss-Hermite numerical integration or expectation-maximization (EM) algorithms.
3. Standard Error & Effect Evaluation: Obtain unbiased parameter estimates, asymptotic standard errors, and calculate simple slopes and regions of significance (Johnson-Neyman technique) at varied levels of the latent moderator.
4. Model Comparison: Because standard global fit indices (CFI, TLI, RMSEA) are not defined for numerical integration models, model fit is evaluated by comparing the LMS model against a linear baseline model without the interaction term using a Log-Likelihood Ratio Test (-2 Delta LL ~ chi^2 with df = 1).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Interaction Significance: Interaction parameter gamma_3 must exhibit p < 0.05 accompanied by a significant Log-Likelihood Ratio Test (Delta D = -2(LL_0 - LL_1) > 3.84, df = 1).
2. Sample Size: Statistical power for latent moderation is notoriously low; minimum recommended N >= 300-400 for moderate interaction effects and N >= 500 for small effects.
3. Information Criteria: Decreases in AIC and BIC (Delta BIC >= 6-10) provide strong evidence favoring the moderated model over the baseline linear model.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Demanding Standard Fit Indices: Reviewers often reject manuscripts asking for CFI/RMSEA on LMS models; authors must proactively explain that conventional covariance-based fit indices are unavailable under numerical integration.
2. Assumption Violations: The classic LMS algorithm assumes normally distributed latent exogenous variables; non-normality can produce inflated Type I error rates (use QML or Quasi-ML if non-normality is severe).
3. Neglecting Linear Main Effects: Interpreting the interaction coefficient without simultaneously retaining and interpreting the main linear components of both predictor and moderator.
terms.apa_reference: Klein, A., & Moosbrugger, H. (2000). Maximum likelihood estimation of latent interaction effects with the LMS method. Psychometrika, 65(4), 457-474. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02296338

terms.core_definition: Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) is a person-centered, model-based mixture modeling technique designed to identify unobserved, mutually exclusive subgroups (profiles) of individuals based on their patterns of responses across continuous manifest variables. In contrast to variable-centered methods (e.g., factor analysis, regression) that assume a homogeneous population, LPA identifies population heterogeneity, assuming the overall distribution is a mixture of distinct multivariate normal sub-populations.
terms.seminal_citation: Gibson, W. A. (1959). Three multivariate models: Factor analysis, latent structure analysis, and latent profile analysis. Psychometrika, 24(3), 229-252.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) according to Vermunt & Magidson (2002).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Indicator Selection & Standardization: Select continuous indicators reflecting the multidimensional phenomenon; standardize indicators if original measurement scales differ.
2. Model Enumeration: Fit a sequence of nested and non-nested models starting with k = 1 profile up to k = K (typically 5 to 7 profiles) under varying variance-covariance structures (e.g., equal variances and zero covariances, varying variances and zero covariances, equal/varying covariances across profiles).
3. Statistical Comparison: Evaluate enumeration using information criteria (AIC, BIC, sample-size adjusted BIC [aBIC]), likelihood ratio tests (Lo-Mendell-Rubin adjusted LRT [LMR-LRT], Bootstrap Likelihood Ratio Test [BLRT]), and classification quality (Entropy).
4. Auxiliary Variable Integration: Incorporate antecedents and distal outcomes using the modern 3-step BCH (Bakk, Tekle, & Vermunt) or ML method to prevent auxiliary variables from shifting latent profile configurations.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Model Selection Criteria: Lowest BIC/aBIC; statistically significant LMR-LRT and BLRT (p < 0.05 comparing k vs. k-1 classes).
2. Classification Quality: Entropy >= 0.80 indicates clear class separation (values > 0.70 acceptable if supported by high average latent class posterior probabilities >= 0.85-0.90).
3. Parsimony and Substantive Meaning: Smallest profile should ideally contain >= 5% of total sample (or at least N >= 25-50 cases) to avoid over-extraction of statistical artifacts.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Solely Relying on Statistical Fit: Selecting a high k solution solely because BIC decreases, ignoring theoretical interpretability or extracting trivial 'parallel' profiles differing only in elevation rather than qualitative configuration.
2. Local Maxima Traps: Failing to specify sufficient random starting values (e.g., STARTS = 500 100 in Mplus), resulting in convergence on local rather than global maximum likelihood.
3. One-Step Auxiliary Variable Inclusion: Regressing outcomes directly on profile indicators in a single step, which distorts profile definitions and causes construct contamination.
terms.apa_reference: Gibson, W. A. (1959). Three multivariate models: Factor analysis, latent structure analysis, and latent profile analysis. Psychometrika, 24(3), 229-252. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02289845

terms.vietnamese: Tiêu chuẩn nghiệm tiềm ẩn (Quy tắc Kaiser)
vietnamese_variants: Tiêu chuẩn giá trị riêng lớn hơn 1
terms.core_definition: The Latent Root Criterion, universally known as the Kaiser-Guttman rule (or eigenvalue-greater-than-one criterion), is a classic diagnostic heuristic in exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and principal component analysis (PCA). It dictates that only factors or components with eigenvalues (latent roots) greater than 1.0 (lambda_j > 1.0) should be retained for rotation and substantive interpretation, based on the rationale that a retained factor must account for at least as much variance as a single standardized manifest variable.
terms.seminal_citation: Kaiser, H. F. (1960). The application of electronic computers to factor analysis. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 20(1), 141-151.
terms.expert_notes: tiêu chuẩn eigenvalue >1 không nên dùng đơn độc – bổ sung parallel analysis | LaTeX thô; lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Root Criterion according to Hair et al. (2018); Hair et al. (2018).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Correlation Matrix Decomposition: Compute the correlation matrix R of p observed standardized variables (diag(R) = 1.0).
2. Spectral Decomposition: Solve the characteristic equation |R - lambda * I| = 0 to extract eigenvalues lambda_1 >= lambda_2 >= ... >= lambda_p, where sum(lambda_j) = p.
3. Truncation Rule: Retain factor j if and only if lambda_j > 1.0; drop all subsequent factors where lambda_j <= 1.0.
4. Software Implementation: Default extraction stopping criterion in SPSS, SAS, Stata, and base R packages (factanal/psych).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Theoretical Baseline: lambda = 1.0 represents the average variance explained by a single standardized manifest item (s^2 = 1).
2. Acceptable Context: Can serve as a rough, preliminary upper/lower heuristic when number of variables p is between 20 and 50 and sample size N > 250.
3. Total Variance Explained: Factors retained under Kaiser rule should ideally explain at least 50% to 60% of total cumulative variance in social sciences.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Chronic Factor Over-extraction: Widely documented in psychometric literature (Zwick & Velicer, 1986; Fabrigar et al., 1999) as causing substantial over-factoring, particularly when the number of items is large (p > 30), retaining minor noise factors.
2. Arbitrary Threshold Artifact: Retaining an arbitrary factor with lambda = 1.01 while discarding a factor with lambda = 0.99 despite virtually identical explanatory variance.
3. Sole Dependency in Q1 Manuscripts: Reviewers in top psychometric and behavioral journals almost universally reject factor structures determined solely by the Kaiser criterion; researchers must triangulate with Horn's Parallel Analysis, Scree Plots, and Hull/MAP methods.
terms.apa_reference: Kaiser, H. F. (1960). The application of electronic computers to factor analysis. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 20(1), 141-151. https://doi.org/10.1177/001316446002000116

terms.core_definition: Latent Transition Analysis (LTA) is a longitudinal extension of latent class analysis (LCA) and hidden Markov modeling that investigates changes in discrete latent status membership over repeated measurement waves. By combining measurement modeling (mapping observed categorical or continuous indicators to latent stages at each wave) with structural transition modeling (estimating transition probabilities between classes over time), LTA allows researchers to model developmental stage-sequential progressions, relapses, and stability.
terms.seminal_citation: Collins, L. M., & Wugalter, S. E. (1992). Latent class models for stage-sequential dynamic latent variables. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 27(1), 131-157.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Latent Transition Analysis (LTA) according to Collins & Lanza (2010).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Latent Class Specification: Define latent class membership C_t at each wave t based on manifest indicators Y_1t, ..., Y_Jt.
2. Measurement Invariance Across Time: Impose equality constraints on indicator item response probabilities (rho_{j|c}^(t) = rho_{j|c}^(t+1)) across waves to guarantee that class definitions remain qualitatively identical over time.
3. Transition Probability Matrix: Estimate transition probabilities tau_{c_t | c_{t-1}} = P(C_t = c_t | C_{t-1} = c_{t-1}), capturing the probability that an individual transitions to class c_t at wave t given membership in class c_{t-1} at wave t-1.
4. Covariate & Moderator Structuring: Estimate multinomial logistic regressions to evaluate whether individual attributes or interventions predict specific transitions (e.g., probability of transitioning from 'novice' to 'expert').
terms.benchmarks:
1. Transition Matrix Diagonal: Diagonal probabilities tau_{cc} represent class stability over time; off-diagonal probabilities reflect stage progression or regression.
2. Measurement Invariance Test: Likelihood ratio test comparing metric-constrained vs. freely estimated measurement models across waves must yield non-significant drop in fit or lower BIC/aBIC.
3. Sample Size: Requires large samples, typically N >= 500-1,000, due to geometric expansion of cross-classified transition cells across multiple time points.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Ignoring Measurement Invariance: Estimating transitions without enforcing longitudinal invariance on indicator probabilities, which confounds true developmental stage transition with shifting item calibrations.
2. Unidentified or Sparsely Populated Transitions: Rare transition pathways with near-zero observed cells leading to boundary parameter estimates (probabilities collapsing to 0 or 1 with blown standard errors).
3. Local Minima: Mixture longitudinal models are highly prone to local maxima; models must be run with 500 to 1,000 random start values.
terms.apa_reference: Collins, L. M., & Wugalter, S. E. (1992). Latent class models for stage-sequential dynamic latent variables. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 27(1), 131-157. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327906mbr2701_8

terms.core_definition: The Law of Large Numbers (LLN) is a fundamental theorem of probability theory and mathematical statistics stating that as the number of identically distributed, independent random trials (n) increases, the sample average (X_bar_n) converges asymptotically toward the true theoretical expected value (mu). LLN exists in two mathematical formulations: the Weak Law of Large Numbers (WLLN, convergence in probability) and the Strong Law of Large Numbers (SLLN, almost sure convergence), providing the axiomatic foundation for sample-based empirical research and frequentist statistical inference.
terms.seminal_citation: Bernoulli, J. (1713). Ars conjectandi, opus posthumum. Impensis Thurnisiorum, Fratrum.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Law of Large Numbers (LLN) according to Bernoulli (1713).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. WLLN Formulation (Khinchin): For independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) random variables X_1, ..., X_n with finite mean E[X_i] = mu: lim_{n -> inf} P(|X_bar_n - mu| >= epsilon) = 0 for any arbitrary epsilon > 0.
2. SLLN Formulation (Kolmogorov): Under the same i.i.d. conditions: P(lim_{n -> inf} X_bar_n = mu) = 1, establishing that the sample trajectory converges to the true mean with probability 1.
3. Empirical Role: Justifies Monte Carlo simulations, resampling techniques (bootstrapping), survey sampling consistency, and unbiased parameter estimation across frequentist econometrics.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Assumption Check: Requires that the first moment (theoretical mean mu = E[X]) exists and is finite. Does not hold for distributions with undefined means (e.g., Cauchy distribution).
2. Asymptotic Convergence Rate: By Chebyshev's inequality, error bound decreases at rate O(1/sqrt(n)): Var(X_bar_n) = sigma^2 / n.
3. Practical Sample Heuristic: While LLN operates as n -> inf, in standard finite populations, stable empirical approximations typically emerge when n >= 30-100 for well-behaved symmetric distributions.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Confusing LLN with the Central Limit Theorem (CLT): LLN asserts that the sample mean converges to a constant (the expected value mu), whereas CLT describes the asymptotic shape and normal distribution of the standardized sampling distribution around that mean.
2. The Gambler's Fallacy ('Law of Small Numbers'): Mistakenly assuming that small samples must balance out deviations (e.g., expecting a string of heads to be 'corrected' by tails in short runs).
3. Heavy-Tailed & Fat-Tailed Breakdowns: Applying standard sample averaging in economic or financial contexts characterized by infinite variance or power-law distributions (Pareto tails) where sample means fluctuate erratically and fail to stabilize.
terms.apa_reference: Bernoulli, J. (1713). Ars conjectandi, opus posthumum. Impensis Thurnisiorum, Fratrum. (Translated by Sylla, E. D., 2006, Johns Hopkins University Press).

terms.core_definition: A Lawlike Generalization is a universal empirical proposition that asserts an invariant, nomological relationship between classes of phenomena and is capable of supporting counterfactual and subjunctive conditional statements. In the philosophy of science (Hempel, Nagel, Armstrong), a statement qualifies as lawlike if it possesses genuine explanatory necessity, general scope, and systematic integration within an overarching scientific theory, distinguishing it from mere accidental empirical regularities.
terms.seminal_citation: Hempel, C. G., & Oppenheim, P. (1948). Studies in the logic of explanation. Philosophy of Science, 15(2), 135-175.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Lawlike generalizations according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Syntactic Structure: Formulated as universal conditional propositions: 'For all x, if F(x), then G(x)' or probabilistic nomological claims 'In condition C, P(G | F) = p'.
2. Counterfactual Testing: Must support counterfactual conditionals: 'If an instance x had possessed property F, it would have possessed property G'.
3. Empirical Confirmation: Subjected to rigorous empirical disconfirmation across varied contexts, boundary conditions, and population regimes.
4. Theoretical Embeddedness: Integrated into a deductive-nomological network where the generalization can be derived from higher-order theoretical principles.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Counterfactual Robustness: Must hold across hypothetical and unobserved cases within the defined theoretical boundary.
2. Scope and Invariance: Must demonstrate resilience across space, time, and diverse operationalizations without collapsing into ad-hoc historical descriptions.
3. Epistemological Standard: In social sciences and management, lawlike status is rarely absolute but evaluated through quasi-laws or empirical regularities robust across multi-country meta-analyses.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Accidental Regularity Conflation: Mistaking a localized, historically contingent correlation (e.g., 'All Fortune 500 CEOs in 1980 were male') for an intrinsic lawlike principle.
2. Post-Hoc Rationalization: Formulating sweeping universal claims after data mining (HARKing) without subjecting them to independent out-of-sample replication.
3. Ignoring Boundary Conditions: Presenting a localized organizational behavior finding as a universal law without delineating institutional, cultural, or industry boundary constraints.
terms.apa_reference: Hempel, C. G., & Oppenheim, P. (1948). Studies in the logic of explanation. Philosophy of Science, 15(2), 135-175. https://doi.org/10.1086/286983

terms.core_definition: The distinction between Lawlike Generalizations and Accidental Generalizations is a foundational demarcation problem in the epistemology of science. A lawlike generalization reflects an objective, nomological necessity rooted in causal mechanisms and systematically supports counterfactual inferences (e.g., 'All copper conducts electricity'), whereas an accidental generalization is an empirical regularity that happens to be true due to historical coincidence or circumstantial restriction without possessing underlying causal necessity (e.g., 'All coins in my pocket are copper').
terms.seminal_citation: Goodman, N. (1955). Fact, fiction, and forecast. Harvard University Press.
terms.expert_notes: Rác Markdown/bảng; mảnh trích; bị cắt cụt
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Lawlike Generalizations vs Accidental Generalizations according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. The Counterfactual Test (Goodman's Criterion): Apply the subjunctive test. If an entity were to enter condition A, would outcome B necessarily follow? Lawlike propositions sustain this test; accidental regularities fail.
2. Projectibility Assessment: Determine whether the predicate is 'projectible' to future, unobserved instances under inductive logic.
3. Causal Mechanism Verification: Identify whether an invariant underlying generative mechanism (e.g., free electrons in metal vs. random pocket selection) connects the antecedent to the consequent.
4. Empirical Stress-Testing: Test the relationship across external experimental perturbations to rule out spurious confounders.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Goodman's Projectibility: Regularity must be inductively extendable to future instances without generating Goodman's 'grue' paradox.
2. Counterfactual Validity: High confidence in theoretical predictions under altered environmental parameters.
3. Boundary Transparency: Explicitly defined spatial-temporal boundary conditions that prevent localized anomalies from masquerading as universal rules.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Confusing Statistical Significance with Lawlikeness: Treating a statistically significant regression coefficient (p < 0.001) from cross-sectional data as proof of a nomological law without establishing causality or counterfactual validity.
2. Survivorship & Selection Biases: Deriving 'laws of organizational success' by examining only enduring corporate giants, confusing survival artifacts with causative laws.
3. Overgeneralization in Qualitative Research: Elevating thick ethnographic descriptions of a specific organization into universal behavioral laws.
terms.apa_reference: Goodman, N. (1955). Fact, fiction, and forecast. Harvard University Press.

terms.term: Latent Dirichlet Allocation / Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)
terms.vietnamese: Phân bổ Dirichlet tiềm ẩn / Phân tích phân biệt tuyến tính
vietnamese_variants: Phân tích biệt số tuyến tính Fisher
terms.core_definition: The acronym LDA denotes two distinct, foundational methodology techniques across quantitative social and computational sciences: (1) Latent Dirichlet Allocation (Blei, Ng, & Jordan, 2003), a generative probabilistic three-level hierarchical Bayesian model for unsupervised topic modeling of unstructured text corpora; and (2) Linear Discriminant Analysis (Fisher, 1936), a supervised dimensionality reduction and classification method that finds a linear combination of continuous features that maximizes between-class variance relative to within-class variance.
terms.seminal_citation: Blei, D. M., Ng, A. Y., & Jordan, M. I. (2003). Latent Dirichlet allocation. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 3, 993-1022.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of LDA according to Đánh giá chất lượng chủ đề qua chỉ số Topic Coherence (Cv score > 0.50) và Perplexity..
terms.benchmarks:
1. For Topic Modeling (Blei LDA): Evaluate model fit using Topic Coherence (Cv score >= 0.50 or high NPMI) and perplexity on held-out validation texts; optimal topic count K selected at the inflection point of coherence.
2. For Linear Discriminant Analysis (Fisher LDA): Assess discrimination using Wilks' Lambda (Lambda -> 0, p < 0.05), canonical correlation squared (R_c^2), and cross-validated classification accuracy (e.g., leave-one-out cross-validation accuracy exceeding proportional chance criteria by at least 25%).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (Topic Modeling):
   - Model document generation: Each document is represented as a random mixture over latent topics, where each topic is characterized by a Dirichlet distribution over vocabulary words.
   - Inference: Use Collapsed Gibbs Sampling or Variational Expectation-Maximization to estimate document-topic proportions (theta_d) and topic-word distributions (phi_k).
2. Linear Discriminant Analysis (Fisher's Classification):
   - Compute within-class scatter matrix S_W and between-class scatter matrix S_B.
   - Solve the generalized eigenvalue problem S_W^-1 * S_B * w = lambda * w to obtain discriminant vectors w maximizing Rayleigh's quotient.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Ambiguity in Academic Text: Using the raw acronym 'LDA' without specifying whether computational text modeling (Dirichlet) or statistical classification (Fisher) is intended.
2. Over-interpretation of Topics: In topic modeling, treating noisy, polysemous word clusters as coherent theoretical constructs without independent human validation or intruder-word testing.
3. Covariance Homogeneity Violation in Fisher LDA: Violating the equal covariance matrix assumption (Box's M test p < 0.001), in which case Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) or multinomial logistic regression should be deployed.
terms.apa_reference: Blei, D. M., Ng, A. Y., & Jordan, M. I. (2003). Latent Dirichlet allocation. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 3, 993-1022. https://doi.org/10.1162/jmlr.2003.3.4-5.993

terms.vietnamese: Thiên lệch thời gian dẫn
vietnamese_variants: Thiên lệch thời gian phát hiện sớm
terms.core_definition: Thiên lệch thời gian dẫn (Lead-Time Bias - Feinleib, 1971; Morrison, 1993) là hiện tượng đánh giá sai lầm hiệu quả của một chương trình tầm soát phát hiện sớm (early screening / early detection). Thiên lệch xuất hiện khi việc chẩn đoán sớm làm tăng khoảng thời gian sống sót được ghi nhận kể từ thời điểm chẩn đoán đến khi tử vong, tạo ra ảo giác rằng bệnh nhân sống lâu hơn nhờ tầm soát, trong khi trên thực tế thời điểm tử vong thực tế của bệnh nhân hoàn toàn không thay đổi.
terms.seminal_citation: Feinleib (1971); Morrison (1993)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Lead-Time Bias according to Feinleib & Zelen (1969).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Thời gian dẫn (Lead Time): Khoảng thời gian từ khi bệnh được phát hiện qua tầm soát sớm đến thời điểm lẽ ra bệnh mới bộc lộ triệu chứng lâm sàng. 2. Nếu đo lường thời gian sống sót từ ngày chẩn đoán (Survival from diagnosis): Nhóm tầm soát luôn có thời gian sống sót dài hơn nhóm không tầm soát đúng bằng khoảng thời gian dẫn, ngay cả khi chương trình tầm soát hoàn toàn vô hiệu. 3. Khắc phục: Đo lường tỷ lệ tử vong đặc hiệu theo nguyên nhân trên toàn bộ dân số (Cause-specific mortality rates) hoặc dựa vào các thử nghiệm ngẫu nhiên có đối chứng (RCTs) với thời điểm bắt đầu theo dõi là ngày phân bổ ngẫu nhiên.
terms.benchmarks: Được áp dụng để giải ảo các chương trình tầm soát ung thư, chẩn đoán sớm khủng hoảng doanh nghiệp hoặc hệ thống cảnh báo sớm rủi ro tài chính. Chuẩn mực đánh giá hiệu quả can thiệp bắt buộc phải dựa trên việc giảm tỷ lệ tử vong tổng thể chứ không được dựa trên thời gian sống sót kể từ lúc chẩn đoán.
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Sử dụng tỷ lệ sống sót sau 5 năm (5-year survival rate) làm tiêu chí chứng minh hiệu quả của phương pháp tầm soát sớm. Tỷ lệ sống sót sau 5 năm bị bóp méo nghiêm trọng bởi cả thiên lệch thời gian dẫn lẫn thiên lệch độ dài (Length-time bias).
terms.apa_reference: Feinleib, M. (1971). The persistent problem of lead time bias. Journal of Chronic Diseases, 24(5), 285–286. https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9681(71)90097-6

terms.vietnamese: Lý thuyết trao đổi lãnh đạo - thành viên
vietnamese_variants: Mô hình trao đổi dọc đôi
Quan hệ lãnh đạo - nhân viên
terms.core_definition: Leader-Member Exchange (LMX) Theory is a foundational relational leadership paradigm positing that leaders do not utilize an identical supervisory style with all subordinates; rather, they develop idiosyncratic, differentiated dyadic exchange relationships varying in quality. High-LMX relationships (in-group) are characterized by mutual trust, respect, reciprocal influence, and emotional support going beyond the formal employment contract, whereas low-LMX relationships (out-group) are restricted to strictly formal transactional obligations defined by employment contracts.
terms.seminal_citation: Graen, G. B., & Uhl-Bien, M. (1995). Relationship-based approach to leadership: Development of leader-member exchange (LMX) theory of leadership over 25 years. The Leadership Quarterly, 6(2), 219-247.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Leader-Member Exchange Theory (LMX) according to Graen & Uhl-Bien (1995).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Dyadic Relationship Evolution: Follows three life-cycle stages: (a) Stranger stage (contractual, low-LMX), (b) Acquaintance stage (tentative expansion of roles), and (c) Mature partnership (reciprocal social exchange, high-LMX).
2. Measurement Instrumentation: Primarily measured using the standardized LMX-7 scale (Graen & Uhl-Bien, 1995) or multidimensional LMX-MDM (Liden & Maslyn, 1998, assessing Affect, Loyalty, Contribution, and Professional Respect).
3. Methodological Design: Assessed via dyadic matched surveys (subordinate ratings and supervisor ratings) analyzed using Multilevel Modeling (HLM/Mplus) to account for nesting of multiple subordinates within supervisors, isolating within-group LMX differentiation from average between-group LMX quality.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Scale Reliability: LMX-7 must display Cronbach's alpha >= 0.85, with CFA establishing distinct construct validity from transformational leadership, perceived organizational support, and trust.
2. Dyadic Agreement: Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC(1) and ICC(2)) must be reported when aggregating to group-level LMX differentiation (typically ICC(1) > 0.10, ICC(2) > 0.60, r_wg(j) > 0.70).
3. Predictive Validity: Consistently predicts job performance (rho ~ 0.30), organizational citizenship behaviors (rho ~ 0.35), and negatively predicts turnover intentions (rho ~ -0.31).
terms.pitfalls:
1. Single-Source Common Method Bias: Collecting both LMX quality and subordinate performance outcomes from the subordinate alone, inflating structural path estimates due to common method variance.
2. Ignoring LMX Differentiation: Treating LMX solely as an individual-level perception while ignoring the adverse group-level effects of high intra-team differentiation (which can foster perceptions of injustice and team conflict).
3. Cross-Sectional Reverse Causality: Assuming high LMX causes high performance, when high-performing subordinates are frequently selected into high-LMX in-groups by leaders from day one.
terms.apa_reference: Graen, G. B., & Uhl-Bien, M. (1995). Relationship-based approach to leadership: Development of leader-member exchange (LMX) theory of leadership over 25 years. The Leadership Quarterly, 6(2), 219-247. https://doi.org/10.1016/1048-9843(95)90036-5

terms.vietnamese: Câu hỏi dẫn dắt / Câu hỏi mớm lời
terms.core_definition: A Leading Question is an inquiry structured in a phrasing, tone, or grammatical form that implicitly or explicitly signals the preferred, expected, or socially desirable answer, thereby distorting the respondent's true perception and introducing systematic measurement bias. In survey methodology, cognitive interviewing, and qualitative research, leading questions undermine construct validity, contaminate memory retrieval, and invalidate statistical and qualitative inferences.
terms.seminal_citation: Loftus, E. F., & Palmer, J. C. (1974). Reconstruction of automobile destruction: An example of the interaction between language and memory. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 13(5), 585-589.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Leading Question according to Schindler (2022).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Syntactic & Lexical Mechanisms:
   - Unbalanced framing: 'Don't you agree that our organization's sustainability policy is outstanding?' (nudging assent).
   - Presupposition loading: 'How often did you encounter problems with our incompetent customer support?' (presupposes incompetence as a factual given).
   - Loaded adjectives and emotive vocabulary.
2. Cognitive Distortion: Triggers acquiescence response bias, activates confirmation heuristics, and induces the 'misinformation effect' (Loftus), where suggestive phrasing alters episodic memory reconstruction.
3. Questionnaire Auditing: Protocol vetting via pre-testing, cognitive walk-throughs, and expert panel reviews using the Question Appraisal System (QAS-99).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Neutrality Standard: Questions must present balanced alternatives (e.g., 'To what extent do you favor or oppose...').
2. Pilot Pre-Testing: Expert evaluation and cognitive interviews (N = 10-20) must demonstrate zero detectable directional skew or respondent acquiescence cues.
3. Qualitative Rigor: In qualitative interview transcripts, researcher prompts must show low-inference, open-ended elicitations (e.g., 'Can you tell me about your experience with...') rather than confirmatory probing.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Subtle Presupposition: Failing to recognize covert leading premises embedded in Likert-type stems, biasing respondents toward the affirmative pole.
2. Double-Barreled Leading Stems: Combining two questions with a leading value-laden descriptor (e.g., 'Should the company expand its generous training and fair promotion system?').
3. Compromised Qualitative Credibility: Qualitative dissertations whose interview transcripts reveal leading probes are frequently challenged by reviewers as lacking confirmability and reflexivity.
terms.apa_reference: Loftus, E. F., & Palmer, J. C. (1974). Reconstruction of automobile destruction: An example of the interaction between language and memory. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 13(5), 585-589. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0022-5371(74)80011-3

terms.vietnamese: Sự bất lực tập nhiễm (Martin Seligman)
vietnamese_variants: Hội chứng bất lực tập nhiễm
Tâm lý bất lực thụ động
terms.core_definition: Learned Helplessness is a psychological construct developed by Martin Seligman and colleagues positing that when humans or animals experience repeated, uncontrollable adverse events, they develop a generalized expectancy that outcomes are independent of their voluntary actions. This expectation leads to three distinct deficits: motivational (passivity and cessation of proactive behavior), cognitive (inability to perceive subsequent response-outcome contingencies), and emotional (depression, anxiety, and demoralization). In organizational and behavioral research, the reformulated attributional model links learned helplessness to pessimistic explanatory styles.
terms.seminal_citation: Seligman, M. E., & Maier, S. F. (1967). Failure to escape traumatic shock. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 74(1), 1-9.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Learned Helplessness (Martin Seligman) according to Overmier & Seligman (1967).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Triadic Experimental Paradigm (Seligman): Subjects exposed to three conditions: Escapable aversive stimuli (controllable), Inescapable aversive stimuli (uncontrollable), and No-treatment control. When transferred to a new solvable task, only the inescapable group exhibits passive failure to respond.
2. Reformulated Attributional Model (Abramson, Seligman, & Teasdale, 1978): When bad events occur, individuals make causal attributions along three bipolar dimensions:
   - Internal vs. External: Attributing failure to self (causes self-esteem deficit).
   - Stable vs. Unstable: Attributing failure to unchangeable factors (causes chronic deficit).
   - Global vs. Specific: Attributing failure to all life domains (causes generalized deficit).
3. Psychometric Measurement: Assessed in behavioral research using the Attributional Style Questionnaire (ASQ) or Expanded ASQ (EASQ).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Scale Metrics: Composite negative attributional style score (CoNeg) computed from ASQ across internal, stable, and global ratings; Cronbach's alpha should be >= 0.75-0.80.
2. Behavioral Manifestation: Demonstrated when individuals fail to initiate coping or creative problem solving even after task constraints have been removed.
3. Workplace Impact: Strong negative predictor of job performance, employee voice, and proactive innovation; mediator between toxic supervisory leadership and burnout/turnover.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Conflating Original vs. Reformulated Models: Using Seligman's 1967 behavioral conditioning animal framework to explain complex human organizational behaviors without incorporating the 1978 cognitive-attributional dimensions.
2. Ignoring Trait vs. State Differences: Treating learned helplessness strictly as an immutable personality trait rather than acknowledging dynamic state-level fluctuations shaped by organizational climate and abusive supervision.
3. Over-pathologizing Rational Passivity: Diagnosing learned helplessness when an employee's withdrawal is actually a rational, strategic response to severe systemic workplace hostility.
terms.apa_reference: Seligman, M. E., & Maier, S. F. (1967). Failure to escape traumatic shock. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 74(1), 1-9. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0024514

terms.vietnamese: Phương pháp độ lệch tuyệt đối tối thiểu
terms.core_definition: Least Absolute Deviations (LAD)—also termed L1-norm estimation, median regression, or minimum absolute errors—is a robust statistical estimation method that estimates regression parameters by minimizing the sum of the absolute residuals rather than the sum of squared residuals (L2-norm in Ordinary Least Squares). By focusing on the conditional median rather than the conditional mean, LAD is substantially more resilient to severe outliers, extreme leverage points, and fat-tailed, non-Gaussian disturbance distributions.
terms.seminal_citation: Boscovich, R. J. (1757). De litteraria expeditione per pontificiam ditionem. Ex typographio Palladis.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Least Absolute Deviations according to Rất vững trước các điểm ngoại lai (outliers) cực đoan và phân phối đuôi dày (heavy-tailed distributions)..
terms.benchmarks:
1. Outlier Breakdown Point: Substantially higher robustness against vertical outliers compared to OLS (which has a 0% breakdown point where a single extreme point can arbitrarily distort the slope).
2. Efficiency Ratio: Under ideal Gaussian errors, LAD relative efficiency compared to OLS is 2/pi (~64%); under Laplace (double-exponential) or heavy-tailed Student-t errors, LAD efficiency vastly exceeds OLS (> 100-200%).
3. Statistical Significance: Evaluated via rank inversion tests, Wald tests, or bootstrapped percentile confidence intervals (B >= 1,000 replications).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Optimization Objective: Minimize the loss function S_LAD(beta) = sum_{i=1}^n |y_i - x_i' * beta| with respect to the vector beta.
2. Non-differentiability & Linear Programming: Because absolute value functions have non-differentiable cusps at zero, standard calculus (gradient descent) cannot be directly applied. Parameters are obtained using linear programming algorithms (e.g., Simplex algorithm, interior point methods, or Barrodale-Roberts algorithm).
3. Median Regression Equivalence: In quantile regression (Koenker & Bassett, 1978), LAD represents the specific quantile tau = 0.50.
4. Standard Error Derivation: Asymptotic variance depends on the sparsity function (the reciprocal of error density at the median, 1/f(0)), typically calculated via robust kernel estimation or pairs bootstrapping.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Susceptibility to Leverage Points: While highly robust to vertical outliers in the dependent variable (Y), LAD regression remains vulnerable to extreme high-leverage outliers in the predictor space (X); researchers should use robust S-estimators or MM-estimators if bad leverage is present.
2. Non-Unique Solutions: In small samples with discrete covariates, the LAD objective function can produce non-unique optimal hyperplanes.
3. Overlooking Non-Differentiability in Custom Scripts: Attempting to optimize LAD using standard Newton-Raphson or unconstrained gradient solvers without smoothing.
terms.apa_reference: Boscovich, R. J. (1757). De litteraria expeditione per pontificiam ditionem. Ex typographio Palladis. (See also: Koenker, R. (2005). Quantile Regression. Cambridge University Press).

terms.term: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)
terms.vietnamese: Toán tử thu nhỏ và chọn lọc tuyệt đối tối thiểu (LASSO)
terms.core_definition: The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), developed by Robert Tibshirani (1996), is a penalized regression and machine learning method that performs both variable selection and continuous coefficient shrinkage. By appending an L1-norm penalty (proportional to the sum of absolute parameter magnitudes) to the ordinary least squares or maximum likelihood loss function, LASSO shrinks parameter estimates toward zero and drives coefficients of uninformative predictors exactly to zero, yielding sparse, interpretable models in high-dimensional datasets ($p > n$).
terms.seminal_citation: Tibshirani, R. (1996). Regression shrinkage and selection via the lasso. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 58(1), 267-288.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
