1. Conflating Selection with Contagion: Observing that connected friends hold identical political views and falsely concluding that friend A converted friend B, ignoring that they became friends because they already shared those views (selection homophily).
2. Ignoring Baseline Availability: Concluding a minority group exhibits strong inbreeding homophily without adjusting for the relative demographic size of that group in the organization.
3. Cross-Sectional Attribution: Inferring homophilous tie formation mechanisms from cross-sectional network snapshots without longitudinal panel tracking.
terms.apa_reference: McPherson, M., Smith-Lovin, L., & Cook, J. M. (2001). Birds of a feather: Homophily in social networks. Annual Review of Sociology, 27(1), 415-444. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.soc.27.1.415

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích gộp mạng lưới (So sánh đa can thiệp)
vietnamese_variants: So sánh can thiệp trực tiếp và gián tiếp
terms.core_definition: Phân tích gộp mạng lưới (Network Meta-Analysis - NMA - Lumley, 2002; Lu & Ades, 2004; Salanti, 2012) là bước tiến mang tính cách mạng trong tổng quan hệ thống, cho phép so sánh hiệu quả tương đối của ba hoặc nhiều can thiệp/chính sách khác nhau (A, B, C...) đồng thời trong cùng một mô hình toán học thống nhất, bằng cách kết hợp cả bằng chứng so sánh trực tiếp (Direct evidence từ các thử nghiệm A vs B) và bằng chứng so sánh gián tiếp (Indirect evidence thông qua nhóm đối chứng chung C).
terms.seminal_citation: Lumley (2002); Lu & Ades (2004); Salanti (2012)
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Network Meta-Analysis according to Bắt buộc kiểm tra giả định chuyển tiếp (Transitivity assumption) và tính nhất quán (Inconsistency test giữa direct và indirect p > .05). Xếp hạng can thiệp qua diện tích SUCRA (Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve).; Salanti (2012).
terms.benchmarks: Được coi là đỉnh cao bằng chứng của Y học thực chứng và Đánh giá chính sách công (PRISMA-NMA Extension). Chỉ số SUCRA dao động từ 0% (tệ nhất) đến 100% (can thiệp tối ưu nhất).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Xây dựng đồ thị hình học mạng lưới bằng chứng (Evidence network plot): Các nút là các phương pháp can thiệp, độ dày của đường nối thể hiện số lượng nghiên cứu so sánh trực tiếp. 2. Giả định tính bắc cầu (Transitivity) và Giả định tính nhất quán (Consistency): Hiệu ứng trực tiếp A vs B phải tương thích toán học với hiệu ứng gián tiếp suy ra từ (A vs C) và (B vs C). 3. Ước lượng thông qua mô hình phân cấp Bayes (Bayesian hierarchical models) hoặc mô hình thường nghiệm đa biến (Multivariate frequentist models). 4. Xếp hạng hiệu quả bằng Chỉ số SUCRA (Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Bỏ qua kiểm định tính không nhất quán (Inconsistency testing bằng Node-splitting method). Nếu có sự mâu thuẫn lớn giữa bằng chứng trực tiếp và gián tiếp, toàn bộ kết quả xếp hạng mạng lưới sẽ bị sai lệch hoàn toàn.
terms.apa_reference: Salanti, G. (2012). Indirect and mixed-treatment comparison, network, or multiple-treatments meta-analysis? Many names, many benefits, many concerns for the next generation evidence synthesis tool. Research Synthesis Methods, 3(2), 80–97. https://doi.org/10.1002/jrsm.1037

terms.term: Network Meta-Analysis Protocol and SUCRA Metrics
terms.vietnamese: Giao thức phân tích gộp mạng lưới và thước đo SUCRA
terms.core_definition: Giao thức phân tích gộp mạng lưới và thước đo SUCRA (Salanti, Ades, & Ioannidis, 2011) quy chuẩn hóa quy trình phân tích và xếp hạng thứ bậc hiệu năng của toàn bộ các can thiệp cạnh tranh trong một mạng lưới bằng chứng phức tạp.
terms.seminal_citation: Salanti, Ades, & Ioannidis (2011)
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1735
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Network Meta-Analysis (NMA) according to Salanti (2012).
terms.operational_mechanism: 1. Tính toán ma trận xác suất xếp hạng: Xác suất P(r, k) là can thiệp k xếp ở vị trí thứ r. 2. Diện tích dưới đường cong xếp hạng tích lũy (SUCRA): SUCRA_k = ∑_(j=1)^(m-1) cum_P(j, k) / (m - 1), trong đó m là tổng số can thiệp. 3. Vẽ biểu đồ đóng góp mạng lưới (Contribution plot) để xác định mức độ chi phối của từng so sánh trực tiếp lên ước lượng gián tiếp.
terms.benchmarks: Báo cáo bảng xếp hạng thứ bậc kèm chỉ số SUCRA và trung vị thứ hạng (Mean rank). Luôn đi kèm biểu đồ Forest plot so sánh mọi can thiệp với một can thiệp chuẩn tham chiếu (Reference comparator).
terms.pitfalls: Bẫy phản biện: Tuyên bố một can thiệp là 'vượt trội nhất' chỉ dựa vào chỉ số SUCRA cao hơn vài phần trăm (ví dụ SUCRA 85% vs 82%) mà không kiểm tra khoảng tin cậy trùng lặp giữa hai can thiệp.
terms.apa_reference: Salanti, G., Ades, A. E., & Ioannidis, J. P. (2011). Graphical methods and numerical summaries for presenting results from multiple-treatment meta-analyses: An overview and tutorial. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 64(2), 163–171. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclinepi.2010.03.016

terms.vietnamese: Nhóm không bao giờ tiếp nhận can thiệp (Never-Takers)
vietnamese_variants: Đối tượng kiên quyết không tuân thủ
terms.core_definition: Never-Takers constitute one of the four latent compliance subpopulations identified in the Angrist, Imbens, and Rubin (1996) Principal Stratification framework for Instrumental Variables and randomized encouragement trials. Defined by the potential treatment assignment vector $D_i(Z) = 0$ for all $Z \in \{0, 1\}$, Never-Takers are individuals who will never take the treatment or adopt the intervention, even if they are randomly assigned, encouraged, or incentivized to do so ($D_i(1) = 0$ and $D_i(0) = 0$). In LATE estimation, because never-takers experience zero variation in treatment uptake, their treatment effect is unidentifiable, and the instrumental variable estimator excludes them from the Complier causal estimand.
terms.seminal_citation: Angrist, J. D., Imbens, G. W., & Rubin, D. B. (1996). Identification of causal effects using instrumental variables. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 91(434), 444-455.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Never-Takers according to Angrist, Imbens, & Rubin (1996).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Latent Potential Treatment Vector: D_i(1) = 0 (when instrument encourages treatment, they refuse); D_i(0) = 0 (when instrument discourages treatment, they refuse).
2. Identification in Randomized Encouragement Trials:
   - Among individuals randomly assigned to the encouragement arm (Z = 1), those who fail to take treatment (D = 0) are an observable mixture of Never-Takers.
   - Proportion of Never-Takers: P(Never-Taker) = P(D = 0 | Z = 1).
3. Exclusion Restriction Implication: Under the standard exclusion restriction, the instrument Z has zero causal impact on outcome Y among Never-Takers: E[Y(1, D=0) - Y(0, D=0) | Never-Takers] = 0.
4. Principal Stratification Role: Analyzed in clinical and educational policy trials to characterize the demographic and psychological barriers preventing resistant non-compliers from engaging with interventions.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Observed Proportion: Directly estimated from the non-compliance rate in the treatment-assigned group: pi_NT = 1 - E[D | Z=1].
2. Causal Exclusion: The estimated Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) applies strictly to Compliers and cannot be extrapolated to Never-Takers.
3. Baseline Covariate Profiling: High-quality policy trials profile Never-Takers using multinomial weighting to inform targeted outreach interventions.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Generalizing LATE to Never-Takers: Assuming that an educational voucher intervention that showed high LATE among compliers would produce the same benefits if mandated for never-takers.
2. Conflating Never-Takers with Defiers: Confusing never-takers (who consistently refuse treatment in all states) with defiers (who do the exact opposite of encouragement).
3. Exclusion Restriction Violation: If being assigned to treatment causes frustration or demoralization among never-takers that directly affects outcome Y, the exclusion restriction is violated.
terms.apa_reference: Angrist, J. D., Imbens, G. W., & Rubin, D. B. (1996). Identification of causal effects using instrumental variables. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 91(434), 444-455. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1996.10476902

terms.vietnamese: Thang đo Newcastle-Ottawa
vietnamese_variants: Thang đánh giá chất lượng NOS
Công cụ đánh giá nguy cơ sai lệch nghiên cứu quan sát
terms.core_definition:
Thang đo Newcastle-Ottawa (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale - NOS, được phát triển bởi nhóm nghiên cứu hợp tác giữa Đại học Newcastle, Australia và Đại học Ottawa, Canada dẫn đầu bởi G. A. Wells et al., 2000; Stang, 2010) là công cụ được sử dụng phổ biến nhất trên toàn cầu để đánh giá nguy cơ sai lệch (Risk of Bias) và chất lượng phương pháp luận của các nghiên cứu phi ngẫu nhiên (Non-Randomized Studies - NRS), cụ thể là các nghiên cứu đoàn hệ (Cohort studies) và nghiên cứu bệnh - chứng (Case-Control studies), khi thực hiện Tổng quan hệ thống (Systematic Review) và Phân tích gộp (Meta-Analysis). Công cụ NOS sử dụng hệ thống 'Chấm sao' (Star rating system) với tối đa 9 sao phân bổ trên 3 phân vùng phương pháp luận cốt lõi:
1. Chọn lựa đối tượng nghiên cứu (Selection of study groups - tối đa 4 sao).
2. Tính tương đồng giữa các nhóm so sánh (Comparability of groups - tối đa 2 sao).
3. Đo lường kết quả hoặc yếu tố phơi nhiễm (Ascertainment of outcome / Exposure - tối đa 3 sao).
terms.seminal_citation: Wells, G. A., Shea, B., O'Connell, D., Peterson, J., Welch, V., Losos, M., & Tugwell, P. (2000). The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for assessing the quality of nonrandomised studies in meta-analyses. Ottawa Hospital Research Institute.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1741; LaTeX thô; nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Newcastle-Ottawa Scale according to Hệ thống xếp hạng sao (tối đa 9 sao) qua 3 nhóm tiêu chí: Lựa chọn nhóm nghiên cứu (4 sao), Tính so sánh được (2 sao), và Đo lường kết quả/phơi nhiễm (3 sao). Nghiên cứu ≥ 7 sao được xếp loại chất lượng cao..
terms.short_definition: Công cụ chuẩn vàng đánh giá chất lượng phương pháp luận và nguy cơ sai lệch trong các nghiên cứu quan sát (nghiên cứu đoàn hệ và bệnh-chứng) trong tổng quan hệ thống và phân tích gộp.
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Xác định thiết kế của từng nghiên cứu thành phần: Lựa chọn biểu mẫu đánh giá NOS chuẩn phù hợp cho Nghiên cứu Đoàn hệ hoặc Nghiên cứu Bệnh - Chứng.
2. Thực hiện đánh giá độc lập bởi hai thẩm định viên (Two independent reviewers): Từng thẩm định viên chấm sao độc lập theo cẩm nang hướng dẫn (coding manual).
3. Chi tiết các tiêu chí chấm sao cho Nghiên cứu Đoàn hệ:
 - Chọn lựa (Tối đa 4 sao): Tính đại diện của đoàn hệ phơi nhiễm (1 sao); Lựa chọn đoàn hệ không phơi nhiễm từ cùng quần thể (1 sao); Xác định tình trạng phơi nhiễm qua hồ sơ khách quan (1 sao); Chứng minh kết quả chưa xuất hiện tại thời điểm bắt đầu nghiên cứu (1 sao).
 - Tính tương đồng (Tối đa 2 sao): Kiểm soát biến gây nhiễu quan trọng nhất (1 sao); Kiểm soát các biến gây nhiễu bổ sung (1 sao).
 - Kết quả (Tối đa 3 sao): Đánh giá kết quả bằng thẩm định mù độc lập hoặc hồ sơ bệnh án (1 sao); Thời gian theo dõi đủ dài để kết quả xuất hiện (1 sao); Mức độ đầy đủ của việc theo dõi đoàn hệ (tỷ lệ mất dấu < 20% hoặc có phân tích đối chiếu, 1 sao).
4. Đối thoại giải quyết bất đồng: Thảo luận hoặc xin ý kiến chuyên gia thứ ba khi có sự khác biệt về số sao.
5. Báo cáo và tích hợp trong Meta-Regression: Sử dụng điểm số NOS để phân tích dưới nhóm (Subgroup analysis) nhằm kiểm tra xem các nghiên cứu có chất lượng thấp có làm sai lệch kết quả tổng hợp hay không.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Thang phân loại chất lượng tổng thể theo chuẩn AHRQ (Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality):
 - Chất lượng tốt (Good quality / Low risk of bias): Đạt 3-4 sao phần Chọn lựa VÀ 1-2 sao phần Tương đồng VÀ 2-3 sao phần Kết quả (Tổng thường ≥ 7 sao).
 - Chất lượng khá (Fair quality): Đạt 2 sao phần Chọn lựa VÀ 1-2 sao phần Tương đồng VÀ 2-3 sao phần Kết quả.
 - Chất lượng kém (Poor quality / High risk of bias): Đạt 0-1 sao phần Chọn lựa HOẶC 0 sao phần Tương đồng HOẶC 0-1 sao phần Kết quả (Tổng ≤ 4-5 sao).
2. Điểm số tối đa: 9 sao tuyệt đối.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Tính tin cậy giữa các thẩm định viên thấp (Low Inter-rater Reliability): Nghiên cứu của Stang (2010) và Hartling et al. (2013) chỉ ra rằng một số câu hỏi của NOS (đặc biệt là tiêu chuẩn 'thời gian theo dõi đủ dài') mang tính chủ quan cao, dẫn đến hệ số đồng thuận Kappa giữa hai người chấm thường thấp nếu không có bảng quy ước tiêu chuẩn tiền trạm.
2. Chỉ báo cáo tổng điểm gộp (Total Star Count Fallacy): Tạp chí Q1 và sổ tay Cochrane Handbook khuyến cáo không nên chỉ nhìn vào tổng số sao (ví dụ: 'Nghiên cứu đạt 7/9 sao') vì một nghiên cứu có thể đạt 7 sao nhưng lại nhận 0 sao ở phần Kiểm soát biến nhiễu cốt lõi, khiến toàn bộ kết luận nhân quả của nó sụp đổ.
3. Nhầm lẫn giữa chất lượng báo cáo (Reporting quality) và chất lượng phương pháp luận (Methodological quality): Tác giả viết bài có thể làm nghiên cứu rất tốt nhưng không trình bày chi tiết trong bài báo, dẫn đến việc bị trừ sao oan uổng.
terms.apa_reference: Wells, G. A., Shea, B., O'Connell, D., Peterson, J., Welch, V., Losos, M., & Tugwell, P. (2000). The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for assessing the quality of nonrandomised studies in meta-analyses. Ottawa Hospital Research Institute. http://www.ohri.ca/programs/clinical_epidemiology/oxford.asp

terms.term: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS - Non-Randomized Studies Quality Assessment)
terms.vietnamese: Thang đo Newcastle-Ottawa (Thẩm định chất lượng nghiên cứu đoàn hệ & bệnh chứng)
terms.core_definition: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) là công cụ thẩm định chất lượng phương pháp luận phổ biến và được trích dẫn nhiều nhất thế giới dành cho các nghiên cứu quan sát phi thực nghiệm (gồm Nghiên cứu đoàn hệ - Cohort studies và Nghiên cứu bệnh chứng - Case-control studies) trong các bài tổng quan hệ thống và phân tích tổng hợp (Wells et al., 2000; Stang, 2010). Thang đo sử dụng 'hệ thống gắn sao' (Star system) với tối đa 9 sao để đánh giá nghiên cứu trên 3 góc độ: Lựa chọn nhóm nghiên cứu (Selection), Tính tương đồng (Comparability), và Đo lường kết quả/phơi nhiễm (Outcome/Exposure).
terms.seminal_citation: Wells, G. A., Shea, B., O’Connell, D., Peterson, J., Welch, V., Losos, M., & Tugwell, P. (2000). The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for assessing the quality of nonrandomised studies in meta-analyses. Ottawa Hospital Research Institute; Stang, A. (2010). Critical evaluation of the Newcastle-Ottawa scale for the assessment of the quality of nonrandomized studies in meta-analyses. European Journal of Epidemiology, 25(9), 603-605.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1740
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) according to Wells et al. (2000).
terms.operational_mechanism: Cấu trúc hệ thống 9 sao của NOS: (1) Lựa chọn (Selection - tối đa 4 sao): Tính đại diện của nhóm phơi nhiễm, Lựa chọn nhóm không phơi nhiễm, Xác định phơi nhiễm, và Chứng minh kết quả chưa xuất hiện lúc bắt đầu; (2) Tính tương đồng (Comparability - tối đa 2 sao): Kiểm soát biến gây nhiễu quan trọng nhất (1 sao) và các biến gây nhiễu bổ sung (1 sao); (3) Kết quả/Phơi nhiễm (Outcome/Exposure - tối đa 3 sao): Đánh giá kết quả độc lập, Thời gian theo dõi đủ dài, và Tỷ lệ theo dõi đầy đủ.
benchmarks: Quy ước phân loại chất lượng theo số sao: 7 - 9 sao: Nghiên cứu chất lượng cao (Good / High quality); 5 - 6 sao: Nghiên cứu chất lượng trung bình (Fair quality); 0 - 4 sao: Nghiên cứu chất lượng kém (Poor quality / High risk of bias).
Tiêu chuẩn sao Comparability: Phải nêu rõ tên biến gây nhiễu bắt buộc phải kiểm soát (như tuổi tác, chỉ số BMI) trước khi cho sao.
Đánh giá độc lập bởi ít nhất 2 tác giả trong bài tổng quan hệ thống.
pitfalls: Cho sao tùy tiện ở mục Tính tương đồng: Cho 2 sao mà nghiên cứu hoàn toàn không chạy mô hình hồi quy đa biến hoặc ghép cặp kiểm soát biến gây nhiễu.
Không sửa đổi tiêu chí thời gian theo dõi cho phù hợp với bệnh học: Đặt tiêu chuẩn theo dõi 1 tháng cho một căn bệnh ung thư cần theo dõi 5 năm.
Thiếu thỏa thuận liên đánh giá viên: Hai tác giả chấm điểm chênh lệch nhau từ 3-4 sao mà không thảo luận thống nhất.
terms.apa_reference: Wells, G. A., Shea, B., O’Connell, D., Peterson, J., Welch, V., Losos, M., & Tugwell, P. (2000). The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) for assessing the quality of nonrandomised studies in meta-analyses. Ottawa Hospital Research Institute.

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật nhóm danh nghĩa (NGT)
terms.core_definition: The Nominal Group Technique (NGT) is a structured, face-to-face small-group consensus-building methodology developed by André L. Delbecq and Andrew H. Van de Ven (1971). Designed to overcome the psychological pathologies of traditional unstructured brainstorming (e.g., dominance by aggressive personalities, groupthink, evaluation apprehension, social loafing), NGT brings participants together physically or virtually as a 'nominal' group (working independently in each other's presence) through a highly structured 4-phase protocol: silent idea generation, round-robin recording, structured clarification, and independent mathematical voting.
terms.seminal_citation: Delbecq, A. L., & Van de Ven, A. H. (1971). A group process model for problem identification and program planning. The Journal of Applied Behavioral Science, 7(4), 466-492.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of NGT according to Quy trình 4 pha: Tạo ý tưởng thầm lặng → Thu thập vòng tròn → Thảo luận làm rõ → Bỏ phiếu xếp hạng độc lập..
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Phase 1 (Silent Generation in Writing): The facilitator presents the focal research problem; participants spend 10-15 minutes working in complete silence writing down their ideas without consulting peers.
2. Phase 2 (Round-Robin Recording): The facilitator goes around the room asking each participant for one idea at a time; all ideas are recorded verbatim on a public flipchart without critique or debate until all ideas are exhausted.
3. Phase 3 (Structured Clarification & Discussion): Each listed item is discussed sequentially to ensure mutual comprehension, eliminate semantic redundancy, and elaborate reasoning.
4. Phase 4 (Independent Mathematical Voting & Ranking): Each participant privately ranks or scores the top items (e.g., selecting top 5 items and allocating weights 1 to 5) on private ballot cards.
5. Aggregation: The facilitator tallies individual mathematical votes to generate the final group priority ranking.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Group Size: Typically 5 to 9 participants per nominal group session (can be scaled using multiple simultaneous tables).
2. Participation Equity: Equal voice guaranteed by the round-robin protocol; no single individual can dominate discussion.
3. Reliability: Yields significantly higher idea quantity, conceptual diversity, and satisfaction than unstructured focus groups.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Premature Debate During Recording: Allowing participants to argue or criticize ideas during Phase 2, which re-activates evaluation apprehension and inhibits timid participants.
2. Facilitator Manipulation: The facilitator rephrasing or censoring participant ideas during recording, distorting the authentic voice of the group.
3. Neglecting Final Member Checking: Reporting raw voting tallies without presenting the final prioritized list back to the group for brief confirmatory consensus.
terms.apa_reference: Delbecq, A. L., & Van de Ven, A. H. (1971). A group process model for problem identification and program planning. The Journal of Applied Behavioral Science, 7(4), 466-492. https://doi.org/10.1177/002188637100700404

terms.vietnamese: Ngưỡng bảo thủ HTMT (HTMT ≤ 0.85)
terms.core_definition: The Conservative HTMT Threshold (HTMT ≤ 0.85) is the rigorous psychometric benchmark introduced by Jörg Henseler, Christian M. Ringle, and Marko Sarstedt (2015) for evaluating Discriminant Validity in Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and covariance-based SEM. Henseler et al. demonstrated through extensive Monte Carlo simulations that the classic Fornell-Larcker criterion and cross-loadings exhibit unacceptably low sensitivity in detecting discriminant validity violations, whereas maintaining an HTMT ratio strictly at or below 0.85 reliably guarantees that two conceptually distinct theoretical constructs do not overlap empirically.
terms.seminal_citation: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Ngưỡng Bảo thủ (HTMT ≤ 0.85) according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Mathematical Formulation: HTMT_ij = [ sum_{g=1}^K_i sum_{h=1}^K_j r_{ig, jh} / (K_i * K_j) ] / sqrt( [ 2 / (K_i * (K_i - 1)) * sum_{g<h} r_{ig, ih} ] * [ 2 / (K_j * (K_j - 1)) * sum_{g<h} r_{jg, jh} ] ).
2. Calculation Logic: The average of the heterotrait-heteromethod correlations divided by the geometric mean of the average monotrait-heteromethod correlations.
3. Application Boundary: HTMT <= 0.85 is mandatory when constructs are conceptually distinct and theoretically distant (e.g., Employee Trust vs. Turnover Intention; Brand Love vs. Price Consciousness).
4. Inference Testing: Supplement point estimate with bootstrapping (5,000 resamples); the 95% or 99% bootstrap confidence interval of HTMT must not contain 1.0 (HTMT_inference).
terms.benchmarks:
1. Conservative Decision Rule: HTMT_ij <= 0.85 establishes rigorous discriminant validity.
2. Bootstrap Confidence Interval: The upper bound of the 95% one-tailed or 90% two-tailed bootstrap confidence interval must be strictly < 1.0.
3. Superiority: Monte Carlo simulations show HTMT achieves sensitivity rates >= 97-99% in detecting discriminant validity violations, compared to < 54% for Fornell-Larcker.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Relying Exclusively on Fornell-Larcker: Reporting only the Fornell-Larcker matrix in modern SEM papers, which Q1 reviewers routinely reject as outdated and insensitive.
2. Relaxing to 0.90 for Distinct Constructs: Using the liberal 0.90 cutoff when theoretical constructs are conceptually distinct, masking empirical redundancy.
3. Ignoring High HTMT Ratios: Proceeding to structural path modeling when HTMT > 0.85, which causes severe multicollinearity and distorted structural regression slopes.
terms.apa_reference: Henseler, J., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2015). A new criterion for assessing discriminant validity in variance-based structural equation modeling. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 43(1), 115-135. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-014-0403-8

terms.vietnamese: Ngưỡng nới lỏng HTMT (HTMT ≤ 0.90)
terms.core_definition: The Liberal HTMT Threshold (HTMT ≤ 0.90) is the permissive psychometric threshold formulated by Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2015) and endorsed by Hair et al. (2022) for establishing Discriminant Validity in structural equation modeling when the two latent constructs under evaluation are conceptually, theoretically, or semantically very similar or closely related facets of a broader higher-order construct (e.g., Affective Commitment vs. Normative Commitment; Customer Satisfaction vs. Service Quality).
terms.seminal_citation: Hair, J. F., Hult, G. T. M., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2022). A primer on partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Ngưỡng Nới lỏng (HTMT ≤ 0.90) according to Henseler et al. (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Theoretical Justification: The researcher must formally argue in the literature review that the two constructs are conceptually adjacent and expected to share high natural theoretical covariance.
2. Decision Threshold: HTMT_ij <= 0.90 indicates that despite strong empirical correlation, the two constructs remain statistically distinct from one another.
3. Upper Ceiling Warning: If HTMT exceeds 0.90 (e.g., HTMT = 0.93), discriminant validity is formally violated; the two constructs cannot be treated as separate entities in the structural model.
4. Remedial Actions for HTMT > 0.90:
   - Combine the two constructs into a single broader composite construct.
   - Model them as first-order dimensions of a higher-order reflective construct.
   - Re-examine indicators and eliminate cross-loading or semantically redundant items.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Permissible Context: Applicable strictly to conceptually adjacent constructs; distinct constructs must adhere to HTMT <= 0.85.
2. Statistical Rejection Point: HTMT > 0.90 definitively indicates lack of discriminant validity.
3. Bootstrapping Criterion: The upper bound of the 95% bootstrap confidence interval must remain strictly < 1.0.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Blanket Application of 0.90: Using the 0.90 threshold across all construct pairs in a study without justifying conceptual proximity.
2. Defending HTMT > 0.90: Attempting to argue that HTMT = 0.92 is 'acceptable' because Fornell-Larcker passed; HTMT > 0.90 indicates construct redundancy.
3. Over-Purification: Deleting dozens of survey items blindly to force HTMT below 0.85 when 0.90 is theoretically legitimate for adjacent facets.
terms.apa_reference: Hair, J. F., Hult, G. T. M., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2022). A primer on partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-80519-7

terms.vietnamese: Hệ thống Ngưỡng Hệ số Tải Thực nghiệm (Chuẩn mực Outer Loadings)
vietnamese_variants: Quy chuẩn hệ số tải Hair et al.
terms.core_definition: Hệ thống các ngưỡng giá trị tới hạn của hệ số tải nhân tố (Factor Loadings trong CFA / Outer Loadings trong PLS-SEM) được thiết lập dựa trên cơ sở toán học về tỷ lệ phương sai trích xuất của từng biến quan sát: Phương sai biến quan sát được giải thích bởi biến tiềm ẩn chính bằng bình phương của hệ số tải (Loading²).
terms.seminal_citation: Nunnally, J. C., & Bernstein, I. H. (1994). Psychometric theory (3rd ed.). McGraw-Hill; Hair, J. F., Hult, G. T. M., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2022). A primer on partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; tên mục không phải thuật ngữ | Lưu ý: "chênh lệch < 0.30" cần diễn đạt rõ (chênh tải chính – tải chéo ≥ 0.20/0.30 là quy ước)
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Ngưỡng tải thực nghiệm according to Hair et al. (2018).
terms.benchmarks: Thang chuẩn mực quốc tế Hair et al. (2022) và Nunnally & Bernstein (1994): (1) Loading ≥ 0.708: Ngưỡng lý tưởng tuyệt đối (vì 0.708² = 0.50, tức biến tiềm ẩn giải thích được trên 50% phương sai của câu hỏi đo lường); (2) 0.60 ≤ Loading < 0.708: Chấp nhận được trong nghiên cứu thực nghiệm nếu tổng thể AVE ≥ 0.50; (3) 0.40 ≤ Loading < 0.60: Chỉ xem xét loại bỏ nếu việc loại bỏ giúp tăng AVE và CR vượt ngưỡng; (4) Loading < 0.40: BẮT BUỘC XÓA BỎ NGAY LẬP TỨC.
terms.pitfalls: Giữ lại các biến có loading < 0.40 làm ô nhiễm ma trận đo lường và kéo sụt AVE của toàn bộ cấu trúc; tự ý xóa các biến có loading 0.65 trong khi thang đo chỉ có 3 biến quan sát.
terms.apa_reference: Hair, J. F., Hult, G. T. M., Ringle, C. M., & Sarstedt, M. (2022). A primer on partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (3rd ed.). SAGE Publications.

terms.vietnamese: Chủ đề chuyên biệt và Chủ đề mới nổi (Bản đồ thư mục học Cobo)
vietnamese_variants: Chủ đề ngách vs chủ đề mới nổi
terms.core_definition: The distinction between Niche Themes and Emerging Themes constitutes the left-hand column classification within the Cobo (2011) science mapping strategic framework based on Callon's Centrality and Density. Located in the low-centrality domain (indicating limited external interaction with the broader discipline), Niche Themes (Upper-Left: Low Centrality, High Density) are highly specialized, internally coherent, isolated academic subfields, whereas Emerging Themes (Lower-Left: Low Centrality, Low Density) represent peripheral, nascent research frontiers—or alternatively, dying research topics in decline.
terms.seminal_citation: Cobo, M. J., López-Herrera, A. G., Herrera-Viedma, E., & Herrera, F. (2011). Science mapping software tools: Review, analysis, and cooperative study among tools. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 62(7), 1382-1402.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Niche Themes vs. Emerging Themes according to Cobo et al. (2011), Bansal et al. (2024).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Quadrant Coordinate Mechanics:
   - Niche Themes (Upper-Left: Low Centrality, High Density): Possess high internal cohesion (density) but weak structural bridges to external fields (centrality). Represents isolated scholarly subcultures, highly technical specialized methods, or esoteric applications.
   - Emerging or Declining Themes (Lower-Left: Low Centrality, Low Density): Weak internal cohesion and weak external ties. Represents early-stage conceptual innovations exploring new phenomena, or obsolete research paradigms undergoing decay.
2. Disambiguating Emerging from Declining Themes: Require longitudinal multi-period science mapping (e.g., comparing Period 1 [2010-2015], Period 2 [2016-2020], and Period 3 [2021-2025]). If publication volume and citation growth accelerate across periods, the theme is Emerging; if volume contracts, it is Declining.
3. Software Execution: Automated in Bibliometrix (R `thematicMap`), SciMAT, and VOSviewer.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Identification Thresholds: Positioned strictly to the left of the median Callon centrality line (Centrality < 50th percentile).
2. Emerging Growth Rate: An emerging theme must exhibit a positive compound annual growth rate (CAGR >= 15-20%) in publication output over recent years.
3. PhD Proposal Positioning: Targeting an Emerging Theme with high growth potential provides an ideal academic foundation for high-impact doctoral dissertation contributions.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Conflating Emerging with Declining: Mislabeling a dying, abandoned research topic in the lower-left quadrant as an 'exciting emerging trend' without conducting longitudinal growth verification.
2. Isolating in Niche Traps: Conducting doctoral research strictly within a high-density, low-centrality Niche Theme without building conceptual bridges to broader disciplinary conversations, resulting in low citation impact.
3. Sensitivity to Temporal Segmentation: Slicing bibliometric time periods arbitrarily, which distorts quadrant positioning.
terms.apa_reference: Cobo, M. J., López-Herrera, A. G., Herrera-Viedma, E., & Herrera, F. (2011). Science mapping software tools: Review, analysis, and cooperative study among tools. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 62(7), 1382-1402. https://doi.org/10.1002/asi.21525

terms.vietnamese: Phân tích gộp mạng lưới (Network Meta-Analysis - NMA)
vietnamese_variants: Phân tích tổng hợp mạng lưới
So sánh điều trị đa phương pháp
terms.core_definition: Network Meta-Analysis (NMA)—also termed Multiple Treatments Meta-Analysis or Mixed Treatment Comparisons (Lumley, 2002; Lu & Ades, 2004)—is an advanced evidence synthesis methodology that simultaneously compares the comparative efficacy and safety of three or more competing interventions across an interconnected network of randomized controlled trials. Combining both Direct Evidence (head-to-head trials comparing Intervention A vs. B) and Indirect Evidence (synthesizing trials comparing A vs. C and B vs. C through a common comparator C), NMA calculates relative effect sizes between treatments that have never been directly compared in a single trial and ranks treatments probabilistically (SUCRA rankings).
terms.seminal_citation: Lu, G., & Ades, A. E. (2004). Combination of direct and indirect evidence in mixed treatment comparisons. Statistics in Medicine, 23(20), 3105-3124.
terms.expert_notes: Nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of NMA according to Bắt buộc kiểm tra giả định chuyển tiếp (Transitivity assumption) và tính nhất quán (Inconsistency test giữa direct và indirect p > .05). Xếp hạng can thiệp qua diện tích SUCRA (Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking Curve)..
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Network Geometry: Construct an evidence network graph where nodes represent competing interventions and connecting edges represent direct head-to-head clinical trials (edge thickness proportional to study count).
2. Core Methodological Assumptions:
   - Transitivity Assumption: Common comparator C is clinically and methodologically similar across both trial sets (A vs. C and B vs. C) to justify indirect comparison.
   - Coherence / Consistency Assumption: Direct evidence and indirect evidence must statistically agree: tau_{AB(Direct)} = tau_{AB(Indirect)}.
3. Statistical Estimation: Estimated using Bayesian hierarchical models via MCMC (WinBUGS, Stan) or frequentist graph-theoretical models (`netmeta` in R).
4. Inconsistency Evaluation: Evaluated globally via the Design-by-Treatment interaction model (Higgins et al., 2012) and locally via node-splitting.
5. Treatment Ranking: Compute the Surface Under the Cumulative Ranking curve (SUCRA; Salanti et al., 2011) to rank all treatments from 0% (worst) to 100% (best).
terms.benchmarks:
1. SUCRA Reporting: SUCRA percentages accompanied by mean ranks and rankograms for each intervention.
2. Inconsistency Benchmark: Global design-by-treatment test p > 0.05 indicates acceptable consistency between direct and indirect evidence.
3. PRISMA-NMA Compliance: Adheres strictly to the PRISMA-NMA reporting guidelines for network meta-analyses.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Intransitivity Violations: Combining trials where the common comparator (e.g., 'standard care') was executed with vastly different pharmacological protocols in different decades.
2. Disconnected Networks: Attempting to run NMA on an evidence graph with disconnected islands or isolated treatment loops that lack a shared bridge.
3. Over-Interpreting SUCRA Rankings: Treating small rank differences (e.g., SUCRA 78% vs. 74%) as conclusive clinical superiority when confidence intervals overlap heavily.
terms.apa_reference: Lu, G., & Ades, A. E. (2004). Combination of direct and indirect evidence in mixed treatment comparisons. Statistics in Medicine, 23(20), 3105-3124. https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.1875

terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số tương thích không quy chuẩn (NNFI / TLI)
terms.core_definition: The Non-Normed Fit Index (NNFI)—universally known in structural equation modeling and confirmatory factor analysis as the Tucker-Lewis Index (TLI; Tucker & Lewis, 1973; Bentler & Bonett, 1980)—is an incremental goodness-of-fit index that evaluates the relative improvement in fit of a target hypothesized model compared to a baseline null independence model. By incorporating a penalty for model complexity (degrees of freedom), NNFI rewards parsimonious models and is resilient to variations in sample size, though its non-normed mathematical structure permits values to occasionally fall below 0 or exceed 1.0.
terms.seminal_citation: Tucker, L. R., & Lewis, C. (1973). A reliability coefficient for maximum likelihood factor analysis. Psychometrika, 38(1), 1-10.
terms.expert_notes: LaTeX thô; nguồn ghi ngưỡng
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of NNFI according to Giá trị TLI/NNFI ≥ 0.90 là chấp nhận được; ≥ 0.95 là xuất sắc..
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Mathematical Formula: TLI = NNFI = [ (chi^2_null / df_null) - (chi^2_target / df_target) ] / [ (chi^2_null / df_null) - 1 ].
2. Complexity Penalty: Note that chi^2 / df is the expected value of chi-square under proper specification; models with fewer estimated parameters (larger df_target) receive a positive bonus, penalizing over-parameterized models.
3. Comparison with CFI: Unlike the Comparative Fit Index (CFI) which truncates strictly to [0, 1], NNFI is non-normed; under over-fitting or small samples, NNFI can exceed 1.0 (e.g., 1.02) or drop below 0.
4. Robust Estimation: Under robust estimators (MLR/MLM), report robust TLI incorporating Satorra-Bentler or Yuan-Bentler scaled chi-squares.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Rigorous Cutoff (Hu & Bentler, 1999): TLI / NNFI >= 0.95 indicates superior model fit; values between 0.90 and 0.95 indicate acceptable fit.
2. Sample Size Independence: Unlike chi-square, NNFI performance is stable across sample sizes (N = 100 to N = 10,000).
3. Parsimony Comparison: When comparing two competing models, the model with higher NNFI/TLI is preferred because it balances explanatory power with parameter parsimony.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Panic Over Values Exceeding 1.0: Believing that TLI = 1.01 represents a computational error; because it is non-normed, values slightly > 1.0 simply reflect extreme model parsimony or sampling noise.
2. Inappropriate Baseline in Non-Standard Models: Using default independence models when estimating models with mean structures or longitudinal invariance without properly adjusting df_null.
3. Reporting Single Cutoffs Mechanistically: Solely checking TLI >= 0.90 without simultaneously verifying CFI >= 0.95, RMSEA <= 0.06, and SRMR <= 0.08.
terms.apa_reference: Tucker, L. R., & Lewis, C. (1973). A reliability coefficient for maximum likelihood factor analysis. Psychometrika, 38(1), 1-10. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02291170

terms.vietnamese: Noema và Noesis (Ý thức hướng đích trong hiện tượng học Husserl)
vietnamese_variants: Ý hướng tính hiện tượng học
terms.core_definition: Noema and Noesis represent the foundational correlational dyad of intentionality in the transcendental phenomenology of Edmund Husserl (1913/1982). Husserl established that all human consciousness is intentional—it is always consciousness of something. Noesis denotes the subjective act, mode, or process of consciousness (e.g., the intentional act of remembering, perceiving, judging, or fearing), whereas Noema denotes the intentional object as it appears to consciousness, encompassing its objective meaning, sense, and noematic core (the remembered past event, the perceived building, the feared outcome).
terms.seminal_citation: Husserl, E. (1913/1982). Ideas pertaining to a pure phenomenology and to a phenomenological philosophy: First book (F. Kersten, Trans.). Martinus Nijhoff Publishers.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Noema and Noesis according to Husserl (1913).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Transcendental Correlation: Consciousness is structured as an inseparable intentional synthesis: Noesis (subjective experiencing act) <---> Noema (the experienced object as meant).
2. Epoché and Phenomenological Reduction: Suspend the 'natural attitude' (the assumption that objects exist independently of consciousness) to investigate the noetic-noematic structure.
3. Qualitative Research Operationalization (Moustakas, 1994):
   - Noetic Analysis: Analyzing how participants perceive, feel, judge, and mentally construct meaning around a crisis (the act of experiencing).
   - Noematic Analysis: Reconstructing the textural description—what was experienced, the concrete qualities and attributes of the phenomenon as described by participants.
   - Structural Synthesis: Combining textural (noematic) and structural (noetic) descriptions to arrive at the universal essence of the lived experience.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Phenomenological Depth: Analysis must capture both what was experienced (noema) and how it was experienced (noesis).
2. Essence Extraction: Transcending mere descriptive summaries of participant words to reconstruct the essential invariant psychological structure of the phenomenon.
3. Epoché Transparency: Documenting the researcher's bracketing journal to ensure personal preconceptions do not distort noetic interpretation.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Collapsing Noema into Real Physical Object: Treating the Noema as an objective physical entity in the world rather than the object-as-meant in consciousness.
2. Psychologizing Noesis: Reducing Noesis to purely biological brain states or cognitive mechanics, ignoring its transcendental meaning-giving function.
3. Superficial Textural Description: Writing qualitative dissertations that describe only noematic surface details while completely ignoring the noetic modes of consciousness and sensemaking.
terms.apa_reference: Husserl, E. (1982). Ideas pertaining to a pure phenomenology and to a phenomenological philosophy: First book (F. Kersten, Trans.). Martinus Nijhoff Publishers. (Original work published 1913). (See also: Moustakas, C., 1994, Phenomenological Research Methods, SAGE).

terms.vietnamese: Dữ liệu định danh (Nominal Data)
vietnamese_variants: Dữ liệu phân loại rời rạc
terms.core_definition: Nominal Data represents the lowest, most fundamental level in S. S. Stevens' (1946) classic fourfold hierarchy of measurement scales (Nominal, Ordinal, Interval, Ratio). In nominal measurement, numbers or alphanumeric labels serve exclusively as qualitative identifiers or categorical tags to designate distinct, mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive categories without any inherent quantitative magnitude, distance, or rank order. Mathematical operations are restricted to equivalence relations ($=$ or $\neq$), counting frequencies, mode identification, and contingency table association tests.
terms.seminal_citation: Stevens, S. S. (1946). On the theory of scales of measurement. Science, 103(2684), 677-680.
terms.expert_notes: Lộ tên file nội bộ
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Nominal data according to Saunders et al. (2019); Saunders (2019).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Mathematical Definition: Let universe U be partitioned into discrete categories C = {c_1, c_2, ..., c_k}. The mapping f: U -> C satisfies f(a) = f(b) if and only if a and b belong to the same qualitative category.
2. Permissible Transformations: One-to-one substitutions (invariance under any one-to-one transformation: f'(x) = g(f(x)) where g is bijective). Re-coding [Male = 1, Female = 2] to [Male = 100, Female = 200] leaves statistical meaning unchanged.
3. Descriptive Statistics: Frequencies, percentages, proportions, and the Mode (arithmetic mean and median are mathematically meaningless).
4. Inferential Testing: Pearson's Chi-Square Test of Independence (chi^2), Fisher's Exact Test, Goodness-of-Fit chi-square; association metrics include Cramér's V, Phi coefficient, and Cohen's Kappa for inter-rater agreement.
5. Econometric Encoding: Converted into k-1 dummy (indicator) variables (0/1) for regression modeling, or analyzed directly via Multinomial Logistic Regression.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Permissible Operations: Equality and inequality only (=, !=); ordering (<, >) and arithmetic (+, -, *, /) are strictly invalid.
2. MECE Requirement: Categories must be Mutually Exclusive (each case fits only one category) and Collectively Exhaustive (every case fits a category).
3. Association Benchmark: Cramér's V (0 to 1): V < 0.10 (weak), 0.10-0.30 (moderate), > 0.30 (strong association).
terms.pitfalls:
1. Computing Means on Nominal Codes: Calculating the arithmetic mean or standard deviation of nominal variables (e.g., 'mean gender = 1.45' or 'mean industry = 3.2'), which is statistically invalid and meaningless.
2. The Dummy Variable Trap: Including all k dummy variables alongside an intercept in OLS regression, causing perfect multicollinearity and matrix non-invertibility.
3. Treating Nominal as Ordinal: Imposing an arbitrary numerical ordering onto unordered categories (e.g., assigning 1 = Red, 2 = Blue, 3 = Green in regression) rather than using dummy encoding.
terms.apa_reference: Stevens, S. S. (1946). On the theory of scales of measurement. Science, 103(2684), 677-680. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.103.2684.677

terms.vietnamese: Kỹ thuật nhóm danh nghĩa (Phương pháp luận đồng thuận NGT)
vietnamese_variants: Kỹ thuật ra quyết định nhóm NGT
terms.core_definition: The Nominal Group Technique (NGT) is an established structured group consensus decision-making methodology formulated by André L. Delbecq and Andrew H. Van de Ven (1971) to maximize creative problem-solving and democratic prioritization among diverse stakeholders. Operating on the principle that individuals generate higher quality and greater volume of ideas when working initially in silent contemplation rather than unstructured interactive brainstorming, NGT orchestrates small panels through four rigid phases to eradicate dominance by vocal participants, eliminate status hierarchies, and resolve conflicting organizational priorities.
terms.seminal_citation: Delbecq, A. L., & Van de Ven, A. H. (1971). A group process model for problem identification and program planning. The Journal of Applied Behavioral Science, 7(4), 466-492.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Nominal Group Technique according to Quy trình 4 pha: Tạo ý tưởng thầm lặng → Thu thập vòng tròn → Thảo luận làm rõ → Bỏ phiếu xếp hạng độc lập..
terms.benchmarks:
1. Group Panel Size: Optimal panel size is 5 to 9 participants; larger groups should be partitioned into parallel tables with final inter-group vote pooling.
2. Voting Consistency: Kendall's Coefficient of Concordance (W) computed across individual rank ballots (W >= 0.70 indicates strong group consensus).
3. Equality of Voice: Round-robin phase ensures 100% equal contribution rate across senior executives and junior personnel.
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Phase 1 (Silent Idea Generation): Participants silently record thoughts on paper regarding a focal question for 10-15 minutes, avoiding verbal exchange.
2. Phase 2 (Round-Robin Recording): The facilitator solicits one idea per participant in turn, writing each verbatim on a central display board until all ideas are cataloged; zero debate or critique is permitted.
3. Phase 3 (Serial Discussion & Clarification): Each listed idea is reviewed sequentially for wording clarification, semantic merging of duplicates, and conceptual elucidation.
4. Phase 4 (Confidential Voting & Mathematical Ranking): Participants independently and privately score or rank the top 5 to 7 prioritized items on anonymous ballots; votes are aggregated mathematically to establish final rank order.
5. Comparison with Delphi: NGT is conducted in a single synchronous face-to-face or virtual session, whereas Delphi is asynchronous, geographically dispersed, and multiround.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Allowing Early Debates in Phase 2: Permitting evaluative or dismissive comments during round-robin recording, which triggers defensive withdrawal.
2. Semantic Smuggling During Clarification: Facilitators or aggressive members altering the original meaning of an item during the clarification phase.
3. Public Hand-Raising Votes: Conducting final voting via public hand-raising instead of confidential ballots, instantly resurrecting conformity pressure and social desirability bias.
terms.apa_reference: Delbecq, A. L., & Van de Ven, A. H. (1971). A group process model for problem identification and program planning. The Journal of Applied Behavioral Science, 7(4), 466-492. https://doi.org/10.1177/002188637100700404

terms.term: Nominal Group Technique (NGT - Applied Health & Organizational Protocol)
terms.vietnamese: Quy trình thực thi kỹ thuật nhóm danh nghĩa NGT
vietnamese_variants: Thực hành NGT trong nghiên cứu y tế và quản trị
terms.core_definition: The Nominal Group Technique (NGT - Applied Protocol) represents the standardized procedural implementation of NGT across clinical guideline development, health services research, and organizational change management (Cantrill et al., 1996; Van de Ven & Delbecq, 1974). By bridging qualitative elicitation of experiential knowledge with quantitative prioritization, applied NGT produces actionable, high-validity consensus agendas for healthcare policy, curriculum redesign, and corporate strategic realignment.
terms.seminal_citation: Van de Ven, A. H., & Delbecq, A. L. (1974). The effectiveness of Nominal, Delphi, and interacting group decision making processes. Academy of Management Journal, 17(4), 605-621.
terms.expert_notes: Trùng #1754
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Nominal Group Technique (NGT) according to Delbecq & Van de Ven (1971).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Pre-Session Preparation: Formulate an unambiguous, non-leading prompt question and assemble a purposively sampled panel of key informants (e.g., patients, clinicians, managers).
2. Structured Workshop Execution (90-120 minutes):
   - Step 1: Welcome and silent writing (15 min).
   - Step 2: Round-robin listing on shared electronic canvas (Miro, Padlet) or physical whiteboard (30 min).
   - Step 3: Discussion, grouping of themes, and elimination of literal redundancy (30 min).
   - Step 4: Confidential 5-point rank ordering (15 min).
3. Quantitative Aggregation Formulas: Calculate Mean Rank, Summed Score, and Relative Priority Index (RPI) for each item: RPI_j = (sum v_{ij}) / (N * v_max).
4. Member Verification: Display final mathematical aggregate rankings back to the workshop participants immediately for brief member reflection and validation.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Completion Timing: Complete cycle executed within a single structured 2-hour workshop.
2. Item Retention Threshold: Items receiving votes from >= 50% of panellists or accumulating an aggregate priority score in the top tertile are retained.
3. Transparent Reporting: Published studies must report the exact prompt question, number of participants, initial item count, merged item count, and full rank-order voting distribution.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Premature Thematic Collapsing: Merging subtly distinct items into vague umbrella categories during Step 3, which dilutes specific operational actionability.
2. Facilitator Bias in Prompt Formulation: Phrasing the core prompt with subtle normative expectations that nudge participants toward administrative priorities.
3. Lack of Follow-Through Strategy: Treating the NGT ranked list as a final research output without linking prioritized items to empirical measurement or policy implementation.
terms.apa_reference: Van de Ven, A. H., & Delbecq, A. L. (1974). The effectiveness of Nominal, Delphi, and interacting group decision making processes. Academy of Management Journal, 17(4), 605-621. https://doi.org/10.2307/255641

terms.vietnamese: Giá trị mạng lưới lý thuyết / Giá trị quy luật Nomological
vietnamese_variants: Hiệu lực mạng lưới lý thuyết
terms.core_definition: Nomological Validity (Giá trị quy luật lý thuyết) là đỉnh cao của việc chứng minh giá trị khái niệm (construct validity), do Lee Cronbach và Paul Meehl sáng lập trong bài báo kinh điển năm 1955. Giá trị này được xác lập khi một cấu trúc đo lường mới vận hành đúng như những gì được dự đoán bởi một 'Mạng lưới quy luật' (Nomological Network) - tức là nó có mối quan hệ tương quan, tác động tích cực, tiêu cực hoặc trung gian một cách hợp lý và có ý nghĩa thống kê với các cấu trúc lý thuyết khác đã được khoa học thừa nhận vững chắc từ trước.
terms.seminal_citation: Cronbach, L. J., & Meehl, P. E. (1955). Construct validity in psychological tests. Psychological Bulletin, 52(4), 281-302.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Nomological Validity according to Cronbach & Meehl (1955).
terms.operational_mechanism: Quy trình kiểm định mạng lưới Nomological: (1) Xây dựng mạng lưới lý thuyết tiên nghiệm chỉ rõ cấu trúc mới X có tiền đề (antecedents) là gì, biến hậu quả (consequences) là gì, và biến tương quan tương đồng là gì; (2) Thu thập dữ liệu đồng thời trên cấu trúc mới và các cấu trúc trong mạng lưới; (3) Chạy mô hình SEM hoặc ma trận tương quan; (4) Đối chiếu: Nếu cấu trúc mới tương quan thuận với tiền đề giả thuyết (ví dụ: Động lực nội tại tương quan thuận với Hiệu suất công việc) và tương quan nghịch với đối cực (suy giảm Ý định nghỉ việc), thì giá trị Nomological được xác nhận.
benchmarks: Phù hợp với hướng và độ lớn dự kiến lý thuyết: Mọi liên kết trong mô hình cấu trúc phải có dấu (+ hoặc -) và p-value < 0.05 đúng như dự báo lý thuyết.
Không được có mối tương quan phi lý: Cấu trúc mới không được tương quan mạnh với các biến hoàn toàn xa lạ hoặc mâu thuẫn nhận thức luận.
Độ phù hợp toàn diện của mô hình mạng lưới: Mô hình SEM chứa mạng lưới Nomological phải đạt chuẩn fit tốt (CFI ≥ 0.95, SRMR ≤ 0.08).
pitfalls: Xây dựng mạng lưới Nomological nghèo nàn: Chỉ kiểm tra mối quan hệ với duy nhất một biến phụ thuộc đơn lẻ thay vì một hệ thống các tiền đề và hậu quả đa dạng.
Thang đo mới tương quan quá cao với cấu trúc đã có (r > 0.85): Rơi vào bẫy 'bình mới rượu cũ' (Jangle Fallacy) - cấu trúc mới thực chất chỉ là một bản sao chép của một khái niệm đã tồn tại.
Bỏ qua các mối quan hệ nghịch đảo dự kiến: Không đưa các biến có quan hệ tiêu cực giả thuyết vào mạng lưới để kiểm tra tính đối xứng.
terms.apa_reference: Cronbach, L. J., & Meehl, P. E. (1955). Construct validity in psychological tests. Psychological Bulletin, 52(4), 281-302. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0040957

terms.vietnamese: Thử nghiệm không thua kém (Non-Inferiority Trial)
vietnamese_variants: Thử nghiệm lâm sàng không kém hơn
terms.core_definition: A Non-Inferiority Trial is an experimental clinical trial design whose primary objective is to demonstrate that a novel experimental intervention (e.g., a cheaper, less toxic, or more convenient drug) is not unacceptably worse than an established standard active comparator by more than a predefined, clinically acceptable non-inferiority margin ($\Delta$). Unlike superiority trials (which test whether treatment exceeds control) or equivalence trials (which test whether two treatments are indistinguishable within a symmetric window), non-inferiority trials utilize an asymmetric, one-sided hypothesis testing framework.
terms.seminal_citation: Blackwelder, W. C. (1982). "Proving the null hypothesis" in clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 3(4), 345-353.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Non-Inferiority Trial according to Piaggio et al. (2012).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Hypothesis Formulation: Let mu_T be novel treatment efficacy, mu_C be active comparator efficacy, and Delta > 0 be the pre-specified non-inferiority margin.
   - Null Hypothesis (Inferiority): H0: mu_C - mu_T >= Delta (treatment is inferior by at least Delta).
   - Alternative Hypothesis (Non-Inferiority): H1: mu_C - mu_T < Delta (treatment is not inferior by more than Delta).
2. Margin Determination (Delta): Determined based on clinical judgment and historical statistical evidence from prior placebo-controlled trials to preserve at least 50% of the active control's established efficacy effect over placebo.
3. Analysis Populations: Crucially evaluated on BOTH Intention-to-Treat (ITT) and Per-Protocol (PP) populations. In non-inferiority designs, ITT is non-conservative because non-compliance and protocol deviations dilute treatment differences toward zero, artificially favoring the non-inferiority claim.
4. Decision Rule: Non-inferiority is formally established if the lower bound of the two-sided 95% (or one-sided 97.5%) confidence interval for the treatment difference (mu_T - mu_C) lies strictly above -Delta.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Dual Concordance: Non-inferiority must achieve statistical significance in BOTH the Intention-to-Treat (ITT) AND Per-Protocol (PP) populations.
2. Regulatory Guideline Alignment: Margin selection must comply with FDA (2016) and EMA (2005) guidance documents.
3. Assay Sensitivity: Historical evidence must establish that the active comparator retained efficacy within the trial setting.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Inflating the Non-Inferiority Margin (Delta): Setting an excessively wide margin Delta to guarantee a significant non-inferiority claim, which permits clinically ineffective or harmful treatments to be deemed 'non-inferior'.
2. Relying Solely on ITT Analysis: Presenting only ITT results, which biases the trial toward accepting non-inferiority due to non-adherence dilution.
3. Creeping Non-Inferiority (Biocreep): Progressively comparing new generations of drugs to previous marginally non-inferior drugs, causing gradual cumulative loss of true therapeutic efficacy.
terms.apa_reference: Blackwelder, W. C. (1982). "Proving the null hypothesis" in clinical trials. Controlled Clinical Trials, 3(4), 345-353. https://doi.org/10.1016/0197-2456(82)90024-1

terms.vietnamese: Chỉ số Tucker-Lewis (Chỉ số Phù hợp Phi Chuẩn hóa TLI / NNFI)
domain_tags: Độ phù hợp Mô hình (Model Fit)
terms.core_definition: Chỉ số độ phù hợp mô hình so sánh gia tăng do Ledyard Tucker và Charles Lewis (1973) phát minh ban đầu cho phân tích nhân tố, và được Bentler & Bonett (1980) đưa vào SEM dưới tên gọi Non-Normed Fit Index (NNFI). TLI so sánh mức độ cải thiện của hàm hợp lý trên mỗi bậc tự do giữa mô hình đề xuất và mô hình cơ sở rỗng. Nhờ có thành phần phạt độ phức tạp (Degrees of freedom penalty), TLI không bị tăng lên một cách giả tạo khi thêm các tham số tự do như chỉ số NFI cổ điển.
terms.seminal_citation: Tucker, L. R., & Lewis, C. (1973). A reliability coefficient for maximum likelihood factor analysis. Psychometrika, 38(1), 1–10. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02291170; Bentler, P. M., & Bonett, D. G. (1980). Significance tests and goodness of fit in the analysis of covariance structures. Psychological Bulletin, 88(3), 588–606.
terms.expert_notes: Định nghĩa và ngưỡng kiểm định chuẩn hóa từ Cơ sở dữ liệu Viết tắt Học thuật (Acronym Registry).
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Non-Normed Fit Index (Tucker-Lewis Index - TLI) according to Giá trị TLI/NNFI ≥ 0.90 là chấp nhận được; ≥ 0.95 là xuất sắc..
terms.benchmarks: Quy chuẩn đánh giá: TLI ≥ 0.95 (xuất sắc) và TLI ≥ 0.90 (chấp nhận được). Khi so sánh giữa hai mô hình lồng nhau cạnh tranh, mô hình nào có TLI cao hơn được đánh giá là tiết kiệm (parsimonious) và tối ưu hơn về mặt cấu trúc.
terms.pitfalls: Hiểu lầm khi thấy TLI > 1.0 (cho rằng phần mềm bị lỗi): Vì TLI không bị chuẩn hóa gò bó trong khoảng [0, 1], trong các mẫu nhỏ hoặc khi ma trận tương quan rất mạnh, giá trị của nó có thể vượt nhẹ quá 1.0.
terms.apa_reference: Tucker, L. R., & Lewis, C. (1973). A reliability coefficient for maximum likelihood factor analysis. Psychometrika, 38(1), 1–10.

terms.vietnamese: Sai số do không phản hồi (Non-Response Error)
vietnamese_variants: Sai số do bỏ cuộc khảo sát
terms.core_definition: Non-Response Error is a major component of the Total Survey Error (TSE) framework (Groves et al., 2004) occurring when members of the designated sample fail to participate in the survey (Unit Non-Response) or fail to answer specific questionnaire items (Item Non-Response), and those who do not respond differ systematically from those who do on the substantive variables of interest. Non-response error is not merely a function of response rate; it depends mathematically on both the non-response rate and the magnitude of the difference between respondents and non-respondents: $\text{Bias}(\bar{y}_r) = \frac{M}{N} (\bar{Y}_r - \bar{Y}_m)$.
terms.seminal_citation: Armstrong, J. S., & Overton, T. S. (1977). Estimating nonresponse bias in mail surveys. Journal of Marketing Research, 14(3), 396-402.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Non-Response Error according to Dillman et al. (2014).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Mathematical Formulation: Bias(y_bar_r) = (m / n) * (y_bar_r - y_bar_m), where n is total sample size, m is number of non-respondents, y_bar_r is respondent mean, and y_bar_m is non-respondent mean.
2. Diagnostic Testing Protocols:
   - Wave Analysis (Armstrong & Overton, 1977): Compare early respondents with late respondents (who required extensive follow-up prods, acting as a proxy for non-respondents) via independent t-tests across focal constructs.
   - Archival / Frame Comparison: Compare respondent demographics (age, gender, firm size) against known population frame statistics.
   - Non-Respondent Follow-Up Sub-sample: Contact a random 10-20% sample of initial non-respondents via intensive telephone or in-person outreach to directly measure y_bar_m.
3. Post-Survey Corrections: Apply Post-Stratification Weighting, Propensity Score Weighting, or Full Information Maximum Likelihood / MICE imputation.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Wave Analysis Criterion: No statistically significant differences (p > 0.05) between early and late survey waves across focal study constructs.
2. Response Rate Standards: Response rates >= 50-60% traditionally sought, though modern survey science demonstrates that low response rates with low non-response bias can outperform high response rates with selective non-response.
3. TSE Reporting: Methodology sections must report response rates calculated according to standard AAPOR (American Association for Public Opinion Research) formulas.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Equating High Response Rate with Zero Bias: Assuming an 80% response rate guarantees zero error; if the remaining 20% non-respondents differ sharply on the outcome, bias remains severe.
2. Ignoring Non-Response in Cross-Sectional Studies: Submitting survey research to Q1 journals without conducting wave analysis or non-response testing, triggering automatic reviewer rejection.
3. Unverified Informal Substitutions: Allowing field interviewers to replace non-responding households with willing neighbors, converting probability sampling into non-probability convenience sampling.
terms.apa_reference: Armstrong, J. S., & Overton, T. S. (1977). Estimating nonresponse bias in mail surveys. Journal of Marketing Research, 14(3), 396-402. https://doi.org/10.1177/002224377701400320

terms.vietnamese: Mối liên hệ phi ngụy tạo (Non-Spurious Association)
vietnamese_variants: Mối liên hệ không giả tạo
terms.core_definition: A Non-Spurious Association is the third mandatory criterion in John Stuart Mill's (1843) classic triad of causal inference (alongside Covariation and Temporal Precedence), stating that an observed statistical correlation between an independent variable ($X$) and a dependent variable ($Y$) cannot be explained away as the coincidental artifact of a third, unmeasured confounding variable ($Z$) that causes both. If a third variable $Z$ simultaneously produces $X$ and $Y$ ($X \leftarrow Z \rightarrow Y$), the bivariate association between $X$ and $Y$ is spurious; true non-spuriousness exists if and only if the relationship persists when all relevant confounders are controlled or neutralized.
terms.seminal_citation: Simon, H. A. (1954). Spurious correlation: A causal interpretation. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 49(267), 467-479.
terms.expert_notes: Đã chuẩn hóa từ bảng trích xuất sang định dạng từ điển chuẩn.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Non-spurious association according to Hunt (2015).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Graphical Confounding Topology: Spuriousness occurs in fork causal DAGs: X <- Z -> Y. Controlling for Z d-separates X and Y, collapsing their partial correlation to zero: Corr(X, Y | Z) = 0.
2. Statistical Testing (Partial Correlation): r_{XY.Z} = [ r_{XY} - (r_{XZ} * r_{YZ}) ] / [ sqrt(1 - r_{XZ}^2) * sqrt(1 - r_{YZ}^2) ]. If r_{XY.Z} drops to zero, the original correlation r_{XY} was entirely spurious.
3. Methodological Elimination Strategies:
   - Experimental Randomization: Random assignment of X breaks all arrows from upstream confounders Z into X.
   - Statistical Conditioning: Multiple regression, propensity score matching, panel fixed-effects.
   - Quasi-Experimental Identification: Instrumental variables, Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).
4. Sensitivity Analysis: Frank's Impact Threshold for Confounding (ITCV) or VanderWeele's E-value quantifying the strength an unmeasured confounder must possess to render the observed association spurious.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Partial Slope Stability: Focal regression slope beta_1 must remain statistically significant and substantively stable after introducing exhaustive vectors of theoretically plausible confounders.
2. E-Value Benchmark: An E-value > 2.0 to 3.0 indicates that an unmeasured confounder would have to be associated with both exposure and outcome by a risk ratio of 2-3-fold to nullify the effect.
3. Longitudinal Replication: Establishing that X predicts changes in Y over time while partialling out baseline Y and third-party trends.
terms.pitfalls:
1. The Stork-Baby Fallacy: Citing high bivariate correlations (e.g., number of storks and human birth rates) without recognizing common geographic or seasonal third-factor confounders.
2. Post-Hoc Rationalization of Spurious Trends: Creating elaborate narrative theories to explain spurious longitudinal correlations resulting from shared macro trends (e.g., US cheese consumption correlating with golf revenue).
3. The Kitchen-Sink Over-Correction: Controlling for intermediate mediators or colliders in an attempt to prove non-spuriousness, which inadvertently introduces collider stratification bias.
terms.apa_reference: Simon, H. A. (1954). Spurious correlation: A causal interpretation. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 49(267), 467-479. https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1954.10483515

terms.vietnamese: Giả thuyết phi định hướng (Nondirectional Hypothesis)
terms.core_definition: A Nondirectional Hypothesis (or Two-Tailed Hypothesis) is a declarative scientific proposition predicting that a relationship, difference, or treatment effect exists between two or more constructs or groups, but deliberately refrains from specifying the positive or negative mathematical direction of that effect (e.g., 'There is a significant difference in employee job performance between remote and in-office workers'; $H_1: \mu_1 \neq \mu_2$). Employed primarily in exploratory, nascent, or contested research domains where existing theoretical frameworks offer conflicting predictions, nondirectional hypotheses mandate the use of two-tailed statistical tests, distributing Type I error probability ($\\alpha$) equally into both tails of the sampling distribution.
terms.seminal_citation: Neyman, J., & Pearson, E. S. (1933). On the problem of the most efficient tests of statistical hypotheses. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, 231(694-706), 289-337.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Nondirectional hypothesis according to Creswell & Creswell (2023).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Statistical Formulation:
   - Null Hypothesis: H0: theta = theta_0 (or mu_1 - mu_2 = 0).
   - Alternative Hypothesis: H1: theta != theta_0 (or mu_1 - mu_2 != 0).
2. Critical Value Split: For significance level alpha = 0.05, the rejection region is divided symmetrically: alpha/2 = 0.025 in the lower tail and alpha/2 = 0.025 in the upper tail.
3. Critical Test Statistics: Critical z = +/- 1.96 (contrasted with directional one-tailed z = +1.645 or -1.645).
4. Confidence Interval Inversion: A two-tailed hypothesis test rejected at alpha = 0.05 corresponds exactly to a 95% two-sided confidence interval excluding the null value theta_0.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Rejection Rule: Reject H0 if test statistic t <= -t_{crit, alpha/2} OR t >= +t_{crit, alpha/2}.
2. Theoretical Justification: Recommended when empirical literature is contradictory, theory is exploratory, or discovery of an unexpected effect in the opposite direction carries vital scientific value.
3. Q1 Journal Standard: Elite journals in business, psychology, and social sciences universally mandate two-tailed testing as the default standard to curb researcher opportunism.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Directional Language Drift: Writing a nondirectional formal hypothesis (H1: difference exists) but phrasing all theoretical literature and discussion in strictly directional terms (e.g., 'Method A is better').
2. Switching to One-Tailed Post-Hoc: Converting a nondirectional test to a one-tailed test after seeing an empirical p-value of 0.07 to artificially claim p = 0.035, which constitutes severe p-hacking.
3. Power Deficit in Confirmatory Research: Using nondirectional hypotheses when strong, uncontested theoretical consensus exists, unnecessarily sacrificing statistical power.
terms.apa_reference: Neyman, J., & Pearson, E. S. (1933). On the problem of the most efficient tests of statistical hypotheses. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, 231(694-706), 289-337. https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1933.0009

terms.vietnamese: Lý thuyết Tai nạn Tất yếu (Normal Accident Theory - Charles Perrow)
vietnamese_variants: Lý thuyết tai nạn bình thường
Thuyết rủi ro hệ thống Perrow
terms.core_definition: Normal Accident Theory (NAT)—formulated by sociologist Charles Perrow in his seminal work Normal Accidents: Living with High-Risk Technologies (1984)—posits that in modern complex socio-technical systems (e.g., nuclear power plants, chemical manufacturing, commercial aviation, algorithmic financial trading), catastrophic accidents are inevitable and 'normal' (systemic properties). Perrow demonstrated that when a system exhibits the structural combination of High Interactive Complexity (unplanned, unfamiliar, and invisible feedback interactions among subcomponents) and Tight Coupling (time-dependent processes with rigid sequences, zero slack, and rapid invariant cascades), minor independent operator errors or component failures inevitably interact unexpectedly to produce catastrophic systemic collapse that baffles operators and defeats safety redundancies.
terms.seminal_citation: Perrow, C. (1984). Normal accidents: Living with high-risk technologies. Basic Books.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Normal Accident Theory (Charles Perrow) according to Perrow (1984).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Two-Dimensional Structural Grid (Perrow Matrix):
   - Interactive Complexity (Linear vs. Complex): Linear systems have predictable, segregated causal steps; Complex systems have branching paths, feedback loops, shared equipment, and multi-functional components.
   - Coupling (Loose vs. Tight): Loosely coupled systems have operational slack, delays, and localized buffers; Tightly coupled systems have immediate time-dependency, invariant process sequences, and no capacity to pause.
2. The Structural Trap: Tightly coupled, interactively complex systems cannot be rendered safe purely by adding warning devices and redundancies; adding redundant safety subsystems actually increases interactive complexity, creating novel failure pathways.
3. Centralization-Decentralization Paradox: Tight coupling requires centralized rapid executive authority; interactive complexity requires decentralized frontline operator discretion. Systems possessing both characteristics face irreconcilable organizational design contradictions.
4. Methodological Operationalization: Applied in qualitative disaster post-mortems, forensic engineering case studies, and safety culture audits.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Typology Diagnostic: Case studies must formally classify systems along both axes (Interaction and Coupling).
2. Root Cause Tracing: Explanations must trace systemic failure to the unexpected interaction of multiple small anomalies rather than lazily scapegoating 'operator error'.
3. Rival Framework Comparison: Contrast findings with High Reliability Organization (HRO) theory (Weick & Sutcliffe), evaluating whether organizational mindfulness can overcome NAT structural traps.
terms.pitfalls:
1. The Human Error Scapegoat Trap: Concluding that a disaster was caused purely by 'individual operator negligence', ignoring the structural interactive complexity that made operator comprehension impossible.
2. Misinterpreting 'Normal': Confusing Perrow's term 'normal' with frequent or routine; Perrow meant that accidents are an inherent, inevitable structural characteristic of the system architecture.
3. Over-Engineering Redundancy: Proposing additional automated safety devices as the sole solution without recognizing that added technological layers increase interactive complexity.
terms.apa_reference: Perrow, C. (1984). Normal accidents: Living with high-risk technologies. Basic Books. (Revised ed., 1999, Princeton University Press).

terms.vietnamese: Phân phối chuẩn (Phân phối Gauss)
terms.core_definition: The Normal Distribution (also known as the Gaussian Distribution or Bell Curve), formalized mathematically by Carl Friedrich Gauss (1809) and Pierre-Simon Laplace (1812), is the paramount continuous probability distribution in statistics and empirical research. Characterized by its symmetric bell-shaped probability density function completely specified by two parameters—mean ($\mu$) and variance ($\sigma^2$), denoted $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$—the normal distribution serves as the axiomatic foundation of parametric statistical inference, justified empirically by the Central Limit Theorem (CLT) which guarantees that the sum or average of a large number of independent random variables converges to normality regardless of the underlying population distribution.
terms.seminal_citation: Gauss, C. F. (1809). Theoria motus corporum coelestium in sectionibus conicis solem ambientium [Theory of the motion of heavenly bodies moving about the sun in conic sections]. Perthes et Besser.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Normal Distribution (Gaussian) according to Gauss (1809).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Probability Density Function (PDF): f(x) = [ 1 / (sigma * sqrt(2*pi)) ] * exp( - (x - mu)^2 / (2 * sigma^2) ) for -inf < x < inf.
2. Symmetry & Moment Properties:
   - Mean = Median = Mode = mu.
   - Skewness = 0.0 (perfect distributional symmetry).
   - Kurtosis = 3.0 (Excess Kurtosis = Kurtosis - 3 = 0.0, mesokurtic baseline).
   - Inflection points located exactly at mu +/- sigma.
3. The Empirical 68-95-99.7 Rule:
   - ~68.27% of observations fall within mu +/- 1*sigma.
   - ~95.45% of observations fall within mu +/- 2*sigma (precisely 95% within mu +/- 1.96*sigma).
   - ~99.73% of observations fall within mu +/- 3*sigma.
4. Standard Normal Transformation (Z-score): z = (x - mu) / sigma, transforming N(mu, sigma^2) to standard normal N(0, 1).
5. Normality Diagnostics: Evaluated via Shapiro-Wilk test, Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, Anderson-Darling test, and graphical Q-Q plots.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Skewness / Kurtosis Acceptability: For univariate normality in SEM, |Skewness| < 2.0 and |Excess Kurtosis| < 7.0 (Curran et al., 1996; Kline, 2016).
2. Standard Score Conversion: Enables calculation of standardized effect sizes (Cohen's d) and p-values.
3. CLT Threshold: Sample size N >= 30-50 generally justifies relying on asymptotic normality of the sample mean.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Confusing Normality of Variables with Normality of Residuals: In multiple regression, OLS assumes that the regression disturbances (residuals) are normally distributed, NOT the raw independent or dependent variables.
2. Over-Reliance on Significance Tests in Huge Samples: Rejecting normality based purely on a statistically significant Shapiro-Wilk test (p < 0.001) in samples of N > 1,000, where trivial, harmless deviations trigger false rejections.
3. Fat-Tailed Financial Misapplication: Assuming financial asset returns or catastrophic risks follow Gaussian distributions, which catastrophically underestimates the probability of extreme tail events (black swan events; Taleb).
terms.apa_reference: Gauss, C. F. (1809). Theoria motus corporum coelestium in sectionibus conicis solem ambientium. Perthes et Besser. (See also: Laplace, P. S., 1812, Théorie analytique des probabilités, Courcier).

terms.vietnamese: Biểu đồ xác suất chuẩn / Biểu đồ Q-Q (Q-Q Plot)
vietnamese_variants: Đồ thị phân vị chuẩn Q-Q
terms.core_definition: A Normal Probability Plot (predominantly implemented as a Quantile-Quantile or Q-Q Plot; Wilk & Gnanadesikan, 1968) is a graphical exploratory diagnostic technique used to evaluate whether an observed empirical dataset or regression residual distribution conforms to a theoretical normal distribution. By plotting the quantiles of the empirical sample distribution against the corresponding theoretical quantiles of a standard normal distribution, the Q-Q plot allows researchers to detect departures from normality—including positive/negative skewness, heavy/light tails, and discrete outliers—with nuanced visual clarity that formal statistical significance tests cannot provide.
terms.seminal_citation: Wilk, M. B., & Gnanadesikan, R. (1968). Probability plotting methods for the analysis of data. Biometrika, 55(1), 1-17.
terms.core_definition_en: Academic definition of Normal Probability Plot (Q-Q Plot) according to Wilk & Gnanadesikan (1968).
terms.operational_mechanism:
1. Plot Construction Mechanics:
   - Step 1: Sort observed sample data of size n in ascending order: x_{(1)} <= x_{(2)} <= ... <= x_{(n)}.
   - Step 2: Compute plotting positions (empirical cumulative probabilities): p_i = (i - a) / (n + 1 - 2a) (e.g., Blom's formula with a = 3/8: p_i = (i - 0.375) / (n + 0.25)).
   - Step 3: Compute theoretical quantiles by evaluating standard normal inverse CDF: q_i = Phi^(-1)(p_i).
   - Step 4: Plot observed values x_{(i)} (or standardized residuals) on vertical axis against theoretical quantiles q_i on horizontal axis.
2. Visual Interpretation Diagnostics:
   - Linear 45-degree alignment: Perfect normality.
   - Convex upward curve: Positive skewness (right-skewed).
   - Concave downward curve: Negative skewness (left-skewed).
   - S-shaped curve (tails bending away from line): Heavy tails (leptokurtic, fat tails).
   - Inverted S-shaped curve: Light tails (platykurtic).
   - Isolated outer dots: Extreme outliers.
terms.benchmarks:
1. Alignment Heuristic: Observed points must adhere tightly to the diagonal reference line across the interquartile range (-1.0 < z < +1.0); minor wandering in outer extreme tails (|z| > 2.5) is expected in moderate samples.
2. Preferred Diagnostic: Recommended over formal numerical tests (Shapiro-Wilk) in large samples because Q-Q plots allow qualitative assessment of whether deviations are substantively consequential.
3. Residual Diagnostic Standard: Mandatory exhibit in regression and ANOVA diagnostic appendices.
terms.pitfalls:
1. Over-Interpreting Extreme Tail Wiggles: Treating minor tail fluctuations as proof of non-normality in small samples (N < 50), where sampling noise naturally creates tail dispersion.
2. Plotting Raw Variables Instead of Regression Residuals: Checking Q-Q plots of raw independent variables rather than regression error terms.
3. Ignoring Clustering in Discrete Data: Misinterpreting stair-step horizontal bands on Q-Q plots caused by discrete 5-point Likert scales as distributional anomalies.
terms.apa_reference: Wilk, M. B., & Gnanadesikan, R. (1968). Probability plotting methods for the analysis of data. Biometrika, 55(1), 1-17. https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/55.1.1

terms.vietnamese: Khoa học bình thường và Khoa học cách mạng (Thomas Kuhn)
vietnamese_variants: Khoa học chuẩn tắc vs Cách mạng khoa học
terms.core_definition: The distinction between Normal Science and Revolutionary Science is the central historical and epistemological model of scientific progress introduced by Thomas S. Kuhn in The Structure of Scientific Revolutions (1962). Normal Science describes the cumulative, puzzle-solving enterprise carried out by scientific communities operating within an accepted, unquestioned Paradigm (shared ontological assumptions, exemplars, and methodological tools).
